# `#538` (lcalenzerodrop, closing #530's chain): the width row covered ONE of the four byte lanes -- a variant that serviced wide writes at lane 3 only swept it 3/3

*The MEASURED sections were filled from each table's `TABLE.out` after its run -- never from the predictions.*

**Detector-only.  No product line changes.**  `#530` (8bd97e4) shipped `regress/lca_widewrite_probe.py`, the width row its
closing pass 6 owed: one PROM GETENV write of 16 bytes at (C=16, k=0, lane 3), and a contract claiming it caught *"any
guard that declines a len > 8 WRITE"*.

## WHAT PASS 2 FOUND, AND WHAT THE FLAGSHIP RULED

`#530`'s pass 2 (`regress/artifacts/lcaisalane/p2_8bd97e4_20260918/`) and its §F2 adjudication pass
(`panel_20260918_190129`) measured seven one-edit variants the row cannot see -- the Opus seat, 102 legs on unmodified
alphabook1, every value predicted first (`regress/artifacts/lcalenzerodrop/opus_p2_20260918/`).  The §F2 pass overturned
my provisional "debt" ruling eight of eight.  **fable5 ruled last (identity verified, claude-fable-5-1), narrower than the
panel's headline:**

* **ONE floor breach, `vc`** -- `&& (len <= 8 || (P & 3) == 3)` services wide writes at the rowed lane only.  LANE is a
  floor axis because the body's `data[ofs]` distinguishes all four lanes, so the floor is {write arm} x {lane 0-3}.
* **The other six are clause-(e) debt, disclosed against ALREADY-RULED classes** -- width cut-offs above 16 (the body tests
  `len` only against 0), ports (`p_port10`), the discarded sparse bits (`lcaisasize`), chunk position (a stateless handler).
* **The popular two-cell fix {mc2, kbc1024} is a COVERING, not a closure** -- a lane-1-only exemption escapes both
  (grok, glm).  *Closing at the address the variant used, rather than closing the partition, is the `#499` error -- and my
  provisional ruling and the panel's modal answer made it from opposite sides.*

## THE CLOSURE

* **Four cells, one per lane, each an ISOLATED session** (a read-arm fall-through writes zeros into store_buf's source,
  so shared sessions would confound): `wide` (SCR 0x2ff, lane 3 -- the shipped cell, its row names kept), `l0w16` (MCR
  0x2fc, lane 0), `low16` (8259 IMR 0x21, lane 1), `l2w16` (MSR 0x2fe, lane 2).  13 rows.
* **The width is pinned by CONSTRUCTION** -- no forwarded byte distinguishes a 16-byte chunk from a 4-byte one at the same
  address, so each cell declares its chunk list and the probe asserts the chunk landing on each observed register is wider
  than 8.
* **Two harness defects of the first version fixed:** the retry now fires only on a session that is still ALIVE (it used to
  retry a dead one, and could record a host death as a pass); the exit status is non-zero on FAIL.
* **The contract ENUMERATES**: what is caught at each lane, and eight disclosed classes, each with its warrant -- `p_port10`
  and `lcaisasize` cited by name.  **Three wrong records corrected in place:** the parent header's *"The width cell is
  therefore COVERED"*, the old clause (iii)'s shared-predicate warrant, and the `live` row's "device signature" label.

**fable5 (claude-fable-5-1, identity verified) ruled CLOSES, CONTINGENT on a full re-run on the final instrument.**
The instrument changed after the table, so "a comparison owes ONE instrument":

- **THE HARNESS (L1, unshipped): the emulator's WAIT STATUS never reached `alive`.**  `alive` came only from pty read
  timing, so a death after the last observation, or a silent hang, PASSED.  codex demonstrated it with an in-memory
  mock of the real `session()`; the Opus seat had flagged it as hardening.
  - Fix: drain the pty to EOF after `quit`, THEN close, reap, and require a clean exit.  Draining first matters,
    because closing the master first SIGHUPs the child and scores a clean run as a death.
  - Measured both ways: status 0 on a clean run, 256 on alphavmkill's `exit(1)`.
  - The committed parent (`lca_isalane_probe.py`) and 54 other pty probes are filed as the class `ptywaitstatus`,
    with the peer's codex J6 reading: all 55 non-USED files have the blind spot.
- **`l2w16 live` was not a round-trip control.**  The MSR resets to 0 and ORs 0xb0 on every access, so preset 0x00
  read 0xb0 whether or not the write landed.  The preset is now 0x01.
- **The probe now creates `alpha_dummy.bin`.**  It is untracked, so a fresh clone would red every row.
- **The contract is re-worded as L4s, each moving no cell into or out of the floor:**
  - (ii) port bits ABOVE the lane (`P & 3` are lane bits, inside the floor);
  - (iv) any STATEFUL decline;
  - (vii) EQUIVALENT: a3 = 16 against a 16-byte string transfers no NUL at all;
  - (viii) an added forward AFTER the lane byte is visible;
  - new (ix): lane 2's value bits under the MSR's `| 0xb0`;
  - new (x): the inner forward's width;
  - new (xi): the chunk ladder, confirmed at measurement by KILLLEN8, and disclosed for the future (a source presence
    pin is filed);
  - `== L` for L != 3, and address misroutes, are labelled DERIVED.
- **The parent header's first-version present tense (:164-169) and its lane-3-specific fold (:179) are corrected in
  place, comment-only.**
- **Receipts:** `logs/bins.md5` (18 hashes; only w_base == w_restored) and `logs/BUILD_PHASE.out`.

# `#537` (fbsmlane): #442's harness could never pass its own self-mutant lane -- because of one character -- and the pin it was given certified only that SOME row killed

**Owner ruling 2026-09-18: FIX it, do not re-date it.**  `gate_offline.sh` had carried `fbpending_bound` in
`SM_EXEMPT` since `#442`, dated 2026-09-20.  The harness always had its `@@SELFCHECK@@` comparator control, but
its SELF-MUTANT lane never ran, and the two catch different failures.  Ledger row `fbsmlane` diagnosed why on
2026-08-27 and named the fix shape; this round is that fix, measured, plus the pin the panel found wrong.

## THE DEFECT

`selfmutant.py` reads a verdict only as `\b([A-Z0-9_]+_PASS)\b`.  The harness printed `FBBOUND_VERDICT=PASS` --
an `=` where the pattern needs `_` -- so no run of it could ever be read as passing, and a lane wired to it could
only ever report SETUP.  Latent host-side detector debt; nothing guest-visible.

## THE FIX -- four files, no emulator code

* `diff_fbpending_bound.c` prints the house token, `FBBOUND_PASS` / `FBBOUND_FAIL`, and gate 2's `#442` verdict
  row greps `^FBBOUND_PASS$` in the same edit -- the coupling `fbsmlane` warned about: rename the token without
  the grep and a dead lane becomes a red gate.
* `gate_offline.sh` calls the lane with the flags only this harness needs -- it is the one differential that
  LINKS ~221 `build/` objects instead of compiling standalone -- and with RELATIVE `-I` paths, so the lane
  compiles the MIRROR's mutated `dev_footbridge.c`.  An absolute `-I` would compile the pristine copy in both
  arms; `selfmutant.py`'s binary-identity check then SETUPs, so the row reds rather than lies -- measured below
  as N2.  `fbpending_bound` moves from `SM_EXEMPT` to `SM_COVERED`.
* **The pin is R3's `cats, slowest legal` row, case-qualified -- not `R4`, the aggregate `#442` added to be
  pinned.**  See the next section.
* `selfmutant.py`'s timeout-margin comment gains the 13th lane's timings; `fbpending_bound.why` corrects two
  sentences; the gate paragraph that said the lane "DOES NOT RUN YET" becomes its discharge note.

**AND A STRAY FRAGMENT `#442` LEFT IN THE SAME FILE.**  `' ' ') -lm -L/usr/X11R6/lib -lX11"` sat below the
`rtc_range` lane call.  It opened a quote that ran to the apostrophe in "run.sh's" six lines later, and executed a
command named `' '` on every gate run -- `command not found`, rc 127, reproduced in isolation.  Harmless under
`set -u`, because only comments were swallowed, but a fragment, not code.  Removed.

## THE PIN -- `#442`'s PREMISE WAS FALSE, AND THE AGGREGATE PIN IT JUSTIFIED IS VERDICT-EQUIVALENT

`#442` added `R4 every case bounded` (`failures == 0`) as the lane's pin, reasoning that `selfmutant.py` requires the
pinned row id to name exactly one row while R1 and R3 each print seven times.  **The two passes took that apart
from both ends:**

* **The Opus seat, pass 2, MEASURED that an R4 pin certifies only that SOME row kills.**  Blind R3
  (`>= 1` -> `>= 0`) and tighten R1 (`trough >= 0` -> `>= 1`) together: R3 detects nothing, R1 reds, R4 follows --
  and the lane says `SELFMUTANT_OK ... killed by the named row: FAIL R4`.  Each edit alone is green on the fix,
  which makes the pair a licensed reach-the-guard composite rather than a steered one.
* **The codex seat, §F2, found the premise itself false:** the helper matches the pin ANYWHERE in the printed line,
  so R3's row for ONE case names exactly one row.

So the lane pins `R3 the reset still owes one interrupt        cats, slowest legal`.  The string spans the
harness's row-name padding, so a one-space drift SETUPs loudly rather than silently (measured).  R4 stays as the
every-case summary, and its printed name loses "(the selfmutant pin)".

*Harder on the finding, as the Opus seat was on its own: the composite lost no DETECTION -- the tightened R1 carries
R3's check -- so the R4 pin lost "which row", not a caught defect.  Filing it would have been defensible.  What made
in-round right is that the fix is one string in material not yet shipped (L1).*

# `#530` (lcaisalane): a guest BYTE access to an ISA port 2 or 3 mod 4 ended the host, and the one pass that could not close was the detector's width coverage, not the fix

*`#530` lands AFTER `#531`-`#535` although its number is older: it was held open for exactly one
owed pass -- the width row below -- and a round is not committed while its own closing verdict says
DO NOT CLOSE.*

**`dev_lca.c`'s `DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_isa)` held the last guest-triggerable host kill in the file.**
Measured with a comment-stripping parser on 2026-09-18: HEAD carries exactly ONE live `exit(1)` in
`dev_lca.c`, at `lca_isa`; with this fix applied the file carries NONE.  Every other `exit(1)` the file
once held was removed by `#516` and `#518`, and survives only in the comments that record them.

## THE DEFECT

The access function computed `ofs = relative_addr & 3` and then `if (ofs > len) { fatal(...); exit(1); }`.
So a guest ended the emulator with a **byte** access to an ISA port 2 or 3 mod 4, or a **word** access to
a port 3 mod 4 -- ordinary BWX loads and stores, ungated -- and at a port 3 mod 4 also with the 1- or
2-byte HEAD of an unaligned access that `memory_rw` splits at 1 KB.  Separately, the READ arm discarded
the fetched byte at `ofs == len`, so a lane-1 byte read answered zero with a false success.

## THE FIX (+17 / -7)

The byte for ISA port P sits at buffer position `(P & 3) % len` on **both** arms -- the lane for the
21066's own len 4/8 accesses, and the rule the write arm already applied wherever the old guard let it
run.  `len == 0` is refused before the `%` (no producer reaches it).  One byte is forwarded whatever
`len` is; the size field `a<4:3>` is not decoded here (filed: `lcaisasize`).

## WITNESS -- rung 3

`regress/lca_isalane_probe.py`, on unmodified `-E alpha -e alphabook1`: **13/16 on the committed build**
-- a byte read at lane 1 answers zero with a false success, and lanes 2 and 3 end the process -- and
green post-fix with the same script.

## THE DETECTOR, AND WHY THE CHAIN TOOK SEVEN PASSES

352 rows across the `{write, read} x {DROP, SWAP, DUPLICATE, ADD-OTHER}` forward-count product, with
`m_lenzero` measured separately as the sixteenth mutant (37/37, EQUIVALENT: no producer delivers
`len == 0` -- warranted by the CALLERS, since `store_buf` bottoms out at `store_byte` and a CPU access
is 1..8 bytes; *not* by `memory_rw`'s truncation, which only clips `len` down and proves nothing about
an entry length of 0).

**Closing pass 6 did not close, and it was right not to.**  `table7_20260916/CLOSE6_VERDICT.md`: a
file-reading seat named a clause-(d)-shaped width mutant, `&& len <= 8`, predicted to sweep 352/352,
and the verdict set the stop condition before any leg ran -- *escapes AND len > 8 is guest-reachable ->
L2, add a len > 8 row in-round.*  Both halves are now established:

* **It escapes.**  `#530`'s own `KILLLEN8_RUN.out` (the guard form `len == 0 || len > 8`) and the
  2026-09-18 `M2_len8` leg both score **352/352**.
* **len > 8 IS guest-reachable.**  `store_buf()` (`memory.c:837-857`) issues `memory_rw` at `psize` in
  {1024, 256, 64, 16, 4, 1}, and the PROM GETENV callback (`cpu_alpha_palcode.c:141-144`) hands it a
  guest-controlled destination `a2` AND length `a3`.

**Why no existing row could ever see it** -- the distinction Fable drew and which makes a ROW mandatory
rather than a contract line: `&byte, len` diverges INSIDE the probed width set, so a contract line
discharges it; `len <= 8` diverges only OUTSIDE it.  The probe is instruction-driven and the widest
Alpha store, STQ, is 8 bytes -- *no instruction-driven row can ever express len > 8.*

## THE OWED ROW -- `regress/lca_widewrite_probe.py`, the NON-INSTRUCTION path

Shipped as its OWN file rather than folded into `lca_isalane_probe.py`: folding it in would move 352
measured rows and owe a full re-measure to show nothing shifted.  The parent's header now says where the
cell is covered, so an edit that deletes the new file re-opens it visibly.

`wide getenv`: boot with `-o ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP`, preset the ns16550 SCR (port 0x2ff) with a 1-byte STB,
then `CALL_PAL 0x3fffffe` (the word `machine_alpha.c:189` stores at the PROM entry) with `a0 = 0x22`
(GETENV), `a1 = 0x8` (BOOTED_OSFLAGS), `a2 = k0(SP(0x2ff))`, `a3 = 16`.  `0x5fe0` fails the 1024/256/64
alignment tests and passes 16, so `store_buf` issues exactly ONE 16-byte `memory_rw`; `lca_isa` forwards
`s[(0x2ff & 3) % 16] = s[3] = 'D'`.  Predictions written first (`PRETABLE.out`, 14:59:49).

    base        WIDEWRITE_RESULT=3/3   predicted 3/3   wide getenv = 0x44 ('D')
    M2_len8     WIDEWRITE_RESULT=2/3   predicted 2/3   wide getenv = 0x5a (the PRESET)
    KILLLEN8    WIDEWRITE_RESULT=2/3   predicted 2/3   wide getenv = 0x5a (the PRESET)

**Every value matched the prediction written before any run.**  Source: `logs/TABLE.out`, all three legs
postdating the 16:12:41 instrument, no retries, a `WIDEWRITE_DONE` sentinel on each.

**Both "only a run settles" items are now settled.**  `-o` delivers the boot string on alphabook1 (`s[3]`
arrived).  And execution does NOT resume at `pc + 4` after an inline `CALL_PAL 0x3fffffe`:
`alpha_prom_call` ends with `cpu->pc = cpu->cd.alpha.r[ALPHA_RA]` (`cpu_alpha_palcode.c:153`), because
the real PROM entry is reached by `jsr`.

> **RUN 1 WAS AN L1 CONSTRUCTION FAILURE, and it is preserved rather than hidden**
> (`logs/run1_L1_no_return_address/`, with a `WHY.txt`).  The row executed the `CALL_PAL` inline without
> loading `ra`, so the PROM call returned to address 0, phase 4 never ran, and base, M2 and KILLLEN8 all
> read 0 alike.  **The PRETABLE had pre-committed that a base leg short of 3/3 means the ROW is broken and
> no mutant score means anything** -- so it was read as a construction defect, fixed (the return address
> is now COMPUTED from the instruction layout, not typed in), and re-run.  *Deciding before the run what a
> failing base leg would mean is what stopped run 1's identical zeros from being read as a result.*

**The product code is not touched by the row.**  At len 16, `(relative_addr & 3) % 16` reduces to
`relative_addr & 3`, in [0,3], safe (probe header `:159-162`).

## AN INDEPENDENT REPLICATION -- AND IT SAT UNREAD IN THIS ROW'S OWN DIRECTORY

`regress/artifacts/lcalenzerodrop/opus_getenv_20260918/` holds an Opus seat's measurement from **08:16 --
hours before the width row was built** -- reaching the same verdict by a different road: `a1 = 6`
(`PROM_E_BOOTED_FILE`), port `0x3ff`, `a3 = 64`.  Base put `s[3] = 'h'` (0x68, from `alpha_dummy.bin`) on
the SCR; `&& len <= 8` left the preset.  **Two instruments, two variables, two ports, one answer.**

**And it already loaded `ra`** -- `RA = 26`, the return address computed from the instruction layout as
`idx + 1`, exactly the fix run 1 then needed.  *The answer to run 1's L1 failure was sitting in this row's
own artifacts directory, unread.*  It is the fifth unread-review instance of the session; the discipline it
argues for is the one already written down: **open the row's own directory before building in it.**

It is preserved as a WITNESS and marked FROZEN: it `exec()`s the first 459 lines of
`lca_isalane_probe.py`, whose header grew 12 comment lines in this commit, so a re-run would slice the parent
in the wrong place.  The shipped detector is `lca_widewrite_probe.py`.

## THE SHIPPED FILE IS ITSELF MEASURED

`regress/lca_widewrite_probe.py` differs from the measured instrument in exactly ONE code line -- `DUMMY`'s
path made relative, as the parent's is -- checked by a parser that compared 152 code lines per side and
found exactly 2 differing.  It was then **re-run as shipped** against the same three binaries
(`logs/certify_shipped/`, instrument md5 `72f489f8`): **base 3/3, M2 2/3, KILLLEN8 2/3**, no retries.
*"Equivalent rewrite" is an argument; this is a measurement.*

## FILED OR REOPENED, NOT FIXED HERE

* **`lcawidefold` REOPENS.**  Only `s[3]` reaches the port; the other fifteen bytes of a 16-byte store
  are dropped.  Its recorded reopen condition was *"a guest found issuing GETENV into the ISA window"* --
  and `wide getenv` is exactly that guest.  Reopened, not re-filed.
* **An M2 side effect, recorded as an observation about the MUTANT:** under `&& len <= 8` a wide store
  falls into the READ arm, whose zero-fill writes `data[]` -- which here is `store_buf`'s SOURCE, the
  emulator's own `boot_string_argument`.  Shipped code returns before that loop.

# `#535` (pcc2c040mienannounce): #512's detector had one uncovered cell -- and it ran in no gate at all

**Late-dissent disposition 2: a MEASURED false pass against a shipped detector's floor, repaired in a follow-up
commit.**  No emulator code changes; the #512 fix itself was judged REAL-AND-RIGHTLY-FIXED by all nine assess seats.

**THE HOLE.**  Every announce row of `regress/pcc2_c040_probe.py` (`c040 says`, `c040 once`, `c040 predirty`) writes
`0x04` -- MIEN clear.  The sessions that write `0x06` (MIEN|C040, what an MVME187 driver actually programs) never
looked for the announce.  agy's late seat PREDICTED an announce gated on `!MIEN` would pass every row; the Opus seat
BUILT it in a scratch clone and MEASURED **16/16** on the shipped probe
(`regress/artifacts/pcc2c040kill/opus_mien_20260918/M_announce_notmien.raw`).  MIEN is a body-tested operand of the
repaired path, so this is a floor cell, not coverage debt: L2.

**THE REPAIR -- one row, no new session.**  `c040 says mien` reads the announce from the existing `c040 noassert`
transcript (a `0x06` write).  Measured by Opus on a clean clone: base **17/17**, `M_announce_notmien` **16/17**
(`rep_BASE.raw`, `rep_M_announce_notmien.raw`); re-measured here on `build/gxemul` (source identical to HEAD but for
a comment-only hunk; binary newer than source): **17/17**.  The code is byte-identical to Opus's measured copy once
comments are stripped.

**AND THE LARGER FINDING: THE PROBE RAN IN NO GATE.**  Its manifest entry said so (`wiringcliff`), so all sixteen shipped
rows defended nothing.  It is now wired into `gate_arm.sh` beside the other PCC2 probes, by row name, with a completion
sentinel and emitted/green/red counts pinned (17 at first, 18 after pass 2).  It needs only the binary (mvme88k/mvme187 constructs from the PROM).

**PASS 2 FOUND THE SAME CLASS A SECOND TIME, AND IT WAS REPAIRED IN-ROUND (L1).**  `panel_20260918_153836`: seven
RATIFY-WITH-FINDINGS; the Opus seat DO NOT RATIFY on measurement.  It built five new mutants and ALL FIVE escaped the
17-row probe.  Two were the same class as the hole this round repaired: **presence x MIEN** was the first pass's cell,
**COUNT x MIEN** is this one -- mutants A (latch skipped while MIEN is set) and F (latch bit set only while MIEN is
clear) print the announce SEVEN times in the MIEN-set session and every row stayed green (codex and glm predicted the
class independently).  Per the repair-chain rule the second instance owes the class closure, so the whole {MIEN} x
{latch} product for the announce is now rowed: `c040 once mien` counts the announce in the same `td` transcript.
**Measured: BASE 18/18, A 17/18, F 17/18**, each red on exactly that row (`r535_20260918/opus535/r2_*.raw`, all ending
`PCC2C040_DONE`); the committed probe's code is identical to the measured copy with comments stripped.  The gate now
lists and pins **18**.

conjunct) is clause (e).

**Records corrected in place:** the probe's own "does NOT catch a fix that announces correctly and fails to suppress"
contract paragraph described only the first seven rows and is marked SUPERSEDED (the L2 rows kill that mutant, 14/16).

# `#534` (stagetokens repair): four tools read one ledger field, and each had its own copy of what it meant

**`#532` shipped without a pass 2.  The pass then ran and did not ratify it** (fable5, `claude-fable-5-1`,
`regress/artifacts/stagetokens/pass2_20260918/fable5_adjudication_20260918.md`; nine seats in
`panel_20260918_083716` plus the Opus seat).  This round is the repair it adopted, and it is harness-only: no
`src/` file changes.  Witness `harness:` -- the controls below fail on mutants of the tools themselves.

## THE CAUSE, STATED ONCE

Four readers of `entries[].note` -- `check_stage_panels.py`, `check_fable_queue.py`, `gen_dashboard.py`,
`check_fix_seats.py` -- each carried their own copy of the stage tokens.  Every mis-classification measured in
`#532` and its pass 2 was one copy not mirroring another.  **So the literals AND the classification now live in
`tools/pipeline/stage_tokens.py`**, and precommit section **H2** refuses a token spelled as a code string anywhere
else in `tools/pipeline/` (an AST walk: docstrings and comments describe tokens, and are exempt).

**AN ENTRY HAS TWO INDEPENDENT PROPERTIES** -- *is it an answer?* and *does it exempt its whole stage?* -- and
`#532`'s code asked them as one `if ... continue`.  A single-seat re-read is BOTH; the new entry-scoped
`[NOT A SEAT ANSWER]` is NEITHER.

## WHAT CHANGED, BY RULING

* **R2 -- entry-scoped marker.**  Fourteen entries that meant only *"this entry is not a seat answer"* carried the
  STAGE-scoped no-panel token, which would have pre-silenced any panel later recorded on those stages.  Converted.
* **R3 / F1 -- two exemptions were FALSE.**  `asiceventaddr`'s panel was pass 2 on its own commit `9ca9cca` (ran
  6/9: now HELD for fable5, opus5 and deepseek, whose answer there is a thinking burn).  `pcc2c040assertrow`'s
  panel WAS convened on it; fable5 recommended filing the re-fire, **the owner chose REOPEN AND HOLD**, so its four

# `#533` (landiskaux): landisk's wdc aux register sat at the PC-layout `+0x206`, so the kernel's soft reset landed on unmapped memory

**One `case`, and the address is a primary-source constant rather than a derivation.** `dev_wdc.c`'s
"Special hacks for individual machines" switch had no `MACHINE_LANDISK` arm, so landisk kept the pre-switch
`alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206` and registered `wdc_altstatus` at `0x14000206`. The OpenBSD 7.6
landisk kernel writes Device Control at `0x1400002c`.

    case MACHINE_LANDISK:
            alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x2c;
            break;

Appended AFTER the IQ80321 case, so a later missing `break;` in the new arm cannot fall into an older one.

## THE WARRANT -- three independent routes to 44

* NetBSD `sys/arch/landisk/dev/wdc_obio.c` v1.11 and OpenBSD v1.5 both `#define WDC_OBIO_AUXREG_OFFSET 0x2c` and
  map the aux register at `or_addr + WDC_OBIO_AUXREG_OFFSET`, UNSCALED, while the command registers use `i * 2`.
  Copies preserved in `regress/artifacts/landiskaux/rung3_opus_20260918/{netbsd,openbsd}_wdc_obio.c`.
* The codex seat disassembled the 7.6 ramdisk: `add #44,r5` before the mapping call, and `mov.b r7,@r6` at
  `0x8c15f6e8`, the census's store PC.
* The 2026-08-27 boot census (`regress/artifacts/landiskaux/census_20260827/`): exactly TWELVE byte writes to
  `0x1400002c`, ZERO reads, four runs, two instruments.

**`0x16 * addr_mult` IS NOT HOW THE SOURCE STATES THE ADDRESS, AND THIS ROUND NEARLY SHIPPED IT.**  *(L4, corrected 2026-09-18 from a peer session's late review: this heading said "IS NOT THE ADDRESS", which is false -- `0x16 * 2 == 0x2c`, and line 101 of this same block says those spellings "all ARE" the address.  It EVALUATES to the address; what is wrong with it is that it implies a stride-scaling nothing supports.)* `0x16` is `0x2c / 2`, a factorisation
of the measured answer -- the landisk-shaped echo of macppc's `WDC_AUXREG_OFFSET 0x16 << 4 = 0x160`. The
2026-08-28 pass 1 (`brief_p1_20260828.md`) had already said *SHIP `+ 0x2c`* and called the multiplier route
superseded; a 09-18 prep entry reintroduced it and the 09-18 pass-1 brief inherited it. The panel caught it.
*Prior work on disk, not folded in -- the census was read and the verdict beside it was not.*

## WHAT IT FIXES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

The first of the twelve writes is `0x0c` = `WDCTL_RST | WDCTL_4BIT`, a real ATA **soft reset**, silently lost
before this change. Six carry `WDCTL_4BIT` and five `WDCTL_IDS`. **The fix DELIVERS the `WDCTL_IDS` (nIEN)
writes; it does NOT implement nIEN** -- the aux handler acts on `WDCTL_RST` only.

The pre-switch `+0x206` is untouched and still serves every machine without a case. Only landisk moves.
Unmapping `0x14000206` on landisk is measured safe: the census records zero accesses there, and nothing else is
registered between the end of `wdc` (`0x1400000f`) and RAM at `0x1e000000`.

## WITNESS AND DETECTOR

**Witness (rung 3), MEASURED by the Opus seat on unmodified `-E landisk`** --
`regress/artifacts/landiskaux/rung3_opus_20260918/`: the same guest program pre-fix (a Device Control
store to `0x2c` is swallowed, status stays `0x09`) and post-fix (the reset lands, status `0x01`), with a RAM
liveness control and a device signature (`0x2c` reads back the status byte). The census is the rung-4 pre-fix
half.

**Detector: `regress/landisk_aux_probe.py`, 6 rows, wired into `gate_sh_rounding.sh` IN THIS COMMIT.** Every row
reads a guest-visible register; none rests on the `[ wdc: ... ]` debug line, which goes quiet under `-q`.

    pre-fix                    1/6   prefix_HEAD.out  (build/ = the working tree MINUS the landisk case;
                                    build's dev_sh4.c carries other rounds' uncommitted lines -- no effect on these rows)
    fix                        6/6

**Kill table**, scratch clone, baseline `cmp` CLEAN, clone restored before the legs
(`regress/artifacts/landiskaux/detector_20260918/logs/TABLE.out`). `PRETABLE.out` was written BEFORE the table
and predicted every score; all six matched:

    base     6/6  1,1,1,1,1,1
    M_head   1/6  1,0,0,0,0,0   no landisk case
    M_0x16   3/6  1,0,1,0,0,1   `+ 0x16'
    M_0x2d   3/6  1,0,1,0,0,1   `+ 0x2d'
    M_both   4/6  1,1,0,1,1,0   keep the 0x206 registration AND add 0x2c
    M_above  3/6  1,0,1,0,0,1   case above IQ80321 without break

*Writing PRETABLE caught a copied prediction: `M_0x16` was first written 1/6, as if it were the pre-fix state.
It is not -- `0x206` is unmapped under it too -- so the two `0x206` rows are green and the score is 3/6, which
is what it measured. Predictions are derived per mutant, never copied.*

`M_both` is killed ONLY by the two `0x206` rows. A detector that rowed `0x2c` alone would pass a fix that
registered both addresses.

## THE FIX CHANGES BOOT BEHAVIOUR, SO A BOOT WAS MEASURED -- and the first attempt failed for a reason not under test

The soft reset that used to vanish now reaches `wdc_new_command_reset()`. The Opus seat asked whether a real
landisk boot still completes; nothing had shown it. `drive_guest.py landisk` (the gate_crossfamily rig, WITH a
64 MB disk attached) on both binaries, `regress/artifacts/landiskaux/boot_20260918/`:

    fixed    VERDICT=PASS  7.4 s  1,879,401,505 instrs  SH7751R,42   unmapped 0x1400002c in emulator log:  0
    pre-fix  VERDICT=PASS  7.3 s  1,879,418,819 instrs  SH7751R,42   unmapped 0x1400002c in emulator log: 12

`wd0` attaches in both. **The pre-fix log's twelve unmapped accesses reproduce the census on the gate's own rig,
and the fixed log's zero is the same script going green -- a rung-4 witness by clause (i).**

*The FIRST boot attempt read `REASON=EXITED NINSTRS=0 VERDICT=FAIL`. It was the apparatus: `drive_guest.py`
changes directory before `execvp`, so the RELATIVE binary path did not exist and the emulator never started.
Caught by asking whether it failed for the reason under test -- zero instructions is a launch that did not
happen, not a boot that broke -- and by running the pre-fix binary as a control.*

## PASS 2 -- nine seats, and the ask-again found nothing that reaches the floor

`panel_20260918_083716` plus the Opus seat, fable5 adjudicating last. The fix passed every seat. The one
permitted ask-again produced:

* **`case MACHINE_LANDISK:` -> `default:`** (codex, kimi, and MEASURED by Opus): 6/6 here, but it moves every
  caseless machine off `+0x206`, and `wdc_altdigin_probe.py` in the same gate kills it at **17/22**
  (`regress/artifacts/landiskaux/opus_askagain_20260918/`). Carried elsewhere; now named in the contract.
* **A registration widened to cover `0x206`** (Opus, measured 6/6): guest-equivalent on landisk, because the aux
  handler declines every nonzero offset. The `aux 206 gone` note claimed "UNMAPPED" -- corrected to "unmapped
  OR declined, cannot tell" (L4).
* **Equivalent spellings** of the address (grok): `0x16 * addr_mult`, `| 0x2c`, `+ 44`, the absolute -- all ARE
  `0x1400002c` on landisk. Not escapes.
* **A detector-side weakening** (grok): moving the probe's old-address oracle `0x206 -> 0x207` keeps 6/6 and lets
  `M_both` pass. Those two rows are `M_both`'s only killers; the contract now says their constant is load-bearing.
* **The reset-bit test** (glm): not this probe's property -- every store here is `0x0c`, RST set -- and **carried by
  NOTHING WIRED.** A first draft said `wdc_altoffset_4bit_probe.py` in `gate_hygiene.sh`; fable5 measured that false
  three ways (the probe is unwired, `gate_hygiene.sh` names it only in a comment listing it OUTSIDE its
  denominator, and it writes only RST-set values). `if (idata & WDCTL_RST)` -> `if (idata)` escapes every wired
  row. Outside this round's (d) closure (a different function), so coverage debt, not a floor breach: FILED as
  `wdcrstbitonly`, and deliberately NOT rowed here -- a seventh row would re-table six mutants and turn a
  records-only repair into a floor-bound diff that owes its own pass.
* deepseek's objection that "unmapped memory" contradicts the collision check is REFUTED on reading: pre-fix,
  `0x2c` WAS unmapped, which is what the collision check shows.

**DISCLOSED, not rowed:** the initialiser `+0x206` changing (landisk overwrites it, so no landisk row can see
it); IQ80321 losing its own `break` (no IQ80321 rig); the registration width 2 -> 1 (every access here is one
byte at offset 0 -- `wdcaltwidth`); keying on `machine_type` alone.

## LATE REVIEW (a peer session's Opus seat, 2026-09-18) -- evidence in `regress/artifacts/landiskaux/latereview_20260918/`

* **A rung-3 witness in ONE frozen script** (`lax_probe.py`, md5 `75b241ba05c2`): **8/17 pre-fix, 17/17 post-fix**
  (`probe_t1_base.out`, `probe_t1_fix.out`).  Rung-4 boot compare: unmapped writes to `0x1400002c` go 12 -> 0, and under
  `-v` the post-fix build logs ALT. CTRL x12 in the census's exact order.
* **THE ROUND'S ONE GUEST-VISIBLE ATTACH CHANGE, which the census had left NOT SETTLED:** with a CD image attached, pre-fix
  OpenBSD mis-attaches it as a phantom `wd0 ... <ST506> 68MB` disk; post-fix it recognises ATAPI.  Mechanism at rung 3
  (`lax_cd_probe.py` 1/3 -> 3/3): COMMAND_RESET is set at exactly one site, the aux-register RST arm, so the ATAPI
  signature was unreachable before the fix.  No gate uses a landisk CD.
* **`0x2c` has an independent source**: the booted OpenBSD 7.6 kernel's `wdc_obio_attach` maps `iobase+0x2c` for 2 bytes
  (`add #44,r5` at `0x8c16017c`).
* **A premise corrected**: "a wrong multiplier maps the register SILENTLY" is false except for windows still covering
  `0x2c`; the `winm1` mutant is warning-silent there but `landisk_aux_probe.py` kills it (3/6) -- a contract line now says so.
* **Filed, not fixed (late-dissent disposition 3):** `landiskauxorder` -- the case landed LAST, making IQ80321's `break`

# `#532` (stagetokens): reading 23 unread seat answers took two hard gates from GREEN to RED — and the honest fix was a token that did not exist

**HEAD had ZERO stage violations. The working tree had NINETEEN, and every one was created by
recording seat answers that already existed on disk.** Measured, not reasoned: the two checkers
were run against `git show HEAD:tools/pipeline/ledger.json` and then against the working ledger.

Recording a seat's remark about row X promotes X's stage from ABSENT — or from a 1-seat FILING —
to a 2..8-seat "short panel", and a short panel is exactly what sections H and I redden on.

> ### *** SO THE GATES FIRED BECAUSE THE RECORD GOT MORE HONEST, AND THE ONLY WAY TO GREEN THEM
> ### WITH THE EXISTING TOKENS WOULD HAVE BEEN TO WRITE A FALSE SENTENCE INTO THE LEDGER. ***

`check_stage_panels.py` predicted this in its own comment years before it happened here:
*"any pass that sweeps filed rows can promote a filing into a short stage without anyone deciding
to."* It did not predict the scale.

## THE SORTING RULE IS THE BRIEF'S SUBJECT, NEVER THE SEAT COUNT — it overturned my sort THREE times

The mechanical test: read the `ev` field for its panel dir, open that dir's `brief_sent.md`, and
ask **was this panel convened ON THIS ROW?**

| row | recorded seats | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `asiceventaddr` | **8** | NOT a stage — all eight cite `panel_20260826_222557`, a pass 2 on a COMMENT-ONLY commit to a vendored header. ***FALSE — corrected by `#534` (fable5 F1): that commit, `9ca9cca`, IS this row's own commit, so the stage RAN 6/9. It is now HELD for fable5, opus5 and deepseek (a thinking burn in that panel).*** |
| `diskimagesign`, `pcc2genctlc040alias`, `sh4dmacie` | 8 each | REAL stages — they share `panel_20260917_100431`, whose brief IS convened on them |
| `pcc2c040assertrow`, `pcc2c040returnmutant` | 8 / 2 | NOT subjects — that brief's five `### commit` headings do not include them; they are SIBLING rows of the `#512` work |

**The count is a CORRELATE of "a panel ran"; the brief's subject is the thing itself.** My first
pass sorted by count and was wrong in both directions at once — a row with eight recorded seats
that is not a stage, and rows with the same count that are.

*(Incidental records note: `panel_20260917_100431`'s own heading reads "WHY THESE SIX AND NOT THE
OTHER TEN" while the body carries FIVE `### commit` headings. Counted, not assumed.)*

## THE TOKEN: `[NOT A PANEL STAGE: NO PANEL CONVENED]`

Neither existing token was TRUE of this situation. `RE_READ` says **SINGLE-SEAT** and these carry
2, 3, 4, 6 and 8; `ANNOTATION` asserts a **pre-2026-08-16 vintage** that is simply false of a
2026-09-17 entry. The file's own history records the last time someone reached for the nearest
token to turn a gate green — *"THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT CLEARING THAT USED THE TOKEN ABOVE, WHICH
WOULD HAVE PUT A FALSE STATEMENT IN THE LEDGER"* — and that attempt was backed out. This is that
lesson obeyed rather than re-learned.

**THE TOKEN STATES THE GENERAL CLAIM AND THE NOTE CARRIES THE SPECIFIC REASON**, which is a
deliberate break from the two tokens above it. A first draft read `INCIDENTAL SEAT MENTION` — true
of eleven of the twelve stages and **FALSE of `ip30abortkill`'s `assess`**, whose two entries are a
rung-3 WITNESS BUILD and a ship-order ADJUDICATION: real work on that very row, and not a panel
seat answer at all. Rather than ship a token that is a lie about one of its own members, it was
rewritten to the only claim both gates actually need.

Negative-controlled in both directions on BOTH gates before it touched real data: a synthetic
3-seat post-cutoff stage reds `STAGE_PANELS_FAIL` and `FABLE_QUEUE_FAIL` without the token and
passes both with it — **and the token entry is proven not to count as a seat**, or marking a gap
would close it.

## TWO MIRRORING BLIND SPOTS, FOUND BY ASKING WHAT THE *OTHER* TOOLS DO WITH A TOKEN THEY DO NOT KNOW

* **`check_fable_queue.py` never knew `RE_READ`**, which has been in `check_stage_panels.py` since
  2026-08-21. A stage could pass section H and red section I on the same ledger entry.
* **`gen_dashboard.py` knew none of them.** `cell()` matched on `seat` + `phase` alone — and the
  tokens are conventionally written with `seat: "fable5"`, so **every annotation rendered as a
  FABLE CELL: the dashboard asserted that the flagship seat had answered stages on which no panel
  was ever convened.**

> **That second one is not cosmetic, and it is the INVERTED form of the failure this whole layer
> exists to prevent.** A missing cell reads as *"seat failure, never agreement"* — the legend says
> so out loud. A FABRICATED cell reads as agreement from the one seat whose agreement carries the
> most weight, and nothing anywhere contradicts it. The carrier already names this shape for
> mis-defanged markers: *"Defanging does not merely hide an obligation; it MANUFACTURES a seat
> answer that never happened."*

Controlled by rendering with the pre-fix generator: it emits **25,154 more characters**, and those
are exactly the fabricated cells.

> ### *** BOTH HALVES OF THAT CONTROL WERE WRONG.  Corrected by `#534` (fable5, `#532` pass 2, F3). ***
>
> **No cell was fabricated.** Measured on the pre-fix generator: zero token entries rendered as agreement --
> 1,415 `ok` cells before the change and 1,415 after.  ANNOTATION rendered as the held glyph, NOPANEL as the
> seat-failure glyph, HELD as its own `d`.  The tool was blind to the tokens and rendered them by ACCIDENT, which
> is a real defect; "the dashboard asserted the flagship had answered" is not what it did.  **And `25,154`
> reproduces nowhere**: by render boundary the delta is 30,242 / 22,589 / 28,385 bytes -- a frozen number.  The
> fix itself then over-reached: filtering HELD blanked real held cells and filtering ANNOTATION blanked honest
> annotations.  `#534` renders HELD as itself and every non-answer as a distinct `∅` with its note as tooltip.

**One cause for both: a token was added where it was needed and never mirrored.** The cheap
question that found them is the one worth carrying — *before relying on a token, ask what every
OTHER tool that reads this field does with it.*

## WHAT WAS CLEARED, AND WHAT REMAINS

19 -> 7 in section H, 16 -> 7 in section I. Nine stages annotated *(`#534` F2: the deriver `stage_tokens.py --census` gives **13 NOPANEL entries / 13 stages at `686d179`** and 0 at its parent; "nine" above and "eleven of the twelve" earlier were hand counts of one population, and of those 13, TWO were FALSE (`asiceventaddr`, `pcc2c040assertrow` -- `#534` F1/R3) and TWO were entry-scoped records (`lcalenzerodrop`, `stagetokens` -- `#534` R2); the other entry-scoped uses were written after `686d179`.  Listed by `git show 686d179:tools/pipeline/ledger.json`, not counted by hand)*; six closed rows named
individually in `fable_queue.md` for their flagship-only `regress` review (a prose mention does
not count — an id counts only where it HEADS an entry); two stages held-and-queued in one action,
per the directive that holding and queueing are one action and not two.

**The seven that remain are 8/9 missing only `fable5`**, and are the batch the flagship seat is
answering. Nothing was annotated to make them go away.

## AND THE REASON ALL OF THIS WAS WORTH DOING: `lcalenzerodrop`, FILED HIGH

`#530`'s CLOSING PASS was recorded with three seats and the round closed. **The dir holds five,
and four of them dissent** — codex *"DO NOT CLOSE YET"*, glm / deepseek / minimax *"NOT A VALID
CLOSING PASS"*. The round closed on `agy`, the single GO.

Their argument converges from four independent directions on one contradiction: if the fix's own
comment premise *`len 0 has no producer`* is TRUE, then `if (len == 0) return 0;` is **DEAD CODE**,
so a DROP of it is observationally identical to base, scores **352/352**, and contradicts the

## THE DISPOSITION WAS SETTLED BY THE HEADER THIS FILE ITSELF CITES

`dev_sgi_ip30.c` says "according to Linux/IP30" three times, so Linux's
`arch/mips/include/asm/sgi/heart.h` is the document the code was written FROM, and it is the
document that settles what the code MEANT:

    set_isr    +0x10020   "set interrupt status register"          write-side
    clear_isr  +0x10028   "clear interrupt status register"        write-side
    isr        +0x10030   "interrupt status register (read-only)"   READ-only

| site | member | what shipped |
|---|---|---|
| `0x10020` | **4 ACCEPT** on WRITE *(label contested -- see below)*, **2 DECLINE (silent)** on READ | the store is kept; the read declines SILENTLY rather than mirroring `d->isr` |
| `0x10028` | same | same |
| `0x10030` | **3** on WRITE; READ unchanged | the clear-on-write is DROPPED |
| `DEVICE_TICK` | **3** | the counter update still runs; delivery is not implemented |

## TWO ROW DEFECTS THE FIX EXPOSED, BOTH L1, BOTH REPAIRED IN-ROUND

**`acc 20000` expected a counter not to count.** It stored `0x1234` and wanted it back; it read
`0x161c`, and **`0x161c − 0x1234 = 0x3E8 = 1000` exactly** — `DEVICE_TICK`'s
`d->reg_0x20000 += 1000`. *The device was right and the row was wrong*: as written it was **red
on a correct build** and could never signal the defect it shipped with. The replacement oracle
is stronger ON ONE AXIS AND WEAKER ON ANOTHER — the counter is always a multiple of 1000 and `0x1234` is not, so the
residue is an exact multiple **iff the store landed**, which pins reachability the old literal
compare only achieved by accident on a tickless run.

**`isr keep` read the wrong load.** It issues three commands and used `printed()`, which is
`re.search` — the FIRST match — so it read the `0x10020` load the fix correctly declines (`0x0`)
instead of the `0x10030` read-back it wants. **Pre-fix this was invisible**, because the seeding
write aborted and the row read `died`. Repaired with `printed_last()` beside the existing
reader, same pattern, differing only in selection.

## THE RE-PIN OWED A RED, AND IT WAS MEASURED

Three `txt` rows pinned the literal `"IP30 legacy interrupt rewrite"` — the PRE-FIX message,
which this round renames. Re-pinning is necessary **and observationally identical to fitting the
test to the binary**, so the order discriminator was run explicitly:

    pre-fix HEAD   + OLD oracle        11/18    the three txt rows PASS
    pre-fix clone  + RE-PINNED oracle   8/18    the three txt rows FAIL   <- the red
    post-fix       + RE-PINNED oracle  18/18

**THESE THREE ARE THE 18-ROW INSTRUMENT AND THEY STAY AS THEY ARE.** They are not the round's
headline figures -- those are 8/21 and 21/21 above -- they are the ORDER PROOF for the oracle
correction, and an order proof is a statement about three runs of ONE instrument at one moment.
Re-measuring them on the 21-row form would not strengthen it and would quietly destroy the only
evidence that the re-pin preceded the code change.

`REPIN_prefix_20260917.out`, measured in a scratch clone restored by `git show HEAD:` (never
from a backup), verified to carry 4 `abort()` lines before being trusted, built fresh, with a
clone-local sentinel and no project tree mutated. **Without that middle row the score moves
11 → 18 with no way to tell which part is the fix and which is the re-pin.**

*Assessed and not changed: `reg_0x20000` is a 52-bit counter and `reg_0x30000` a 24-bit compare
per `heart.h`, and the tick's "only interrupt if the counter has passed the compare" TODO is
still a TODO — this round removes the host death, not the missing delivery subsystem.*

> ### *** "STRICTLY STRONGER" WAS FALSE, AND THE opus5 F2 SEAT MEASURED IT. ***
>
> The replacement oracle accepts `(readback - 0x1234) % 1000 == 0`, and **N = 0 IS ADMISSIBLE**.
> So with `d->reg_0x20000 += 1000;` DELETED the readback is exactly `0x1234`, the residue is 0,
> and the row is GREEN: `MH_nocounter` **27/27**, a total clean sweep.
>
> It is stronger for **store reachability** (the old literal compare passed only on a tickless
> run) and **weaker for counter liveness** (the old compare at least required a specific value).
> *That is the dropped-qualifier class: a trade restated as a strict improvement.*
>
> ### *** AND THAT PARAGRAPH WAS ITSELF WRONG -- THE THIRD ERROR IN THIS COMMENT'S LINEAGE,
> ### REFUTED BY THE fable5 ADJUDICATOR AND VERIFIED HERE IN ONE LOOK. ***
>
> It read: *"The consequence is an L3, not a tidy-up. The counter update is the DE-ESCALATION
> ACCEPT SIDE of the de-fatalised TICK arm, and nothing pins it — so the round's claim to have
> pinned the accept side of each de-fatalised predicate is false at that arm."*
>
> **`DEVICE_TICK` reads:**
>
>     d->reg_0x20000 += 1000;              <- UNCONDITIONAL
>     if (d->imask0 & ((int64_t)1<<50)) {  <- the predicate the fix de-fatalised
>
> The counter runs on **every** tick regardless of bit 50. The fix neither introduces it nor
> gates it, so `MH_nocounter` mutates **pre-existing, fix-independent** behaviour — **COVERAGE
> DEBT, filed as optional**, not a clause-(d)/L3 obligation. And the accept side of the
> predicate that *was* de-fatalised is pinned, by `tick 50` (alive) and `tick 50 txt` (announce).
> **So the round's accept-side claim is TRUE, and my correction impugned it wrongly.**
>
> **The lineage is the lesson: `tick 49` → `acc 20000` → "L3 obligation". Three claims, two of
> them corrections, and only the L4 deletion was right.** In the adjudicator's words, *"the
> correction inherited more authority than the fact, and the over-grade then propagated into the
> CHANGELOG."* This project's rule is that a correction earns a SECOND reading rather than less
> of one; seven lines of comment defeated it three times.
>
> *And this is the SECOND time this comment has been corrected. It first credited `tick 49`;
> grok caught that; the correction moved the credit to `acc 20000` and was also wrong.
> **A correction carries more authority than the error it replaces, so it earns a second
> reading, not less of one** — and this one moved a false credit onto a row that cannot carry
> it either.*

## THE CHAIN CLOSES -- KILL TABLES 4 AND 5, AND EVERY PREDICTION WRITTEN DOWN FIRST

`PRETABLE4.out` (03:06:49) and `PRETABLE5.out` (04:30:15) each precede their table's launch, so
every prediction below was recorded before the run that tested it.

    TABLE 4, base 32/32                      TABLE 5, base 33/33
    V1 31/32  xbit rev            KILL       V2 32/33  xbit rev2          KILL
    V3 31/32  latch 1x            KILL       V8 33/33  -- none --         ESCAPE (disclosed)
    V4 31/32  latch 28wr          KILL       V1 32/33  xbit rev           KILL (regression)
    V5 31/32  latch 30wr          KILL
    V6 30/32  latch tick+xbit rev KILL
    V7 32/32  -- none --          ESCAPE (disclosed)
    V2 32/32  -- none --          *** ESCAPED: a row I built wrong ***
    V8 28/32  four rows           *** KILLED: a mutant I built wrong ***

**THE DENOMINATOR, because a bare zero does not close a chain.** Ten cells: `{4 announce sites}
x {announce fires, latch sets}` + `{2 collision directions}`. Six were closed before table 4;
tables 4 and 5 killed the remaining four (`V2`/`V1` the two collision directions, `V4`/`V5` the
two remaining latch-sets, `V6` the tick latch-set). **Two cells are DISCLOSED WITH A RULING and
both were MEASURED to escape** — the counter (fix-independent, per the fable5 ruling) and the
width axis at 0x10020 (outside the floor by the `pcc2widthkills` bound). **Zero cells outside
the enumeration.** That is the fable5 fork's first branch, so **the chain CLOSES** and the
escape hatch — drop the latch axis wholesale to disclosed debt — remains unspent.

### THE TWO MISPREDICTIONS WERE BOTH MINE, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT KINDS OF WRONG

**`V2` — a bad ROW.** A clobber can only bite if the clobbered class's bit was *already set*.
`xbit isr` runs tick -> ISR, so when the tick assigns, the ISR bit has never been set and the
row is green on the mutant. I gave the mirror the opposite ORDER but not the opposite
OPERAND-AND-COUNT. *The `#499` shape a third time this round — and the same defect the opus5
seat diagnosed in the original `xbit`, reproduced inside the repair for it.* Fixed by ADDING
`xbit rev2` rather than re-aiming, since `xbit isr` still carries a real claim.

> **`V8` — a bad MUTANT, and this is the more dangerous failure because it looks like a
> success.** 28/32, four rows red. It was anchored on the FIRST `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE)`
> in the file — `case 0x10000`, the **interrupt mask register**. Every tick row arms bit 50 with
> a 64-bit `sd`, so `&& len == 4` refused that store and four rows died **for a reason unrelated
> to the cell under test.**
>
> **Had I not checked WHICH rows died, I would have recorded the width axis as covered when it
> was never tested** — a false "covered" in the contract, strictly worse than the honest
> "disclosed" it would have replaced. Re-aimed to guard #3 and verified by dry-run diff; the
> correct mutant then escaped, as originally predicted.

**A PREDICTION THAT WAS PRE-REGISTERED AND HELD.** `PRETABLE5` predicted `V1` kills via
`xbit rev`; it did not say whether `xbit rev2` would *also* red. I derived beforehand that it
would not — under `V1` the ISR assignment clobbers nothing (TICK was never set), the tick then
sets its own bit, and the second ISR access is correctly silent. **Measured: `xbit rev` alone.**
So the two collision rows separate BY DIRECTION, which is stronger than either row firing on
both: the signature identifies *which* clobber, not merely that one happened.

**AND `V7`/`V8` ESCAPING AS PREDICTED IS A RESULT, NOT A GAP.** A written prediction of an
ESCAPE landing says the disclosure is honest rather than a hedge — the cell is named, ruled on,
and now measured.

## THE fable5 ADJUDICATION -- ROSTER 9/9, AND THE RULING WENT AGAINST ME TWICE

The ninth and last seat. **Identity verified rather than assumed**, per standing directive: it
returned the liveness token, the verbatim first line of `CHECKPOINT.md`, and **named its own
model** (`claude-fable-5-1`) — an Agent invocation can silently land elsewhere, and this round
had no way to tell without asking.

**VERDICT: RATIFY THE FIX; DO NOT RATIFY THE DETECTOR AS SHIPPED. The latch-axis closure is
IN-ROUND, not filed.** Six of opus5's eight escapes weaken `d->warned |= IP30_W_*` statements
**the fix's own diff introduced** — the canonical clause-(d) shape — so L2 by the floor. And the
contract already claimed to catch two of them, measured false, which is an L4 to edit in-round
regardless. Filing was refused *because this closure had been mis-declared complete once
already.*

### THE TWO RULINGS AGAINST ME

**(1) My counter-pin correction was itself wrong — the third error in one comment's lineage.**
`DEVICE_TICK` increments `reg_0x20000` **unconditionally, two lines above** the `imask0 &
(1<<50)` guard the fix de-fatalised. So `MH_nocounter` mutates **pre-existing, fix-independent**
behaviour: coverage debt, not an L3 obligation — and the accept side of the de-fatalised
predicate *is* pinned, by `tick 50` + `tick 50 txt`. **My correction impugned a claim that was
true.** Lineage: `tick 49` → `acc 20000` → "L3 obligation" — *three claims, two of them
corrections, and only the L4 deletion was right.*

**(2) My `§OWED` misfiled my own doubt.** I named F10 as the disposition I least trusted; it is
F13, and fable named the incoherent cell exactly. Axes: `{read announces}` × `{message
per-offset distinct}`. Rejecting F10 while keeping F13 sits at **(announce YES, distinct NO)** —
an undistinguished FALSE message that steals the write-side bit. Defensible on neither axis.

### F13 RESOLVED: MEMBER 2, SILENT DECLINE -- AND IT MADE THE CLOSURE *SMALLER*

Both read arms are now silent. That kills two defects at once: the announce **said the wrong
thing** (all five ISR sites print "interrupt-status rewrite not implemented", and a read is not
a rewrite) and it **stole the bit** — one benign guest read consumed the single shared
`IP30_W_ISR` latch and permanently silenced the genuine write-side diagnostic, including the
architecturally-wrong `0x10030` write this round cares most about.

**ISR announce sites 5 → 3, so the enumeration went from FOURTEEN cells to TEN.** *Resolving the
design question removed four cells of detector work rather than adding them.*

> ### *** AND IT IMMEDIATELY INVALIDATED ONE OF MY OWN ROWS -- THE THIRD TIME THIS ROUND A FIX
> ### DESTROYED THE CHANNEL A ROW RESTED ON. ***
>
> `latch 1x` counted announces from the two READ arms. The moment they went silent it read
> `got=0 want=1` — vacuous by construction, measuring a channel the repair had removed. Caught
> only because the base was re-measured **before** the closure was built on top of it.
>
> The three instances: de-fatalisation removed the **death** channel (the tick pair, codex);
> the silent decline removed the **announce** channel (`kill 20/28 rd txt`, anticipated); and
> the same repair removed the announce `latch 1x` was counting (**not** anticipated).
>
> **The general form: a repair must be checked against every row whose oracle reads the channel
> it changes.** A row invalidated that way goes green or red for reasons unrelated to the mutant
> it names — the exact vacuity the CHANNEL rule exists to catch, arriving through a door that
> rule does not watch. `latch 1x` is re-aimed onto the two WRITE arms, which keep their store
> *and* announce.

### THE CLASS CLOSURE -- TEN CELLS, AND THE MEASUREMENT I NEARLY UNDER-RAN

Enumerated from the function's own inputs: `{4 announce sites} × {announce fires, latch sets}` +
`{2 collision directions}`. Six were already closed; four rows close the rest — `latch 28wr`,
`latch 30wr`, `latch tick` (the `ME` flood cell, ranked worst of the eight) and `xbit rev` (the
`MA` direction `xbit` runs backwards).

Two of those need a **second forced `DEVICE_TICK`**. Fable allowed an unbuildable cell to be
disclosed with its apparatus reason — **but only after being measured unbuildable.** Measured,
counting ticks by the unconditional `reg_0x20000 += 1000`:

    step 1 / 2 / 3 / 8 / 1000  ->  ONE tick
    step 65536 / 70000         ->  TWO
    step 140000                ->  THREE

> **STOPPING AT `step 8` WOULD HAVE DISCLOSED TWO BUILDABLE CELLS AS UNBUILDABLE** — a false
> exemption written into the contract on an under-tested measurement. The threshold is ~65536
> because `machine.c` decrements `ticks_till_next` by **one** per single-step, so these rows are
> slow *by construction*: that is the price of the cell, not an accident.

*Two apparatus errors on the way, both caught by loud failures rather than luck: a bare `step N`
spliced between op-sequences, and — worse — an **invented address constant** (`0x0ff20000`)
where the probe defines `A_C20000`. The load returned the SENTINEL, which is the
hand-assembled-constant trap; a plausible value would have been believed.*

### THE CHAIN'S STOP CONDITION, PRE-COMMITTED

Converging, not `#392` — the fix has been stable and approved since pass 1, and every pass has
been about the detector. **But closure was declared one pass early**, because kill table 2
counted the latch mechanism as two cells when it is roughly eight. *A bare zero against a wrong
enumeration does not close a chain* — this round's own citation of that rule, with itself as the
counter-example.

**The fork that makes it terminate:** one closure diff, one verifying pass confirming **zero
cells outside the stated enumeration**, denominator named. Only already-enumerated cells now
killed → the chain **closes**. A fifth escape **outside** the enumeration → the
fresh-process-probe-versus-shared-lifetime-latch architecture is the root cause, and the latch
axis drops **wholesale to disclosed debt** rather than becoming pass six.

sites, two latch failure modes, one declined-read value; the two axes deliberately NOT swept are
named in the contract below. *"Zero found" and "zero looked for" must not render the same.*

`M6` is the point of the exercise: **21/21 clean sweep before, 26/27 after**, killed by
`xbit isr got=0 want=1` — the tick consuming the shared bit and silencing the ISR arm, exactly
the derivation `PRETABLE2.out` recorded before the run.

> ### *** TWO ORACLE SHAPES THIS PROBE DID NOT HAVE, AND `M9` PROVES THE FIRST WAS NECESSARY
> ### RATHER THAN DECORATIVE. ***
>
> **`latch 1x` COUNTS announces instead of detecting one.** Under `M9` the arm announces on
> EVERY access: measured `got=2 want=1`. **A presence oracle reads `yes` on the fix AND on the
> mutant** — it cannot see the defect at all. Had that row been written `yes`/`no` it would have
> been VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the CHANNEL rule's own failure mode arriving one level
> along, inside the repair for it.
>
> **`xbit isr` / `xbit tick` put BOTH announce classes in ONE device lifetime.** Every other row
> in this probe runs in a fresh process, and a shared bit is only corrupt when two classes meet
> — so no fresh-process row can see a collision, however many there are. On the fix both read
> **1**, which is *the first direct measurement that the two latch bits are independent* — the
> round's central product-code claim, which the grok seat correctly called "a prediction sitting
> beside real measurements with no row behind it."
>
> *The recipe came from the measuring seat, including its warning that its own first attempt was
> a defective apparatus: `ticks_till_next[n] = 0`, so the tick's single free firing lands on the
> session's FIRST `machine_run` and a seeding store placed before the arm silently consumes it.
> ARM BIT 50 FIRST.*

**THE SIGNATURES DISAMBIGUATE, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY WITH A COST WORTH WRITING DOWN.**
`M6` reds `xbit isr` ALONE; `M7` reds `kill 20 wr txt` AND `xbit isr`, because the `xbit`
session's ISR access is itself a write at `0x10020`. So the pair separates "the bits collided"
from "that arm's announce is gone." **But `xbit isr` is therefore NOT a pure collision detector**
— it reds for two causes, and only `kill 20 wr txt` separates them. *The two rows are COUPLED:
delete `kill 20 wr txt` as redundant and `xbit isr` silently stops meaning what its comment
says.* Recorded because a future reader pruning rows would have no other way to know.

**`M1_del28store` WAS RE-RUN ON PURPOSE.** `#462` measured that adding rows perturbs other
mutants' scores, so table 1's five kills were claims about an instrument that no longer existed.
`PRETABLE2.out` stated plainly that "six new independent sessions cannot perturb it" was
REASONED, NOT MEASURED, and named `M1` as its single test. Measured: **26/27, `isr clr` alone,
`0x5a5a -> 0x5050` — identical to table 1.** The claim is now measured rather than asserted.

### THE CONTRACT (vacuity-floor clause (e)) -- what this detector is designed to catch

**CATCHES**, each with a measured kill: reinstating any of the four `abort()` calls; deleting the
announce at ANY of the six sites; deleting either surviving store; re-inserting the dropped
`0x10030` clear-on-write; moving the tick guard between bits 49 and 50; mirroring `d->isr` into a
declined read; collapsing the two latch bits onto one; defeating the latch mask outright.

**DOES NOT CATCH, disclosed rather than discovered later:**
* **the WIDTH / `len` axis** — the probe uses only `lw`/`sw`/`ld`/`sd`. This is `#499`'s own axis
  and it is unexplored here.
* **POSITION / translation (clause (f))** — no row asserts WHICH cell an access lands on, so a
  re-map that keeps the probed offsets distinct is invisible.
* **latch-macro RENUMBERING** — measured EQUIVALENT (all uses go through the macros, no
  observable differs), so it is a RESULT rather than a gap.
* **`dev_sgi_ip30_2`** — a different device, filed separately as `ip30asdvasdvnb`.

## PASS 2 DID NOT RATIFY, AND FOUR OF ITS FINDINGS WERE DEFECTS IN THIS ROUND'S OWN WORK

Seven scriptable seats answered (`_scratchpad/panel_20260917_215210`). **The kimi CLI was on its
weekly 403 wall and its seat is COVERED by the `kimi-k3:cloud` substitute, not lost** — recorded
by transport, as the ledger requires. opus5 was still running and **fable5 is held by standing
directive until every other seat has spoken**, so the stage stands at **7 of 9 and every ruling
below is PROVISIONAL ON ITS FACE.**

Not one seat ratified. Four findings were verified against the code — not taken on a seat's word
— and repaired in-round; two more were corrected in the records above.

| # | finding | seats | grade | repair |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | the latch comment's `ONE BIT PER SITE` is false — five ISR paths share one bit | codex, grok, glm | **L4** | comment restated as the invariant that makes the design correct |
| 2 | the tick pair stops discriminating post-fix — both rows read `alive` | codex, minimax | **L1** | both re-aimed onto the announce channel; `tick 50 txt` added |
| 3 | `kill 30 txt` read the `isr keep` transcript, which writes 0x10020 | agy | **L1** | re-bound to the 0x10030 session |
| 4 | nothing observed that `d->isr &= ~idata` still runs at 0x10028 | deepseek, glm, kimi, minimax | **L2 FLOOR BREACH** | row `isr clr` added |
| 5 | nothing pinned that the 0x10030 write is *discarded* | agy, glm, kimi | — | row `isr drop 30` added |
| 6 | the counter pin credited `tick 49`; `acc 20000` is the row | grok | **L4** | comment corrected |

**THE ONE WORTH CARRYING IS #3, AND NOT FOR ITS SIZE.** `kill 30 txt` was bound to a session that
writes **0x10020** and never touches 0x10030 — and because **all five ISR announces are byte-
identical**, it read `yes` off the wrong arm and sat GREEN while structurally blind to its own
named mutant. *The shared message is correct design — it is what makes the unqualified `(once)`
marker true — and it is exactly what made this undetectable by reading the output.* Pre-fix the
row reddened because its seeding session DIED, not because the announce it claims to observe was
absent: **right colour, wrong reason, on both builds.**

It is the **third** rolling-`t` defect in this one probe, after `acc 20000` and `isr keep`. All
three have the same shape — a row reading a transcript variable that a later `session()` call has
since overwritten — and the class is now closed by construction: every `t`-reading row binds to
the session immediately above it, verified by listing them in file order.

**FINDINGS REJECTED, WITH WARRANTS, because a round that accepted everything has stopped arguing:**
`deepseek`'s latch-macro renumbering is a true clean sweep but an **EQUIVALENT** mutant — all uses
go through the macros and no observable differs — so it is a RESULT, not a gap. `glm`'s request to
put the register offset in the warn text is **refused and filed**, and finding #1's own invariant
is the warrant: qualifying the message obliges qualifying the latch, so it is a coupled change
rather than a text edit. `codex`'s two extra option-set members are refused — halting the guest on
a legal-looking register write is worse than what shipped, and alias/forwarding is precisely what
`heart.h` rules out. `deepseek`'s claim that a guard-growth mutant at 0x10020/0x10028 would redden
no row is **measured false**: `kill 20 wr` and `kill 28 wr` exist and die.

**FILED, NOT FIXED:** `ip30asdvasdvnb` — an UNLATCHED guest-drivable `fatal()` with a keyboard-mash
message (`asdvasdvnb`) in `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_ip30_2)`, found by grok. Verified upstream residue
against HEAD. It is out of scope because it carries no `abort()`: a host kill and a log flood are
different semantic classes, and the round-scope rule admits a second site only in the same class.

**A BRIEF DEFECT OF MINE, recorded as such:** glm correctly objected that `heart.h` was never
INLINED, so every specific drawn from it — the offsets, `(read-only)`, the 52/24-bit widths — was

> ### *** 21/21 DOES NOT DISCHARGE THE FLOOR, AND THIS ROUND WILL NOT IMPLY OTHERWISE. ***

# RECORDS 2026-09-17 -- **SEVEN ROUNDS SHIPPED WITH NO ROUND BLOCK IN THIS FILE, AND TWO OF THEM ARE THE ROUNDS THE VACUITY FLOOR WAS MINTED FROM.** Assessed, not changed: no code is touched and no round block is reconstructed.

A records-integrity audit asked whether the CHANGELOG and the ledger disagree in *either*
direction. The usual direction — written down but wrong — is what every gate here looks for.
**This is the inverse, and nothing looks for it:** rounds that shipped code and were never
written up.

    #439  020a672 374706b            13 CHANGELOG mentions   the 8253 counter-latch: the driving seat REFUSED the panel
    #441  9de16b7 799f48f            1  CHANGELOG mentions   sh4bcr: two guest instructions ended the emulator process
    #443  6bec468 3536d86            13 CHANGELOG mentions   sh4pcicexit: one guest LOAD ended the host, on 116 of 137 
    #466  9ca9cca                    0  CHANGELOG mentions   asiceventaddr: state the domain restriction where the even
    #487  6faba0f eb8fafb            0  CHANGELOG mentions   landiskaux: the census is RE-TAKEN and the panel's gate is
    #493  3521a22                    0  CHANGELOG mentions   wdcaltoffset: a durable rung-3 witness for a live sev-high

**Measured against a live denominator of 293 round-block headings**, so the search is
checkable rather than merely empty. Twelve commits, all present in `refs/heads/main`.

## None is a void number, and that is the check that makes this a defect

This project has a void number (`#289`), so a missing heading is not automatically a breach —
it is one only if the number shipped. **All seven shipped.** Three are ordinary defect fixes:

* **`#441 sh4bcr`** — *two guest instructions ended the emulator process*
* **`#443 sh4pcicexit`** — *one guest LOAD ended the host, on 116 of 137 offsets*
* **`#493 wdcaltoffset`** — *a rung-3 witness for a live sev-high defect*

> ### `sh4bcr` and `sh4pcicexit` are the two rounds the VACUITY FLOOR cites as its founding
> ### evidence — *"sh4bcr's first detector passed a mutant reinstating the very host kill its
> ### round removed; sh4pcicexit's passed the original kill verbatim"* — and **neither has a
> ### block in the file a reader would go to.** A future reader re-deriving the floor's warrant
> ### finds the rule, finds the rounds named, and finds nothing under either number.

## Why no gate caught it

Section H checks that seats were FIRED; section G checks that a seat which ANSWERED was
RECORDED; `check_cited_artifacts.py` checks that a CITED PATH EXISTS. **Nothing asks whether a
round that shipped has a block at all** — every existing check starts from a record and tests
it, so a record that was never written is outside all of them by construction.

## Disposition: recorded, not reconstructed

Writing seven retroactive round blocks out of commit messages would manufacture records, which
is worse than the gap. This entry names every round and its commits so the rounds are findable;
the reconstruction is filed as `changelogroundgap` for a round that can do it from each round's
own artifacts.

*The checker that would close this is a ledger-row-to-CHANGELOG-heading existence test,
forward-only from a cutoff — the `check_bugfile_sync.py` idiom. **Filed, not built:** a tooling
change owes two negative controls and ships as its own harness round, not as a rider here.*

*Deriver and its own correlate-check are recorded on the queue row. In short: the obvious
`^#+ .*#NNN` pattern tests the literal number while the class is "is this round documented",
and this file really does use range headings (`## #89–#94`) that would report 0 for a round
they document. Checked — no range heading covers any of the seven, and the bracketing headings
confirm each gap (R9=#435 and R10=#437 straddle #436; R12=#440 and R13=#442 straddle #441).*

# ADJUDICATION 2026-09-17 -- **A NINE-SEAT PANEL, A MEASURING SEAT AND AN ADJUDICATOR REFUTED TWO ROWS I FILED THE SAME DAY.** No round number: this is a review campaign, and the code obligations it produced ship as their own follow-up commits.

## WHAT THE DAY ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED

Two panels (seven scriptable seats each), five standalone grok jobs, the Opus 5 measuring seat, and
a Fable 5.1 adjudication on a COMPLETE 9-of-9 roster.  **The measuring seat and the adjudicator
between them withdrew two queue rows I had filed hours earlier, corrected a census three times, and
found two MEASURED TOTAL ESCAPES against detectors that shipped with their fixes.**

### THE TWO ESCAPES -- L2, BY DIFFERENT ROUTES, AND THE ROUTE DECIDES THE REPAIR

    M1_sh4latchleak     f532bb6 #453  `1u << 0)` -> `1u << 0) || channel != 0`   27/27  ESCAPE
    M2_gdromnodatawidth 7c9dd9e #462  `idata = 0;` -> `if (len == 4) idata = 0;` 60/60  ESCAPE

**M1 is a clause-(d) joint cell.**  `channel` indexes the guard's own operand
`d->val_reported[cls][instance]`, which the repair path reads AND writes, so the floor is
`{channel} x {fresh, set}`.  Rows X4a/X4b use `wr()` -- a SINGLE store -- and **a single store can
measure that the FIRST diagnostic appears but never that a SECOND does not**, which is exactly what
the "one line per channel per device lifetime" CEILING claims.  (1,set) and (7,set) are open.

**M2 is NOT a joint-cell axis, and the Fable adjudication overturned the measuring seat's route
here.**  `DEVICE_ACCESS(dreamcast_gdrom_dma)` never TESTS `len`, so width induces no body
partition; and "sibling parity" is a PRE-TABLE CHECK, not a floor clause.  It is L2 purely as a
**measured false pass against the shipped CONTRACT**, which claims to catch conditioning of the
`idata = 0` clear *"at either declining arm"* -- and catches it at one.

> **SAME GRADE, DIFFERENT OBLIGATION.**  M2's repair owes a corrected CONTRACT LINE as well as a
> row; M1's owes a disclosure of channels 2..6.  Flattening both to "floor breach" would have lost
> that, and the measuring seat had explicitly declined to grade its own findings: *"I am the seat
> that found them, so I should be the last person trusted to grade them."*

# MARKER CENSUS 2026-09-17 -- **THE DERIVER THIS PROJECT HAS RE-RUN FOUR TIMES IS ITSELF KEYED ON A CORRELATE.** No code changed. Found by the glm and minimax seats, and the correction lands on a premise *I had inlined into a nine-seat brief that morning as SETTLED*.

The carrier's marker deriver greps the LITERAL `(once)`.  Today it printed **41 occ / 7 files**, and I
put that in the late-review brief's SETTLED PREMISES block with the gloss *"~82% of all suppression
markers"*.

**Two seats challenged it from the packet alone.**  minimax: `f532bb6`'s marker is `(once per
channel)`, *"invisible to the S2 `grep -o '(once)'` census"*.  glm reached the same place.  Neither
could read the tree; both named exactly what would settle it.  **Run against the tree, they are
right, and the shortfall is larger than either said.**

## THE REAL POPULATION, derived by FAMILY rather than by literal

    41  (once)                             11  (once per offset)
     5  (once per bit)                      4  (once per offset per direction)
     1  (once per encoding)                 1  (once per direction)
     1  (once for each channel)
    ---------------------------------------------------------------
    64  (once...) family, LINE-BASED grep
    71  (once...) family, allowing a marker to span a WRAPPED C STRING
     3  (further occurrences suppressed)    4  (reported once ...) in three spellings

> **THE LITERAL SEES 41 OF 71.  It misses 30 -- 23 to qualified spellings and SEVEN MORE to
> string wrapping**, `f532bb6`'s own `"... (once per"` / `"channel) ..."` among them.  The
> `(once...)` family is **~90%** of all markers, not the 82% I wrote.

## *** THE CLASS IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT ALREADY NAMED, AND THE CARRIER'S OWN DERIVER IS AN
## *** INSTANCE OF IT ***

The rule on record is *"a deriver must key on what DEFINES the class, never on a correlate -- a
correlate's error is invisible because the output is still a plausible number."*  **A latch marker
is defined by ANNOUNCING SUPPRESSION, not by the four characters `(once)`.**  So the carrier's
deriver measures a correlate, and it has been re-run four times (14, then 24, then 40, then 41)
with every re-run confirming the drift and none questioning the KEY.

*That is the third correlate-keyed deriver found today, after the review-coverage one keyed on
ledger ids.  The pattern is not carelessness -- a literal is the easiest thing to grep, and its
output always looks like a fact.*

## A MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT CAUGHT BY CONTRADICTION, recorded because it nearly shipped

My verification script printed **71 total** and **"+0 only visible after joining"** in the same
line.  Those cannot both be true if the line-based count is 64.  **Cause: Python's `[^)]*` matches
newlines, so `re.findall` over whole-file text ALREADY spanned the wrapped strings and my
"join continuations" step was a no-op.**  `grep` is line-based and does not.

So the 64-vs-71 gap is not an artifact -- **it IS the wrapped markers**, reached by a different
route than the one I built.  *A contradiction in your own output is the cheapest signal there is,
and this file says so; it worked.*

## WHAT CHANGED, AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT

The **ADVICE is unchanged and strengthened for the fourth time**: `(once)` is what a new site
should use, and the N=1-per-instance SHAPE is untouched.  **No product code changed.**  What is
corrected is the DERIVER and the premise I inlined from it.  The carrier's deriver block now
carries the family form beside the literal one.

*Cost of the wrong premise: none, because the brief stated it as a derived output with its date
and the packet-fed seats challenged it anyway -- which is the premise-audit instruction earning
its paragraph for the fourth recorded time.*

## *** THE LIMIT OF THIS AUDIT, STATED BECAUSE IT CHANGES THE REMEDY ***

**The ledger records what was WRITTEN DOWN, not what was FIRED.**  `precommit_check.sh` section H has
exactly the same limit and says so in its own header.  This project has a documented day on which
SEVEN panels ran and roughly FORTY seat entries were never recorded.

So each of these 37 rows is one of two things, and they must not be conflated:

    the seats never reviewed it         -> a REVIEW gap.  Fire them.
    they reviewed and nobody recorded   -> an UNREAD REVIEW.  The answers may still be on disk in a
                                           panel dir -- and this project has THREE TIMES found real

The late-review brief therefore asks the seats directly: *if you recognise a fix and believe you
already reviewed it, say so.*  That converts a review gap into a records gap for the cost of one
sentence, and the two have different remedies.

self-contained so no seat needs git), put to the full panel; **then Fable reviews AND adjudicates**,
last, per the standing rule that Fable does not run until the other seats have had their say.

Findings are dispositioned under the LATE-DISSENT rule, since this material is already committed:
**closure changes the LICENSE, never the truth-value.**  Wrong record -> corrected in place; measured
false pass -> follow-up commit; everything else -> filed as a new queue item carrying the dissent
