# `#528` (mapledmaaddr): an ordinary guest read of the Dreamcast Maple bus's DMA-address register ended the emulator — AFTER the model had computed the right value

**THE DEFECT.** `src/devices/dev_dreamcast_maple.c`, `DEVICE_ACCESS(dreamcast_maple)`, case `0x04`
(`MAPLE_DMAADDR`), read arm:

```c
fatal("[ dreamcast_maple: TODO: read from dmaaddr ]\n");
odata = d->dmaaddr;
exit(1);
```

The field is fully modelled: the write arm stores it, and `maple_do_dma_xfer()` consumes it (it tests `!d->enable` and
`addr & 0x1f`).  Its sibling `MAPLE_ENABLE` (`0x14`) answers the same shape of read quietly.  A guest reading back the
address it had just programmed killed the host process.

**THE FIX — ACCEPT (member 4 of the option set).**  Delete the `fatal()` and the `exit(1)`; keep the value, with no
latch and no announce — the read is implemented, so an "unimplemented" message would be a wrong record in product
code.  `break` into the common tail (which writes `odata` on a read), never `return`.  Upheld 9/9 at pass 1 and never
disputed afterwards.  **FAULT (member 5) is NOT AVAILABLE on SH4**: `memory_rw.c` has no `MEM_SH` exception arm, so a
handler's `return 0` silently skips the load and leaves the destination register untouched — worse than a decline
(the Opus seat, verified by the flagship seat).  *Filed: the carrier's member-5 clause should say "nor SH, where the
idiom silently skips the load" — not made here, because `tools/CLAUDE.md` carries an earlier session's unreviewed
delta and section J requires the two copies to match.*

**THE WITNESS.**  Rung 3, cold debugger, unmodified `-E dreamcast`, guest `mov.l` through real decode:
`regress/artifacts/mapledmaaddr/agy_maple_witness_20260912.py` — committed build **4/12** (`witness_committed.out`,
12:43:56: the host dies on the first read with the TODO text), fix **12/12** (`witness_fix.out`, 12:45:03), same
script, committed leg first; liveness and device-signature (`MAPLE_SPEED` mask) controls green in both.  Admitted by
the flagship seat; its `read quiet` row (keyed on one literal) was ruled channel-invalid and NOT inherited.

## The detector — `regress/maple_dmaaddr_probe.py`, 37 rows, `gate_sh_rounding.sh` (gate 10) pin 37

Every register access is a real SH4 guest instruction stepped through the debugger (the device is `DM_DEFAULT`, so
`dump`/`put` never reach it); every load destination is POISONED; the header carries a CONTRACT and a NOT COVERED list
(clause (e)).  Its value rows cover the accept cell, every other case label, all eight single-bit narrowings of the
selector (0x05 by `mov.b`, 0x06 by `mov.w`, 0x00, 0x0c, 0x14, 0x24, 0x44, 0x84), 16- and 8-bit reads, the consumer's
partitions and their joint cell, read side effects (clear, set or clear one bit, a sibling write), a third-read
counter, and survival.  **It took SEVEN kill tables**, and the history is the point of this block:

| table | instrument | runs | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 `killtable_20260912/` | 16 rows | 14 | 12 exact; `M_RET0` hit its stated alternate, `M_ZEROEXIT` 13/16 |
| 2 `killtable2_20260912/` | 29 rows | 25 | 24 exact, zero escapes; one timing-dependent extra red |
| 3 `killtable3_20260912/` | 35 rows, grammar + counts | 32 | **32 exact, zero escapes** |
| 4 `killtable4_20260912/` | 35 rows, + blank/CR/prompt counts | 8 | 8 exact (targeted) |
| 5 `killtable5_20260912/` | 37 rows, exact owed transcript, pre-`quit` snapshot | 21 | 20 exact (the miss is on the OLD instrument, below) |
| 6 `killtable6_20260912/` | 37 rows, whole transcript through EOF | 17 | 17 exact |
| 7 `killtable7_20260912/` | **37 rows, full-line disassembly + EOF + exit status** | 21 | **21 exact**; BASE 37/37 x3 |

Each ran in a scratch clone of `build/` with a clone-local sentinel, a frozen instrument, a `PRETABLE.out` written
before it ran and a separate `POSTTABLE.out`; every restore was cmp-CLEAN and FRESH.  Tables 4–7 are TARGETED on a
stated superset warrant (each new silence condition only adds reds; value rows unchanged), measure BASE for a false red,
and re-run every predicted survivor on the PREVIOUS instrument too, so each escape is measured rather than inferred.

## The silence channel — the lesson, because the floor held and the oracle kept failing

The floor (flagship ruling, pass 1): **silence over every read interval** — a diagnostic-alone reinstatement is half
of clause (b).  The ORACLE for it was replaced six times, and every replacement but the last was swept by a diagnostic
it could not see:

| oracle | swept by | found by |
|---|---|---|
| a literal (`dreamcast_maple` in the transcript) | `fatal("[ maple: DMAADDR read ]")` | codex, glm, kimi |
| a quiet grammar | `fatal("0x%08x\n", ...)` — the shape of a `print` answer | codex |
| grammar + per-class counts | `fatal("\n")` — the grammar's blank line | grok (read late) |
| + blank / CR / prompt counts, `quit` echo EXEMPT | `fatal("GXemul> quit\n")` 35/35 (the exemption) | Fable |
| exact owed transcript, pre-`quit` snapshot | `atexit()` printing after the snapshot — 37/37 | deepseek, kimi, glm; Opus measured |
| whole transcript through EOF | `abort()`/`_Exit(1)` at exit keyed on the field — 37/37; a disassembler swap; an exit handler outlasting a bounded read | Opus measured; codex, kimi, deepseek |

The shipped oracle compares each read session's WHOLE transcript, from the first prompt to the pty's EOF, with the
exact line sequence the commands owe — every echo, value, `put` confirmation, and every stepped instruction's
disassembly line IN FULL (`disasm_line()`, rendering `sh_cpu_disassemble_instr`'s text) — rejects any CR that is not
the pty's CRLF, and requires every read session to reach EOF inside the post-`quit` cap and to exit 0.

> **A SILENCE ORACLE BUILT AS A WHITELIST HAS A SHAPE TO HIDE IN; ONE THAT STOPS OBSERVING AT A POINT IN TIME HAS AN
> INTERVAL TO HIDE IN.**  Twice a repair reproduced the class inside itself: table 5's snapshot NARROWED the window
> table 4's whole-buffer grammar had covered (glm; table 5's PRETABLE had called it "a strict tightening"), and table
> 4's count shipped an exemption.  The class-closure rule fired at pass two and was applied at pass four.

**AND ONE WINDOW NO FINITE TEST CLOSES, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN ROWED** (the Opus seat, measured): a session spans, after
its first stepped instruction, only that instruction's device tick and the two ticks `cpu_run_deinit()` runs at
shutdown — about three.  A report keyed on a later tick (every 4th: 37/37, `M_TICKPERIODIC4`, a survivor BY DESIGN in
table 7) prints only when the guest runs freely.  Running longer only moves the window.  **And a coupling**: the
compared transcript runs through those shutdown ticks, so `read silent` also requires every dreamcast device to be
silent on them — a device that prints at shutdown will red all twelve sessions, and that red is NOT the DMAADDR read.

# `#527` (ppcrlwimiwidth, ppcrldimimask): two PowerPC rotate-and-insert instructions computed wrong results — `rlwimi` rotated a 32-bit word at 64-bit width and never wrote a wrapping mask's high word; `rldimi`'s rotate loop consumed its own shift count, so every insert mask was built from `sh == -1`

Both are sibling handlers in `src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c` and share one commit and one joint kill table,
because one build exercises both and each probe is the other's cross-check.  The architecture is Book I
v2.01 (`_scratchpad/ppc_uisa_book1_v201.txt`): rlwimi `r <- ROTL32((RS)32:63, SH); m <- MASK(MB+32,
ME+32); RA <- (r & m) | ((RA) & ~m)` with MASK wrapping when x > y (`:578`), and ROTL32 duplicating the
word into both halves; rldimi `r <- ROTL64((RS), sh); m <- MASK(mb, 63-sh)`.

**rlwimi — two defects in one handler.**  (1) `MODE_uint_t tmp = reg(rs)` held all 64 bits, so
`(tmp << sh) | (tmp >> (32 - sh))` pulled high-word bits DOWN into the rotated low word.  (2) A
wrapping mask (MB > ME) covers the WHOLE high word, which must receive the rotated word; the handler
only walked the low word.  **FIX:** narrow on read, `uint32_t tmp = (uint32_t)reg(rs)`, and BEFORE the
insertion loop `if (mb > me) ra = (ra & 0xffffffffULL) | ((uint64_t)tmp << 32);` — before, because the
loop walks `mb` to `me` and a guard placed after it would never fire (`R_POST_LOOP` measures exactly
that).  A 19-line comment records why a 32-bit `MODE_uint_t` build keeps only the low word, and that this
is NOT a claim that 32-bit MODE removes half the register (Book I §1.2).

**rldimi — two defects in one handler.**  (1) `while (sh-- != 0)` rotated correctly and left `sh == -1`,
so the mask end `63 - sh` was 64 for every encoding.  (2) The mask loop `m ++` never wrapped past bit 63.
**FIX:** rotate a copy (`int m, n = sh;  while (n-- != 0)`) and make the loop circular
(`m = (m + 1) & 63; } while (m != ((64 - sh) & 63))`).

**WITNESSES, rung 3, unmodified in-tree `-E bareppc -M 64` (PPC970).**  rlwimi: committed **14/28**, fix
**28/28** (`artifacts/ppcrlwimiwidth/witness_{committed,fix}.out`, agy's witness).  rldimi: committed
**17/27**, fix **27/27** (`artifacts/ppcrldimimask/witness_*.out`, the Opus seat's).  No Book I error in
either fix: codex checked all 32,768 rlwimi and 4,096 rldimi immediate combinations against a model of
the RTL; grok and kimi re-derived both from Book I independently.

# `#526` (xscaleinten): reading the i80321 interrupt-enable register ended the emulator — AFTER the model had already loaded the correct value into the destination register

**THE DEFECT.** `arm_coproc_i80321_6()` — coprocessor 6 on `-E iq80321` (and Iyonix), installed by
`machine_iq80321.c` — handles `crm 0 / crn 0` as the interrupt-enable register.  Its load arm read:

```c
cpu->cd.arm.r[rd] = cpu->cd.arm.i80321_inten;
fatal("TODO: XScale read from inten?\n");
exit(1);
```

**The destination received the modelled value and the host process then died.**  The register is fully
modelled in both directions: the store arm writes the same field, and `dev_i80321.c` consumes it
(`d->enable = &cpu->cd.arm.i80321_inten`).  A guest reading back its own interrupt enables — which is
what firmware does — ended the emulator.

**THE SIBLING IN THE SAME SWITCH IS THE WARRANT.**  `crn 4` (isteer) has the identical load/store
shape and its read carries no diagnostic and no exit.  `crn 0`'s kill is the switch's outlier —
upstream residue, the exit the author reached while developing, not a policy.

**THE FIX — ACCEPT (member 4 of the option set).**  Delete the two lines; keep the value.  No latch
and no announce: the read is implemented, so a bounded "unimplemented" message would be a wrong
record in product code.  The write arm, and the three kills this round RETAINS in the same handler —
the isteer non-zero write, the isrc write (`TODO: XScale int ack?`) and the unknown-tuple exit — are
untouched and rowed as controls.  Every seat that read the source in two passes upheld ACCEPT.

**THE WITNESS, and one thing it does NOT establish.**  Rung 3, cold debugger, unmodified in-tree
`iq80321`: `regress/artifacts/xscaleinten/agy_xscale_witness_20260911.py`, committed build **11/26**,
fix **26/26** (`witness_committed.out`, `witness_fix.out`).  **Test-first ORDER is not established by
these artifacts**: `witness_fix.out` carries the EARLIER mtime (`02:20:10` against `02:20:23`), and
nothing records that the committed leg was run before the edit.  What IS established, three times, is
that the committed source reproduces the death from a clean rebuild: every kill table's HEAD leg
(11/26, 12/29, 12/30).  *Recorded as a reproducible pre-fix measurement, not as test-first.*

## Pass 2, and the two survivors it found

A nine-seat pass 2 (`_scratchpad/panel_20260912_095235_xscalepass2`, the Opus measuring seat, then a
§F2 adjudication pass `panel_20260912_104522_xpadjud`, then Fable) asked one question: *is there a
clause-(d) mutant this detector does not see?*  **Two, both measured by the Opus seat at 29/29 against
the 29-row instrument, and both confirmed LIVE kills** (`artifacts/xscaleinten/opus_pass2_20260912/`):

* **`if (rd == 0) { fatal; exit(1); }`** after the load.  Every inten read in the probe landed in r3-r7,
  r9, r10 or r15.  `xscale_XM_RD0.log` 29/29; `live_XM_RD0_r0.log` dies, `_r9.log` survives.
* **`if (i80321_inten & 0x00400000) { fatal; exit(1); }`** — bit 22.  The rows drove inten = 0, S1,
  S2 and bit 28 only; union `0xFFA5F05F`, so bits `0x005A0FA0` were never set.  `xscale_XM_MAGICBIT.log`.

**One row closes both:** `RD0_ALLONES` writes all-ones to inten and reads it into a poisoned r0.
Table 3: `M_RD0` 29/30 and `M_MAGICBIT` 29/30, **each failing `RD0_ALLONES` alone**; no other leg's
failure set changed.

**THE GRADE — CLAUSE (e), BOTH CELLS; THE ROW IS L1 CONSTRUCTION.**  Ruled by the flagship seat (Fable 5.1, last, on
7/7 scriptable seats plus Opus), against a three-seat minority that held `rd == 0` as a floor cell by
operand swap.  The floor is the cross-product of the dominating predicates (`crm == 0`, `crn == 0`,
`l_bit`) with the device-STATE lvalues the repair reads; the body reads `rd` as an INDEX and inten as a
SOURCE and tests neither, so both exits are the `idata == k` shape.  The swap reading was rejected on its
own consequence: it makes `rd == 0` floor only because `crn == 0` happens to dominate -- had the arm been
`crn 4`, `rd == 4` would be floor and `rd == 0` not.  **Grading by coincidence is the same vice as
grading by cost, and my own provisional lean ("floor, because one cheap row pins each") was that vice;
it is overturned.**  THE RULE THE NEXT PURE DELETION INHERITS, when its guarded body tests nothing: the
floor is clause (b)'s verbatim reinstatement plus the dominating predicates' accept cell; every
re-introduction keyed on a body-read operand the body does not test is clause (e), disclosed BY CLASS in
the CONTRACT; a row added for one is L1 -- licensed because cheap, never graded floor because cheap.
*And the row's reach, stated rather than implied (codex): all-ones pins every single-bit-SET predicate on
inten, not bit-CLEAR or multi-bit patterns.*

**What the NOT COVERED list now says, because the row closes two partitions and not the class:** an exit
keyed on `rd == k` for an undriven k, or on an exact inten VALUE, is not pinned — the body indexes by
`rd` and copies inten, and tests neither; an exit keyed on `isteer != 0` is EQUIVALENT on this
instrument (isteer can only become non-zero through a write that itself exits); no session makes more
than five inten reads; the ANCHOR rows raise only irq 28.

**Two kill CHANNELS named, because the row names overstate them (kimi):** `ANCHOR_CONTRAST` kills M1 by
HOST DEATH at the read, not through its named "spins, 0x18 never reached" channel; and `D_RESET` /
`D_ZERO` cannot vary under a wrong-source mutant whose substitute is also zero (isteer, isrc and tmr0 are
all 0 in a stepped session) -- they earn their place against the reinstatement class, not that one.

# `#518` (lcabadval): legal LCA register writes terminated the emulator, including the SROM-required clearing of a DMA window

CONF retains its CFG AD field; TB_ENA retains TEN; BASE retains W_BASE, SG and WEN.
MASK validates the normalized contiguous-low-ones field before storing; invalid fields

# `#519` (sgirandomcolour): unsupported colour PUTs replaced guest pixel data with host-PRNG bytes and flooded diagnostics

**THE DEFECT.** The DE colour default included documented YCRCB among 12 of 16 type encodings.
`fatal()` returned; drawing continued into the store and could announce per pixel. The MTE path
did not reach this arm. Width matters: four PRNG bytes at 32 bpp, one at 8 bpp, and at depth 8
four PRNG bytes plus an uninitialised tail. The source comment still says “four HOST-PRNG bytes”
without that qualification; the probe header and ledger review supply it.

**THE FIX.** In `src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c`, the PUT default clears `ok` outside the warning latch;
`if (ok)` guards `memory_rw`. A declined PUT preserves the destination. `SGIRE_W_BADCOLOR`
announces once on its own bit, retaining the attribution prefix. GET and accepted-width buffer
initialisation remain separate concerns (`sgirebufuninit`).

**WITNESS — MEASURED, as reported by the ledger.** Rung 3, agy's independent-transport fallback:
`regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/witness_20260910/HEAD_run1.out`: committed `1ce8296`, **2/5**;
`regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/fix_20260910/FIX519_run1.out`: same script on the fix, **5/5**.
The unsupported YCRCB and reserved PUTs destroyed the paint; the supported RGBA control landed.
Paint `0x11223344` became `0x56e8857a` and `0x38abc4e1` across runs; the control was `0xaabbccdd`.

**THE REPAIR CHAIN — historical measurements reported by the ledger.**
`regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/killtable_20260910/`: frozen BASE **14/14**; all twelve planned
mutants killed, including reinstatement `M1` and whole-file pre-fix `M11`, each **6/14**.
The frozen source differed from the later source by the announce's extra closing bracket;
the record says no row or mutant read that token. Codex could not authenticate saved-log binaries.

(the probe names `M13_widthdecline.raw` and `M14l_lineardecline_vs19.raw`). These are distinct
from the coordinate mutants later assigned the same numeric prefixes.

Grok's non-origin guard escape and latch-bit collision prompted the coordinate row, missing

# `#524` (armbdt): an ARM block transfer through a cold host page spliced bytes across a word boundary — the same instruction at the same unaligned base returned different bytes according to host page-cache warmth

**THE DEFECT.** `arm_pop()` (LDM) and `arm_push()` (STM) each hold one running
`uint32_t addr = *np` and branch on host page residency **per register**:

* **FAST path** (page resident): `p32[(addr & 0xfff) >> 2]` — the `>> 2` truncates the low two bits.
* **SLOW path** (cold page): passed the **RAW, UNMASKED `addr`** to `memory_rw`, whose
  `offset = paddr & offset_mask` is page-granular — **not word-rounded** — and whose transfer is a
  raw `memcpy`.

**So an unaligned base spliced bytes across an architectural word boundary, and which bytes a guest
got depended on whether the host page happened to be resident — a condition invisible to the guest
architecture.** Guest data corruption, on a defect that had sat with no witness for three weeks.

**THE FIX.** `addr & 0xfffffffc` at the two slow-path `memory_rw` call sites. **Never at function
entry:** `if (w_bit) *np = addr;` uses the unmasked running value and Mode 4 writeback derives from
unmasked `Rn`. The code generator already separates the two the same way, emitting `addr &= 0xffc;`.

## The architectural warrant is QUALIFIED, and the round says so at the site

`ddi0100i.txt:7954-7959`: *"For `CP15_reg1_Ubit == 0`, the Load Multiple instructions ignore the
least significant two bits of the address. If an implementation includes a System Control
coprocessor, an address with bits[1:0] != 0b00 causes an alignment exception **if alignment checking
is enabled**. For `CP15_reg1_Ubit == 1`, all non-word aligned accesses cause an alignment fault."*

**An earlier draft of the comment stated this flat, and the row's own 2026-08-29 record already said
"the record must NOT say unqualifiedly" — so the comment broke an obligation the row had already
written down.** Corrected in place.

**And the fork is internally inconsistent about it today**, which is why the qualification is not
academic: `cpu_arm.c:129` **SETS** `ARM_CONTROL_ALIGN` in the default control register, `:474` only
**prints** it, and nothing consults it. The model announces alignment checking and enforces none.
Modelling the fault is a separate round; this fix makes the two paths agree with each other and with
the `Ubit == 0` / checking-off reading the fork already implements on its fast path.

## Witness — rung 3, and the instrument had to earn its own cold page

Cold debugger on the **unmodified in-tree `testarm`**, pty-driven, no `device_add`, no custom
machine. The conditioning is the point: **`put b` writes byte-wise with `CACHE_NONE|NO_EXCEPTIONS`,
populating RAM without updating the translation tables — the COLD seed; `put w` writes words with
`CACHE_DATA` and WARMS the page.** Before every transfer the probe runs `tlbdump 0,r` to confirm the
target is genuinely absent on a cold run and resident on a warm one — **without that, the core
comparison establishes nothing about which path each run took.**

## The clause-(d) floor breach, measured and closed

**Table 2 measured `M_MASK1` — the fix present, its mask weakened `0xfffffffc` → `0xfffffffe` — at
`25/25`. A TOTAL ESCAPE**, and the canonical clause-(d) form because *the fix IS the mask* (this
project's own `#461 m_align1`, `& 3` → `& 1`).

**Cause: every unaligned base the probe drove was `+1`, and `x+1 & ~1 == x+1 & ~3`.**

It was predicted by arithmetic in adjudication and **built anyway**, because this project's rule is
that *"it would sweep the table" is a MEASUREMENT, never an inference.* The prediction was right;
a round that had accepted it unmeasured would have shipped a floor claim it never tested.

**CLOSED with four rows — `+2` bases for LDM and STM plus their PATH controls.** Table 3:

|---|---|---|

| `HEAD` | 19/29 | 10, including both new rows |

> figure for that probe as "Measured"; the figure appears in no `.raw` and no `SCORES.txt`, only in

## Scope: the round closes the generic helpers, NOT the BDT access rule

**Two combined-instruction handlers replace LDM/STM outright and never reach the fixed helpers.**
`netbsd_memset` does `memset(page + (addr & 0xfff), 0, 128)` — raw page offset, no rounding, and its
guards check page bounds and source values but **never reject an unaligned address**. `netbsd_memcpy`
copies through raw `& 0xfff` offsets **while its register-publication reads use `& 0xffc`** — one
handler, two address rules, and its own comment already acknowledges *"the overlap and
unaligned-copy divergences"*.

**Pre-existing, so FILED (`armbdtcombined`) rather than repaired here — but the round may not claim
to have closed the class.**

## Disclosed under clause (e)

* **Residue 3** (see above).
* **The helpers are not restricted to RAM.** An unaligned address can reach device dispatch, and
  rounding can change a device-relative offset near a device boundary.
* **`ddi0100i.txt:3256` (A2-42)** specifies additional UNPREDICTABLE behaviour for ARMv6 unaligned
  multiword accesses to Device or Strongly Ordered memory, so "all callers ignore those bits" would
  be too broad.
* **The edit rounds the VIRTUAL address, before translation**, and `memory_rw` splits translated
  accesses at 1 KB — so the old call could touch, and fault on, a page the corrected call never
  accesses. Intended, and stated rather than discovered later.
* **A separate, untouched Thumb issue:** the helper's PC handling clears both low PC bits while
  Thumb POP's specification preserves the halfword address and specifies interworking.

## *** THE CLAUSE-(d) WORK DID NOT END AT TABLE 3.  IT TOOK THREE MORE PASSES, AN INSTRUMENT
## REPAIR, AND A SEVEN-ROW CLASS CLOSURE -- AND THIS BLOCK RECORDED NONE OF IT UNTIL NOW. ***

Found by the pass-C measuring seat auditing this round's own record: within this block,
`M_MASK7`, `M_PBITCOND`, `read_mem32`, `32/32`, `BIT2` and `39` each appeared **zero** times.
The narrative stopped at *"CLOSED with four rows ... Table 3: BASE 29/29"* while the shipped
detector is 39 rows from table 6.  **A reader would not learn that a `p_bit`-conditioned mutant
was ever considered, and so would not know a `p_bit` cell exists to be left open.**  That is the
gap this section closes.

### PASS B -- the first repair did not close the chain

`M_MASK1` (`& ~1`) was closed with two rows.  The repair-chain pass then found **`M_MASK7`**
(`& ~7`, over-alignment) and **`M_PBITCOND`** also sweeping: every base the instrument drove
-- `0x10000`, `0x2000{1,2}`, `0x2100{1,2}` -- lies in the FIRST word of its 8-byte block, where
`~3` and `~7` agree.  A base with **address bit 2 set** separates them, which is what the
`*_COLD_DATA_BIT2` rows do.

### AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT, FOUND BECAUSE A **BASE** ROW WENT RED

Table 4 reported `BASE 31/32` -- the FIX failing `ARM_STM_COLD_DATA_BIT2`.  A red BASE row blocks
the round, so it was diagnosed rather than explained away, and **the arithmetic would not close**:
two readings of one mechanism that could not both be true.  Instrumenting settled it in one run.

`read_mem32()` searched for the dump line labelled `(addr & ~0xF)` -- **which matches whether or
not the dump START is aligned** -- then indexed `line[12:48].split()` by `(addr & 0xF) // 4`.  An
unaligned start BLANK-PADS the leading groups, `.split()` collapses the padding, and every index
shifts by the number of omitted groups.  **8 of 10 legs changed value when it was repaired**,
including the HEAD leg.  The store had been correct all along; the READ was wrong.  Filed as
`probereadalign`; the repair is to dump from `(addr & ~0xF)` for 16 bytes.

### PASS C -- FIVE clause-(d) mutants, each a TOTAL ESCAPE, measured not read

`regress/artifacts/armbdt/killtable_20260911f_opus/SCORES.txt`, eight legs built in a scratch
clone against the 32-row instrument:

    M_POPP_NONE   p_bit ? addr : (addr & ~3)                32/32
    M_POPP_WEAK   addr & (p_bit ? ~1 : ~3)                  32/32
    M_POPW_WEAK   addr & (w_bit ? ~1 : ~3)                  32/32
    M_SBIT_NONE   s_bit ? addr : (addr & ~3)   BOTH sites   32/32
    M_NPMASK      (*np) & ~3  -- the mask on the WRONG operand  32/32

`M_POPP_NONE` is **clause (b)** -- the removed defect reinstated VERBATIM -- restricted to
`p_bit == 1`.  A NON-EQUIVALENCE CONTROL ran `LDMDB r0!,{r1}` (`0xe9300002`) for real
(`ldmdb_*.out`): BASE `r1 = 0x55667788`; `M_POPP_NONE` and `M_POPW_WEAK` `r1 = 0x00005566` -- the
FIX-ABSENT value -- and `M_NPMASK` `r1 = 0x00000000`, with the writeback `r0 = 0x20006` CORRECT on
all four.  **Three escaping mutants corrupt a guest register on an instruction the detector never
issues**, so "the target is dead" is excluded rather than assumed.  Not a corner case: none of
these encodings is in the 256-entry `cpu_arm_multi.txt` fast list, and `:4810-4811` disables the
optimised path entirely for a BIG-ENDIAN guest, so on BE **every** block transfer goes through
these helpers.

**THE CLASS:** every `p/u/s/w` partition was discharged on the STORE side and undischarged on the
LOAD side, because the only leg varying any of those bits is Thumb PUSH -- which calls
`arm_push()`.  `arm_pop()` was driven at exactly ONE `(p,u,s)` point, `(0,1,0)`.  **And it breaches
this round's OWN enumeration:** `PRETABLE3.out` declares `{site} x {residue} x {word position} x
{p_bit}` and says *"close every cell in ONE diff"* -- it then honoured `{site}` for `M_MASK7`
(adding BOTH the LDM and STM `BIT2` rows) and did NOT honour it for `p_bit`, adding only
`THUMB_PUSH_COLD_DATA_P2`.  **Three cells of a two-by-two.**

*Missable for a structural reason: the load-side cell could not be closed by copying the push row.
The instrument's only `p_bit=1` caller is Thumb PUSH, so closing `{load} x {p_bit=1}` needs a NEW
INSTRUCTION WORD, not a new base.*

### DISCLOSED UNDER CLAUSE (e), not claimed

* `ARM_LDM_MULTI_P2_R2` and `ARM_LDM_MULTI_P2_WB` carry **no measured kill**.  *** THE REASON
  GIVEN HERE WAS WRONG -- it read "secondary assertions on a leg whose primary assertion already
  kills", which implies they COULD kill and happened not to.  They CANNOT. ***  R2 is a
  **FAST-path** observation: the first cold access warms the page, so r2 never reaches the edited
  line.  WB observes `*np`, which no mask mutant touches.  Measured twice and independently
  suspected by a reading seat that called the table *"internally impossible as stated"*.  Filed as
  the class `multiaccesswarms`: **a multi-register leg yields exactly ONE cold observation; more
  assertions mean more SESSIONS, not more registers.**
* *** THIS READ "The STORE side of the {p,u,s} product is not newly rowed: Thumb PUSH already
  varies p and u there."  THAT IS A WRONG RECORD AND IT IS WHY THE STORE GAP SURVIVED A WHOLE
  PASS. ***  **`p` and `u` are ONE SELECTOR with FOUR values -- the addressing mode**, not two
  independent bits: the code tests them NESTED (`if (p_bit) { if (u_bit)`), the architecture names
  the pair as one field, and `generate_arm_multi.c:120` switches on `p*2+u`.  Thumb PUSH is
  hardcoded **DB** (`cpu_arm.c:1670`) and every STM row was **IA** -- so the sentence stated TWO
  MODES OF FOUR as an axis, leaving **IB and DA with no row at all on the store side, at any
  residue or strength**.  The dropped-qualifier class, and the qualifier was load-bearing.
  Closed by `ARM_STM_IB_R7`, `ARM_STM_DA_R7` and `ARM_STM_S_R7`.
* *** THIS LINE SAID a joint `(p_bit && u_bit)` conditioning and `addr & (w_bit ? ~7 : ~3)` were

  `M_PU_WEAK_BOTH` 38/39 (`ARM_LDM_IB_P2`) and `M_W_OVER7_BOTH` 38/39 (`ARM_LDM_DB_P2`). ***
  The disclosure is retired, not carried.
* Big-endian is disclosed rather than rowed, with the `:4810-4811` caveat above.
* **`ARM_LDM_S_P2` IS A SOLE CARRIER (L3):** it is the only killer of `M_SBIT_NONE`, so the whole
  `s_bit` axis rests on one row.  `ARM_LDM_DB_P2` kills five mutants but **no mutant depends on it
  alone** -- appearing in many FAILING lists is a CORRELATE of being load-bearing; being the only
  killer is the property that matters, and the two rows are opposite on it.

### THE FLOOR, RE-DERIVED BY THE ADJUDICATING SEAT -- and my proposed bound was wrong in both halves

I had graded single-axis cells as floor and joints as debt, on the premise that "all four bits are
body-tested" -- true of the ENCLOSING FUNCTIONS, which is what my grep found.  **The joint-cell
rule's "body" is the GUARDED body -- the cold `else` branch -- which tests only the `memory_rw`
return and `cpu->byte_order`.**  So p/u/s/w are SELECTORS, and the join rule is ASYMMETRIC: p,u
flow into `addr` (floor, both sites); s flows into `value` -> `data` on PUSH only; w reaches
nothing either body reads ((e)); `i == ARM_PC` flows into `value = cpu->pc + 12` on PUSH.

**And p/u are ONE SELECTOR WITH FOUR VALUES -- the addressing mode**: the code tests them nested,
the architecture names the pair as one field, and `generate_arm_multi.c:120` switches on `p*2+u`.
So the store side was missing TWO WHOLE MODES: STM rows were all IA and Thumb PUSH is hardcoded
DB, leaving **IB and DA with no row at all**.

    FLOOR = {cold first access} x {pop, push} x {IA, IB, DA, DB}
          + {push} x {s = 1}  +  {push} x {pc in list}             = TEN CELLS

**Regraded under that floor the four passes found 1, 1, 3, 1 breaches -- not 1, 2, 5, 5.  The
rising count was DEBT GRADED AS FLOOR.**  The real growth was geometric: every repair rowed at the
residue of the mutant it had just found, so each pass discovered the next strength.

### THE GEOMETRIC FIX: EVERY ROW AT RESIDUE 7 (mod 8)

`0x_0007` has bits 0, 1 and 2 all set, so ONE access discriminates `~1`, `~2`, `~3` AND `~7`.  It
also closed a gap the table-g closure had SHIPPED: all three of its mode rows accessed `0x20006`
(bit 0 CLEAR), so `addr & (p_bit ? 0xfffffffd : 0xfffffffc)` escaped BY ARITHMETIC -- the round's
residue-3 disclosure went false the moment pass C admitted mode-conditioning.

The three pop mode rows were RE-BASED to residue 7; `ARM_LDM_S_P2` became `LDMIA r0!,{r1}^` at
`0x20007` (over-coverage, since s is (e) on pop, but free, and it closes the (s&&w) joint); and
four store rows were added: `ARM_STM_IB_R7`, `ARM_STM_DA_R7`, `ARM_STM_S_R7`, and
`ARM_STM_PC_DB_R7` -- `STMDB r0!,{r1,pc}` at `0x2100b`.  **In DB the loop starts at r15, so the PC
is accessed FIRST and its access is the cold one, at `0x21007`: one row closes both {push x pc}
and {push x DB}'s bit-2-set residue (E4).**  Its expectation (`CODE + 20`, the model's `pc + 12`)
was derived from source by a seat and cross-checked, not by me; the designing seat said plainly it
could not establish cold-path reachability from source, and **the row is green on BASE, so the
cold path was taken** -- the measurement answered what the reading could not.

# `#525` (wdcaltdigin): the alt-status handler never decoded its offset ON THE READ SIDE — a read of the Drive Address register returned the ALT-STATUS byte, and `#494` closed the write half of the same `if` and left this one open

**THE DEFECT.** `DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus)` computes `odata = status_byte(d, cpu)` unconditionally
and then tests `relative_addr` in **exactly one place** — inside the `else` of
`writeflag == MEM_READ`. So the read path never decoded its own offset, and a READ of offset 1 —
the Drive Address register, `0x3f7` on the PC layout — **returned the alt-status byte: the value of
a different register, from an offset the handler never looked at.** The region is registered two
bytes wide.

**THIS IS THE SYMMETRIC CELL OF `#494`.** That round closed the WRITE half of this same `if` and
left the READ half open. The function's own inputs give a two-by-two:

| direction | offset 0 | offset 1 |
|---|---|---|
| WRITE | Alt Ctrl / `WDCTL_RST` (`#481`) | declined silently (`#494`) |
| READ | alt-status, unchanged | **returned the status byte — closed here** |

Three cells were closed and one was not. *A repair that fixes the cell its mutant used and leaves
the symmetric one is a shape this project has now recorded twice.*

**THE FIX.** Decode the read; `odata = 0` on offset 1; keep the unconditional status calculation,
the common tail and `return 1`. **The registration is deliberately NOT narrowed** — a `2 → 1` at
`memory_device_register()` would close both offset-1 cells structurally, but it moves `0x3f7` from
HANDLED-AND-DECLINED to UNMAPPED, an unmeasured path, and it would leave `#494`'s arm as dead code
carrying a measured comment. Owner ruling: decode the read.

**MEASURED, rung 3, cold debugger, unmodified in-tree machine.** Committed HEAD **14/16**, with both
offset-1 read rows returning the status byte (`0x51` at power-on, `0x58` armed); the fix **16/16**.
Same script both ways. Artifacts under `regress/artifacts/wdcaltdigin/killtable_20260911/`,
`KILLTABLE_DONE` present, `PRETABLE.out` written 51 s before table 1 so its mtime proves the order.

**THE STATUS BYTE IS NONZERO AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT INCIDENTAL.** The clause-(d)-shaped
mutant keeps the offset guard and deletes `odata = 0`, so offset-1 reads return the status byte
again — **and if S were 0 the fixed and broken builds would return the identical byte and the row
would be vacuous.** `dev_wdc_init()` sets `d->error = 1`, so `status_byte()` yields
`WDCS_DRDY|WDCS_DSC|WDCS_ERR = 0x51`; armed by `WDCC_WRITE` it yields `0x58`. Both values are
printed in the log rather than asserted.

> **AND THE SCORES ALONE ARE MISLEADING, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN GLOSSING.** All four
> mutant legs score **14/16**. `SCORES.txt` therefore says nothing distinguishes them. Opening the
> raw logs shows `M_NULL_MEDIUM` fails a **different pair** of rows (`ACCEPT_READ_OFF0_*`) than HEAD
> does (`CORE_READ_OFF1_*`). *The numerator is identical and the whole discrimination lives in the
> row identity — read `probe_<leg>.raw`, never `SCORES.txt`.*

## Clause (d) is N/A-WITH-REASON, not passed

**The DEPENDS-ON enumeration for this repair is EMPTY.** The guarded body is `odata = 0;` — it reads
nothing and tests nothing — and the dominating predicates are `writeflag == MEM_READ` and
`relative_addr != 0`, where **over a two-byte region `!= 0` admits no non-equivalent weakening.**

*Recorded as inapplicable with its reason rather than as discharged: an unrun check and an
inapplicable one must not render the same, and writing "(d) passed" here would have claimed a test
that was never available.* Floor otherwise: (a) HEAD red, (b) `M_REINSTATE` = HEAD, (c)
`M_NULL_MEDIUM` fails the accept rows.

## ATA-2 gives this more warrant than the round first claimed

X3T10 0948D, Note 1 (`_scratchpad/ata2_x3t10_948d.txt:1529-1531`): *"This register is obsolete. It
is recommended that a device **not respond** to a read of this address. If a device does respond, it
shall be sure **not to drive the DD7 signal** to prevent possible conflict with floppy disk
implementations."*

**Declining is the recommended behaviour, not merely a choice. DD7 is bit 7, and `odata = 0` leaves
it clear**, so the returned value satisfies the one constraint the standard places on a device that
does answer. Zero remains an emulator policy **where the standard is silent** — it fixes *which*
non-DD7 value is returned — but it is not arbitrary. `030e961` already recorded this Note as
governing and the comment never cited it; two panel seats raised it independently.

**THE `030e961` DD7 BIT-7 ROW IS DISCHARGED BY SUBSUMPTION:** both `CORE_READ_OFF1_*` rows want
`0x00`, which pins every bit including DD7.

## Disclosed under clause (e)

* **`if (odata & WDCS_DRDY) odata = 0;`** — predicted to escape 16/16. **Debt, not floor**, on the
  test that the guarded body never reads or tests `odata`, it only writes it. *Two rows would close
  it and the recipe is known: SDH `0xb0`, any command to an imageless drive sets
  `d->error |= WDCE_ABRT`, giving HEAD `0x01`, fix `0x00`, mutant `0x01`. `d->error` is one shared
  field, so those rows must go LAST in their session.*
* **`M_NULL_EFFECT` and `M_REINSTATE` are indistinguishable to this instrument** — same score, same
  rows, same bytes. Expected, and stated rather than left for a later pass to find.
* **Two panel-proposed selector mutants DO NOT COMPILE** and are recorded so nobody rebuilds them:
  `struct wdc_data` has no `unit` field (it has `drive` and `base_drive`), and `page_size` appears
  nowhere reachable from `cpu->mem`.

## *** PASS 2 ADDED A THREE-ROW PHASE, BECAUSE A ONE-TOKEN MUTANT SWEPT THE 16-ROW
## INSTRUMENT.  THE ROW DESIGN TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS AND TWO OF MY OWN "MEASUREMENTS" WERE
## OF THE APPARATUS RATHER THAN THE DEVICE. ***

Two seats independently predicted a TOTAL ESCAPE of the shipped 16 rows:

    if (odata & WDCS_DRDY)
            odata = 0;

It keeps the offset guard and nulls the repair **only where DRDY is CLEAR** -- and every row the
instrument drove has DRDY SET (`ST_POWERON = 0x51`, `ST_ARMED = 0x58`), so the mutant zeroes
anyway and is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION.  The adjudication graded it a **pre-ship L1**: correct by
the DEPENDS-ON letter as debt (the guarded body `odata = 0` reads nothing), but the round is still
being built, so it is closed here rather than filed.

### THREE DESIGNS, AND WHY THE FIRST TWO FAILED

The requirement is a status that is **NON-ZERO with DRDY CLEAR**.  That is harder than it looks:

* **"run a session with no disk image"** -- VACUOUS, refuted by READING `status_byte()` at `:584`.
  It sets `WDCS_DRDY | WDCS_DSC` only under `diskimage_exist()`, so with no image and no error the
  status is `0x00` -- and a correctly DECLINED `0x00` cannot be told from a LEAKED `0x00`.
* **"issue `WDCC_DIAGNOSE` to set `d->error`, read ERR = 0x01"** -- REFUTED FROM SOURCE by the
  design seat: `wdc_command()` clears `d->error` at `:933`, calls the reset helper, then detects
  the missing image, sets `WDCE_ABRT` and **RETURNS BEFORE THE COMMAND SWITCH**, so DIAGNOSE's arm
  at `:1054` is unreachable without an image.

**What works is the ABSENT SLAVE plus an armed write.**  Writing `0xb0` to `wd_sdh` selects drive
1; that path (`:2006`) sets only sectorsize/lba/drive/head and touches neither error nor transfer
state, and `status_byte()` recomputes DRDY from the NEWLY SELECTED drive's image.  **`WDCS_DRQ` is
independent of image presence**, so with the W2 write still armed and staged bytes queued the
status is `0x08` -- non-zero, DRDY clear.  The phase sits between the `t8` and `t9` reads, the one
point where DRQ is MEASURED set by the line above it, and `arm_a_write()`'s own `0xa0` reselects
drive 0 afterwards.

    CONTROL_STATUS_EMPTYSLAVE     +7        want 0x08   -- DRQ only; DRDY and DSC CLEAR
    ACCEPT_READ_OFF0_EMPTYSLAVE   offset 0  want 0x08   -- the legal read still answers
    CORE_READ_OFF1_EMPTYSLAVE     offset 1  want 0x00   -- declined while DRDY is clear

The ACCEPT row is present on the design seat's own correction: without it the phase never observes
offset 0 in this state, and a DEAD device would satisfy the CORE row for the wrong reason.

### THE MEASURED KILL (`regress/artifacts/wdcaltdigin/killtable_20260911_drdy/SCORES.txt`)

    LEG BASE      19/19  CONTROL=OK  FAILING: none
    LEG M_DRDY    18/19  CONTROL=OK  FAILING: CORE_READ_OFF1_EMPTYSLAVE  (want 0x00 got 0x08)
    RESTORE       cmp-vs-SEC=CLEAN  binary=FRESH  SENTINEL CLEARED (both parts)

**A row is not discharged by existing; it is discharged by reddening under its mutant.**  The
one-token mutant now dies on exactly the row written for it and disturbs nothing else.  The gate
pin moved 16 -> 19 by hand, with its reason, because a pin that follows the probe cannot tell a
probe that GAINED rows from one that LOST them.

### *** A MEASUREMENT ERROR OF MINE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY SHIPPED AS TWO FALSE
### "MEASURED" CLAIMS IN THE PROBE'S OWN CONTRACT ***

`REGS` is the tuple driving the register readback.  **A row whose register is ABSENT from it is
never read and scores `0x00` -- which is indistinguishable from a device that answered `0x00`.**
`t4/t5/t6` were not in `REGS`, so two earlier PLACEMENTS of this phase reported "status 0x00" and I
wrote each up as a refutation of the DEVICE STATE.  Adding the three registers took the same probe
to 19/19.  **Those placements are UNTESTED, not refuted**, and the probe's comment says so.

*This is the pattern-that-matched-nothing class wearing a register's clothes: a selection that
returns nothing yields a clean, confident, wrong answer, and unlike a crash it looks exactly like a
measurement.  The lesson that generalises: when a new row reads `0x00`, establish that the readback
can SEE the register before concluding anything about the device.*


# `#522` (ppcrldiclzero): `rldicl` wrote ZERO to its destination on every execution — the mask was accumulated into the rotated value and ANDed with a variable that was never anything but zero

**THE DEFECT.** `X(rldicl)` rotates its source, then builds a mask. The mask was ORed into **`tmp`** — the
rotated value — while `tmp2` was assigned `0` immediately above and never assigned again. The destination
got `tmp & tmp2`. **So the register was set to ZERO on every execution, for every source, every rotate
amount and every mask begin.**

`rldicl` is the canonical 64-bit PowerPC masking and zero-extension instruction. `rldicl rA,rS,0,32` *is*
`clrldi`, the standard 32-bit zero-extend that compilers emit constantly, and the manual's own simplified
mnemonics make `srdi rA,rS,n` equal to `rldicl rA,rS,64-n,n`. **This was wrong on the ordinary path, for
ordinary compiler output.**

**THE FIX IS ONE TOKEN**: the mask goes into `tmp2`. The `|=` had *also* destroyed the rotated data by
forcing every mask bit to 1, which is unobservable only because the result was ANDed with zero — so the
one character repairs both.

## WITNESSED AT RUNG 3 BEFORE THE EDIT

`artifacts/ppcrldiclzero/opus_ppc_rldicl_witness_20260910.py`, on unmodified `-E bareppc`, with nothing
added to reach the site: **19/27 committed, 24/27 fixed**, and a **190-cell census** in which every cell
was wrong and every cell returned exactly zero pre-fix, and none did after. A separate log
(`pass2_20260910/opus_threemachine.log`) carries the same pair on `testppc` and on `macppc -e g5` — the
Power Mac G5 model, a PPC970 and therefore 64-bit.

The wants come from the manual's own RTL, not from this tree, and **every encoded word was re-read by the
tree's own disassembler** — a different code path from the execute handler. That matters more than usual
here: a wrong register field yields zero, and zero is the symptom under test, so an unchecked encoder
could have manufactured the entire finding.

**AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS A TRAP, BUILT AND MEASURED.** Replacing the `&` with `|` ships
`ROTL64 | MASK` — an OR where the architecture says AND — and gets **126 of 190 cells wrong**. Deleting
the `& tmp2` outright, *on the fixed code*, ships the rotate alone with the mask ignored. Both are worse
than the original defect in one specific way: they remove the always-zero signature that makes it easy to
spot while leaving the value wrong. Both now have kill-table legs, because **a warning in a comment that
no mutant tests is a claim nobody has checked.**

## THE DETECTOR WAS WRONG TWICE, AND PASS 2 MEASURED BOTH

`regress/ppc_rldicl_probe.py`, **24 rows**, scoped to this one instruction. It deliberately excludes rows
for two sibling defects the witness also found, because a detector carrying permanently red rows is one
nobody reads.

The measuring seat did not answer from the packet. It built seven binaries and ran thirteen probe legs in
its own clone, with its own mutator, and returned **BREACH-FOUND with two total escapes** of the 19-row
instrument:

**`M_SH5` — drop one bit of the shift decode. 19/19.** Every `rldicl` with a shift of 32 or more then
rotates by shift minus 32. *** THE INSTRUMENT WAS BLIND BY CONSTRUCTION. *** The census uses an all-ones
source so that every mask window is non-empty — and rotating all-ones is the identity, so all 126
shift-varying cells compute the same value whatever the rotate amount. The only rotate-sensitive rows
drove shifts of 0 and 8, **both below 32**. Since every logical right shift by 1 to 32 has a shift of 32
or more, **the one form the detector pinned is the one form the mutant gets right.**

**`M_CR0` — feed the condition register the unmasked value. 19/19.** *** NOT AN INVENTED MUTANT: it is
the token the sibling handler ships, correctly, ten lines below, where that variable really is the
destination. *** A future editor harmonising the two writes exactly this. The old instrument could not see
it because it emitted a zero record bit on every encoding, leaving the whole record-form path unexecuted.

**Repaired with three rows and one control**, all measured by the seat before I applied them: two rows at
shifts of 63 and 32, and one on the condition register — which is a three-valued channel here, since the
fix gives greater-than, the defect gives equal, and the mutant gives less-than.

**ZERO ESCAPES across nine mutants.** `M_SH5` is red on the two shift rows and nothing else; `M_CR0` is

**This reproduces the measuring seat's own numbers exactly** — two independently written mutators, two
clones, same figures.

## FIVE RECORDS WERE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED

1. **A wrong citation in PRODUCT CODE.** The comment claimed measurement on three machines while naming
   artifacts that show only one. The seat re-measured rather than merely reporting, so the claim is true
   and the pointer was wrong; it now cites the log that shows it.
2. **A detector row that CANNOT FAIL.** `naive fix` is arithmetic over the probe's own constants and never
   touches the binary — the check-that-cannot-fail shape, inside a detector whose whole purpose is to be
   failable. The docstring called it a measurement. It is now declared carried-not-counted, the
   disposition already invented for a row in `#520`.
3. **A coverage claim refuted by my own table.** The pre-table said the census "walks the cross-product"
   of the two fields. It does not: with an all-ones source it is a function of the mask field alone, and

4. **A superseded wording that survived in two more places** after the product comment was corrected —
   the grep-for-siblings rule, live, in the same hour.
5. **The score log named the previous round**, because the driver was derived by substitution and the

## THE APPARATUS FAILED TWICE AND BOTH ARE PRESERVED

**Table 0 called the previous round's mutator**, which replied "unknown mutant" and exited. The hard-fail
refused rather than measuring an unmutated tree. *** But the failure had a shape worth naming: the table
looked HALF-HEALTHY, not dead. *** Both bracketing legs scored full marks, because both mutators define a
mutant called BASE and answer it identically. Four blanks in a score column were the only signal.

**And building the mutator through a shell heredoc ate a backslash level**, turning every escape into a
real newline — the exact trap the carrier documents, with the documented remedy, which I then used.

The measuring seat preserved its own apparatus failure too: a regex built through a non-raw string turned
`\b` into a literal backspace, so the pattern matched nothing and failed a row on **every** leg including
the baseline. It added a negative control so the regex cannot silently match nothing again.

## CONTRACT (clause (e)) AND WHAT IS FILED

The probe now carries a measured boundary. **Not caught:** source-register edits that are the identity on
the one register every row uses; edits conditioned on a zero destination; and rotate-amount edits that are
the identity at all four rowed shift values.

**Two sibling defects in the same family are filed and unfixed**, both measured: one overwrites
destination bits the architecture requires preserved, for every non-zero shift; the other performs a
32-bit rotate at 64-bit width so high-half data leaks into the result. A design review rejected my
proposed repair for both while confirming both defects. Three further instructions in the family are not
implemented at all.

**A claim of mine about the gates was false and is corrected in place.** I wrote that no gate instantiates
a 64-bit PowerPC processor. One does — it enumerates every advertised machine type, three of which default
to that processor. The correct, narrower finding is that **no gate checks their instruction results**.
That distinction is this project's own witness ladder one level up: construction proves presence, not
reachability. Closing it is its own harness round, and this detector is exempt until then.

# `#521` (mk48nvramkill): EIGHT ordinary NVRAM bytes inside a device's own mapped range ended the emulator, and the accept block's lower bound was one term short

**THE DEFECT.** `dev_mk48txx.c` registers the MK48T08 for `MK48TXX_LEN` = `MK48T08_CLKSZ` = **8192**
bytes. An early accept block passed everything OUTSIDE `[MK48T08_CLKOFF, MK48T08_CLKOFF + MK48TXX_ISEC)`
to the RAM path with a `goto ret`. With `CLKOFF` = `0x1ff0` and `ISEC` = `9`, the `switch` was reached for
`0x1ff0..0x1ff8` — and it holds exactly ONE case, `CLKOFF + MK48TXX_ICSR` = `0x1ff8`. **The other eight
offsets fell to `default:` and called `exit(1)`.** `machine_mvme88k.c` attaches the device unconditionally
in its MVME187 arm, at `0xfffc0000`.

**AND THE BOUNDARY LOOKS DELIBERATE, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED.** The block's own comment says reads and
writes to the RAM part *"or the clock registers"* are OK, and the test reads as though it means
*everything except the clock registers*. Its upper bound is the SECONDS register, so it hands the real
time-of-day registers to the RAM path — harmless, because `mk48txx_update_regs()` writes into that same
array — and captures the eight bytes below them into the fatal switch, which is not. *The bound was one
term short in the direction nobody checks.*

**THOSE EIGHT ARE ORDINARY NVRAM ON THIS PART, and that is what licenses accepting them rather than
declining.** `mk48txxreg.h` says the first bank of eight registers at `(nvramsz - 16)` — exactly `0x1ff0`
— is *"available only on more recent MK48Txx models"*, naming them IFLAGS, IASEC, IAMIN, IAHOUR, IADAY,
IINTR and IWDOG. They are the MK48T59's alarm and watchdog bank; this file implements the MK48T08 alone.
**Two seats reached that conclusion independently and by different routes** — one from the header's prose
and the manufacturer's datasheet, one from the arithmetic that `8192 - 16` is the first fatal address —
and neither was told the other's answer.

**THE FIX IS ONE TOKEN.** The accept block's lower bound gains its missing `+ MK48TXX_ICSR`, so the
`switch` is reached only at `0x1ff8`, which is exactly the case it implements. The `default:` arm becomes
unreachable and is deliberately left in place as a tripwire for a later edit that widens the window
without adding a case. Storage already existed — `reg` is `MK48TXX_LEN` bytes — so this is a **boundary
correction, not new policy**, and no vendored constant is wrong.

## WITNESSED AT RUNG 3 BEFORE THE EDIT

`artifacts/mk48nvramkill/opus_mk48_nvram_witness_20260910.py`, on unmodified `-E mvme88k -e mvme187`,
with nothing added to reach the site: **15/47 on the committed build**, all fifteen controls green and all
thirty-two kill rows red; **46/47 after the fix**.

**THE ORACLE IS A CONJUNCTION and it has to be:** the reaped wait status AND a post-access observable — a
scratch store before the access under test and a scratch load after it. That makes death, a hang, and a
diagnostic that merely complains **three distinguishable states**, which matters in this fork because
`fatal()` has no early-out and does NOT exit, so "it printed a message" is not evidence of death. A
timeout gets its own token rather than being read as a kill.

**TWO MEASURED CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL FILING.** The killing population is **SIXTEEN cells, not
eight** — every offset kills on write as well as read, and all sixteen were driven. And **the kill is
WIDTH-INDEPENDENT**: `len` never enters the guard, so byte, halfword and word accesses all die at the same
start offset. *There is therefore NO width axis to close, and a detector row varying width at a fixed
offset would be non-varying by construction* — the opposite of the recent PCC2 rounds, where width was the
whole defect.

## THE DETECTOR, AND THE TWO TIMES IT WAS WRONG

`regress/mk48_nvram_probe.py`, **57 rows**. It is the round's witness with one row INVERTED: the witness
asserted sixteen offset-named death messages, which is green only while the defect LIVES, so it could
never score full marks on a fixed build. The detector asserts ZERO such messages instead, and that row
still reddens under any mutant restoring the old boundary.

**TABLE 1 FOUND A FLOOR BREACH: `M_ICSR` ESCAPED 47/47.** Moving the accept block's UPPER bound to
`CLKOFF + ICSR` makes the condition `addr < 0x1ff8 || addr >= 0x1ff8` a **tautology** — every address is
accepted, the switch is never reached, and the control register is served as plain RAM while silently
doing nothing. The rows aimed at that offset could not see it because **they are survive-only there**:
they assert the access ran to completion, which is true on the RAM path too. *The pre-table block had
named a channel for those rows that does not exist, so the CHANNEL check was applied and got the answer
wrong; what would have caught it is asking not "can this row vary?" but "can it vary UNDER THIS MUTANT?"*

Repaired with one row, `csr rise`, reading the case's SIDE EFFECT: writing the READ bit 0→1 calls
`mk48txx_update_regs()`, so the row clears the register, poisons a clock slot, drives the edge and reads
the slot back. It needs no new instruction encoding — the scratch register's low byte is `0x5a` and
`0x5a & MK48TXX_CSR_READ` is `0x40`.

**THEN PASS 2 FOUND THE SAME CLASS A SECOND TIME, ON THE EIGHT BYTES THE FIX ACTUALLY ACCEPTS.** The
sixteen kill rows prove the host survives and the guest runs on, and prove nothing about whether the byte
was stored or read back — so a mutant that accepts the access and drops the data passes all sixteen. **Two
consecutive findings of one class is this project's trigger to enumerate the space and close every cell in
ONE diff.** The space is *every offset this detector touches — is the DATA verified, or only survival?*
Nine round-trip rows close it (`0x1fef` plus the eight), each writing a DISTINCT byte so a mutant folding
offsets onto one cell is caught too.

Scratch clone, baseline taken from the repo source, ONE frozen instrument for every leg, sentinel dropped

## OUT OF SCOPE, FILED RATHER THAN FOLDED IN

A second, non-fatal defect three lines above: the accept path reads and writes exactly ONE byte whatever
`len` says, so a four-byte read of the clock block returns a single zero-extended byte where a true
big-endian device read would return four packed ones. **Measured by the witness.** Routing eight more
offsets onto that path newly *exhibits* it there — death used to mask it — but it covers the whole 8192
bytes and a `len`-aware copy is a different fix. One site, one semantic class.

# `#520` (alphatbinegsel): a guest TBIA flushed ONE page and left every other translation live -- `uint64_t a0` made `if (a0 >= 1)` an UNSIGNED compare, so both documented invalidate-everything selectors took the single-page branch

**THE DEFECT, and it is one character of type rather than one of logic.** `PAL_OSF1_tbi` (`case 0x33` in
`src/cpus/cpu_alpha_palcode.c`) takes its selector in `a0`, declared `uint64_t`. The Alpha PALcode contract
gives that selector two NEGATIVE values, and they are the two that matter most: **-1 invalidates everything
with ASM=0 (sparing ASM=1) and -2 invalidates everything**. Under an unsigned compare both are enormous
positive numbers, so both compared GREATER than 1, both took the single-VADDR branch, and both flushed
exactly ONE page using `a1` as the address. **A guest issuing TBIA or TBIAP got one page invalidated and
every other cached translation left live** -- the direction that hands a guest stale translations, which is
silent rather than loud.

**WITNESSED AT RUNG 3 BEFORE THE EDIT**, on an unmodified in-tree machine description, and replicated on a
second build: `artifacts/alphatbinegsel/witness_agy_20260908/` scores **5/7 committed, 7/7 fixed** with
both negative selectors RED pre-fix, and `fix_20260910/{HEAD,FIX520}_run1.out` reproduces that same pair.

**THE FIX IS ONE EXECUTABLE LINE** -- a two-sided window in place of a one-sided test:

```c
if ((int64_t)a0 >= 1 && (int64_t)a0 <= 3)
        cpu->invalidate_translation_caches(cpu, a1, INVALIDATE_VADDR);
else
        cpu->invalidate_translation_caches(cpu, 0, INVALIDATE_ALL);
```

The `else` arm is the conservative one, which is why the two-sidedness is the load-bearing property: every
selector the window does not name -- negative, zero, or above 3 -- now invalidates everything rather than
guessing at a page.

**AND THE CASTS ARE MEASURED REDUNDANT, WHICH THE COMMENT ORIGINALLY GOT WRONG (L4, corrected in the
source).** Raised by the kimi substitute on pass 2 -- *"the load-bearing property of the one executable line
is its TWO-SIDEDNESS, not its SIGNEDNESS"* -- and then CHECKED rather than judged: the unsigned form
`a0 >= 1 && a0 <= 3` agrees with the shipped signed form on **300,037 values with ZERO disagreements**
(every boundary class, the 32-bit and 63-bit boundaries and their neighbours, plus 300,000 random 64-bit
values). The reason is structural rather than lucky -- a negative selector is a huge unsigned value that
fails the UPPER bound exactly where the signed reading fails the LOWER one, so both arrive at the
conservative arm by different routes. **The casts are KEPT** (they state the selector's signedness to a
reader and cost nothing) and the comment no longer claims they are the repair. *A fix whose stated reason is
wrong gets that reason reused.*

## THE CLASS CLOSURE -- nine axes in ONE diff, because three consecutive passes had each bought one cell

This round is the class-closure amendment's second application and its clearest case. **Three consecutive
review passes each found ONE more axis of the SAME guard**: the window's four sides, then the body's other
lvalue (`a1`), then operand magnitude. Buying one cell per pass converges linearly and does not terminate,
so the detector now carries the guard's full axis set enumerated in its own header and closed together:

| axis | cell | row | mutant it kills |
|---|---|---|---|
| lower bound, accept | `a0 = 1` | `bnd lo` | `>=1` -> `>=2` |
| lower bound, reject | `a0 = 0` | `bnd zero` | `>=1` -> `>=0` |
| upper bound, accept | `a0 = 3` | `bnd hi` | `<=3` -> `<=2` |
| upper bound, reject | `a0 = 4` | `bnd out` | `<=3` -> `<=4` |
| interior | `a0 = 2` | `bnd mid` | `&& a0 != 2` |
| negative selectors | `a0 = -1, -2` | `tbia obs` / `tbiap obs` | the original defect |
| `a1`, zero vs non-zero | `a0 = 2, a1 = 0` | `bnd a1z` | `&& a1 != 0` |
| `a1`, magnitude | `a0 = 2, a1 = 0x8000` | `bnd a1hi` | `&& a1 < 0x8000` |
| `a0`, magnitude | `a0 = 0x100000001` | `bnd wide` | `(int32_t)` cast, and `<=3` -> `!=4` |

**THE MAGNITUDE AXIS IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE ESCAPED A FOURTH PASS**, and it was found by deepseek --
the panel's only NOT-RATIFY. `a0` was sampled only in `[-2,4]` and `a1` only at `{0, 0x6000}`, so narrowing
either cast to 32 bits is **invisible at all seven selector values the other rows drive** (verified by
enumeration, zero disagreements: for any small value `(int32_t)a0 == (int64_t)a0`). It is nonetheless a real
behaviour change, and the smallest discriminating input is `a0 = 0x0000000100000001` -- the shipped fix sees
4294967297, fails `<= 3` and invalidates everything, while a narrowed cast truncates to 1 and flushes a
single page. `load_const()` builds only sign-extended 32-bit constants and CANNOT make that value, so the
row loads `a0` from memory with an LDQ off the pointer vector; **no new instruction encoding is introduced
anywhere in the file.**

## THE CONTRACT (clause (e))

The detector catches: any edit to either bound of the window, in either direction; loss of either reject
side; an added conjunct on `a0` or on `a1`; and a narrowing of either comparison's width. **It does NOT
observe ASM/ASN granularity** -- this model's translation cache has no ASM concept, so no row can separate
`-1` from `-2`, and a row claiming to would be vacuous by construction. That is stated in the probe header
rather than glossed. Multi-axis joints over `a0` and `a1` together remain disclosed debt.

## THE ASSESS STAGE, HELD FOR THE FLAGSHIP SEAT SINCE 2026-09-08, AND IT FOUND FOUR MORE WRONG RECORDS

The assess stage carried a live hold for the Opus seat from a deliberate conservation, and a review-phase
answer may not discharge an assess-phase hold. Fired and landed: `artifacts/alphatbinegsel/opus_assess_20260910.md`.

**It RATIFIED the defect reading, the disposition, the `<= 3` bound and every measured score** -- deriving
all twelve legs from the source by hand rather than reading `RESULTS.txt`, and reconciling each one. It
settled the ASM direction from a source the round had not used for that purpose (`21066_66a_hrm.txt:1486`,
on the ITBASM register: writes *"invalidate all entries that do not have the ASM bit set"*), which is
independent of the header comment the round was simultaneously editing. **It also found the `<= 3` bound's
proper authority: `alpha_cpu.h:281-285` defines exactly five selectors and the three selective ones are 1,
2 and 3** -- imported third-party material this round does not touch, and therefore a better warrant than a
header being rewritten in the same diff. Cited in the source now.

**Four L4 corrections, none touching the executable line, none requiring a re-table:**

1. **The detector's own CONTRACT had two false entries in its ROWED list, and the CLAIM -> ROW check never
   looked at it.** `loss of the signed cast` names an edit that is **UNKILLABLE** -- apply it to the
   shipped line and you get exactly the unsigned form measured equivalent over 300,037 values, so it
   scores 15/15 by construction. Worse, it *misdirects*: the unsigned form is the more portable of the
   two, since converting a `uint64_t` above `INT64_MAX` to `int64_t` is implementation-defined under C99
   6.3.1.3p3, so the bullet told a future simplifier they were reinstating the original defect when they
   were improving portability. And `omission of the invalidation entirely` was listed as MEASURED while
   **no mutant in any of the three tables touches the invalidation call** -- nine mutants, every one a text
   replacement on the guard. Both bullets deleted. *The pre-table CLAIM -> ROW check was run, and run well,
   against the product comment only; nothing applied it to the detector's own contract, which is itself a
   set of observable-consequence claims.*
2. **The NO-ANNOUNCE warrant cited the wrong precedent, and the seat was correcting a finding of its own
   that this round had adopted.** `#514` is about an architecturally UNPREDICTABLE OUTPUT the model
   declines to define; leaving a register nobody may read alone is not the same act as silently
   re-interpreting a request a guest made. The real in-file precedent is `swpipl` (case 0x35) and `wrmces`
   (case 0x11), which take a guest value the model cannot honour exactly and silently normalise it.
   **And the file has FOUR sites that meet an unrecognised selector with `fatal()` and `cpu->running = 0`**
   -- including `wrent`, the closest structural sibling of all -- none of which the comment mentioned, so a
   reader concluded the file had no contrary practice. The departure is now stated rather than hidden.
3. **The ITB/DTB conflation was undisclosed and two rows silently depend on its absence.** `a0` = 1, 2 and
   3 are architecturally different requests; this model has one unified cache and services all three
   identically. `bnd lo` and `bnd mid` were labelled "ITB selective" and "DTB selective" -- and would go
   **RED ON A CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION** of the split, since each flushes with one selector and observes
   with an ordinary data load. That is the oracle-correction rule's setup being built into a fresh
   detector. Disclosed, with the re-pin-first obligation written into the contract for whoever implements
   the split.
4. **The disclosed multi-axis joint understated its own size.** It read as a corner; it is a predicted
   **total sweep**, and the seat named the discriminator (`&& !((int64_t)a0 == 1 && a1 == 0)`), which no
   row enters because `bnd lo` drives `a1 = 0x6000` and both `a1 = 0` rows drive `a0 = 2`. Clause (e) only
   lets a later escape land as *"outside the contract, as stated"* if the statement conveys the size.

**The shipped probe therefore differs from the frozen t3 instrument by 27 lines, and the difference is
COMMENT-ONLY** -- checked rather than asserted: every changed line is inside the module docstring or inside
a row's display-only note string, which `row()` prints and never compares. The table's scores describe the
shipped probe's behaviour unchanged.

**One finding RECORDED and not acted on**, because it is a tooling question rather than this round's:
`tally_kills.py` decides what an accept row is by the name prefix `bnd `, which is a correlate rather than
the defining property -- and three of the eight rows it grades that way are reject-side. Not live here
(every `bnd` row carries a real mutant kill), but the check would not say so if it were.

# `#517` pcc2genctlc040alias: a vendored header defined C040 twice, and the second definition was a different register's bits

**THE DEFECT.** `src/include/thirdparty/mvme_pcctworeg.h` carries `PCC2_C040 0x04` (right -- bit 2 of
the General Control Register, matching VMESBCP2's GENCTL page and the value `dev_pcc2.c` uses) and,
seventy lines later, `PCC2_GENCTL_C040 0x03`. **0x03 is FAST | MIEN** -- two other bits of the same
register. The alias has ZERO consumers (deriver: `grep -rn PCC2_GENCTL_C040 src/` finds only the
definition), so it is a loaded trap rather than a live defect: the first future site to reach for the
`GENCTL_` spelling would test the wrong two bits and never the right one. Found by the codex seat on
2026-09-07 while answering a different question about the same file; filed low; taken now because the
owner's standing priority is critical bugs first and EASY-RESOLVABLE ones second, and this is one line.

**THE DISPOSITION IS ANNOTATE, NOT DELETE, and that was adjudicated rather than assumed.** The
flagship seat ranked it "a records/guard fix, not a round" on 2026-09-09. Deleting a definition from a
vendored third-party header is a different licence from annotating one: the addition licence's
discriminator -- a measured delta or a transferred warrant, never "cannot hurt" -- does not reach a
deletion on a zero-consumer warrant, and a reader who greps for the symbol now lands on a warning that
names the right constant instead of on a bare wrong number. The value is left as it was, marked WRONG
on its own line, so nothing that might parse the header changes meaning.

**WHAT THIS IS NOT.** Not a fix to `dev_pcc2.c`, which never used the alias. Not a claim that the
header is otherwise correct -- `PCC2_GENCTL_FAST 0x01` and `PCC2_GENCTL_IEN 0x02` in the same block
were not audited against the manual here and are not vouched for. No detector: there is no observable
behaviour to pin, because no code reads the symbol; a row would be vacuous by construction, and the
witness field says so.

**Propagated** to `est/` and all three build trees with the `#516` batch (the header has three
consumers -- `dev_clmpcc.c`, `dev_pcc2.c`, `machine_mvme88k.c` -- so `src/devices/*.o` and
`src/machines/*.o` were cleared before the rebuild); two-part clearance RUN, CLEAN/FRESH on every row,
`_scratchpad/propagate516.out`.

Witness: `none` (documented-only; a comment on a symbol nothing reads). Seats: codex found it (assess,
2026-09-07); fable5 adjudicated the disposition (2026-09-09); no panel fired on a one-line annotation,
by the loop's judgment, and that judgment is recorded here rather than left to be inferred.

# Records correction to `#512` (pcc2c040kill): `dev_pcc2.c` described a host kill its own code no longer had -- and the same sentence had already gone stale once before, in the same paragraph

**THE WRONG RECORD.** `dev_pcc2.c`'s header carried, under "NOT FIXED HERE, cited so 'twelve kills
removed' is not read as 'file clean'":

    pcc2c040kill (a LEGAL byte write of 0x04 to GENCTL still ends the host in reassert_interrupts).

`#512` (9fa07fe) had converted that arm to a latched decline, witnessed at rung 3 by
`regress/pcc2_c040_probe.py` -- 3/4 committed, 4/4 fixed with the same script, 7/7 with three added
discriminating rows. VERIFIED LOCALLY before editing, not taken from the seat that found it: the only
executable `exit(1)` left in the file is `pcctwo_interrupt_common()`'s `default:` arm, on an unsupported
interrupt LINE ID -- and that one's guest reachability is NOT established (the registration loop exposes
sixteen line IDs and nothing in these files says which unsupported ones a connected device can emit),
so the corrected text calls it a cited exit, not a witnessed kill.

**THE SHARP PART: the clause beside it already carried the IDENTICAL correction for its sibling.** The
same paragraph says of `pcc2defaultkill`: *"this sentence said 'still ends it' until #501's pass 4"*. The
same sentence, in the same list, went stale the same way a second time, and the first correction did
not protect the second clause. **A NOT-FIXED-HERE list is a dated claim wearing the clothes of a
structural note**: it decays every time one of its own members is fixed, by the rounds that read it.
The corrected text says so and names the deriver -- `grep -n 'exit(' dev_pcc2.c`, then read each hit --
rather than trusting the list.

**How it was found, because the route is the lesson.** The codex seat's answer
(`regress/artifacts/pcc2c040kill/codex_analysis_20260908.err`) had been sitting UNREAD -- a zero-byte
`.txt`, the answer in the `.err` -- with no ledger entry. It was the FIRST of ten unread streams opened
on 2026-09-09, and it held a live wrong record; the rest were then opened, and two more live findings
came out (`wiringcliff`'s counts; `sgirekills`' discharged blocker). The unread-review class is this
project's most expensive recorded class, and this was its fourth instance.

**The row stays OPEN, deliberately**: its flagship stages are held for adjudication (a partial ruling
landed 2026-09-09; part (a) of its question is referred to a codex reading). That is a different fact
from the kill being present, and conflating those two is exactly how the wrong sentence got written.

Also corrected in place today, same class: `CHANGELOG.md`'s older "filed, not fixed" list that quoted

and not only on the stale line. Comment-only; propagated with the `#516` batch, clearance CLEAN/FRESH.

# `#516` lcairqstubkill: every ISA interrupt on alphabook1 routed into a function whose whole body was fatal() + exit(1)

**THE DEFECT.** `dev_lca.c` registered the machine's two interrupt handlers as bare kills:

    void lca_interrupt_assert(struct interrupt *interrupt)
    { fatal("lca_interrupt_assert: TODO\n"); exit(1); }        /*  and _deassert, identically  */

`DEVINIT(lca)` registers them for `"<machine>.lca"` and hands that same path to `bus_isa_init`, so
every ISA interrupt -- 8042, UART, IDE, PIT -- ended the host process. **No guard, no inspection of the
argument, no unusual value anywhere**: a store of 0xAA (the standard 8042 self-test command) to ISA
0x64 is four guest instructions, and the host is gone. It was WITNESSED at rung 3 before any edit
(`regress/lca_irqstub_probe.py`, 7c2f8e4, 3/4 with the RED row being the defect) and separately
through the ns16550 on IRQ 4 (`regress/lca_irqstub_uart_probe.py`).

**THE FIX IS OPTION-SET MEMBER 3 AT BOTH STUBS: DECLINE + a bounded, PER-INSTANCE latched announce.**

    struct lca_data *d = (struct lca_data *) interrupt->extra;
    if (d != NULL && !(d->warned & (1u << LCA_W_IRQ_ASSERT))) {
            d->warned |= 1u << LCA_W_IRQ_ASSERT;
            fatal("[ lca: ISA interrupt assert not implemented (Alpha has no "
                "interrupt delivery); ignored  (once) ]\n");
    }

with a SEPARATE latch bit for the deassert stub, so the two are distinguishable. Per-instance
(`interrupt->extra`), not function-static: a function-static bit would let one guest access to one
device instance silence the diagnostic for every other, a class already filed against this tree.

**WHY DECLINE AND NOT IMPLEMENT, stated narrowly: THE HOST STOPS DYING. Interrupts do not start
working -- they were never delivered on this architecture and still are not.** `cpu_dyntrans.c`
delivers pending interrupts for FIVE architectures (ARM, M88K and PPC via `irq_asserted`; MIPS via
COP0; SH via `int_to_assert`) and **has no Alpha arm**; `cd.alpha.irq_asserted` is written at
`cpu_alpha.c:218,:223` and read nowhere. So forwarding would set a field nothing consumes, and the
decline drops nothing that ever worked. (An earlier draft of this comment said "three architectures";
the grok seat counted five. I had grepped `irq_asserted` -- a CORRELATE -- and Alpha's absence is
unchanged and strengthened.) Implementing delivery is a SUBSYSTEM -- dyntrans dispatch, the PALcode
entry, the IPL check -- and is filed as **`alphaintdeliver`** so the missing feature is TRACKED rather
than buried inside a fixed kill. *That filing is what makes the decline honest: "silently missing"
becomes "explicitly owed".*

**Member 5 (FAULT) was NOT available.** `memory_rw.c`'s failed-device branch dispatches an exception
for MIPS and M88K only; Alpha, ARM, i960, PowerPC, RISC-V and SH return `MEMORY_ACCESS_FAILED` without
one. Recorded because the option-set rule says check availability on THIS CPU before choosing.

## The option set had a member the packet did not name: HALT THE GUEST

The disposition chose DECLINE + announce. A further disposition was available and is recorded here
because the design packet never weighed it (the codex audit of that packet caught the omission): STOP
THE GUEST CLEANLY -- `cpu->running = 0` rather than `exit(1)`, the graceful-halt shape the tree
already uses. **REJECTED, and the reason is the same fact that makes this kill severe**: the stub is
entered on ORDINARY ISA interrupts, not on a halt request. Halting on the first one makes
`alphabook1` unbootable -- every keyboard or disk interrupt would stop the machine -- which is
strictly worse than declining. So STOP-GUEST is the right shape for a halt request and the wrong shape
for an unimplemented delivery path, and DECLINE + announce is chosen because the whole claim of this
round is that the host survives AND the guest keeps running.

**The scope line, so "two kills removed" is not read as "interrupts work":** this round removes two of
`dev_lca.c`'s active `exit(1)` calls (the interrupt callbacks) by DECLINING; it does NOT implement
Alpha interrupt delivery, which is `alphaintdeliver` and is the subsystem the decline sits in front of.

# `#515` lcaconfbus1kill: one variable meant two things, and a value the register's own guard ACCEPTS armed a host kill in a different handler

**THE DEFECT.** `DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf)` in `dev_lca.c` used a single `bus` for two unrelated
quantities -- the configuration CYCLE TYPE selected by `d->ioc_conf & 1`, and the DESTINATION BUS:

    bus = d->ioc_conf & 1;
    if (bus == 0) { ...IDSEL scan... } else { fatal("TODO. Non-zero bus."); exit(1); }

The `LCA_IOC_CONF` guard is `if (idata & ~1) { fatal(); exit(1); }`, so **`0x1` is ACCEPTED and
stored**. A guest then needs no unusual value anywhere: store 1 to IOC_CONF, make any access in the
PCI config window, and the host process ends. Two ordinary accesses, nothing refused on the path.

**THE FIX SPLITS THE TWO QUANTITIES AND IMPLEMENTS THE MISSING BRANCH** -- option-set member 7 for
the type-1 decode, member 2 for the alias:

    type1 = d->ioc_conf & 1;   bus = 0;
    if (!type1) { ...IDSEL scan, unchanged... }
    else { bus = (tag >> 16) & 0xff;  dev = (tag >> 11) & 0x1f; }
    ...
    if (type1 && bus == 0)  odata = reg == 0? (uint64_t) -1 : 0;
    else                    { bus_pci_setaddr(...); bus_pci_data_access(...); }

**THE ALIAS ARM IS NOT TIDINESS -- WITHOUT IT THE FIX SHIPS A NEW MISROUTING.** A type-1 cycle whose
bus field is zero selects nothing (type-1 is how a bridge is asked to reach a bus *behind* it).
Forwarding it would set `cur_bus = 0` and hand the access to whichever primary-bus device matched --
`i82378zb` is registered at 0:7:0 -- so decoding `bus` and stopping there replaces a host kill with a
silent wrong destination. The refusal returns `bus_pci_data_access`'s own empty-slot values, read
from `bus_pci.c` rather than assumed.

**PRIMARY SOURCE, read locally and cited narrowly.** 21066/21066A HRM S6.2.9: *"PCI address bits
ad<1:0> come directly from configuration cycle type register (IOC_CONF, Section 6.4.2) bits <1:0>"* --
IOC_CONF selects the CYCLE TYPE and carries no bus number. The type-1 FIELD POSITIONS come from the
PCI Local Bus specification, which S6.2.9 defers to explicitly, **not** from this manual.

**THE FUNCTION TAIL IS PRESERVED ON BOTH ARMS** -- `memory_writemax64` and `return 1` are still
reached. Checked by reading the whole function after the edit, not the diff.
