**A FOURTEENTH VARIANT, MEASURED SEPARATELY** (`table4_targeted/`), because grok's ask-again answer
arrived after table 3 was frozen and its shape is NOT covered by `M12`:

    base    18/18        M13_regconj    17/18        prefix18    8/18

`M13_regconj` hoists the test into the guard -- `if (type1 && bus == 0 && reg == 0)` -- so a non-zero
register is not refused at all but FORWARDED. `M12_regnull` only corrupts the refused *value*; this
one re-opens the misrouting itself.

*** ITS EVIDENCE IS THE STRONGEST SINGLE DATUM IN THE ROUND. *** Under the variant, row `t1 reg4`
reads back **`0x601004300000003`** against a want of `0x0`. That is the real `i82378zb`:
`0x00000003` is its command/status at register 4 and `0x06010043` its class register at 8 -- exactly
what `PCIINIT(i82378zb)` writes (`PCI_CLASS_CODE(PCI_CLASS_BRIDGE, PCI_SUBCLASS_BRIDGE_ISA, 0)
+ 0x43`). **Nothing but a genuine forward to the genuine device produces that number**, so the row
does not merely detect a difference -- it names where the access landed.

*** IT WAS RECORDED AS A PREDICTION FIRST AND MEASURED SECOND. *** The round wrote down that
`t1 reg4` should kill it and marked that PREDICTED, NOT MEASURED -- a prediction written into a
measured column is the frozen-number class. Table 4 is the discharge of that.

*** THE LAST THREE ARE THE ASK-AGAIN'S OWN ESCAPES, AND EACH NOW DIES BY EXACTLY ONE ROW. ***
`M10`/`M11`/`M12` each swept the 14-row table clean; at 18 rows each scores 17/18. **A one-row margin
is the tightest possible evidence that the added row does precisely the job it was added for** --
a larger margin would mean the row was catching something incidental as well.

*** TWO EARLIER TABLES ARE PRESERVED BESIDE IT AND NEITHER IS CITED. ***
`table1_preliminary/` (10 variants, a stale instrument) and `table2_shipped/` (10 variants, 14 rows,
zero escapes) are kept only so the three can be compared. **A comparison owes ONE instrument**, and
the progression is itself the record: the detector got strictly stricter at each step, and the
escapes that motivated each step are visible in the table that preceded it.

## THE ASK-AGAIN: one query, three escapes, all of them one family

Table 2 came back clean at ten variants, so the round spent its single capped adversarial query.
**The cap counts ASKS, never FINDINGS**, so all three were disposed of in-round rather than one
taken and two filed.

    deepseek   `if (type1 && bus == 0 && len == 8)`      every row used an 8-byte access
    kimi       `func = (tag >> 8) & 7`  ->  `& 3`        the only func probe was the anchor's func 2
    codex      the `reg != 0` branch of the refusal       every row used register 0

> **ONE FAMILY: AN AXIS EVERY EXISTING ROW HELD CONSTANT.** Fourteen rows that reinforced each other
> on the axes they *did* vary, and were blind on three they did not. That is what a frozen axis looks
> like from outside, and it is invisible from inside precisely because the rows agree.

**codex ranked its own above the other two and it was right:** `len` and `func` are *values no row
varies*, but `reg != 0` is a **whole branch of the repair's own expression** — `odata = reg == 0?
(uint64_t) -1 : 0` — that nothing reached. Killing `M2_nullval` proves sensitivity to the
register-zero result and establishes nothing about the required zero elsewhere.

*** AND THAT THIRD ONE WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THIS ROUND'S OWN PRE-TABLE BLOCK. ***
`PRETABLE.out` section 2 says, in its own words: *"THE `zero elsewhere' HALF IS NOT ROWED …
DISCLOSED, not silently skipped … Coverage debt, clause (e)."* **A disclosure is an honest record and
it is not a row.** The seat found in one query what the round had identified hours earlier and
deferred — the unread-review shape aimed at a round's own artifact rather than at a seat's answer.

**grok and minimax landed after the panel was first read** (230 b and absent at that moment) and were
NOT scored as failures. grok's arrived as a **fourth shape on the same axis and a worse one**:
`if (type1 && bus == 0 && reg == 0)` hoists the test into the *guard*, so a non-zero register is not
refused at all but FORWARDED — reaching the real `i82378zb` at 0:7:0. Its warrant is what makes it
realistic: *"other registers already return 0 for a missing device"* — true at every empty slot,
**false at the one populated one**. Measured separately in `table4_targeted/`.

**Four rows added, 14 -> 18** (`t1 len4`, `t0 func4`, `t1 reg0`, `t1 reg4`), all L1 construction.
The register pair shares one session deliberately: a bare *"reg 4 returns 0"* row would be vacuous
because unmapped space also reads 0, so the PAIR is the oracle — all-ones then zero, same window,
only the register changing.

**DISPOSITION, stated rather than assumed.** None of the three is a floor breach under the
body-tested-partition reading: `lca_pci_conf` tests `writeflag` in its own code but never branches on
`len`, `func` or `reg`, so they induce no partition and fall to clause (e). **They were closed anyway
on the CLAIM -> ROW check**, because each falsifies a sentence the round's own comment asserts.

**TWO RESIDUALS ARE DISCLOSED AND NOT BUILT**, on grok's own reasoning: the WRITE direction at a
non-zero register, and any bus value other than 0 or 1 (a hardcoded `bus = 1` collapses the decode
but does not reach 0:7:0 — grok named it while declining to propose it, *"this one does not need that
row to be a defect"*). The detector ships with both named in its header, so a later escape is

# `#514` alphaswpctxreg: the OS's context-switch primitive returned its result in the register the ABI tells the caller to discard

**THE DEFECT, and it contradicts the comment directly above it.**  `cpu_alpha_palcode.c:250-251`:

    /*  Return old context in v0.  */
    cpu->cd.alpha.r[ALPHA_A0] = cpu->cd.alpha.ctx;

The third-party ABI wrapper settles the intent independently.  `alpha_pal_swpctx`
(`alpha_cpu.h:449-459`) declares `register unsigned long v0 __asm("$0")` as an **output**.

*** AND THIS PARAGRAPH FIRST SAID THE WRAPPER "LISTS a0 AMONG THE CLOBBERS".  IT DOES NOT, and a
pass-2 seat found it by reading the asm instead of the comment beside it. ***  The clobber list is
`"$1", "$22", "$23", "$24", "$25", "memory"` -- **a0 is `$16` and is not in it.**  a0 is an **IN-OUT
OPERAND**: `"=r" (a0)` as an output, with `"0" (a0)` tying the input to operand 0.  The wrapper's
own *comment* says *"clobbers t0, t8..t11, a0 (above)"*, and the **"(above)"** is doing the work --
it points at that operand.  **The conclusion is untouched** (the caller may not rely on a0 either
way) **and the reason was wrong, which is the half that gets reused.**  **So a correct caller reads the
result from `v0` and may not rely on `a0`: the model published into the register the caller is told
to throw away and left untouched the one it reads.**  A guest calling `ALPHA_SWPCTX()` gets whatever
`v0` happened to hold.

**THE FIX IS ONE IDENTIFIER** -- `ALPHA_A0` -> `ALPHA_V0` -- and six seats confirmed it is
*sufficient*, not merely correct.  **No `a0` write is added**: the architecture marks `a0`
UNPREDICTABLE after the call, and that definition explicitly permits a register to remain unchanged,
so nothing further is owed.  *An earlier draft of mine called `a0` "unobservable by construction";
codex refused that as too strong -- software CAN read `a0`, it simply cannot require a value.*

**THE WITNESS IS RUNG 3 AND IT WENT RED FIRST.**  `regress/alpha_swpctx_v0_probe.py`, on unmodified
`-E alpha -e alphabook1` with real `call_pal 0x30` instructions:

    PREFIX_20260908.out    2/4   measured on fc687db with the file UNMODIFIED
    POSTFIX_20260908.out   4/4   same script, after the one-identifier change

*** A NOTE ON THE FLOOR, because I named the wrong clause and four seats let it pass. ***  I
claimed clause **(d)** was discharged "by construction".  grok refused the NAME while accepting the
conclusion: **(d) enumerates the predicates DOMINATING the edited lines, plus operand swaps from a
GUARDED body.  This diff is a register-index substitution on an UNGUARDED assignment, so that
enumeration is EMPTY** -- and the two written special cases for "the fix adds no predicate"
(de-fatalisation, pure deletion) are neither.  `v0 = a0` is an **RHS COVERAGE** mutant, not a (d)
mutant.  **So (d) enumerated the empty set here, and the three-value oracle IS the coverage** --
recorded so the next one-identifier round does not inherit "by construction" as a floor discharge.

**THE ORACLE CARRIES THREE DISTINGUISHABLE VALUES, and that is what makes it more than a
value check.**  An old context `C = 0x01000000`, a new context `N = 0x01010000`, and a sentinel
`S = 0x00ab0000` seeded into `v0` immediately before the second call:

    v0 == C   correct                          <- what the row asserts
    v0 == S   the handler never wrote v0       <- the shipped defect, measured
    v0 == N   an INCORRECT repair returning the NEW context instead of the old

*A row asserting only "v0 changed" would pass that third case.*  The design is codex's, from the
pass-1 brief's Q4.

**AND THE ATTRIBUTION CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT A WITNESS RATHER THAN A READING.**  `a0 land` reads
`a0` after the second call.  Pre-fix it holds `C`, which proves **the handler RAN and wrote the
wrong register**; had the handler never executed, `a0` would still hold `N`.  One observation, two
hypotheses separated -- and both rows flipped together, 2/4 -> 4/4.

**PASS 1: SIX SEATS, UNANIMOUS on the fix, the severity (`med`) and the scope.**  codex, grok, glm,
kimi, deepseek and minimax.  `opus5` and `fable5` are HELD for the 2026-09-09 adjudication and `agy`
is the measurement reserve, so all three are recorded BY NAME as deliberate non-firings -- which is
neither a seat failure nor agreement.

*** THE PANEL CAUGHT A PREMISE I ASSERTED AND NEVER EXHIBITED, AND THREE SEATS FOUND IT
INDEPENDENTLY. ***  My brief said *"ordering in the handler is correct"* while showing only `:251`
and `:255`.  glm, kimi and minimax all refused to grant it, and kimi named the fork exactly: **if
`:255` read the REGISTER rather than a captured local, `:251` would clobber it and the live defect
would be "swpctx is a silent no-op"** -- a larger bug that the same one-token fix repairs.  Verified
by opening the file: `:165` is `uint64_t a0 = cpu->cd.alpha.r[ALPHA_A0], a1 = ...`, a local captured
at function entry, so the fork does not exist.  **The premise was true, and it was true by luck of
my having read it earlier rather than by anything the brief showed.**

*** MY CENSUS WAS TEXTUALLY RIGHT AND MISLEADING, AND TWO SEATS FOUND IT SEPARATELY. ***  I reported
EIGHT `ALPHA_V0` return sites.  Three -- `:306`, `:356`, `:383` -- are inside `#if 0`, and `:118` is
`alpha_prom_call`, not a PAL handler.  codex and grok arrived at the same corrected figure
independently: **five compiled assignments file-wide, four live PAL returns** (`rdmces`, `swpipl`,
`rdps`, `whami`).  *I grepped for textual presence and reported it as compiled code.*

**glm's triangulation point is the one worth keeping:** the verdict holds *even if both greps were
wrong*, because the comment, the code and the third-party wrapper agree independently.  **The census
was corroboration, never the load-bearing evidence** -- which is why an inflated count did not
change the answer.

**SCOPE, deliberately narrow:** the `// TODO: Don't invalidate EVERYTHING!` in the same arm is
**excluded** -- every seat called it a separate row, and the one-site rule governs.

*** AND THE COUPLING I CLAIMED TO `alphatbinegsel` DOES NOT FOLLOW.  Measured, not argued. ***  I
wrote that *"`#514` has now landed first, so that row owes a re-baselined witness"*, carrying
forward a pass-1 warning that whichever of the two landed second would need re-baselining.  **But
`#514` did not touch the flush at all:**

    git diff --format= 3031a30^ 3031a30 -- src/cpus/cpu_alpha_palcode.c \
        | grep -cE '^[+-].*invalidate_translation_caches'      ->  0

The `INVALIDATE_ALL` in this arm is untouched, and so are both arms of the `tbi` dispatch.  **So no
re-baseline debt was created and the claim is withdrawn** -- in this block, in `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md`
and in the flagship queue.  *The pass-1 warning was conditional on a round that MOVED the flush
observable; this round did not.  I applied its conclusion without re-checking its condition.*

# `#513` sgirekills: five modelled registers ended the host when read back -- and four adversarial passes, three of which found something

**THE DEFECT.**  `dev_sgi_re.c` carried SIX read arms of the form

    } else {
            fatal("TODO: read from CRIME_RE_TLB_A");
            exit(1);
    }

each on the `else` of a `writeflag == MEM_WRITE` test, inside a window whose WRITE path is fully
modelled.  **A guest could store to `CRIME_RE_TLB_A` and reading the same address back ended the
emulator** -- one `ld` on an unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32`.

**FIVE BECAME ACCEPT** -- option-set member 4, because the write arm directly above each one already
computes and stores the value, so nothing is unimplemented and a decline would have shipped a wrong
record in product code.  **`CRIME_RE_TEX` became a latched DECLINE** on its own bit: `sgitexindex`
records its write index as a missing factor of four, only 31 of 112 cells are reachable, `re_tex`
has NO consumer in the file, and that row carries a standing do-not-code ruling -- so accepting the
read would publish a mapping the project has already recorded as wrong.

**THE FIX HAD TO WRITE `odata`, NOT `data[]`.**  The common tail is
`if (writeflag == MEM_READ) memory_writemax64(cpu, data, len, odata);`, so a read arm filling
`data[]` is overwritten before the guest sees it.  A first draft did exactly that and **would have
returned zeroes while looking correct**; it is now mutant `M2_datafill`.

## THE ORACLE-CORRECTION ORDERING, run rather than asserted

Six shipped rows asserted that a len == 8 READ still ends the host.  The fix makes them false *by
succeeding*, so the rows were re-pinned FIRST and the committed build measured RED:

    committed build, re-pinned oracles   30/44        PREFIX_RED_20260908.out
    after the fix, SAME script           44/44       POSTFIX_20260908.out
    after the pass-2 repair, on build/   46/46        POSTFIX46_20260908.out

Every red row on the pre-fix run was a NEW row; all pre-existing rows and all three controls stayed
green.

## FOUR PASSES.  THE PANEL WAS RIGHT THREE TIMES AND I WAS WRONG THREE TIMES.

**PASS 1** refused my six-row design with two floor-shaped holes: an accept row at a window BASE
tests the near bound twice and the far bound never, and a load-only TEX decline row would have been
VACUOUS -- it wants `v0 == 0`, and a later ACCEPT of the zeroed array yields 0 too.  **Both were
then measured**: `M4_readshift` and `M7_farbound` are caught ONLY by the last-slot row, and would
have swept my design clean.

**PASS 2** found an L2 floor breach: aliasing the new latch onto `SGIRE_W_UNMAP_RD` escapes, because
no session read TEX and the unmapped address together.  Repaired with two same-instance rows in both
orderings.  **It also found three wrong records in text I had just written**, including the enum
"next free bit is 1 << 11" -- **which this file already records going false the same way for
`SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP`.  I repeated a documented failure while editing the enum that documents it.**

**PASS 3** found that repair closed ONE cell of FIVE: bits 6, 7, 9 and 10 are the same one-token
edit on the same line.  **My "#392, unbounded" objection was a strawman** -- the cover is LINEAR,
the edited latch against each other used bit.  Closed with one widened row, not four.

*** AND A READING SEAT THEN FOUND A LIVE BUG A GREEN 46/46 RUN HAD ENDORSED. ***  `store()` is
`store(A, addr, op=..., val=...)`; I wrote `store(A, DE_MODE_DST, MODE_LIN_B)`, so the VALUE became
the OPCODE.  Six calls, all wrong the same way -- **the row executed garbage and still scored 46/46,
because its only oracle was the TEX decline count.**  No mutant could have found it: every mutant is
scored against the same broken row.  Repaired twice over -- the calls fixed, AND the row made
SELF-CHECKING (it now wants `1/11`, so a silently-failing setup reds it).

**PASS 4** split 3-2 to close, and the surviving objection was kimi's: **only 2 of 11 aliases had a
logged kill against the FINAL row -- the other nine were carried across a row edit, which this
round own doctrine forbids.**  *"Close every cell in ONE diff" deserves "kill every cell on ONE
probe version."*  Hence the sweep below.

# `#512` pcc2c040kill: one legal guest byte store ended the host

**THE DEFECT.** `dev_pcc2.c`, `reassert_interrupts()`:

    if (d->pcctwo_reg[PCCTWO_GENCTL] & PCC2_C040) {
            fatal("pcc2: C040 interrupt assertions... TODO\n");
            exit(1);
    }

`PCCTWO_GENCTL` is offset 0x02, `PCC2_C040` is 0x04, and the GENCTL write arm stores `idata`
UNMASKED and then calls this helper **in the same access**.  So a single guest `st.b` of `0x04` on
an unmodified `-E mvme88k -e mvme187` terminated the emulator.  No driver, no second access, no
interrupt.

## WITNESS — rung 3, red before and green after with the SAME script

`regress/pcc2_c040_probe.py`.  Committed build **3/4**, the RED row being the defect; after the fix
**4/4**.  Artifacts `witness_HEAD_20260907.raw` and `witness_FIX512_20260907.raw`.

    c040 kill    died(exit1) -> alive     THE DEFECT
    EVIDENCE:    pcc2: C040 interrupt assertions... TODO

The witness carries a same-decode CONTROL (the identical `st.b` to the identical register with a
benign `0x10`, which must survive) and a SITE-ATTRIBUTION row.  Both were required by the grok seat,
which **refused the first design**: *"Survival-only, in pcc2_width_probe.py, with no same-decode
preset and no site-attribution, is not [a witness]."*

## THE FIX — and the site is not where the brief first put it

`reassert_interrupts()` is a void helper called from **ten** sites.  The kill was the FIRST thing in
it, so the repair is not in the GENCTL write arm.  **The file's own idiom for a GENCTL bit that
suppresses interrupt assertion sits seventy lines below the kill, in the same function** -- the
`PCC2_MIEN` test clears `assert` and falls through to the common tail.  The C040 test now sits
beside it, latched with the house `(once)` marker and a new `PCC2_W_C040` enumerator appended to the
existing warn-bit enum (appended at the END, so no existing bit renumbers).

**An early `return` at the old site would have been wrong** and four independent readers proposed
one: it skips `PCCTWO_IPL = 0`, the whole IPL recalculation, the `cur_int_vec[]` updates and the
`INTERRUPT_ASSERT`/`INTERRUPT_DEASSERT` tail.

## THE PRIMARY SOURCE SETTLED TWO QUESTIONS THE PANEL COULD NOT

The minimax seat held the round conditional on the bit value and named the missing artifact exactly:
*"One fact needed: an authoritative PCC2 GENCTL bit map."*  **`_scratchpad/vmesbcp2.txt` -- the
MVME187 board manual -- has been in this project since 2026-09-05, and the carrier says in terms to
open it for a PCC2/MVME187 round.  I had not.**

    ADR/SIZ  $FFF42002 (8 bits)
    DIR      15    14  13  12  11    10    9     8
    NAME     DR0                     C040  MIEN  FAST

Mapping the manual's word-view numbering to the byte (15->7, 10->2, 9->1, 8->0) gives
DR0/C040/MIEN/FAST = **0x80 / 0x04 / 0x02 / 0x01**, all four matching this fork's header.  So
OpenBSD's `mvme88k/include/pcctworeg.h`, which says `C040 0x03`, is a buggy overlapping mask
(`0x03 == FAST|MIEN`) and the fork follows the correct `dev/` header.

**And the same page settles the structure**: a set C040 sends the request *"via the EIPL\* pins **at
the level that is programmed ... in the SCSI Interrupt Control Register**"*, and the IPL register
page adds that IPL2-IPL0 *"always reflect the encoded request level"*.  **C040 selects the DELIVERY
PIN, not the level** -- so the recalculation must stay and only the assertion is suppressed.  MIEN,
by contrast, disables *"both the EIPL\* pins and the INT pin"*, which is why the two tests are
siblings gating one output rather than a nest.

*** PASS 2 THEN REFUSED THE ROUND'S RESPONSE TO ITS OWN GRADE, AND WAS RIGHT. ***  This block first
said *"THE ROUND DOES NOT CLAIM A FLOOR-MEETING DETECTOR"* and shipped, filing the repair.  grok:
*"1 and 2 cannot both stand … 2 is the (e) REMEDY applied to a (d) GRADE.  L2 says replace the

**TABLE 3** (11 rows), after `c040 noassert2`:   M_latchinside 10/11  KILLED

The five tables are kept SEPARATE because each names a different instrument.  Merging them would

*** THE REPAIR'S OWN PASS 2 REFUSED ITS CLOSURE CLAIM — THE SAME ERROR TWICE IN ONE ROUND. ***  I
declared the encounter axis closed on two cells.  The C040 block reads TWO device-state lvalues, so
their product is FOUR, and the empty cell — C040 CLEARED AFTER THE LATCH FIRED — was again filed as
contract debt.  **Four of six seats refused it**; the fifth defended it only conditionally and named
its own condition.  `c040 recover` holds that cell and kills `M_sticky`.

**`M_mienclobber` shows why the collateral row was owed:** `irq live` and `c040 noassert` BOTH stay
green under it — every delivery row passes a fix that suppresses by disabling all interrupts — and
only the GENCTL readback fails, reading `0x04` instead of `0x06`.  Three seats named that mutant
independently.

**And the substitute seat found what no other did:** the liveness control existed for ONE session of
FOUR, so `c040 noassert` reaching completion was consistent with "suppressed correctly" AND with
"no request was ever pending".  Three SCCTX readbacks close it.

**FOUR ROWS DID IT**, and the two design corrections that made them work came from the panel, not
from me:

* **`irq pending` / `irq live`** — a guest store to the CLMPCC IER asserts SCC TX synchronously,
  `pcctwo_interrupt_common` ORs `PCC2_IRQ_INT` into SCCTX, and with C040 CLEAR the interrupt IS
  delivered (pc = 0x8).  **Without the positive control, "no interrupt" is indistinguishable from
  "no request was ever created".**
* **`c040 noassert`** — the same sequence with C040 SET must reach COMPLETION.  **The precondition
  is what makes it work: both rows write MIEN-only GENCTL FIRST, so the line is ALREADY ASSERTED.**
  My first design wrote C040 into a reset GENCTL, leaving the line deasserted — and `return`, which
  merely preserves the incoming line state, would have PASSED.  *Found by a design review before a
  line was written.*
* **`c040 noassert2`** — the SECOND C040 encounter.  `assert = 0` moved inside the latch suppresses
  correctly the first time and skips it afterwards, so a single-encounter row scores 10/10 against
  it.  **Closing the ENCOUNTER AXIS beat adding a row per mutant** — the class-closure rule.

*** A CORRECTION TO THIS BLOCK'S OWN EARLIER TEXT. ***  It said the escape was *"not repairable in
this probe shape, verified two ways"*: that a guest cannot set an ICR INT bit, and that the bit's
only producer is a host-timer callback `step` stops.  **The first is true; the SECOND IS FALSE.**  A
guest store to a DIFFERENT DEVICE — the CLMPCC IER — sets it through the interrupt callback,
synchronously.  *I had checked which stores write the field and concluded no store can cause it to
change; those are different questions.*  The repair needed no new probe shape: `session()`'s
`(cmd, wait, until)` form already existed.

**THE ORACLE IS AFFIRMATIVE, NOT A TIMEOUT.**  Both outcomes stop at a breakpoint and the
discriminator is WHICH PC.  The two obvious oracles are both unusable and both were tried: the
`debug("[ pcc2: IPL … => %s ]")` line executes BEFORE the MIEN and C040 suppressions, so it is green
under the mutant it would be chosen to catch; and `("continue", grace, "GXemul>")` returns True with
ZERO READS, because `rd()` matches `until` against the whole accumulated buffer, which already holds
a prompt from the boot drain.

**RESIDUAL, disclosed under clause (e):** these rows establish delivery under one source, one
priority and two encounters.  They do not cover suppression that corrupts MASK/MIEN/pending state,
suppression that stays stuck after C040 clears, or other sources and priorities.  Note also that
suppression by a *different implementation route* is not a defect — the contract is behaviour, not
the use of a particular local variable.

# `#511` lcashiftub: `0x800 << dev` overflows a signed int on the last iteration

**THE DEFECT.** `dev_lca.c`, in `DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf)`'s device-scan loop:

    for (dev=0; dev<21; dev++)
            if (tag & (0x800 << dev))
                    break;

`0x800` is `2^11` and a plain `int`. At `dev == 20` the expression is `2^31`, which **overflows a
signed 32-bit int** — undefined by C99 6.5.7p4, not merely implementation-defined. Exactly one
iteration overflows; `0x800 << 19` is `0x40000000` and fits.

**THE FIX, one token:** `0x800U << dev`. The operand becomes `unsigned int`, so `2048U << 20` is
`0x80000000U` — inside range — and **nothing else moves**.

> ### *** THE REASON FIRST GIVEN HERE WAS FALSE, AND FOUR PASS-2 SEATS CAUGHT IT. ***
>
> This paragraph said *"`tag` is already a wider unsigned quantity"*. **`tag` is a plain signed
> `int`** (`dev_lca.c:92`: `int tag, bus, dev, func, reg;`). Worse, the claim was **backwards**:
> being *wider* is what would CREATE a difference, not remove one. Had `tag` been `uint64_t`, the
> old `int` `0x80000000` is NEGATIVE and would **sign-extend** to `0xffffffff80000000` for the `&`,
> while `0x800U << 20` **zero-extends** to `0x0000000080000000` — two different masks. glm stated it
> exactly; minimax, deepseek and the kimi substitute each independently refused to ratify the claim
> and named the declaration of `tag` as the settling fact.
>
> **WHAT ACTUALLY HOLDS:** both operands are 32 bits, so the `&` is performed at 32 bits either way
> — `int & int` before, and after, `tag` converted to `unsigned int` by the usual arithmetic
> conversions. **The result's bit pattern is identical**; only its type changes, and it is consumed
> solely as a truth test in `if (...)`. grok, having read the tree: *"The shift arithmetic is right
> and no defined iteration changes its truth value."*
>
> *A wrong reason attached to a right conclusion — and a wrong reason gets reused, which is why it
> is corrected here and in the product comment rather than quietly dropped.*

The emitted code on every compiler this project targets was already what was intended; the repair is
owed by the LANGUAGE, which is why no guest-visible value changes.

## WITNESS — rung 3, and the vehicle already existed

**No new apparatus was built.** `regress/lca_confbus_probe.py` was shipped earlier the same day as
the witness for a *different* row (`lcaconfbus1kill`). Its control read drives a guest `ldq` into
the PCI config window with `ioc_conf == 0`, which takes the `bus == 0` branch with `tag == 0` — so
the scan loop runs all 21 iterations and reaches the overflow **on every run**. Pointing that probe
at `build-asan/gxemul` instead of `build/gxemul` is the whole measurement.

    HEAD    dev_lca.c:125:21: runtime error: left shift of 2048 by 20 places
                              cannot be represented in type 'int'
            artifacts/lcashiftub/ubsan_HEAD_20260907.raw          1 diagnostic

    FIXED   (none)
            artifacts/lcashiftub/ubsan_FIXED_20260907.raw         0 diagnostics

**Same script, opposite outcome — clause (i) exactly.** And the control: the plain `build/` binary
scores `3/4` before and after, with the same three rows green and `bus kill` still RED, because that
is a different defect. **Nothing else moved.**

> ### *** THE ASAN SWEEP COULD NOT HAVE FOUND THIS, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL. ***
>
> `build-asan` has carried `-fsanitize=address,undefined` all along, and `gate_asan_sweep.sh` runs
> every machine type and subtype. But it runs them as
> `"$bin" -V -E "$t" -e "$s" "$DUMMY" </dev/null` — a **CONSTRUCTION** sweep. This shift lives in an
> **access path** that only a guest PCI config cycle reaches, and constructing `alphabook1` never
> executes it. *That is the witness ladder's own rung-2 limit one level down: registration proves
> presence, not reachability.*

> ### *** THE FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS A FALSE NEGATIVE OF MY OWN MAKING, and it is the more useful
> ### half of this round. ***
>
> Run 1 reported **no diagnostic** and I nearly filed that as a finding against `ubsanshiftlane` —
> that the ASAN build fails to report a shift UB it provably evaluates. The cause: **I grepped the
> PROBE's stdout, and a UBSAN message goes to the EMULATOR's stderr**, which lands in the probe's
> internal pty buffer and is never echoed.
>
> **That is the same defect this session had already fixed one level down** — a green row whose
> evidence never reaches the artifact — recurring on the *harness* rather than on a row.
>
> **A PROBE ONLY SHOWS WHAT IT CHOOSES TO PRINT. When looking for output the probe was not written
> to surface, DUMP THE BUFFER; do not grep the summary.** Re-run from a frozen copy in `/tmp` — the
> shipped probe is not edited for a measurement — and the diagnostic was in the first ten lines.
>
> *The wrong answer REASSURED: "no diagnostic" is exactly what a clean build looks like.*

## DETECTOR — stated honestly rather than claimed

The two-direction measurement above **is** the detector, and it is a UBSAN DIFFERENTIAL: a second
binary and a STDERR oracle rather than a value oracle. **It is not wired into a gate**, and wiring it
is `ubsanshiftlane`, filed separately because a new measurement lane added inside a fix round is a
lane nobody reviewed.

The alternative considered and rejected was a SOURCE PIN asserting the expression reads `0x800U`.
`#510`'s own product comments name a source pin as legitimate for this class ("No row can kill a
`1U` -> `1` regression; UBSAN or a source pin can"). It was rejected here because **the differential
already exists and is measured in both directions**, while a source pin would test the text rather
than the behaviour — and this round has the behaviour.

**So the honest statement is: this fix ships with a MEASURED two-direction differential and NO GATE
ROW.** A regression would be caught by `ubsanshiftlane` when that lands, and by nothing before then.

## The irony, which is the reason this site was worth reading twice

**The loop containing the UB is this file's own graceful-degradation PRECEDENT.** Its `dev >= 21` arm
has a commented-out `fatal()`/`exit(1)` with `dev = 0;` substituted, and `lcabadval` cites that very
loop as a transferable in-tree warrant for deleting a host kill. **The safe path contained the
undefined behaviour.**

## PASS 2 — the panel ratified the token and refused two of the round's claims

`_scratchpad/panel_20260907_221353`, preserved at `regress/artifacts/lcashiftub/pass2_c7d7414/`.
SEATS: codex, grok, glm, deepseek, minimax and the kimi-k3:cloud SUBSTITUTE answered (6); the kimi
CLI WALLED on its 403 weekly limit so that seat is COVERED, not lost; agy DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED
(measurement reserve); opus5 and fable5 NOT FIRED, reserved for the 2026-09-09 adjudication.

**grok's verdict:** *"RATIFY the `0x800U` token. DO NOT RATIFY the load-bearing type claim, and DO
NOT RATIFY 'the measurement is the detector.' The shift arithmetic is right and no defined iteration
changes its truth value. `tag` is a signed `int` … Two other PCI IDSEL scanners still evaluate
`1 << 31`."*

**1. The type claim — corrected above, in both places it appeared.**

**2. *** "THE MEASUREMENT IS THE DETECTOR" IS REFUSED, AND THE CORRECTION IS A CATEGORY ONE. ***
An unwired one-shot UBSAN run is a **WITNESS** — it shows the defect and shows it gone. A
**DETECTOR** defends against regression, and nothing here does: no gate runs it, so a future edit
reintroducing `0x800` is caught by nothing. This round's own text called it "the detector" while
also admitting no gate row exists; those two sentences cannot both stand. **It ships with a witness
and no detector**, and gate-wiring remains `ubsanshiftlane`.

**3. *** TWO SIBLINGS, AND MY SIBLING CENSUS'S FILTER IS WHAT HID THEM. ***

    dev_uninorth.c:70   for (dev=11; dev<32; dev++)  if (idata & (1 << dev))
    dev_v3.c:164        for (dev=24; dev<32; dev++)  if (relative_addr & (1 << dev))

Both reach `dev == 31`, so both evaluate `1 << 31` = `0x80000000` — the same signed overflow, in the
same PCI IDSEL-scanner idiom, in two more chipsets. **My census excluded literal `1` as "the
ordinary bitmask idiom".** That exclusion is exactly backwards: `1` has the MOST headroom and is
therefore the ONLY literal that overflows at the maximum shift a `< 32` loop produces. The absence
record it produced is retracted; both sites are filed to `shiftubcensus`.

**Note the repair may NOT transfer unchanged**: `#511`'s "nothing else moves" turned on `tag` being
a 32-bit `int`. `dev_uninorth.c` ands against `idata`, which in that handler is plausibly 64-bit —
**precisely the case where the old sign-extension and the new zero-extension differ.** Each site
needs its own type check.

# `#510` armbfxwidth32: UBFX and SBFX built their mask with an undefined shift

**THE DEFECT.** `cpu_arm_instr.c`. The decoder gives both handlers
`width = 1 + ((iword >> 16) & 31)` (`:4486`, `:4493`), so **`width` reaches 32** — and `1` is a
plain `int`:

    :1316  ubfx   uint32_t mask = (1 << width) - 1;
    :1340  sbfx   uint32_t mask = (1 << width) - 1;
    :1344  sbfx   uint32_t topBitMask = 1 << (width-1);

`1 << 32` shifts by the full width of the type (C99 6.5.7p3); `1 << 31` overflows a signed `int`
(6.5.7p4). Both are undefined. `UBFX rd, rn, #0, #32` is a legal A32 encoding — the architectural
constraint is `lsb + width <= 32`, which `lsb = 0, width = 32` satisfies — so this is
guest-reachable, not a decoder curiosity.

> ### *** ONLY THE WIDTH-32 CASE IS OBSERVABLE, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. ***
>
> Three pass-1 seats said the defect is "two widths wide". That is right about the LANGUAGE and
> needs a qualifier about the SYMPTOM. With `r1 = 0x89abcdef`:
>
>     width  correct       on the committed build   observable?
>     32     0x89abcdef    0x00000000               YES -- the whole register becomes zero
>     31     0x09abcdef    0x09abcdef               no  -- same answer
>
> **At 31 the expression is undefined TWICE and wraps back to the right answer:** `1 << 31` gives
> `INT_MIN`, and `INT_MIN - 1` gives `INT_MAX` = `0x7fffffff`, which IS the correct 31-bit mask.
> **The repair is owed by the language at both widths; only one of them was returning a wrong
> value**, and the round's severity sentence says so rather than claiming both.

**THE FIX**, at all three sites:

    uint32_t mask = (width == 32) ? 0xffffffffU : ((1U << width) - 1);

    if (width < 32 && (x & (1U << (width - 1))))       /*  sbfx, hoisted above the shift  */
            x |= ~mask;

**`1U` is load-bearing and not style: it is what defends width 31; the guard defends 32.** That
distinction was itself a correction — the round's own brief claimed the m88k idiom is safe because
of its GUARD, and three seats pointed out the CAST is what covers `w == 31` there.

At `sbfx`, the `width < 32` test that would have made `topBitMask` moot **sat on the line after
the shift that needed it**. Reordering the `&&` is semantically identical for every width in
`{1..32}` — both operands are ordinary locals with no side effects — and short-circuits before
the shift.

**THE FORK'S OWN IDIOM**, found by running the grep-the-fork step before writing the questions
rather than after: `cpu_m88k_instr.c:532` and `:539`, in `X(clr)` and `X(set)` —
`w == 0 ? 0xffffffff : ((uint32_t)1 << w) - 1`, where the m88k encoding spells full width as `0`.

**WITNESS, rung 3, unmodified `-E testarm`:** `regress/arm_bfx_width_probe.py`. A cold guest
plants one instruction word with `put w`, sets `pc`, steps once, and reads `r0` and `pc` back.

    HEAD  9/11   witness_HEAD_20260907.raw       FIX  11/11  witness_FIXED_20260907.raw
                                                    FIX  14/14  witness_FIXED14_20260907.raw

    *** A CITATION OF MINE DECAYED INSIDE ONE EVENING -- AND GIT GAVE IT BACK, WHICH IS THE
    PART WORTH KEEPING. ***  The follow-up re-ran the probe and MY DRIVER REUSED THE FILENAME
    `witness_FIXED12_20260907.raw' with a `>' redirect, so the working-tree copy stopped holding
    the 12-row run and held a 14-row one instead.  For about an hour this block cited a file that
    said something ELSE -- not unverifiable, but CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN EVIDENCE, which is the
    more detectable form and is how it was caught.

    **The artifact was COMMITTED, so `git checkout' restored it byte-for-byte and the 12/12 score
    is genuine and citable.**  All four numbers below stand on their own logs: 9/11, 11/11, 12/12
    and 14/14.  I first wrote this paragraph saying the measurement was GONE; that was wrong, and

    **The rule this vindicates is not the one I reached for.**  "A measurement cited in a durable

    s w32     0x0         0x89abcdef   0x89abcdef  SBFX #0,#32 -- pins the MASK, see pass 2
    w31       0x9abcdef   0x9abcdef    0x9abcdef   UB that WRAPS BACK to correct -- must STAY right
    mid       0xde        0xde         0xde        small NONZERO anchor
    s clear   --          0x7          0x7         ADDED BY PASS 2: top bit CLEAR, must not extend
    s w31     --          0x9abcdef    0x9abcdef   ADDED BY PASS 2: SBFX at width 31 was UNTESTED
    pc adv    0x8004      0x8004       0x8004      MOV control
    mid pc    0x8004      0x8004       0x8004      UBFX control
    w32 pc    0x8004      0x8004       0x8004      UBFX control AT the failing width
    s w32 pc  --          0x8004       0x8004      ADDED BY PASS 2: the FIRST SBFX pc control

> ### THE pc CONTROLS ARE LOAD-BEARING, AND THE REASON IS THIS ROUND'S OWN SYMPTOM.
>
> The width-32 failure returns **exactly zero** — indistinguishable from a mis-encoded word that
> never executed. This project has been bitten four times by hand-assembled encodings, once in a
> COMMITTED gate row that measured the wrong register for months. A `pc == CODE+4` row proves the
> instruction EXECUTED and returned a wrong value; `mid = 0xde` is a second, independent anchor
> that only a correct encoding AND execution can produce.
>
> ### *** AND THE SENTENCE THAT USED TO SIT HERE WAS FALSE, IN THIS BLOCK, IN THE PROBE COMMENT
> ### AND IN COMMIT `c0c7f55`'s MESSAGE, WHICH CANNOT BE EDITED. ***
>
> All three said the pc control holds **"on EVERY row, w32 included"**. It did not. Only `pc adv`,
> `mid pc` and `w32 pc` asserted pc, and **all three are MOV or UBFX rows — NO SBFX ROW CHECKED pc
> AT ALL.** The SBFX rows are precisely the ones whose expected failure value is *also* exactly
> zero, so they are the case the pc control exists to disambiguate, and they were the case it did
> not cover. `s w32 pc` closes it.
>
> **The failure was one of TIMING, not of knowledge**: the codex pass-2 seat named it, and its body
> was read after the commit had launched. That is this project's own rule about verdict lines
> landing on itself — *a verdict line is written against the brief's framing and is the LEAST
> likely part of an answer to carry a correction*, so the correction was in the body, and the body
> is the part that waited. **A commit message cannot be amended; this block and the probe comment
> ARE the record.**
>
> **A second, quieter gap went with it.** `s w31` did not exist either, so the round's headline
> claim — *"only the width-32 case is observable"* — rested on a UBFX width-31 row and was
> generalised to SBFX with no evidence for it. Both rows now exist and both are green.
>
> **And the encodings are DERIVED from the decoder, not recalled.** Field positions read out of
> `X(to_be_translated)`: `rd = (iword>>12)&15`, and **the source is `rm` = `iword & 15`, NOT
> `rn`** — `rn`'s bits 19:16 are occupied by `widthm1`, which is exactly why the ubfx block takes
> `rm`. Every planted word is checked against the decoder's own mask `0x0fe00070` by an `enc ok`
> row before anything runs.

## WHAT THIS ROUND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FIX

The round-scope rule takes ONE site, and a second joins only if it is WITNESSED, in the same
semantic class, and covered by the SAME detector with no new oracle. Three sites qualify. These
do not, each for a stated reason:

* **`bfi` (`:1409`) — the same expression, in the same file, left alone.** Its
  `width = msb - lsb + 1` takes `msb` and `lsb` from INDEPENDENT five-bit fields, so it spans
  **-30..32**. **465 of the 1024 (msb, lsb) pairs give a strictly NEGATIVE shift count**, undefined by the same clause as the count-too-large case (C99 6.5.7p3), and a further **31 give width exactly 0**, where `1 << 0` is DEFINED but the mask becomes 0 -- semantically wrong rather than undefined. **496 is the `msb < lsb` population, i.e. width <= 0, and an earlier draft of this record used it for the NEGATIVE count. Corrected 2026-09-07 after the pass-2 glm seat enumerated it from the brief's own width formula.** ARM calls `msb < lsb` UNPREDICTABLE. **No seat could settle from the tree what the model
  should do there** — the fork answers that class inconsistently (`cpu_arm_instr_loadstore.c:204`
  picks a defined result for an UNPREDICTABLE halfword load, while `#312`'s own comment argues
  AGAINST halting) — **and the obvious route is wrong as written: `X(und)` expects `arg[0]` to
  hold a PC OFFSET and `bfi`'s holds a REGISTER POINTER.** That is a design question for the
  flagship adjudication, not for whoever writes the diff.
* **`:2685` / `:2823`** — `is_userpage[index >> 5] & (1 << (index & 31))`, reaching `1 << 31`.
  A different semantic class and no row here.
* **`cpu_m88k_instr.c:513`** (`m88k_rot`, `(1 << n) - 1` with `n ∈ {1..31}`) and
  **`cpu_mips_instr.c:1757`** (MIPS `X(ext)`, `(rs << (32-lsb-size))` where that count spans
  `-31..31`) — different CPUs. Both READING findings, neither measured.

> **The m88k one is the sharpest thing the fix-check produced, and it weakens this round's own
> warrant:** `cpu_m88k_instr.c` is the file cited above as carrying the SAFE idiom, at `:532` and
> `:539`. **`:513`, twenty lines up, is the unsafe form.** One file, two neighbouring functions,
> opposite outcomes. *"The fork already knows how to do this" is a weaker warrant than it sounds
> when the same file contains both answers.*

**Site count is EIGHT across three CPUs, in three UB regions** (count >= width, `1 << 31` signed
overflow, negative count). This round closes three.

## Pass 2 ratified the repair and refused the comments

`panel_20260907_192452`, six seats. **grok's verdict: RATIFY THE REPAIR; DO NOT RATIFY THE
COMMENTS, THE "11/11 PINS BOTH HALVES" READING, OR THE 496-COUNT.** All four packet-fed seats
independently confirmed the mask is correct at 1, 31 and 32 and that the `&&` reorder changes no
guest value.

*** THREE ONE-LINE ESCAPES, AND THE VALUABLE PART IS WHY TWO OF THEM CANNOT BE CLOSED. ***

| escape | why it survived a full score |
|---|---|
| `1U` -> `1` in the ternary | `w31` stays green — **it is the very wrap this round's own comment describes** — and `w32` never evaluates the shift. `1 << 31` and `1U << 31` give the SAME mask after the `- 1`. |
| restore `topBitMask` above the `if` | `s w32` stays green: with a correct 32-bit mask `x \|= ~mask` is `x \|= 0`. **`s w32` pins the MASK, not `topBitMask` and not the hoist** — the probe comment calling it "the second-UB row" was wrong about what that row can see. |
| `if (width < 32)` with no bit test | `s mid` stays green because **every byte field of `0x89abcdef` has bit 7 set** (`0x89 0xab 0xcd 0xef`). No row had an SBFX field with the top bit CLEAR. |

**The third is closed in-round** by `s clear` — `SBFX #1,#4` gives field `0x7`, bit 3 clear, so a
correct build returns `0x7` and an always-extend regression returns `0xfffffff7`.

**The first two are DISCLOSED, because they are unkillable by a guest-value row on principle:**
both are DEFINEDNESS repairs, and definedness has no guest-visible value on a non-trapping host.
*** THEY ARE NOT UNKILLABLE IN PRINCIPLE: `build-asan` carries `-fsanitize=address,undefined`, so
a UBSAN DIFFERENTIAL pins both — fixed source produces no shift diagnostic, the `1U`->`1` mutant
produces one. That is a second binary and a STDERR oracle, i.e. a new measurement lane, so it is
filed as `ubsanshiftlane` for its own round rather than bolted onto one whose pass 2 has run. ***

**AND ONE CLAIMED BREACH WAS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT.** glm asserted *"no row ever takes the
sign-extension branch, so deleting `x |= ~mask` still scores 11/11."* The mutant was built with a
pre-registered prediction and measured **10/11, killed by `s mid` alone** — `s mid`'s field is
`0xde`, whose bit 7 IS set, so the branch is taken. Restore verified, sentinel cleared.

### Five comment overclaims, corrected in place

1. *"the mask became 0"* and *"`1 << 31` gives INT_MIN"* — these are **this host's lowering**
   (`shl` takes its count mod 32), not C99 values. Undefined behaviour has no defined result to
   measure. The rows observe the RESULT REGISTER, never the mask.
2. The `sbfx` block was a **verbatim copy of the ubfx one** and quoted a UBFX measurement — a
   sentence about the other function.
3. *"the `&&` reorder is semantically identical"* **understates it.** The old form computed
   `1 << (width-1)` as a PRIOR STATEMENT, and a guard never rescues an expression already
   evaluated. The guest value is identical; DEFINEDNESS at 32 is not. **And with `1U` the shift is
   already defined at 32, so the hoist is load-bearing for a signed `1` and redundant for `1U` —
   calling them equivalent defences was wrong.**
4. *"there is no sign to extend"* at width 32 is the wrong reason — a 32-bit field HAS a sign bit;
   the body is a no-op because `~mask == 0`.
5. **The 496 count** — see below.

### The count was wrong, and two seats caught it independently

This round claimed *"496 of 1024 encodings give a NEGATIVE shift count"* for `bfi`. Enumerated:

    width < 0   465      width == 0   31      width <= 0   496      msb < lsb   496

**496 is the `msb < lsb` population.** 465 are strictly negative; the other 31 give width exactly
0, where `1 << 0` is DEFINED and the mask becomes 0 — semantically wrong, not undefined. glm
derived it from the brief's own width formula and grok reached it separately. *The conclusion is
unchanged; the number was wrong, and it had already propagated into four records.*

grok: the brief's decoder cites `:4486`/`:4493` were the PRE-comment numbers; after the diff they

# `#509` sgimtedepth4dead: a bit-count compared against a byte-count, so the branch never ran

> **LATE-DISSENT DISPOSITION 2, 2026-09-09: MEASURED FALSE PASS against this detector's floor.** The round disclosed the B/C labels under clause (e); the 7g-1 adjudication ruled them FLOOR (the selector flows into the operand the repair reads), after the Opus seat measured `&& dst_tlb == MTE_TLB_A` at 14/14 against a 14/14 base with the closed defect live at B and C (`regress/artifacts/sgimtedepth4dead/killtable3_20260909/`). Repair owed as L2 in a follow-up commit under this number, carried by `sgimtelabelcells`. The record above is left as written; this line is so no reader sees false closure.

**THE DEFECT.** `dev_sgi_re.c`, `do_mte_transfer()`, in the block shared by the `MTE_TLB_A/B/C`
case labels:

    int depth = 8 << ((mode & MTE_MODE_DEPTH_MASK) >> MTE_DEPTH_SHIFT);   /* BITS */
    ...
            x1 /= (depth / 8);          /* the author converting bits -> bytes, correctly */
    ...
            // this makes sure that we copy 32 bits when doing 32-bit transfers.
            if (depth == 4) {           /* ... and comparing against the BYTE count */

`MTE_MODE_DEPTH_MASK` is `0x300` and `MTE_DEPTH_SHIFT` is 8, so the field is two bits and `depth`
takes **only** 8, 16, 32 or 64. **`depth == 4` is unreachable.** Both `|= DE_MODE_TYPE_RGBA`
assignments were therefore dead, every tiled MTE transfer took the `DE_MODE_TYPE_CI` arm — and at
32 bits that arm assigns `buf[0]` alone while `memory_rw` copies **four** bytes from a
`uint8_t buf[8]` that has no initialiser. **Three bytes of host stack per pixel reached guest
memory**, and the pixel's colour was the wrong byte of the background register.

**THE FIX is one token**, and the comment above it already stated the intended condition in words:

    if (depth == 32) {	/*  #509  */

**WITNESS, rung 3, unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32`:** `regress/sgi_mte_fill_probe.py`. A cold guest
programs one RE tile-table entry and the MTE mode/background/destination registers with real `sw`
and `sd` instructions, the last write carrying the transfer-start address bit, then reads the
destination back with a real `lw`. Background `0x11223344` — four distinct bytes, so the
destination's first byte names which colour arm ran.

    6-row witness    HEAD  5/6    witness_prefix_HEAD.raw    fill top got 0x44, want 0x11
    14-row detector  FIX  14/14   killtable2_20260907/BASE.raw
    14-row detector  HEAD 10/14   killtable2_20260907/M1_reinstate.raw

`M1` is the verbatim reinstatement of the removed comparison, so it re-measures the pre-fix state
at a durable path rather than leaving that score in a terminal.

Three of the eight mutants below were **total escapes** against the row set the round proposed.

|---|---|---|
| `fill bot` | pass-1 glm and grok | `dst_mode \|= DE_MODE_TYPE_RGB`. The RGB arm writes `{bg>>24, bg>>16, bg>>8, 0x00}` — **identical to RGBA at dest[0]**, different at dest[3]. Invisible to any first-byte oracle. |

| `copy 4th` | the PRE-TABLE CHECK | `src_mode \|= DE_MODE_TYPE_RGB`. RGB's GET drops only the LOW byte, so dest[0] and dest[1] are unchanged. |

**`copy top` and `copy 2nd` exist because a FILL never reads `src_mode`** — deleting only

deterministically and naming its own reason** instead of scoring an undefined byte. *No precedent
for a gated row was found in this tree; it is raised for the flagship adjudication rather than
asserted as settled.*

**The copy rows use source word `0x1a2b3c4d`, first byte deliberately below `0x80`,** because every

A detector must not stand on undefined behaviour.

## What pass 2 corrected, beyond the breach

**M4 is clause (e), not (d)** — grok's reading, verified here by opening the file. DEPENDS-ON
enumerates the predicates DOMINATING the edited line plus the lvalues the GUARDED BODY reads. That
body is exactly `src_mode |= ...; dst_mode |= ...` and never reads `MTE_MODE_COPY`, which is tested
later in the transfer loop. **Filing M4 as (d) would import its dual into the FLOOR** — and that
dual, `if (depth == 32 && !(mode & MTE_MODE_COPY))`, is a cell this instrument provably cannot
kill: every fill row stays green, `copy top` stays green because `dest[0]` of a same-type copy is
invariant, and the gate OPENS so the tail rows would score bytes a CI-CI PUT never wrote.
Disclosed as clause-(e) debt.

**Three wrong records in the round's own comments**, each found by a seat:

* *"every GET arm computes `buf[0] << 24`"* — **false.** CI shifts nothing; ABGR and the default
  arm shift `buf[3]`. Four of five arms, two of them a different byte. The pre-existing
  `sgirebufshiftub` row's own TITLE carried the same overclaim and is corrected there too.
* *"`depth8 top` reds if the comparison became `!= 8`"* — **false.** `!= 8` is FALSE at depth 8, so
  the branch stays cold and the row is green. **`>= 16` and `!= 8` agree on all four reachable
  depths — they are EQUIVALENT MUTANTS.** *Table 1 had already shown it: M7 was killed by
  `depth16 top` ALONE, one red and not two. The score was read and the row list was not.*
* The header banner still called a 14-row detector *"a witness, expected to FAIL, must not be
  gated"* — true of the 6-row version against HEAD, stale now.

**And the gate flag was renamed `rgba_ran` -> `fill_top_ok`**, because `fill dest[0] == 0x11` is
produced by the RGB arm as well as by RGBA. The flag means *the fill PUT put `bg>>24` at dest[0]*,
not *RGBA specifically ran*; `fill bot` is the row that separates those. A flag whose name
overclaims is how a future reader builds on a fact nobody has.

**One seat's finding was REFUTED by measurement, and one seat's remedy rejected on another seat's:**
glm claimed M3's copy kills "rest on undefined bytes" — under M3 the PUT is RGBA, which writes all
four, and the log shows the defined `0x00`/`0x1a`. deepseek proposed gating the copy rows on
`copy dest[0] == 0x1a`; grok's byte-walk shows that is **vacuous**, since `0x1a` is what BOTH CI-CI
and RGBA-RGBA produce — the gate would always be open, including pre-fix, and the rows would then
score exactly the host stack the gate exists to avoid.

*Both of those seats' errors trace to one ambiguous sentence in the round's own pass-2 brief, which
described the gate as per-row when it is a single shared flag. Two seats recovered the true reading
from `BASE 13/13` alone; two did not. That is a brief defect, not a seat failure.*

The same underlying defect — the CI arm assigning fewer bytes than the transfer copies — is live at

only, and by a different mechanism: it selects a type that assigns four.

> **THE TRAP, named by the pass-1 grok seat and kept in its own words: `#509` fills `buf[0..3]` at
> depth 32, so it ACCIDENTALLY MASKS the 32-bit tiled cell of `sgirebufuninit`. A later round that
> rows only depth 32 on this path WILL LOOK FIXED AND WILL NOT BE. Keep that sibling alive on depth
> 16.**

**So this round does NOT claim the uninitialised-buffer leak is closed**, and `depth16 top` is the
row that keeps the claim honest: if a later edit silently changed the 16-bit cell, it reds.

**Also disclosed rather than rowed:** `MTE_TLB_B` and `MTE_TLB_C` — a repair conditioned on
`dst_tlb == MTE_TLB_A` escapes this detector. Pass 1 **split** on it: codex enumerated 72 admitted
field combinations and called B/C uncovered; grok held that the comparison does not read `dst_tlb`,
so a per-label row would pin the helper's array selection — a different property — and called it
"cheap, not required". *The round adopted grok, i.e. the cheaper reading, over the seat that had
enumerated the space, and that call is queued for the flagship adjudication rather than settled
here.* The LINEAR arm, the `dst_tlb` default arm and `sgirebufshiftub` are out of scope and named
in `PRETABLE.out`.

**And the warrant for RGBA over RGB is CODE INTENT, not a datasheet.** Raised by the minimax seat
and verified: `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` lists sixteen manuals and **none for SGI/CRIME**. The basis is
the dead branch's own choice plus the comment — "copy 32 bits", which RGB's zero-padded low byte

# `#508` alphapfnoffset: the Alpha page-table walk returned a page BASE, dropping the offset

**THE DEFECT.** `memory_alpha.c`, after the third-level PTE validates:

    (*return_paddr) = ALPHA_PTE_TO_PFN(pte3) << pageSizeShift;

`memory_rw.c` then takes `offset = paddr & offset_mask`, which is therefore **always zero** — so every
walked access FILLED ITS TRANSLATION FROM the page's first bytes — *not* "resolved to", which is
the L4 the retrospective pass 2 on this commit found: the Alpha fast path recomputes `addr & 8191`
itself, so a subsequent cache HIT reads correctly and the corruption is the SLOW-PATH FILL. A
codex reachability pass enumerated all 8192
offsets: the walk yields offset zero throughout, differing from the offset-preserving address for
**8191** of them.

**WITNESS, rung 3, unmodified `-E alpha -e alphabook1`:** `regress/alpha_pfnoffset_probe.py`.
**HEAD 5/7** (`probe_head7_20260907.out`), **fix 7/7, same script** (`probe_fix_20260907.out`).
A cold guest `ldq` through a hand-built three-level page table:

| row | HEAD | fix | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `walk off` | `0xaaaa0000aaaa` | `0xbbbb0000bbbb` | `vaddr+8` must return `data+8`, not `data+0` |
| `walk vpn` | `0xcccc0000cccc` | `0xdddd0000dddd` | non-zero VPN, offset in the upper 4 KB |
| five controls | ok | ok | two K0SEG reads, `wasn't found` absent, sentinel, not-unmapped |

**THE SECOND ROW EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIX REVIEW REFUSED THE ROUND WITHOUT IT.** With `VADDR = 0` and
`N = 8`, **six lesser edits also score a clean sweep**: masks `0xfff`, `0x3fff`, `0x7fff`, any mask
including bit 3, a hardcoded `| 8`, and **unmasked `+ vaddr`** — the last correct only because the VPN
is zero on page 0. `walk vpn` kills the three that matter.

> ### *** THIS PARAGRAPH WAS ARITHMETICALLY FALSE AND IS CORRECTED, 2026-09-07, BY THE RETROSPECTIVE
> ### PASS 2 ON THIS COMMIT — which the pre-commit gate demanded because the round shipped without one. ***
>
> It read: *"AND TWO OF THE SIX ARE DELIBERATELY NOT KILLED. `0x3fff` and `0x7fff` are equivalent
> inside an 8 KB page — bits 13 and 14 of an offset are always zero there — so no row can distinguish
> them and none pretends to."*
>
> **The premise is about an OFFSET; the expression masks the FULL VIRTUAL ADDRESS.** That is true of
> `walk off`, whose `VADDR = 0` keeps every candidate mask inside the first page — which is where the
> sentence came from. It is **false of `walk vpn`**, which exists precisely to leave that page:

>     walk vpn drives vaddr = VADDR2 + N2 = 0x3008
>       mask 0x0fff -> 0x0008      mask 0x1fff -> 0x1008   (correct)
>       mask 0x3fff -> 0x3008      mask 0x7fff -> 0x3008
>
> The two wider masks equal **each other** and **both differ from the correct `0x1008`** — bit 13 is
> set, so `base | 0x3008` lands in the NEXT 8 KB page, which nothing planted. **`walk vpn` kills all
> four lesser masks, not three.**
>
> *So the sentence generalised a property of ROW 1 to the whole probe, in the very paragraph
> explaining why ROW 2 had to exist.* The correction makes the detector STRONGER than it claimed —
> the safe direction to be wrong in, and still a wrong record. **NOT separately measured:** no mutant
> was built for either mask; the arithmetic is the warrant, and unlike the survival the old sentence
> asserted, it is checkable by reading.

**A THREE-WAY PLANT MAKES THE ROW DIAGNOSTIC RATHER THAN MERELY RED:** `VAL_B2` at `data2+0x1008` is
correct, `VAL_C2` at `data2+8` is what a `0xfff` mask or a hardcoded `| 8` reads, `VAL_A2` at
`data2+0` is a page-base result. HEAD read **`VAL_A2`**, naming the defect exactly.

**THE FORM OF THE FIX, and every clause of it was argued rather than assumed:**

    (*return_paddr) = (ALPHA_PTE_TO_PFN(pte3) << pageSizeShift)
        | (vaddr & ((1ULL << pageSizeShift) - 1));

* **`|`, not `+`** — numerically identical here (the shifted PFN has bits 12:0 clear), but `|` is what
  every other walk in this tree writes (ARM, m88k, MIPS, PPC, SH), while `+` is this function's own
  *fixed* bootstrap windows. Different sentences.
* **the mask derived from `pageSizeShift`, never a literal.** `:88`'s `0x1fff` is correct for a fixed
  8 KB PROM pocket; beside `<< pageSizeShift` it is how a mask and its shift drift — and **this
  function already carries two names for 13** (`ALPHA_PAGESHIFT` and the local `pageSizeShift`).
* **the parentheses are load-bearing:** `1 << pageSizeShift - 1` is `0x1000`, not `0x1fff`. *The
  existing `N = 8` row already kills that one* (`8 & 0x1000 == 0`).

**A THIRD CONSUMER, found by enumerating the callers rather than assuming one.** `translate_v2p` is
called from three places: `memory_rw.c` (needs the full address — the defect), `cpu_dyntrans.c`
I-fetch (tolerates either; strips the offset itself), and **`debugger_cmds.c` watchpoints, which take
the address directly — so a walked watchpoint has been landing at the page base too.** No caller adds
its own offset, so the mirror defect is absent and the post-fix sweep is not hiding a double-add.

**THE `// TODO.` STAYS, and the round says why.** Restoring the offset leaves it true: `flags` is
never read (`FLAG_WRITEFLAG`, `FLAG_INSTR`, `FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS` all ignored), `ALPHA_PTE_KR/KW/UR/UW`
and `FAULT_ON_*` are untested, granularity hints are ignored, and **`return 2` means writable — so
`memory_rw` caches every walked Alpha page as writable.** *Deleting the comment would record the
translator as finished. It is not.*

**Trees:** `memory_alpha.c` is not in `tools/est_divergence.txt`, so it is shared and landed
byte-identical in all four. `build/`, `build-asan/` and `/tmp/gxsec-build` rebuilt; two-part clearance
CLEAN/FRESH on all three, `est/` part 2 N/A.

# `#507` alphaswpctxptbr: `swpctx` assigned `apcb_ptbr` twice and `apcb_flags` never

**THE DEFECT.** `cpu_alpha_palcode.c`, `case 0x30` PAL_OSF1_swpctx, load-new-context block:

    :278    cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_ptbr    = new_ptbr;
    :282    cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_ptbr    = new_flags;      <-- apcb_ptbr, again

A field-name transposition. The value is loaded correctly — the SAVE stores `apcb_flags` to
`ctx + 40` and the loader reads `new_flags` from `ctx + 40` — and lands on the wrong left-hand side.

**FOUND BY COUNTING, NOT BY READING.** Over the block, `apcb_ptbr` is assigned **twice**,
`apcb_flags` **zero** times, every other field exactly once. Reading it, `:282` looks like an ordinary
assignment in a column of ordinary assignments and the eye supplies the field name it expects; a
one-line census makes the 2-and-0 unmissable. **The same census is the fix's verification:**

    before   apcb_ptbr 2   apcb_flags 0     (every other field 1)
    after    apcb_ptbr 1   apcb_flags 1     (every field exactly 1)

*The block's own comment at `:275` reads "Update all variables in the pcb simultaneously" — directly
above the list that fails to. A claim of completeness is the least-checked line in a block, because
it reads as a description of the code beneath it.*

**THREE CONSEQUENCES, and the row originally recorded one.**
1. `apcb_ptbr` ends up holding the flags word — the clobber the witness first measured.
2. `apcb_flags` is never loaded **by `swpctx`**, so the incoming context's flags are dropped. (It is
   not unwritten in general: `wrfen` at `:221` assigns the field, so the in-cpu value is whatever
   the last `wrfen` left, or 0 from the zeroed cpu struct.)
3. **The SAVE then publishes that stale word into the OUTGOING PCB.** *The bug propagates outward
   into guest memory, not only inward into the cpu struct.* It does not necessarily publish ZERO,
   and whether it changes the planted word depends on any intervening `wrfen`.

**WITNESS, rung 3, unmodified `-E alpha -e alphabook1`:** `regress/alpha_harness_probe.py`.
**HEAD 7/10** (`probe_head10_20260907.out`), **fix 10/10, same script** (`probe_fix_20260907.out`):

| row | HEAD | fix | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `swpctx ptbr` | `0xbbbb2222` | `0xaaaa1111` | `PCB_A+16` must hold A.ptbr |
| `swpctx notflags` | `0xbbbb2222` | `0xaaaa1111` | the defect's exact signature |
| `swpctx flags` | **`0x0`** | **`0xbbbb2222`** | `PCB_A+40` must hold A.flags |
| six controls | ok | ok | encoder, live, exec, palgate, swpctx alive, swpctx mapped |

> ### *** THE THIRD ROW EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIX REVIEW REFUSED TO RATIFY THE ROUND WITHOUT IT. ***
>
> grok ratified the one-token product fix and then declined to call it the round: *"Both red rows read
> the same `got`: `A+16`. A build that only stops clobbering PTBR — delete `:282`, or assign
> `new_flags` to any other field — also scores 9/9. **Consequence 2 is unpinned.**"*
>
> That is a clause-(d) gap in the WITNESS rather than in the fix, and the repair it named cost one
> readback on a page `swpctx mapped` had already proved was backed: `A+40` is `0` on HEAD (a save of a
> never-loaded field) and `FLAGS_VAL` after. **Three red rows now pin three distinct consequences
> instead of one cell read twice.**

**NO READER RELIES ON THE STALE FIELD.** Every `apcb_flags` site in `src/` was enumerated: `wrfen`
`:221` writes the whole word without reading it; `:222-223` publishes what it just stored; the SAVE at
`:243-244` publishes to the outgoing PCB (which today propagates the bug and after the fix carries the
loaded value — the PAL contract); `ALPHA_PCB_FLAGS_FEN`, `_PME` and `ALPHA_IF_CODE_FEN` are header-only
and unused; `memory_alpha.c:46` reads `apcb_ptbr`, not flags. *Sticky-FEN-across-`swpctx` is a PAL bug,
not a behaviour a reader is entitled to.*

**TWO PREMISES OF MINE CORRECTED BY THE REVIEW**, both in the direction of less confidence:
`apcb_flags` **is** written globally (by `wrfen`), so "never assigned at all" holds only inside the
load block; and the in-cpu value is **last `wrfen` or 0 from the zeroed cpu struct**, not "whatever
the previous context left" — `swpctx` has never loaded that field from any PCB.

**FILED IN PASSING, not fixed here:** `PAL_clrfen` (`0xae`) is named and user-mode-whitelisted but has
**no `case`**, so it reaches the default arm and stops the CPU.

**Trees:** `cpu_alpha_palcode.c` is not in `tools/est_divergence.txt`, so it is shared and landed
byte-identical in all four. `build/`, `build-asan/` and `/tmp/gxsec-build` rebuilt; two-part clearance
CLEAN/FRESH on all three, `est/` part 2 N/A (source tree — inapplicable, not unrun).

# `#506` lcaconfwidth: the LCA kill diagnostic named a value the guard ACCEPTS

**THE DEFECT.** `dev_lca.c`'s `LCA_IOC_CONF` write arm stores the full 64-bit value, guards on all 64
bits, and reports 32:

    d->ioc_conf = idata;                              /* the FULL value is stored */
    if (idata & ~1) {                                 /* the guard sees 64 bits   */
            fatal("TODO: Write to unimplemented bit of"
                " IOC_CONF: 0x%x\n", (int)idata);      /* the message sees 32     */
            exit(1);
    }

A guest `stq` of `0x100000000` sets bit 32. `idata & ~1` is true, so the process dies — and
`(int)idata` is **0**, which is a value this same guard **accepts**. *The kill message named an
acceptable value while killing on an unacceptable one*, in the one place a wrong record is hardest to
recover from: the process is gone and the log is all that is left.

**WITNESS, rung 3, on an unmodified `-E alpha -e alphabook1`:** `regress/lca_confwidth_probe.py`.
**HEAD 4/6** (`regress/artifacts/lcaconfwidth/probe_head_20260907.out`), **fix 6/6, same script**
(`probe_fix_20260907.out`) — clause (i) satisfied by the pair, not by argument:

| row | HEAD | fix | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `live` | alive | alive | control: the session survives the legal write |
| `ioc rt` | `0x1` | `0x1` | control: guest `stq 0x1` then guest `ldq`, SAME decode |
| `kill fired` | yes | yes | control: the IOC_CONF arm announced — not HAE, not unmapped |
| `kill width` | **`0x0`** | **`0x100000000`** | the message must name the value that ACTUALLY killed |
| `kill notzero` | **`0x0`** | wider | `0x0` is a value this guard ACCEPTS |
| `died` | died | died | control: `exit(1)` really ran |

**THE FIX IS THE FILE'S OWN SIBLINGS, COPIED.** `TB_ENA`, `W_BASE0`, `W_MASK0`, `W_BASE1` and
`W_MASK1` — twelve to ninety lines away — already print `0x%" PRIx64` with `(uint64_t)idata`. This arm
was the outlier **among the value-guard diagnostics** -- not the file's only narrowing site, since the
`default:` arm carried the same cast and this round fixes it too. `PRIx64` already resolved in the file
(5 uses), so no include changed, and **no gate,
hygiene grep or probe in `regress/` matches this message's text**, so changing it turns nothing else
red.

**TWO SITES, AND THE RECORD DISTINGUISHES THEM RATHER THAN LUMPING THEM.**
* `:205` **IOC_CONF** — the sharp instance. The guard is on the **value**, so the narrowed message can
  name a value the guard would have accepted. This is what the witness measures.
* `:319` **the `default:` arm** — the same narrowing, but its guard is on the **offset**, so the
  printed value is wrong *without* being one the guard would have accepted. Fixed for consistency,
  not because it can mislead the same way.

> ### *** THE FILED RECORD PRESCRIBED THE WRONG FIX **AND** CLAIMED IT MATCHED THE SURROUNDING CODE.
> ### Corrected in `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` before the edit. ***
>
> It said the repair was `` `0x%llx` with a `(long long)` cast, the file's own idiom elsewhere ``.
> **`dev_lca.c` uses `PRIx64` five times and `%llx` never**, and the siblings **keep** the cast rather
> than dropping it. A design brief of mine then compounded it by saying to *drop* the cast — a third
> wrong form. **A record that names a fix and asserts it matches the neighbours is the most costly
> kind to get wrong: it discourages the one check — reading a sibling — that catches it.**

**FOUR DESIGN CORRECTIONS FROM THE GROK SEAT, each of which would have produced an unreadable or
falsely-green run** (`regress/artifacts/lcaconfwidth/grok_witness2_20260907.txt`):
* `load_const` cannot build either operand — LDA/LDAH make 32-bit sign-extended constants, the K0SEG
  address needs bits 63..42 and the value needs bit 32. Both are planted with `put d` and loaded with
  `ldq` while `ptbr` is still 0.
* **Debugger `dump` cannot be the read-back.** It calls `memory_rw` with `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, and LCA
  registers `DM_DEFAULT` rather than `DM_READS_HAVE_NO_SIDE_EFFECTS`, so the handler is *skipped* and
  the caller gets the pre-zeroed buffer — **the unmapped signature produced by a hit.**
* **`put d` of the killing value is not rung 3.** `store_64bit_word` goes through `memory_rw` with
  `CACHE_DATA` and no `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, so it enters the handler and `exit(1)`s — a real kill caused by
  no guest instruction.
* **A miss is not only "unmapped → nothing".** Offset 0 of the window is HAE, which `break`s with no
  kill, so a store there is silent *inside* the LCA window. `ioc rt` is what separates the two.

**AND THE PROBE'S FIRST DRAFT SCORED 6/6 ON THE COMMITTED BUILD** because it asserted the DEFECT as
the passing state. That reads as success and would have gone red the moment the bug was fixed — a
detector-of-the-defect wearing a witness's clothes. The sibling `alpha_harness_probe.py` had the
polarity right (7/9) in the same tree on the same day. *The cheap tell: ask what the row does AFTER
the fix; if the answer is "goes red", the polarity is inverted whatever the score says.*

**Trees:** `dev_lca.c` is not in `tools/est_divergence.txt`, so it is shared and landed
byte-identical in all four. Rebuilt `build/`, `build-asan/` and `/tmp/gxsec-build`; two-part clearance
CLEAN/FRESH on all three, `est/` part 2 N/A (source tree — inapplicable, not unrun).

**Honest limit:** `(int)0x100000000 == 0` is implementation-defined, not guaranteed by C99. GCC and
Clang truncate to the low 32 bits, which is what this tree builds with, so the witness holds on this
build and the round claims nothing about the language.

# `#505` sgirergbroundtrip: the RGB GET read the pad byte and dropped the red channel — and the panel refuted my reason before a different file supplied a better one

**THE DEFECT.** `horrible_getputpixel()`'s RGB arms are not inverses of each other:

    PUT RGB   buf[0] = c>>24;  buf[1] = c>>16;  buf[2] = c>>8;  buf[3] = 0;
    GET RGB   *color = (buf[1] << 24) + (buf[2] << 16) + (buf[3] << 8);

PUT lays the three channels at bytes 0, 1, 2 and an explicit pad at 3. GET reads 1, 2, 3 — the pad
included, the red channel discarded. **RGB is the only 32-bit colour mode in the file that fails its own
round trip**, and a copy with an RGB source turns `0xaabbccdd` into `0xbbccdd00`.

**WITNESS, rung 3, on an unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32`:** `regress/sgi_re_rgb_probe.py`.  *** THIS BLOCK ORIGINALLY CITED
`regress/artifacts/sgirergbroundtrip/rgb_witness.py`, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST AND ON THE EVIDENCE OF
that directory never did.  Corrected 2026-09-08 when sgirergbroundtrip was closed; the witness is
real -- its header opens "sgirergbroundtrip -- RUNG-3 WITNESS" and restates the defect -- and only
the pointer was wrong.  A citation nobody follows is indistinguishable from a citation that works. ***
Both ladder controls are present and were green in every run — `live` (a guest store and load through RAM)
and `devsig` (`CRIME_DE_STATUS` reads `0x1e000000` where RAM reads 0) — plus a sibling accept control,
`copy lin_a`, which drives an **RGBA** source through the same helper and proves a repair did not break the
neighbour.

---

## *** THE PANEL REFUTED MY ATTRIBUTION, AND IT WAS RIGHT TO. ***

The brief argued the GET is the wrong arm on two grounds. Four seats attacked both, independently:

* **Ground 1 was CIRCULAR.** *"PUT's `buf[3] = 0` is an explicit pad write, so a GET reading byte 3 reads
  the pad"* — that assumes PUT is authoritative, which is exactly the question.
* **Ground 2 was NEUTRALISED.** I appealed to RGBA's byte order; ABGR uses the opposite one, **and the
  default/raw GET arm uses ABGR order too**, so the file offers no single order to appeal to.
* **The measurement is ARM-NEUTRAL.** `0xbbccdd00` is simply what the code does. Under a pad-FIRST
  container it is the *faithful* result and PUT is the bug. **A round-trip failure cannot say which end
  failed** — which is the whole reason this needed a panel and not a fix.

### The settling fact is in `dev_sgi_gbe.c`, and no seat found it

The scanout reads the same tile memory back for display:

    color = (buf[i]<<24) + (buf[i+1]<<16) + (buf[i+2]<<8) + buf[i+3];   /* byte 0 = MSB */
    case CRMFB_MODE_TYP_RGB8:      // Used by NetBSD's X11 server
            *r = color >> 24;  *g = color >> 16;  *b = color >> 8;      /* byte 3 UNUSED */

**R = byte 0, G = byte 1, B = byte 2, and byte 3 is ignored — exactly what the PUT arm writes.** So the pad
sits at `buf[3]` *because the consumer ignores `buf[3]`*, not because PUT writes a zero there. Different
file, opposite direction, and independent of which DE arm is right: that is what makes it non-circular.

### And glm dissolved the ABGR objection from the other end

> *"for the same color, RGBA and ABGR write **identical memory bytes**, `[R,G,B,A]`; they differ only in
> register word order … among the five 4-byte arms, the RGB GET is the lone container outlier — your case
> is stronger than you stated."*

Verified by reading: RGBA word `0xRRGGBBAA` → `buf[RR,GG,BB,AA]`; ABGR word `0xAABBGGRR` →
`buf[RR,GG,BB,AA]`. **My "opposite byte orders" claim was about the register WORD. The question is about
the memory CONTAINER, and on the container all three 4-byte PUT arms agree.** The objection I had invited
turned into the strongest supporting argument, from the seat that raised it.

**codex's reservation is kept and is in the contract:** *"GET is the best-supported repair site for this
emulator's RGB layout; hardware fidelity and real-driver usage remain unproved."* No CRIME/RE datasheet is
in `_scratchpad/` — checked by `ls`, not assumed — so this ships as an **internal-consistency fix warranted
by the tree's own consumer**, never as a claim about silicon.

---

## *** THE PANEL ALSO CAUGHT MY ORACLE, AND IT WOULD HAVE FAILED A CORRECT FIX. ***

The witness's success row pinned **`0xaabbccdd`**, the source word. A corrected RGB GET returns
**`0xaabbcc00`** — RGB carries three channels and the pad is not transported, which PUT's own `buf[3] = 0`
says from the other side.

**Four seats named `0xaabbcc00` independently** — grok, glm, the kimi substitute, and codex — against a
brief that had stated otherwise. The row was re-pinned **before** the code changed and the committed build
re-measured RED under the new expectation, which is the oracle-correction rule's order discriminator
satisfied rather than asserted.

*The surviving row is stronger for it: `rgb chan` pins the exact post-fix value, so a fix that moves the
bytes to some **third** wrong place still reds — which a "not the corrupt value" row could never do.*

**This is the second time in one day that I built a conclusion on a premise I had not thought to
question** — the first was `sgilinearnegidx`, withdrawn at `a264a34` because a variable's declared type
three lines above the code I quoted refuted it. There the premise was a type; here it was which arm is
authoritative. The queued rule question `sgilinearnegidxpostmortem` asks whether the premise-audit
instruction needs a self-directed twin, and this round is its second instance.

---

## Residuals filed, none of them the round's subject

All three came from seats volunteering something under the found-something-else licence:

* **`sgirgbscanoutrow`** — the round's strongest evidence is a claim about `dev_sgi_gbe.c` that **no row
  observes**. A row would need a framebuffer oracle, i.e. a different probe shape. Filed as an explicit
  no-row sentence by the PRE-TABLE CLAIM→ROW check rather than omitted.
* **`sgirebufshiftub`** — `buf[i] << 24` on a `uint8_t` promotes to **signed** `int`, so any byte ≥ 128
  is a signed-shift overflow (UB). Pre-existing on all four GET arms; `#505` replaced one instance of the
  idiom with another, which is the right minimal-surgical choice. Filed, and grok agrees it is *"not a
  reason to block"*.
* **`sgirebufuninit` SHARPENED** — glm widened it from one exposure to three, and the third was new: at
  `bufdepth` 1 or 2 the RGB/RGBA/ABGR GETs read bytes that the guest's own read never filled. `#505`'s own
  GUARD-FIELD-vs-BODY-FIELD check found the same disagreeing state and **declined to row it** — a row here
  would attribute a pre-existing defect to a round that neither created nor cured it.

  > #### *** THIS BULLET FIRST READ *"the RGB/RGBA/ABGR GETs read `buf[2..3]`"* AND GAVE THE DECLINE'S
  > #### REASON AS *"the exposure is identical before and after this edit"*.  **BOTH ARE FALSE OF RGB, AND
  > #### `#505` IS WHAT FALSIFIED THEM.**  Corrected 2026-09-07, before commit. ***
  >
  > Three seats on the `sgirebufuninit` panel said the read-side sentence was too broad — grok: *"its GET
  > sentence is false of RGB as the file sits"*; glm: *"asserted in prose, not in the enumerated table, and
  > under the packet's own model it is wrong"*; minimax: *"the table is asymmetric — write direction
  > enumerated, read direction mentioned in one sentence only."*  The codex seat then supplied the
  > per-arm table, and it is **verified here by reading `dev_sgi_re.c`'s GET arms**:
  >
  > | GET arm | unassigned bytes consumed after a 1-byte read | after 2 bytes | after 4 or 8 |
  > |---|---|---|---|
  > | CI | none | none | none |
  > | **RGB** | `buf[1..2]` | **`buf[2]`** | none |
  > | RGBA / ABGR / default | `buf[1..3]` | `buf[2..3]` | none |
  >
  > **RGB never touches `buf[3]` any more, because this round is what stopped it**: the GET went from
  > `buf[1..3]` to `buf[0..2]`.  So the exposure is **not** identical before and after — for RGB this
  > round *reduced* it by one byte.
  >
  > **The DECLINE still stands and is now better warranted**: the round did not create or worsen the
  > uninitialised read, it shrank it.
  >
  > *** BUT "the remaining exposure is on arms this diff does not touch" WAS WRONG, and a pass-2
  > review of this round caught it. ***  **RGB retains exposure in the EDITED arm**: after this
  > change a 1-byte read still consumes `buf[1..2]` and a 2-byte read still consumes `buf[2]`.  The
  > diff shrank RGB's exposure from `buf[1..3]`/`buf[2..3]`; it did not remove it.  PUT
  > initialisation is unchanged, and RGBA/ABGR/default GET are untouched.  **What was wrong was the REASON, and a wrong reason gets reused** — this project has
  > twice cited one before anyone reopened the file.
  >
  > *Worth naming plainly: the false sentence was written INSIDE the round that falsified it.  A block
  > describing a fix inherits the pre-fix file's facts unless each one is re-read against the post-fix
  > source, and nothing prompts that re-reading — the diff looks like the thing that changed, and the
  > prose looks like the thing that describes it.*
