## The fix

```c
	case DE_MODE_TYPE_RGB:
		/*  #505: ... (the full warrant is in the comment; the code is one line)  */
		*color = (buf[0] << 24) + (buf[1] << 16) + (buf[2] << 8);
		break;
```

**The low byte stays zero on purpose.** RGB carries three channels, so a corrected read of
`0xaabbccdd` yields `0xaabbcc00`, **not** the source word — which is what PUT's own `buf[3] = 0` says
from the other side, and what the panel had to correct me on.

### *** THE FLOOR BREACH, AND IT WAS IN MY OWN DETECTOR. L2, REPAIRED IN-ROUND. ***

`M6_cond` is the canonical clause-(d) form — guard kept, repair conditioned on a field the guarded
body reads:

```c
	case DE_MODE_TYPE_RGB:
		if (bufdepth == 4)  *color = (buf[0]<<24)+(buf[1]<<16)+(buf[2]<<8);   /* the fix */
		else                *color = (buf[1]<<24)+(buf[2]<<16)+(buf[3]<<8);   /* the defect */
```

**Every session in the 6-row detector used `BUFDEPTH_32`, so `bufdepth` was 4 in all of them and the
mutant's fix branch was the only one the detector ever executed.** It proved the fix works exactly
where I measured it and said nothing whatever about anywhere else. `bufdepth` is not an exotic
choice: it is read by the guarded body (it is `memory_rw`'s transfer length) and comes from **bits
8-9 of the same mode word** whose bits 4-7 the guard reads. The DEPENDS-ON closure enumerates it
first, not last.

**Repair: `rgb depth64`, one extra session at `BUFDEPTH_64`.** Width 8 keeps `buf[0..2]` filled so
the row stays a *value* oracle; widths 1 and 2 would read uninitialised bytes (`sgirebufuninit`) and
make it non-deterministic — **8 is the only other width that can carry a value oracle at all.**

### *** AND THE MUTANT I BUILT TO CHECK FOR THE `#499` SHAPE WAS ITSELF MIS-BUILT.  Pass 2 caught it. ***

I added `M7_cond8` to test whether I had repaired only the cell M6 named, and recorded its 7/8 as
proof the width axis was closed. **The kimi substitute — a packet-fed seat that cannot read the
repo — refuted it from the packet's own arithmetic:**

> *"`M7_cond8` cannot be both 'the mirror of M6' and score 7/8; a mirror predicts 5/8."*

```
M6_cond   if (bufdepth == 4) FIXED else DEFECT   ->  width 4 fixed, width 8 defective
M7_cond8  if (bufdepth != 8) FIXED else DEFECT   ->  width 4 fixed, width 8 defective
```

**Over the only two widths any row drives, {4, 8}, those are the same function.** M7 re-measured M6.

**MEASURED, table 3 (`killtable3_20260907/`): the true mirror `M9_truemirror`
(`if (bufdepth == 8) FIXED else DEFECT`) scores 5/8** — exactly what kimi derived — with three
width-4 rows red. **So the width axis is closed, but by `M9`, not by the mutant this block first
credited.** The conclusion survives; its evidence did not, and a claim resting on a mutant that
measures nothing is a wrong record however right the conclusion turns out to be.

**Pass 2 also named LOCATION as an unpinned axis** and predicted `if (ofs == K)` would sweep 8/8,
since every row writes at ofs 0. **`M10_ofs` reds four rows instead** — because the source pixel is
read at `src_x = 0x40`, so `ofs` is 0x40 on every GET and 0 only on the destination PUT. The rows
discriminate on location already, **by an accident of the probe's geometry rather than by design**,
which is recorded as exactly that: covered, unintended, and fragile to anyone who moves `SRC_OFS`.

### `M4_or` is an equivalent mutant, which is a result and not a hole

`+` → `|` on `(buf[0]<<24) + (buf[1]<<16) + (buf[2]<<8)`. The three fields are disjoint — bits 24-31,
16-23, 8-15 — so `+`, `|` and `^` compute the same value. Verified two ways: enumerated over 80 byte
triples with zero disagreements, and its row values are byte-identical to base. Of the three
explanations the carrier gives for a mutant that will not die, this is *"the target is dead"*: there
is no behavioural difference for any test to detect. *Honest caveat: that derivation assumes
well-defined arithmetic, and `sgirebufshiftub` records that `buf[i]<<24` on a `uint8_t` is
signed-shift UB for bytes ≥ 128. The measurement settles it for this compiler; the derivation alone
would not.*

### *** KILL TABLE 4: A SECOND FLOOR BREACH, ON AN AXIS NOBODY HAD LOOKED AT. ***

`regress/artifacts/sgirergbroundtrip/killtable4_20260907/`:

| run | score | |
|---|---|---|
| base | 8/8 | |
| **`M12_linear`** | **8/8** | *** CLEAN SWEEP — clause (d) floor breach *** |

```c
	case DE_MODE_TYPE_RGB:
		if (linear)  *color = (buf[0]<<24)+(buf[1]<<16)+(buf[2]<<8);   /* the fix    */
		else         *color = (buf[1]<<24)+(buf[2]<<16)+(buf[3]<<8);   /* the defect */
```

**Every row in the detector drove LIN_A**, so `linear` was true in all eight and a repair conditioned
on it applied everywhere the detector looked. `linear` is `tlb_mode > 3` and it **dominates** the
edited lines through the `if (!linear && (x < 0 || …)) return;` guard, so it is inside the DEPENDS-ON
closure — a floor breach, not coverage debt. **L2, repaired in-round** by `rgb tiled`, a ninth row
driving a TLB_A source.

**Turning the prediction into a measurement required correcting the seat's form.** deepseek proposed
conditioning on `tileptr`; that cannot discriminate addressing mode, because
`tileptr &= ~0x80000000` strips the linear flag **before** the switch. `linear` is the variable the
source keeps, and building the mutant in the shape the code permits is what made it measurable.

**AND THE NEW ROW CAUGHT MY OWN SETUP ERROR ON ITS FIRST RUN, which is what a row is for.** It read
`0x77665544` — `FG_VAL`, which this probe's own `DE_FG` comment names as *"what a declined GET
leaves"*. The cause: `re_tlb_a` is `uint16_t[256]` filled by a **halfword** loop
(`d->re_tlb_a[tlbi] = data[hwi]*256 + data[hwi+1]`), not `uint32_t` like `re_linear_a`. The `<< 32`
shift that is correct for LINEAR_A lands in `re_tlb_a[2]` and leaves `[0]` at zero, giving
`tileptr = 0` and a declined access. Corrected to `<< 48`. **A row that passed quietly here would
have been vacuous by construction — it would have measured a declined access, not a tiled one.**

### *** BUILDING THE ROW THAT CLOSES THE BREACH TOOK TWO CORRECTIONS, AND THE ROW REPORTED BOTH. ***

`rgb tiled` went red twice before it went green, and both times it read exactly `0x77665544` —
`FG_VAL`, which this probe's own `DE_FG` comment names as *"what a declined GET leaves"*. **The value
was self-documenting: the GET was never reaching the RGB arm at all.**

**Correction 1 — the array is halfwords, not words.**

```c
	uint16_t	re_tlb_a[256];              /* vs uint32_t re_linear_a[32] */
	...
	for (size_t hwi = 0; hwi < len; hwi += sizeof(uint16_t)) {
		d->re_tlb_a[tlbi] = data[hwi]*256 + data[hwi+1];
		tlbi++;
	}
```

An 8-byte store fills `re_tlb_a[0..3]` from four big-endian halfwords, so the element that lands in
`[0]` is bits 63..48. The `<< 32` shift that is **correct for `RE_LINEAR_A`** — because
`re_linear_a` is `uint32_t` — puts the value in `re_tlb_a[2]` and leaves `[0]` at zero.

**Correction 2 — a tiled tile pointer must carry its own valid bit, and the linear path hides that.**

```c
	// The highest bit seems to be set for a "valid" tile pointer.
	if (!(tileptr & 0x80000000))
		return;                          /* silent decline */
	tileptr &= ~0x80000000;
```

`LIN_A` sets that bit **explicitly** — `tileptr = 0x80000000 | (re_linear_a[n] << 12)` — so a probe
built from the linear path never learns it exists. `TLB_A` takes it from the stored value:
`tileptr = re_tlb_a[n] << 16`, and `re_tlb_a` is `uint16_t`, so bit 31 of `tileptr` **is bit 15 of the
register**. `re_tlb_a[0] = 2` yields `0x00020000`, the guard rejects it, and the GET returns without
touching `*color`.

Fixed by `re_tlb_a[0] = 0x8002`, giving `tileptr = 0x80020000` → valid → masked to `0x20000`.

> **A ROW THAT HAD GONE GREEN THROUGH EITHER MISTAKE WOULD HAVE BEEN VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION** — it
> would have measured a *declined* access while claiming to measure a *tiled* one, which is the
> refusal-effect vacuity `#489` paid for four times. It went red instead, twice, and named the value
> that explained why.

*And there is a lesson about the breach itself: `M12_linear` swept 8/8 precisely because no row had
ever driven the non-linear path — and closing it required two facts about the device that the linear
path conceals. **An axis nothing exercises is also an axis nobody has had to learn**, which is why
the cost of closing one is systematically underestimated.*

### *** PASS 3 REFUSED TO CLOSE THE CHAIN, AND IT WAS RIGHT: A THIRD FLOOR BREACH. ***

The repair-chain rule says a repair made in response to a pass 2 owes its own pass, and that the chain
closes on the first pass finding **zero** breaches. Pass 3 found one, and **five seats declined to
ratify** — codex (`NOT ESTABLISHED YET | OPEN`), grok (`NOT RATIFY`), minimax, deepseek and the kimi
substitute (`NOT CLOSED`).

**THE BREACH IS A JOINT CELL, and it is the documented consequence of what I did.** Two axes had each
been closed on their own:

| | bufdepth 4 | bufdepth 8 |
|---|---|---|
| **LIN_A** | `rgb chan`, `rgb samemode` | `rgb depth64` |
| **tiled** | `rgb tiled` | *** UNROWED *** |

A repair conditioned on `(bufdepth == 4 || linear)` is **true in all three rowed cells** and therefore
scores 9/9 by construction. **grok, the kimi substitute and deepseek each derived that cell
independently**, and the kimi seat wrote the mutant out in exactly that form — from the packet, without
reading the tree.

> **This is precisely the shape the class-closure amendment predicts:** *"when two consecutive passes
> find breaches of one class, the next repair owes the CLASS CLOSURE — enumerate the full space from
> the function's own inputs, close every cell in ONE diff."* I repaired cell-by-cell twice, at exactly
> the address each mutant used, and got the third breach the rule exists to prevent.

**Closed with `rgb tiled64`** — the fourth corner, tiled source at `BUFDEPTH_64` — **in the same diff
as the gate fix below**, rather than as another single cell.

### grok read the GATE against the PROBE, which nobody else did

> *"`gate_arm.sh` still pins **8** rows and never names `rgb tiled`."*

True, and it would have shipped. The gate's row list omitted the new row and its denominators pinned 8
against a probe emitting 9. **It would have failed loudly** — emitted 9, wanted 8, which is the safe
direction — **but `rgb tiled` would have been uncounted by name while appearing in the total.** Both
new rows are now named and the pins are 10.

*A detector and its gate are two artifacts, and every review so far had read the probe against itself.*

### Two apparatus lessons, both from rules I was actively applying

* **`rgb tiled` is a prefix of `rgb tiled64`** — the padded-column trap's *dangerous* direction, live
  for the first time in this round. The two-space idiom prevents it; the pre-flight confirmed every
  name matches exactly one rendered row. Had the block used the one-space form, `rgb tiled` would have
  matched both rows and the check would have read `2`.
* **A bare `&` in a shell call killed a probe run**, in a variant the carrier does not record: it
  documents a *zero-byte* log, and this left a **truncated 381-byte one** stopping after `devsig`,
  because the process ran ~2 s before its shell exited. **The completion-sentinel rule caught it** —
  no `SGIRGB_DONE`. Size alone read as a run in progress.

## Two apparatus defects in my own work, recorded rather than quietly fixed

* **Table 1's driver used `grep -c 'FAIL$'` for its red-row column**, which also matched the summary
  line `SGIRGB_WITNESS=FAIL` — inflating every *failing* run's count by exactly one. The scores were
  never affected (they come from the sentinel) but the column beside them was wrong. **That is this
  project's own unanchored-grep trap, in a script written while applying its rules.** Table 2 anchors
  it.
* **The detector's gate block was pre-flighted mechanically before the gate ever ran**, in both
  directions of the padded-column trap: longest row name 15 characters against a `%-16s` column
  (*one* character of margin), and no name a prefix of another. The sibling block was bitten by the
  one-space form on its first run; this one was not.

# Round #504 sgirandompixel -- a failed pixel read handed the caller `random()` and the destination write stored it; the arm now declines with a latched announce, witnessed at rung 3 and backed by a five-mutant table

`src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c`, `horrible_getputpixel()`.  Its `default:` arm printed a diagnostic, had its
`exit(1)` **commented out**, and then executed `*color = random(); return;`.  `*color` is the CALLER's
variable, and in `draw_primitive()` the failed source read and the destination write share one `color` in one
loop iteration -- so a declined read did not decline: it substituted a random value and the next line stored
it.

*** THE UNHANDLED VALUE IS A DOCUMENTED MODE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN A CURIOSITY. ***  The arm
switches on `tlb_mode = (mode >> 10) & 0x7` and implements 0, 1, 2 and 4.  `src/include/thirdparty/crmfbreg.h`
defines FIVE modes, and `DE_MODE_LIN_B` (`0x1400`) extracts to **5**.  Four of the five documented modes work
and the fifth returns random data.  Both mode words are ordinary device registers written by ordinary stores.

**RUNG-3 WITNESS, BUILT AND MEASURED** -- `regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py`, real guest instructions on an
unmodified committed `-E sgi -e ip32`, no `device_add`.  Both mandated controls green (liveness through RAM; a
device signature RAM could not produce).  The destination received `0x4b1763a1`, `0x2ee4b4df`, `0x7433cdc1` on
successive runs -- **bit 31 clear every time**, because glibc `random()` is 31-bit, which is what makes the
oracle deterministic although the value is not: inequality with a `0xaabbccdd` source is CERTAIN, not 2^-32.

**THE DESIGN CAME FROM THE PANEL AND SO DID THE ONE THING THAT MADE THE WITNESS WORK.**  grok specified it and
warned that the obvious probe FINDS NOTHING: at reset the destination mode is TLB_A with its valid bit clear,
so the write silently returns and the destination is unchanged -- a false negative that looks like a clean run.
**I hit that trap anyway**, from a direction it had also named: a 64-bit store writes the HIGH word to `[n]`,
so storing `0x10` left the tile pointer at 0 and every pixel went to physical address 0.  **The ACCEPT control
is what caught it**; a probe carrying only defect rows would have reported no defect.

**THE FIX IS MEMBER 3 (DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE) IN THE MINIMAL SCOPE**, 3 of 5 answering seats, and the two
dissents were refuted on a point both file-reading seats reached independently: they voted FAULT, but **the
device access that triggers this already succeeded** -- the store to PRIMITIVE|START was accepted -- so there
is nothing left to fault.  grok: *"'member 5 is available here' is true of IP32 and FALSE OF THIS CALL SITE."*
codex argued for the fuller form (an explicit success result, every read site suppressing its dependent write);
**a return value plus seven call sites is not ONE SITE**, so the reopening rule takes grok's scoping and
codex's form is filed as `sgirandomskipput` rather than dropped.

**TEST-FIRST, IN THE ORDER THE ORACLE-CORRECTION RULE FIXES.**  The witness PASSES while the defect is PRESENT,
so its oracle had to invert.  Re-pinned FIRST, the COMMITTED build measured **RED at 7/8**
(`prefix_repinned_RED.out`), and only then was the code changed -- 8/8 after, same script.  Without that order
a re-pin cannot be told from fitting the test to the binary.

**THE KILL TABLE** (`artifacts/sgirandompixel/killtable/`, BASE 8/8 opening AND closing, clone clean, no
sentinel; every score re-derived by DIFFING each result against `BASE.out`, never the driver's echo):

| mutant | score | rows red |
|---|---|---|
| `M_RANDOM` -- verbatim reinstatement (clause (b)) | 6/8 | value AND latch count |
| `M_ZERO` -- guard kept, repair nulled (clause (d)) | 7/8 | value only, `0x0` |
| `M_NOLATCH` -- drop the latch guard | 7/8 | latch count, **4 vs 1** |
| `M_SILENT` -- member 2 instead of member 3 | 6/8 | both diagnostic rows |
| `M_EXIT` -- restore `exit(1)` | 4/8 | four rows; the machine dies |

*** TABLE 1 FOUND TWO DEFECTS IN THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF, BOTH REPAIRED IN-ROUND UNDER L1. ***
* **`lin_b diag once` was VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION and `M_NOLATCH` escaped 8/8.**  The probe drew a **1x1**
  rectangle, so an UNLATCHED announce also fired exactly once and the count channel could not vary.  **The
  pre-table CHANNEL check is exactly the check that should have caught it** -- I named the channel and never
  asked whether the session could MOVE it, which is the half that matters.  Repaired to **1 wide x 4 tall**:
  HEIGHT not width, because LIN_A addressing is `ofs = x & 4095` (y ignored), so four rows rewrite one byte
  and the value oracle survives, while four columns would overlap and destroy it.
* **`M_RANDOM` was MIS-BUILT** -- it also silenced the announce, so it reddened three rows and died for TWO
  reasons; an over-determined mutant cannot attribute its kill to the channel its row names.  Corrected to
  restore both halves the fix changed, which is what clause (b) asks for.  *My PRETABLE prediction of 7/8 was
  then wrong for a third reason and the measurement was right: the fix changed TWO things, so a verbatim
  reinstatement necessarily reddens two rows.*

**PASS 2: SHIP.  Six seats answering, none walled, none down** -- the fullest roster of the session, and it
cost one liveness call: **kimi had walled on three consecutive panels and returned its token on the first
re-fire**, then answered 72 KB.  A wall is a moment, not a state.  Both FILE-READING seats answered with NO
verdict line, and reading them in full is where the round's one finding was.  codex **re-derived all 40 row
outcomes (8 rows x 5 mutants) from the preserved artifacts** and confirmed the table, saying plainly it ran
nothing itself.  grok answered **NONE IS WRONG** to the five-way disposition question and named the question's
own frame as the unsupported assumption -- the SECOND seat that day to make that correction independently
(row `briefforcedwrong`).

**THE ROUND'S ONE L4, AND IT WAS SELF-INFLICTED IN THE ENUM THIS ROUND EXTENDED.**  `SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP`'s comment
still said *"the next free bit is 1 << 10; the enum ends HERE on purpose"* -- both false once
`SGIRE_W_BADMODE = 1 << 10` was appended below it.  **That is the duplicate-enumerator collision this file
already paid for and warns about four lines earlier**; a duplicate enumerator is legal C, silent, and crosses
devices because all four handlers share one allocation.  I read that warning while placing the bit, obeyed it,
and left the signpost pointing at the bit I had just taken.  Fixed by DEMOTING the superseded sentence inside
its own correction, leaving exactly one live next-free claim, on the last enumerator.

**FILED, not fixed** -- five rows, each named in the shipped comment so no reference dangles:
`sgirandomskipput` (the declined read still lets the caller write fg -- codex's fuller form),
`sgirelinb` (LIN_B unimplemented; the panel REFUSED to endorse implementing it as LIN_A-with-the-other-array,
because case 4 carries its own `TODO... probably not correct!` and the MTE path checks validity and searches
by page while case 4 indexes directly -- symmetry is supporting evidence, not a transferred warrant),
`sgirandomcolour` (**grok found a SECOND `random()` site nobody else saw**: the colour-mode `default:` fills
four bytes the same way), `sgitileptrsilent` (the sibling arm declines with no announce at all -- from the
sibling-parity check), and `sgirenamedstmode` (the diagnostic says `dst_mode` although the parameter is also
passed as src_mode; the round DID reword it, which broke the probe's anchor and reddened two rows on a FIXED
build, and **moving the anchor to match would have been the laundering shape** -- the wording went back).

**Wired into `gate_arm.sh`** beside its two siblings, following that block's own two lessons: the completion
sentinel is checked BEFORE any row, and the denominator is summed arithmetically across three rows, because a
single count cannot tell a LOST row from a FAILING one.

*** AND THE GATE'S FIRST RUN FAILED ON THE BLOCK I HAD JUST WRITTEN -- THE PADDED-COLUMN TRAP, IN ITS
MATCHES-TWO-ROWS DIRECTION. ***  `FAIL sgi_re randompixel row: lin_b diag  got=2 want=1`, while the probe
itself emitted 8 rows, 8 green, 0 red.  **The probe was right and my CHECK was wrong**: I wrote
`"^$v .*ok$"` with ONE space, so the pattern for `lin_b diag` also matched the row `lin_b diag once`.
**The sibling block eight lines above uses TWO spaces** -- I copied that block's comments and lessons and not
its pattern.

Fixed to the house idiom and **pre-flighted against the real probe log before re-running the 15-minute gate**,
which is the two-second check the carrier prescribes for exactly this: each of the eight patterns now selects
exactly 1, summing to 8, and the NEGATIVE CONTROL still reproduces `got=2` under the old one-space form.

*** AND THEN I RAN TWO GATES AT ONCE, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THE HARNESS RULES FORBID MOST PLAINLY. ***

I read run 1's log as finished -- it had 177 `ok' rows, 1 `FAIL', and the randompixel block complete at the
tail -- fixed the pattern, and launched run 2.  **Run 1 was still executing.**  Its log carried no
`RB_GATE_DONE', and I never looked for one: I counted ROWS and read the TAIL, both of which look identical on
a finished run and on a run that is merely past the section you care about.

**The carrier states the rule in capitals and I had quoted it into this very round's gate block four hours
earlier:** *A PRESERVED LOG IS VERIFIED BY ITS COMPLETION SENTINEL, NOT BY ITS EXISTENCE.*  The block I wrote
checks `SGIRAND_DONE' BEFORE any row for exactly this reason.  I applied the rule to the probe and not to the
gate that runs it -- **knowing a rule and having it fire on the right object are different problems**, which is
the carrier's own diagnosis of itself.

**WHAT IT COST, and the damage is to evidence rather than to the tree.**  Both runs default to
`LOGDIR=/tmp/gxregress' and `gate_arm.sh' greps probe logs there BY NAME, so for about six minutes two runs
wrote and graded the same files.  **Every verdict from both runs is discarded** -- not because any of them
looked wrong, but because a measurement taken from a shared, concurrently-written log is not a measurement.
Detected by an impossible pair: two `python3'->`gxemul' chains under DIFFERENT parents, one aged 05:42 and one
00:04, when a single gate runs one probe at a time.

**The pre-flight of the row patterns SURVIVES**, and it is worth saying why rather than re-running it for
comfort: it ran BEFORE run 2 was launched, so it had a single writer; and what it tested -- which pattern
selects which row NAME -- is a property of the probe's `%-16s' format, not of which run produced the file.

**Fixed STRUCTURALLY rather than by resolving to be careful**, since being careful is what just failed: the
runner now REFUSES to start when a `gxemul' is already alive, and clears `$LOGDIR' first so a killed run's
stale probe log cannot be graded as the new run's.  The refusal matches on the process IMAGE, never on a
script name -- git-bash `ps' is argument-blind, so a name pattern can never match and would be a check that
cannot fail.

*** AND THE DASHBOARD GENERATOR REFUSED TO RENDER THIS ROUND, WHICH IS THE THIRD TIME TONIGHT A TOOL CAUGHT ME
RATHER THAN THE OTHER WAY ROUND. ***

`gen_dashboard.py` exited with *"REFUSING TO RENDER -- seat ids used by entries but declared by no column"*,
naming `'main'` (2 entries) and `'main-loop'` (5).  **All seven were mine, written during this session** as I
recorded triage and prep work: I had been using the ledger's `entries' list as a general worklog.

**IT IS NOT A NAMING NIT.  `entries' IS THE SEAT ANSWER LIST.**  `check_stage_panels.py` COUNTS entries to
decide whether a stage's nine seats were fired, so a main-loop note parked there **MANUFACTURES A SEAT ANSWER
THAT NEVER HAPPENED** -- the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape inverted, and the carrier already records
exactly this mechanism for a wrongly-defanged hold marker falling through into the seat tally.  Left alone, my
seven notes would have made four rows look better-reviewed than they are.

All seven migrated into `state_note', where the row's narrative belongs, each carrying a header saying why it
moved; every remaining entry names one of the nine declared seats, verified by re-reading the file after the
edit.  The dashboard then rendered: 242 in work, 111 closed, 9 seats.

**The generator is the hero here and it is worth saying why it worked:** it does not warn and continue, it
REFUSES -- and it prints the orphan ids, their counts, and the rows they sit on, so the fix is mechanical.
That is the opposite of the two defects this same round found in `panel.sh`'s history, where a message
reported an action the code did not take.  *A check that stops the pipeline is worth ten that advise it.*

**ATTRIBUTION NOTE, because the gate ran with an uncommitted file in the tree.**  `regress/sgi_de_primop_probe.py`
carries an unrelated in-flight edit that this commit deliberately does NOT include, and `gate_arm.sh` runs that
probe -- so the run that cleared this round was not, strictly, a run of the committed tree.  **Checked rather
than waved past:** `git diff -U0` on it is 20 added / 6 removed lines, and every one is comment prose or a
`row()` NOTE argument -- no `want', no oracle, no session, no store.  Notes do not participate in the row's
`got == want' comparison and the gate matches on row NAME plus `ok$', so the verdicts are identical either way.
*The carrier's comparison-run rule -- a note change shows up as an apparent behavioural difference -- binds a
base-versus-mutant DIFF, which this is not.*

**The margin is ONE CHARACTER and the comment now says so**, because this trap's other direction is silent:
the probe prints `"%-16s"` plus an explicit space, so a name of N chars is followed by `(16-N)+1` spaces.
The longest row name here is `lin_b diag once` at **15**, leaving exactly two.  **A name of 16 or more makes
the two-space pattern UNSATISFIABLE -- the check stops testing anything and stays GREEN**, which is how a row
quietly stops being tested.  Growing a name past 15 requires widening the probe's `%-16s` in the same diff.

# Round #503 lunaabsentcpu -- the LUNA-88K interrupt controller called an absent CPU's NULL handler: a store to an interrupt mask on the DEFAULT one-CPU machine terminated the simulator; the walk is now bounded to the slots DEVINIT connected, with a 37-row rung-3 detector

`src/devices/dev_luna88k.c`.  `reassert_interrupts()` walked `for (cpu = 0; cpu < MAX_CPUS; cpu++)` and called
`d->cpu_irq[cpu].interrupt_assert(...)`.  **DEVINIT only `INTERRUPT_CONNECT`s the slots the machine actually has**,
and `luna88k_data` is allocated zeroed, so an unpopulated slot's function pointer is the memset's NULL.  On the
DEFAULT one-CPU machine a guest store of `0xfc000000` to `INT_ST_MASK1`, followed by a store to `SOFT_INT1` or to
any device line that mask enables, follows a null function pointer and the process dies.  **Pre-existing upstream**:
the HACK comment's per-count connects and this walk are both the 0.7.0 import.

**WITNESS, rung 3** -- a real guest instruction through real address decode on an UNMODIFIED in-tree machine
description, `regress/luna_absentcpu_probe.py`.  It carries both mandated controls: a LIVENESS control (a known
value returns through the same decode) and a DEVICE-SIGNATURE control (the observed value could only have come from
this device).  Symptom on the pre-fix committed build, clean after, same script.

**THE FIX** captures `devinit->machine->ncpus` into `d->ncpus` and bounds the walk to it, so **the walk bound and
the connect predicate are the same number by construction** rather than by coincidence.  Three hunks, no behaviour
change for any populated slot.

**THE PASS-2 REVISION, and why it is not "cannot hurt".**  Pass 1's form captured `ncpus` ABOVE the `> 4` exit.
The Fable pass-1 seat asked for the capture to move below it or for a clamp; the minimax pass-2 seat supplied the
reason that makes it more than tidiness -- **with the capture above the exit, that exit became LOAD-BEARING for the
walk's bound**, where pre-fix the walk was bounded by `MAX_CPUS` whatever `ncpus` was.  The revision removes a
dependency the fix itself had introduced.  Per the repair-chain rule, that revision owes its own pass; brief written
(`brief_lunaabs_p6.md`), panel owed.

*** A RECORD CORRECTION THAT OVERTURNS A CORRECTION, and the displaced wording was CLOSER TO RIGHT. ***
The capture comment ended *"(delete that exit and a 5-cpu machine would walk `cpu_irq[4]`)"*.  **Measured FALSE by
the Opus seat**: `machine_luna88k.c` carries a SECOND `ncpus > 4` guard AFTER its `device_add`, so deleting the
device's exit lets DEVINIT capture 5 and the MACHINE layer ends the run before any guest instruction -- measured
both ways at `-n 5`; base prints the device's message, the mutant prints the machine's, both exit 1, **neither
walks**.  Deleting BOTH exits is what would walk `cpu_irq[4]`.
**And the sharper half: the pass-3 refutation that produced that wording was itself wrong.**  kimi and grok had
overturned the pass-2 phrasing *"<= MAX_CPUS by construction, not by that exit"* -- but **both seats read only the
device file and neither saw the machine-layer guard**, so the wording they displaced was closer to the truth than
the correction that replaced it.  Corrected in place in the shipped comment, and said plainly here rather than
silently superseded.  *A correction carries more authority than the error it replaces, which is why it earns a
second reading and not less of one -- the third instance of that class in this project.*

**THE DETECTOR** -- `regress/luna_absentcpu_probe.py`, 37 rows, five kill tables.  `killtable5` on the shipped
instrument: **BASE 37/37**, and every one of the twenty-six distinct mutants is KILLED -- `M_NOASSIGN` 19/33,
`M_HARD1` and `M_ENX1` 26/35 and 26/33, `M_OFFBY1` 26/29, `M_EN0`/`M_ENSH1` 30/35, `M_CALLGUARD` 31/33,
`M_GUARDASSERT` 31/32, `M_NULLA` 31/32, `M_LATCH`/`M_REVERT` 30/32, down to `M_DEASSERT0` and `M_NOCLEAR` at 36/37.
**One mutant does not die and that is a RESULT, not a gap**: `M_NULLAB` scores 37/37, and its warrant was corrected
during the round -- the empty-name stub path it edits is **dead code**, so the mutant is EQUIVALENT rather than an
escape.  Recorded with its warrant, per the rule that a mutant which will not die has exactly three explanations and
silently re-aiming it picks one without measuring which.
**Five mutants were additionally CROSS-SCORED on the frozen v5 instrument** (`*_on_v5.out`), which is what makes the
v6 rows' contribution a measurement rather than a claim: `M_ENP1` and `M_SWP1` are 34/34 -- clean sweeps of v5 --
and 35/37 on v6, so those rows are the reason they die at all.

**TREES.**  `dev_luna88k.c` is a SHARED file -- the divergence set was DERIVED (`tools/est_divergence.txt`, six
paths) and does not contain it -- so the fix landed byte-identically in all five copies.  **Two-part clearance RUN,
not asserted**, on every tree that has a binary: `build` (pmax), `/tmp/gxsec-build` (arc) and `build-asan` all
report PART1 CLEAN / PART2 FRESH after a rebuild; **`est/` is a SOURCE tree and its part 2 is N/A, stated rather
than left blank** -- an unrun check and an inapplicable one must not render the same.  The build script takes the
binary's own freshness as the oracle rather than `make`'s exit status, which has been observed reporting 0 on a
failed build.

*** PASS 2 (the repair-chain pass this REVISION owed) REFUTED THE REVISION'S OWN RATIONALE. ***  The pass-1
form captured `ncpus` above the `> 4` exit; the pass-2 revision moved it below, on the argument that this
removes a dependency the fix had introduced.  **It does not** (codex, GPT-6 Astra at max).  Above or below, the
assignment supplies the same bound whenever execution reaches the walk, because the walk is downstream of the
exit either way -- with the capture above, a 5-cpu machine stores 5 and the exit ends the process before any
walk; with it below, the exit fires before the store.  **Neither reaches the walk, and both placements rely
equally on initialization rejecting excessive counts.**  A CLAMP to `MAX_CPUS` is what would buy independence,
and the addition licence refuses one without a measured delta -- the seat found no failure in any accepted
configuration.  **Disposition: KEEP the relocation, CORRECT the claim (L4, in-round).**  A second precision fix
in the same comment: the walk bound and the connect predicate carry the same VALUE, not one shared field -- the
predicates still read `machine->ncpus` while the walk reads the snapshot.  The same seat confirmed the snapshot
is stable in this fork (counts assigned during configuration, CPUs created before devices, no later mutation or
CPU-add path), which is the premise the brief had deliberately left as a question.

**AND IT PREDICTED TWO SURVIVORS, BOTH SINCE MEASURED AT 37/37** (`killtable6_codexpred/`, BASE 37/37 opening
and closing, clone clean, no sentinel):

| mutant | score | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu < (d->ncpus & -d->ncpus)` -- the lowest set bit | **37/37 TOTAL ESCAPE** | disclosed clause-(e) debt |
| `software_interrupt_status[cpu] & 1` | **37/37 TOTAL ESCAPE** | disclosed clause-(e) debt |

*** BOTH ARE MEMBERS OF FAMILIES THIS PROBE HAD ALREADY DISCLOSED, WHICH IS CLAUSE (e) WORKING RATHER THAN A
FLOOR BREACH. ***  The `& 1` mutant is the `== 1` cell opus5 disclosed on pass 4 -- the body tests
NONZERO-ness and never partitions the nonzero class, and every SOFT value any session writes is 1, so any
predicate true of 1 preserves every observation.  Two spellings, one cell.  The lowest-set-bit mutant is the
`ncpus`-dependent fold **kimi NAMED on pass 5 before any member existed**, writing that such a fold "is the
IDENTITY at every count this probe boots -- 1, 2 and 4 -- and folds only at `-n 3', which no session boots".
It is identity at 1, 2 and 4 and under-walks only at 3, exactly as predicted.  **The pass-5 disposition stands:
disclosed debt, not clause (d)** -- `(d->ncpus & -d->ncpus)` does not READ like the same check, which is clause
(d)'s own test, and every single-token weakening of that bound IS rowed and DOES die (`M_OFFBY1`, `M_REVERT`,
`M_HARD1`, `M_SKIP1`).  Contract upgraded from NAMED to MEASURED in probe v8 (docstring-only, proved by
comparing executable structure with docstrings stripped against the frozen v7 the table ran).  Closure is one
`-n 3` session and would close the whole family; filed as `lunancpus3` rather than taken in-round, because the
round's scope is the walk bound and a new session is new apparatus with its own load sensitivity.

**FILED, not fixed.**  `lunaabsentmaskdecl`: the absent slots' MASK and SOFT registers remain guest-writable
storage with readback.  This fix bounds the WALK and takes none of the six de-fatalisation dispositions for the
REGISTERS -- a board-model question rather than a crash, and the pass-6 brief asks explicitly whether it should have
been in-round.  `lunadefaultstop`: the default-machine stop path, raised in the same passes.

# Round #502 m88kexcdeliver -- the MC88100 model stopped EVERY guest CPU for seven trap-like exception classes; now it delivers them (VBR + 8*vector, shadows and PSR per the manual), and a 22-row detector pins the delivery

**2026-09-05.  HIGH.  `src/cpus/cpu_m88k.c` (`m88k_exception()`, 63+/12-), new `regress/m88k_exc_probe.py`, `regress/gate_m88k_rounding.sh` (gate 11).**
Artifacts: `regress/artifacts/m88kexcdeliver/` (both pass briefs, the pass-1 and pass-2 panel answers, the Opus and Fable pass-2 answers,
`PRETABLE_m88kexc.out`, three kill tables, the Opus pass-2 table, every probe output named below).

## The defect

`m88k_exception()` marked only RESET / INTERRUPT / INSTRUCTION_ACCESS / DATA_ACCESS `implemented`; MISALIGNED_ACCESS (4),
UNIMPLEMENTED_OPCODE (5), PRIVILEGE_VIOLATION (6), BOUNDS_CHECK_VIOLATION (7), ILLEGAL_INTEGER_DIVIDE (8), INTEGER_OVERFLOW (9) and
ERROR (10) printed a VERBOSITY_ERROR line and fell to the fallback `vector < M88K_EXCEPTION_USER_TRAPS_START && !implemented`, which
sets `running = false` on EVERY guest CPU: one `divu` by zero, in either mode, ended the emulation.  Real hardware delivers
VBR + 8*vector and the guest OS turns it into a signal.  Pre-existing upstream (the fallback is the 0.7.0 import; `git log -L`
returns only that commit); surfaced by the 2026-09-05 retrospective re-check of #380 (batch 2: GPT-6 Astra read-only, Fable 5.1
adjudicating).  Reachability, MEASURED rather than derived: the instruction raise sites (PRIVILEGE 10 literal sites, ILLEGAL_DIVIDE 4,
OVERFLOW 3, MISALIGNED 1, UNIMPLEMENTED 1) AND a supervisor `tb0/tb1/tcnd`, whose 9-bit field names any vector directly
(`m88k_exception(cpu, ic->arg[2], 1)`), so BOUNDS (7) and ERROR (10) -- which the filing called "latent, no raise site" -- ARE
reachable today (pass 1, Opus: supervisor `tb1 0,r3,7` halted HEAD).  The filing's sentence is corrected in place (ledger, OPEN LIST).

## Witness (rung 3) and fix

`regress/m88k_exc_probe.py`: cold-debugger rows on the COMMITTED, UNMODIFIED `testm88k` machine -- a guest program planted with `put w`,
registers seeded, `br .` at every vector entry, `breakpoint add <entry>`, `continue`, then `reg` / `reg 0,0`.  HEAD `83df95c`:
**0/9** (`probe2_head.out`), **0/10** (`probe10_head.out`), **3/22** with the final instrument (`probe_v3_head.out`: the 3 are the two
rows whose CORRECT answer is HALT and the pre-existing user vector 128); every trap-like class printed `unimplemented vector=` and the
machine stopped.  The fix: **9/9 -> 10/10 -> 22/22** (`probe2_fix.out`, `probe_v3_fix.out`, `probe_v3_fix_final.out` on the
rebuilt tree).

The fix is D1 of the six-member set -- DELIVER, at BOTH sites: `implemented = true` (at VERBOSITY_INFO, the level of the four
already-delivered classes) in the first switch, and a bare `case ... break` for the seven in the tail switch.  **The one-site form was
MEASURED (pass 1, Opus) to halt at the tail `default:` ("internal error") with pc/SXIP/PSR already correct -- only the
machine-still-running bit distinguished it from delivery**, which is why every fault row asserts the STOP channel before pc.  SFU1
(114/115) stays at the fallback by design (row `m88kexcsfu1`); vectors 11..113 and 116..127 (117 with the two SFU1 ones) stay at the
fallback and the detector's negative-control rows pin that they STILL halt.  D4 (make the tail default deliver everything) was named
by the pass-1 panel and not adopted -- bigger blast radius -- filed `m88kexctaildefault`.  Structural consequence, stated in the
comment: with `implemented` = {0..10} and tail labels for {0..10}, the tail `default:` is now UNREACHABLE for vectors < 128; it is
kept as the tripwire for an eighth class.

## The detector, and the four times it was found wanting before it shipped

v1 (9 rows) shipped with the fix build at 16:16.  What each pass found, and what changed -- every score names its log:

| found by | escape (score on the probe of the time) | repair |
|---|---|---|
| table 1 (`killtable/`, 13 mutants, 9 rows) | `M_ERRORDROP` **9/9**: switch 1's ERROR arm is reached ONLY by a trap naming 10 (the re-route enters AFTER switch 1) | row `errortb` (tb1 naming 10); table 2 (`killtable2/`): M_ERRORDROP 9/10, M_ERRORTAIL 8/10, M_REVERT1 9/10 |
| Opus pass 2 (`opus_p2_logs/`, 15 mutants) | `M_NOVBR` (`pc = 8*vector`) **10/10** -- no row set VBR; `M_SFRZTRAP` (`if (!is_trap)` -> `if (true)`) **10/10** -- the (SFRZ set, trap) cell empty; `M_SFIPNOTGT` / `M_DSLOTSWAP` **10/10** -- dslot's SNIP and SFIP were ONE number (0x1000e) | rows `vbrtb` (VBR 0x2000, entry 0x2038 -- the one ANCHORED row), `trapfrozen` (div0 handler = tb1 naming 7 with SFRZ set -> 0x38, shadows frozen); dslot geometry `br.n +16` (SFIP 0x10016 != SNIP 0x1000e) |
| grok, deepseek, glm (independently); codex for PRIVILEGE | `if (!is_trap) implemented = true;` escapes every instruction-route row (privtb is NOT the trap route: X(tb0)'s user-mode filter raises PRIVILEGE with is_trap 0) | rows `misaligntb unimpltb div0tb ovftb privsuptb` |
| Opus, codex, kimi, Fable (four seats) | pass-1 F14 was wrong: the exact PSR compare pinned carry only at its pre-fault value 0 -- "unchanged" was unobservable | row `ovfc` (PSR C set before the overflowing add -> 0x9000000b) |
| Fable review seat | "no row can observe the level" was FALSE: `main.c` lowers every subsystem to WARNING after startup, so an ERROR-level `[ exception <CLASS>: ]` line prints in a free-running transcript and INFO does not | the LEVEL channel on every DELIVER row (`bad=level`) |
| codex | tail guard `<` -> `<=` sends user vector 128 into the tail default | row `usertb` (tb1 naming 128 -> 0x400) |
| kimi | no NEGATIVE-CONTROL rows: the probe could not tell D1 from the rejected D4 or from delivering SFU1 | rows `resid50` (tb1 naming 50: EXPECT HALT) and `sfu1h` (div0 handler = a legal divu with SFD1 set -> SFU1 -> EXPECT HALT) |
| Fable 9b, codex | "one user-mode divu by zero" was derived (div0 is supervisor) | row `udiv0` |

**Table 3** (`killtable3/`, v3 probe frozen md5 `28302f55`, 22 fault rows + 2 controls, BASE 22/22 before and after, clone
`cmp`-clean and sentinel-free at both ends): M_ISTRAP 17/22 (the five trap rows), M_NOVBR 21/22 (vbrtb STOP), M_SFRZTRAP 21/22
(trapfrozen STOP), M_SFIPNOTGT 21/22 and M_DSLOTSWAP 21/22 (dslot), M_CARRYCLR 21/22 (ovfc psr), M_LEVEL 3/22 (19 rows bad=level),
M_DELIVERALL 20/22 (resid50 TAILHALT, sfu1h STOP), M_TAILLE 21/22 (usertb TAILHALT), M_REVERT 3/22, M_ERRORDROP 21/22, M_DSLOT 21/22,

enumerated mutant** -- delete it and `M_RRTRAPSFD1` is still caught, by `trapfrozenuser`, at 58/58.  Under the
addition licence *"it cannot hurt"* is not a warrant, so the row needs a real one: it is the SINGLE-AXIS
discriminator, because a row varying two bits cannot say which one fired.  A future edit that opens SFD1 while
leaving MODE closed reds `trapfrozensfd1` and nothing else.  That is the anchor rule's principle one level down.

ITS DENOMINATOR and an enumeration of what was swept.**

**THE RULING AGAINST US:** this round kept `trapfrozensfd1`, whose measured delta against its own mutant is
ZERO, arguing the anchor rule's principle transfers -- a row varying two bits cannot say which fired.  **The
warrant does not transfer**, and the refutation cites this project's own carrier: the anchor rule repairs an
oracle that compares a path with ITSELF, which is not the situation here since the joint row already checks
concrete vector and register expectations; and row demand is bounded *"per enumerated mutant, never per
attribution need"*.  Removing the row loses none of the 56 cells and none of table 15's kills.

when redundancy buys a failure signature, and the carrier sends rule questions to the flagship seat at the next
round boundary.  **Filed as `m88ksfd1row` with the question written out, held for the 2026-09-09

# Round #501 pcc2defaultkill -- the `default:` arm of DEVICE_ACCESS(pcc2) ended the host on any access to an uncased offset, reads included; now reads keep the served byte and writes are declined, one latched announce per offset

**2026-09-05.  HIGH, ranked first by the 2026-09-04 fix-review adjudication.  Product change: `src/devices/dev_pcc2.c`
-- the `exit(1)` replaced by a per-offset latched `fatal()` (`uint64_t warned_unimpl`, one bit per byte offset) that
says DECLINED for a write and SERVED 0x%02x for a read, then `break` to the handler's single `return 1`.  Detector:
`regress/pcc2_default_probe.py`, 46 rows (23 at pass 2; +13 by the pass-2 repair, +10 by the pass-3 repair, below), run by gate 14.  Witness: rung 3, measured before the edit.**

## The defect and its witness

Forty-three of the 0x40 byte offsets have no `case` (derived from `mvme_pcctworeg.h` against the 21 labels; two seats
re-derived it): eighteen NAMED registers the model does not implement (PSCALECNT, GPIO_ICR/PCR, SCCMOIACK, SCCTXIACK,
IEERR, IEICR, IEBERR, SCSIERR, the printer block, SPEED, PRTDATA), the twelve bytes INSIDE the four 32-bit
counter/compare words, and thirteen unnamed offsets.  Any access to one of them -- a READ included, although the
memcpy above the switch had already served it -- reached `default:` and `exit(1)`.

**The witness (`regress/artifacts/pcc2defaultkill/witness_20260905/`), measured on the committed build BEFORE the
edit: 7/13.**  A guest `st.b` to IEICR (0x2a) ends the host with exit status 1, the arm's own `pcc2: unimplemented`
line printed first (the arm was reached); a guest `ld.bu` there likewise -- the READ side kills too; IEBERR and the
in-word byte 0x05 and the alias 0x6a kill the same way.  Liveness (the probe's scratch round-trip) and
device-signature (CHIPID reads PCC2_ID 0x20) controls pass.  **The debugger's `put b` does NOT reach the arm** -- it
survives and prints nothing -- which the filing had called the cheapest witness (measured false; corrected).  The
witness script is the width probe's own `session()` helper: a first draft hand-rolled the pty wait, accepted a
STALE prompt, and read every kill as "survived" -- the carrier's rule about hand-rolled pty plumbing, re-learned.
The combined IEBERR/IEERR row measures IEBERR only (the exiting build dies at the first); IEERR's kill follows from
source (codex).  **13/13 on the fixed build.**

## The design (pass 1: nine seats, `_scratchpad/panel_20260905_021751`, converged)

READ: keep the byte the memcpy served and SAY it is served -- it is the register array's CURRENT byte (inside a running
COUNT word, the tick's; the pass-1 design said "default, not a computed value", corrected at pass 2), so this is not
the option set's member 4 and a bounded announce about it is not a wrong record.  WRITE:
member 3, DECLINE + latched announce -- NOT member 6 (backed accept), on three warrants the seats measured or read:
the file's own cased siblings contradict a blanket store (SCCERR is write-to-clear -- the board manual's SCLR bits
read as zero; the ICRs mask and reassert; PSCALECNT/SPEED/the IACKs are read-only); the addition licence is unmet
(no inspected OpenBSD driver path reaches these offsets on this model -- the rung-3 witness is itself a guest, so the
pass-1 wording "no guest reaches" was too wide: codex, pass 2); a store from the one arm 43 offsets reach adds a bounded-write
surface into `pcctwo_reg[]` at 0x3d.  The Opus seat BUILT both candidates in a scratch clone and measured the
13-row witness at 13/13 under BOTH -- disposition-blind -- so the detector carries read-after-write rows in ONE
session (`ieicr rdawr`, `ieerr rdawr`: store 0x5a then load, want 0x0 -- a backed accept reads 0x5a) with the CASED
write-to-clear sibling `sccerr rdawr` as the control that reads 0x0 under either.

**Two premises of the pass-1 brief were wrong and are corrected here.**  The in-tree guest driver (`if_ie.c`) writes
three of these offsets, but NEVER RUNS on this model: `machine_mvme88k.c:106` installs `unreadable` at the 82596
address, `if_ie.c:407-409` fails its match on `badpaddr()` there, and `ie_setupram()` returns early at `:561-564`
before the PCC2 store at `:609` (Fable, Opus, grok, codex independently; verified).  `ie0` IS configured in
`conf/M187` and `conf/NFS` -- the brief's conf grep looked in the wrong files.  So the HIGH ranking rests on the
witness and severity, not on the driver.  And the alias the model implements (`relative_addr %= PCC2_SIZE`) is the
REAL part's: Motorola VMESBCP2 Table 6-1 lists `$FFF42040-$FFF42FFF  PCCchip2 Registers  Repeated` -- the codex seat
cited it, the manual was fetched into `_scratchpad/` and the line read (`vmesbcp2.txt:4629`).  Two seats had rightly
called the fold unestablished before the manual was on disk.

Recorded alternatives: the codex seat's ONE latch for the whole site, writes only (not adopted: a driver scanning
registers should see each distinct one announced; both forms are bounded).  Corrections to the option set from this
round: `return 0` denotes a FAILED TRANSACTION, not inherently unmapped hardware (an IACK cycle with no interrupt
pending times out on the real part).  Disclosed: the in-word bytes are the interior of IMPLEMENTED counters, declined
here as a width/alignment matter (`pcc2widecompose`), not claimed as unimplemented registers; the IACK offsets
0x23/0x25 are declined like the rest -- modelling them on the SCCRXIACK shape would open two new entries into the
C040 path, so `pcc2c040kill` goes first (filed as a cross-round obligation); per-instance latch scope is not
provable by two fresh sessions (each is a new process) -- a two-instance fixture is filed.

## The detector as it shipped at PASS 2 (`regress/pcc2_default_probe.py`, 23 rows then; 46 now -- see the pass-2 and pass-3 sections; gate 14 pins all 46)

Controls: `live`, `devsig chipid`, `sccerr rdawr` (cased sibling), `genctl rt`, `t1cmp word rt` (the cased arms are
untouched), `put b ctl` + `put b ctl msg` (the debugger path never reaches the arm).  Survival: `named wr`, `named rd`
(all eighteen named offsets in ONE session per direction -- valid because the fix has no per-offset branch;
`named wr msg` localises), `inword wr`, `unnamed wr`, `alias 0x6a`.  Disposition: `ieicr rdawr`, `ieerr rdawr` (0x0,
not the stored byte), `named rd srvd` (the read announce says SERVED, never ignored).  Latch: `named wr msg` 18,
`named rd msg` 18, `latch sameoff` 1, `latch twooff` 2, `latch rw one` 1.  Text: `alias msg` (the announce names the
FOLDED offset), `dir wr text`, `dir rd text`.  The pty helper is the width probe's, extracted at run time -- the
frozen instrument is therefore a PAIR (both files copied beside the table).

## Pass 2 (nine seats on the real diff, `_scratchpad/panel_20260905_055656`): the 23-row detector was BELOW THE FLOOR, six ways

**Roster.**  codex (GPT-6 Astra, max), grok, kimi (the CLI stalled on the 54 KB pointer form -- 4.5 KB of paging
monologue, no answer, `kimi.stall_pointerform.txt` -- and was RE-FIRED ONCE with the 19 KB packet inline; it then
answered), glm and deepseek (thinking-burned on the full packet -- `ollama_*.burn.txt` -- and answered 2 KB
one-question mini packets), minimax, Opus 5 and Fable 5 (Agent seats; answers preserved as `opus5.txt`, `fable5.txt`).
agy DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED (measurement reserve).  Five seats said PASS or GO (kimi, minimax, glm, deepseek; Fable
GO-WITH-CHANGES, provisional); three said NOT CLOSE (codex, grok, Opus).  **Count the arguments: the three carried
measurements or predictions the five had not tested, and the Opus seat's two were MEASURED in its own scratch clone
against the frozen instrument pair (md5-verified equal to the live one).**  The fix itself every seat held right:
the fold bounds the shift (`uint64_t`, `%= 0x40`), `break` reaches the one `return 1`, the latch words are separate
fields both zeroed at DEVINIT, no cased arm is touched -- and, as Opus put it, the arm can only add output where the
old code called `exit(1)`, so no boot that works today can regress -- a sentence with a NARROW warrant (codex, pass 3):
it says only that no previously successful trace entered the arm, not that the surviving arm is boot-validated.

**The six escapes of the 23-row instrument** (every one a clause-(d)-shaped edit of the new arm; the first two
MEASURED at 23/23, the rest predicted from the row list and measured in table 3 below):

| seat | mutant | why 23 rows could not see it |
|---|---|---|
| Opus (MEASURED 23/23) | the read announce's value `-> 0` (one token) | `named rd srvd` counts the PHRASE `served 0x`, never the value; no row served a nonzero byte |
| Opus (MEASURED 23/23) | member 6 on the LATCHED path: `} else if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE) pcctwo_reg[ra] = idata;` | both `rdawr` rows store ONCE to a fresh offset in a fresh process; the latch state was built by `sameoff`/`twooff`/`rw one` and observed on the COUNT channel only |
| grok | the latch SET conditioned on writes | the bit-set cell was reached only through a WRITE (`rw one`); two reads at one offset had no row -- the setter's direction is a third axis the (writeflag x latch) 2x2 hides |
| grok | `if (len != 1) exit(1);` -- the removed kill was width-agnostic, so this is a PARTIAL reinstatement | every default-path row was `st.b`/`ld.bu`; the pass-1 PRETABLE's own SIBLING PARITY sentence said "byte-and-wide" and no row drove wide |
| codex | `|=` `->` `=` at the latch update (forgets earlier bits when a new offset announces) | A,A and A,B and W,R never REVISIT an offset after another has announced; A,B,A wants 2 and the mutant prints 3 |
| Fable | `if (relative_addr == 0x06) exit(1);` -- a re-kill at an offset the rows never drove | writes drove 27 of the 43 offsets and reads 18 (codex's count); the pass-1 contract had DISCLOSED the sampling |

**The diagnosis, from the pass-1 PRETABLE's own GUARD-FIELD line:** *"they disagree only in the latch's own state,
which the sameoff/twooff/rw-one rows build"* -- true, and the state was observed on one channel (the announce count)
while the mutant that matters (Opus M_O2) changes the OTHER channel (the read-back value) in exactly that state.  The
guard/body check found the cell and the row was written against the wrong observable.  And codex found a product
defect the rows could not: the read announce RELOADED `pcctwo_reg[relative_addr]` after the response was copied, and
the SIGALRM tick writes back the two COUNT words (`dev_pcc2.c` `write32(&d->pcctwo_reg[PCCTWO_T1COUNT]..` and T2COUNT)
-- so for the six bytes inside those two words the announced byte could differ from the served one while a counter
runs.  `"the array's default, NOT a computed value"` was therefore also wrong for those six.  **Pass 3 narrowed and
settled this in three readings.**  grok: the tick only READS the compare words and CEN is off at init, so under this
instrument -- `srvd val` lives in T1CMP's interior -- `data[0]` and a reload are the same byte, and `srvd val text` pins
the constant-0 mutant, NOT the reload (Opus then MEASURED the reload mutant at a clean sweep; disclosed in the contract).
Fable: the mid-handler race is unreachable because ticks run between guest instructions -- REFUTED by reading
`src/core/timer.c`: `timer_tick(int signal_nr)` IS the SIGALRM handler and calls `timer->timer_tick(timer, timer->extra)`
directly, and `dev_pcc2.c` registers `pcc_timer_tick` with `timer_add`, so the pcc2 tick is signal-driven and can land
anywhere, the copy-to-announce gap included.  Fable's SECOND reason needs no timing and is added to the comment: on the
#119 END-SPAN path the read is zero-filled while the array byte is kept, so a reload would announce a value the guest
did not receive (Opus adds a third backstop: `memory_rw.c` `#95` pre-zeroes the buffer before device dispatch).
`data[0]` is definitionally what was served -- the right operand under every reading.

**The repair (one diff, class closure -- the repair-chain amendment: consecutive cells of one class are closed
together, not one per pass).**  PRODUCT: both announces carry `(len %d)`; the read announce prints `data[0]` -- the
byte actually SERVED -- with a comment saying why.  DETECTOR, 36 rows (+13): `latch rd rd` and `latch rd wr` complete
the setter x tester product (W,W `sameoff`; W,R `rw one`; R,R; R,W); `latch aba` pins accumulation across offsets;
`sameoff val` reads back after the SECOND write (the latched path's disposition); `srvd val` + `srvd val text` serve
a byte the GUEST wrote (a word store through the cased T1CMP arm puts 0x34 at 0x05) and pin the announced value;
`wide wr` (+`msg`) and `wide rd` (+`srvd`) drive `st.w`/`ld.w` at uncased word-aligned offsets and pin the width
text; `inword wr`/`unnamed wr` now drive all 12 / all 13, and `inword rd`/`unnamed rd` read them -- **every one of
the 43 uncased offsets is written once and read once**; `wr declined` pins the word.  Row names stay under 14
characters (the gate's `%-16s` anchor).  RECORDS (the L4s the seats named): the kill-table header's `c76e053a ==
live` (run 1's md5 against run 2's table; the live probe was `a96b8bcf`); "three predictions exact" (four); the
M_EXIT diagnosis (its 16-row red SET was right, only the numeral and the derived score were wrong); "would have
shipped green and counted nothing" (the gate FAILED 25/844 and caught it); the `alias 0x6a` row saying "not proven
of the real part" beside a docstring citing Table 6-1; `unnamed wr` describing an overrun M_BACKED's end-span guard
prevents; "four arms up" (ten case blocks); "no guest reaches these offsets" (the witness IS a guest -- limited to
the inspected OpenBSD driver paths); "unnamed" made explicit as "the fork header has no label" (the manual names
0x39 as SPEED's second byte and 0x3b as PRTDATA's low byte -- codex).  Pass-2 mini-packet findings adopted: the
announce under-described a wide read (deepseek, grok, Opus, codex all named it) -- fixed by the width label.
Rejected: minimax's "unsafe" label on the M_RDKILL prediction miss (a predicted-green row that went red is the
SAFE direction, by the round's own rule).  Recorded, not adopted: codex's per-instance latch point is `pcc2latchinst`
(filed); Opus noted there is NO mvme88k boot rig (`grep -l mvme regress/*.sh` is empty), so the two gate-14 probes are
this device's entire coverage -- a fact for the queue, not this round.

## The findings, each checked from the tree before it was credited

1. **The enumeration was false for five arms** (Astra).  The contract listed GENCTL, VECBASE, SCCICR, SCCTX, SCCRX,
   SCSIICR, SCCERR, PSCALEADJ, MASK as arms with "NO `if' on state or idata".  **Five of them test their HUH?
   bits**: `dev_pcc2.c:464` VECBASE `idata & ~0xf0`, `:565` SCCICR and `:579` SCCTX `& ~0x1f`, `:593` SCCRX
   and `:613` SCSIICR `& ~0xdf` -- on the COMPOSED idata (the `if' lines, MEASURED by grep at the time of this
   sentence; the block first cited the pre-edit `fatal()' lines, and a first correction subtracted one from stale
   numbers -- the fable5 pass-13 seat had the right ones).  Every wide value the rows drove at them (0x0303,
   0xaab8, the rb4/rb8 lanes) has bits outside the mask -- and this block first said `&& (idata & ~mask)` at any
   of the five would SWEEP the 242-row table clean, five open cells, L2.  **MEASURED FALSE in part 13 (M_HUHV
   249/251, `latch all zero` red):** the six `latch all*` rows write 0x0000 / 0x0001 / 0x0003 (as h, w, d, forward
   and reversed) at every block and count twelve announces; 0x0000 is HUH?-clear at VECBASE (0x0001 and 0x0003 have
   bit 0 set, outside 0xf0 -- this paragraph first said 'two rows, 0x0000 and 0x0001, at these arms', which the
   kimi-k3 and deepseek seats caught), and all three are HUH?-clear at the 0x1f/0xdf arms -- so the partition WAS
   HELD, by
   announce-count channels the enumeration did not know it had.  Astra had said exactly this ("existing rows
   may discharge their partitions; the enumeration must actually show that") and the main loop wrote the
   sweep as a fact anyway.  The enumeration L4 stands (five arms called "no `if'"); the five `rbq` rows add the
   LANDING channel (the readback of the stored masked value) -- a strengthening, not a floor repair -- and the
   grading is corrected from L2 to L4 + coverage.  *An enumeration is checked against the BODY and against the
   ROWS before a breach is declared; a clean sweep is a MEASUREMENT, never an inference.*
2. **"INT clear with a count pending -- UNREACHABLE" was unsupported, and its converse is a real state** (Astra).
   `pcc_timer_tick()` (`:180`) increments the counts from the host timer WITHOUT calling `reassert_interrupts()`;
   INT is set at the next `DEVICE_TICK` (`:389`), so the cell exists in that window -- not constructible by a
   probe, DISCLOSED, not "unreachable" (grok's pass-11 "reassert sets INT before any guard runs" was wrong).
   **And INT SET with count ZERO is constructible**: the TxICR body zeroes the count on an IEN-clear write and
   clears INT only on ICLR; reassert only SETS it.  The pass-11 enumeration dismissed INT as derived from the
   count.  (label, INT set, own count 0) is a reachable joint state of two body-read lvalues -- a floor cell under
   BOTH argued bounds -- and no row held it.  -> `pend2 zctl/rbz`, `pend1 zctl/rbz` (below), contract corrected.
3. **"Every held write sets at most one of the three" was false** (Astra): 0x0018 sets IEN and ICLR.  Contract
   reworded; the kill logic was unaffected (a single-axis conjunct on any one bit still lands one write).
4. **The product comment "every arm uses `idata'" was false** (Astra): SCCERR stores a constant, IPL ignores the
   value.  Comment corrected (ten of twelve; both decline too -- the neighbouring lanes have no home).
5. **The carrier and the CHANGELOG graded ONE finding two ways** (Astra): clause (d) said the pass-11 ICLR escape
   was "L1 construction", the pass-11 block says L2.  The CHANGELOG's is the ruling; the carrier corrected in
   place, root and tools copy.
6. **`pcc2huhflood`'s "`acc all` trips SCCICR/SCCTX" was false** (Astra): `0x10 & ~0x1f == 0`.  The correction
   written here first said "0x10 trips VECBASE (`& ~0xf0`) and TxCTL" -- ALSO FALSE: `0x10 & ~0xf0 == 0` (bit 4 is
   inside 0xf0).  0x10 trips TxCTL's `& ~7` and PSCALEADJ's unconditional print, and none of the five HUH? arms.
   Caught by the Opus pass-13 seat by arithmetic; the third "a correction is not safer than the thing it
   corrects" of this chain.  Filing corrected twice.
7. **"A debugger-visible read clears SCCRX INT" conflated two paths** (Astra): pcc2 is registered `DM_DEFAULT`,
   so the debugger's `dump` bypasses it; a GUEST read runs the side effect.  Addendum corrected.

Checked and NOT credited: Astra's "0xb8 & 0x04 == 0 -- the Opus derivation misclassified it" is true of the
seat's answer file and appears in no record (the fills already name lanes 0xdd and 0x44) -- but the VALID half of
the same finding, that the rb4/rb8 lanes 0xdd/0x44 DO carry COVF so "held at NO cell" was false, drove the

   (`machine_mvme88k.c:106` installs `unreadable` at the ie0 address 0xfff46000; `if_ie.c:407-409` fails its

   (the register array already backs every offset and the memcpy read path already serves it) / FAULT.

every idata bit the body tests is written both clear and set -- because the bare state floor does not catch
`M_ICLR` (an idata-bit x state joint) and would grade it debt while the record grades it L2.  Multi-axis idata
joints stay clause-(e) debt.  **Astra dissents** for the Opus strength-t covering array and is recorded, not

here ("`t` is a judgment input": FALSE, `t` is the body's longest conjunction and is read off the code):
(i) COST -- TxICR has seven binary axes and a strength-4 array over them is tens of cells per arm, each a pty
write+readback, so the 2^k objection arrives by another door; (ii) a covering array certifies that a tuple
OCCURS, not that an observable differs -- it cannot be the floor without the CHANNEL obligation doing the work.  Under
the adopted floor, finding 2 is a floor cell no row held (M_ZINT2/M_ZINT1 red ONLY their new rows: an L2
repair in-round), while finding 1's cells were HELD by the announce-count rows (measured; its rows are a
channel strengthening under L4, as corrected above).  Carrier amended (root + tools copy).

first carried.**  The `latch all*` family -- six announce-count rows that write 0x0003 / 0x0001 / 0x0000 (as
halfword, word and dword, forward and reversed) at EVERY block and want twelve announces -- drives HUH?-CLEAR values

register bit 3 is dead, the same class as bits 6-7.  The original sentence had been right and the
accepted correction made it false: *a correction is not safer than the thing it corrects*, and one AND
would have kept it.  Reverted in the contract, the pass-10 block and the carrier.  The other fifteen
held (fable5: all defensible; grok: all check; codex: #2 carried a false premise -- a C `int` is finite
-- which the carrier now says differently; deepseek: #13's wording contradicted #5 -- the VALUE

## H1 -- the rule's own author ruled against its letter

The held question: does the adopted rule -- the cross-product of the body-tested partitions -- demand
rows for the ICLR, INT and 0xe0 partitions the pass-10 repair disclosed by count (112 of 128 cells)?

* **Read literally, yes** (codex, glm, minimax, deepseek): "governs what a landed write DOES, not
  whether it lands" is no exclusion -- an extra conjunct on ICLR or 0xe0 at the GUARD changes whether
  the write lands exactly as IEN does, and IEN was rowed.  codex's constructive census: 96 reachable
  cells at guard entry (two labels, two opposite-timer states, eight idata classes, three stable target
  states), the 32 "count pending, INT clear" cells reachable only through an unmeasured interleaving.
* **The flagship seat, asked to be harder on its own rule than on anyone, bounded it:** the rule
  ENUMERATES joint cells wherever the body distinguishes them; the FLOOR -- the cells a row is OWED for
  -- is the cross-product of the guard's dominating predicates with the device-STATE lvalues the fix's
  own repair path reads that are jointly reachable through its own data flow.  The bits of the single
  value being written are single-operand MARGINALS, not floor.  At TxICR: {label} x {p1} x {p2}, eight
  cells, all rowed by pass 10; the idata joints are clause-(e) debt.  The letter, it said, is 2^k in the
  `if`-count and compounds across twelve arms -- `#392` in the rule's clothes.  Adopted, and written
  into the carrier as the correction of its own one-day-old paragraph.
* **grok's generating set is what the debt costs when it has a warrant:** per idata axis, a set/clear
  pair at every rowed pending cell, so any single-axis extra conjunct reds; unreachable partitions
  disclosed with the derivation (INT clear with a count pending: the tick increments only under IEN and
  `reassert_interrupts` sets INT before any guard runs).
* **The measuring seat's bound, put beside Fable's for pass 12 (the remaining split):** axes = the
  lvalues the body's code makes DECISIVE -- tested in an `if` OR used as an index or selector (which puts
  the T1/T2 axis in at TxCTL, where `relative_addr` is an RMW index no `if` tests); demand = a COVERING
  ARRAY of strength t, t = the longest conjunction the body itself writes (four here), cost O(2^t log k)
  rather than 2^k; disclose BY STRENGTH -- "kills every conjunction of at most t of the N axes" -- which is
  falsifiable and would have made the pass-11 escape unwritable; t and the axis list are read off the diff
  once and no pass may raise t.  It withdrew its own pass-10 "demand INCREMENTAL" as having no stopping
  rule.  Three consecutive passes found ONE class of breach -- an unvaried axis crossed with a varied one,
  190 -> 194 -> 203 -- so the class-closure amendment says the next repair owes THE ENUMERATION across the
  arms, not another cell; the seat derived (not measured) that at TxCTL the rule enumerates {COVF} x
  {idata & ~7} with two of four cells unheld.
* **The measuring seat built the disclosed cell:** `&& !(pending_timer2 && (idata & PCC2_TTIRQ_ICLR))` at the TxICR guard scored **203/203, a TOTAL
  ESCAPE**, on its own clone (`pass11_seats_20260904/opus/M_ICLR.out`; predicted at 16:56 before the
  16:59 mutate script), with a POSITIVE CONTROL proving the write LANDS rather than the mutant never
  reaching the binary -- mutant `CONTROL_RB=0x13, DECL=0` against baseline `0x31, DECL=1`: the store
  gives 0x33, the strobe clears INT and decrements the pending count to 0, reassert leaves INT clear.
  *Entering the cell corrupts the register and silently consumes a pending timer interrupt, with all
  203 rows green.*  A `BASE2` run on the post-edit instrument (md5 12c7a97b) also read 203/203, closing
  a one-instrument straddle the seat reported on itself: its runner re-copied the live probe between
  BASE and the mutant while the main loop applied docstring-only corrections at 17:12 -- seven text
  lines, 203 identical (name, want) pairs, but a class worth naming: **a driver that re-copies its
  instrument straddles any edit, and the main loop should not edit a probe while a seat measures it.**

**Disposition.**  The floor is Fable's; the generating set is cheap (twelve wide writes appended to
three existing sessions, no new session).  **The GRADING is the Opus seat's: L2, a floor breach repaired
in-round, not debt-with-a-warrant** -- by the round's own pass-3 sentence, written into the probe by that
seat, that *a disclosure cannot discharge a floor clause, or every breach becomes a sentence*, and
because the cell sits inside the closure on every bound anyone proposed (the adopted product, Fable's
data-flow floor once the ack path is read as state the fix's own repair touches, Opus's strength-4 or
strength-2 array).  The repair is identical under either grading; the record has to say which holds,
and it is the stricter one.  The contract now says, by name, what is floor, what is held beyond it,
and what is disclosed and why.  The pass-9 Opus dissent and minimax's R3 "correctly sensed
the exponentiality H1 had to fix" (fable5); the fix is the bound, not the dissent's arity cut.

## The repair

At every rowed pending cell -- `pend2` and `pend1` at both labels, `pendboth` at both -- the tested
bits of idata are now written both clear and set: IEN already (0x0000 / 0x0013), now ICLR (0x0018 =
IEN|ICLR: a landed write keeps IEN, and the strobe clears INT and decrements the count, so it reads
0x10) and the HUH? bits (0x0020: a landed write reads 0x20 at an armed ICR and 0x00 at an idle one,
zeroes the count, and PRINTS the HUH? line -- counted by a `huh` row per session as a second channel).
Twelve readbacks (`*c`, `*h` at each label) and three `huh` rows; the new writes are appended so the
existing readback indices do not move.  A landed 0x0020 reads the same 0x20 as a landed 0x0000 at an
armed ICR, which is why the `huh` rows exist: the readback alone would not separate `M_HI` from
`M_PENDBOTH`.  Under a count-conditioned mutant the order matters -- a landed 0x0018 decrements the count
and a landed 0x0000 or 0x0020 zeroes it, so the guard re-arms for the later writes -- and every
prediction in `PRETABLE_pass11.out` (Section 19, with the four mandated checks) derives the readbacks in
session order.  Rows with no mutant in the part-11 table are named there rather than left to be found.

## The verdicts (the nine-seat roster: seven reading seats answering plus the measuring seat; agy deliberately not fired)

The pass carried a RULE QUESTION by name -- does the clause-(d) closure include joint states of two
body-read lvalues -- with the pass-9 Opus dissent quoted verbatim.  Counting arguments, not seats:
seven of eight landed seats put the pair INSIDE the closure (fable5, codex, grok, glm, deepseek, the
kimi-k3:cloud substitute for the weekly-walled CLI; opus5 measured); minimax put it OUTSIDE the floor
"under the contract's letter" while calling the shipped row right anyway.  **The dissent's
discriminator failed three ways** (fable5, glm, the kimi substitute): plausibility is not derivable by
reading; the mutant was written and measured, so it is an edit someone writes; and "single-operand is
complete" is measurably false, since `&& idata != 2` is single-operand and escapes (disclosed, not
killed).  **And the main loop's own proposed bound -- pairs of body-read lvalues over a finite
reachable space -- was REJECTED by the flagship seat as self-refuting:** the counts are `int`, so
"finite" fails on its motivating case; "reachable guest state" would force rowing `idata == 2` that
the same record discloses; a PAIRS cap misses `#499`'s four axes.  grok reached the same three
objections independently.

**The rule adopted, from neither argued side** (fable5's sentence, codex's equivalence-class form):
a joint cell is in clause (d) exactly when the guarded body's OWN CODE distinguishes it -- each
lvalue at the partition the body's own tests induce; the enumerated cells are the CROSS-PRODUCT of
those partitions, never arbitrary boolean functions of the read-set; a value the body never tests as
a case is disclosed under clause (e).  Finite, derivable from the diff by reading the body's `if`s,
and it enumerates `#499`'s width x component x direction x position cells from `len`, `writeflag`
and `relative_addr`.  The De Morgan form of the gap it closes, from the kimi substitute: `!(p1 &&
p2)` is `p1 == 0 || p2 == 0` -- neither disjunct true of all its lvalue's held values, the
disjunction true in every row, so a per-lvalue disclosure test could never fire on it.  Written into
`CLAUDE.md` clause (d) (and the tracked copy) with this provenance.

{IEN}:** each of the three timer sessions (`pend1`, `pend2`, `pendboth`) now wide-writes at BOTH
labels with idata `0x0000` and `0x0013` (IEN|IL3, so a landed write reads 0x20 or 0x33 at an armed ICR
and 0x00 or 0x13 at an idle one -- never the preset), the idle timer's ICR preset to `0x11` first; nine readbacks (`pend2 rbi/rb1/rb1i`, `pend1
rbi/rb2/rb2i`, `pendboth rbi/rb1/rb1i`); the decl rows stay at 1 -- the announce is latched once per

the ICLR, INT and 0xe0 partitions (112 cells) -- they govern what a landed write DOES to the counts,
not whether it lands.  (This block first said "rowing them costs about thirty more wide writes" --

## The adjudication -- the chain does not close here, and the seat that measured the escape dissents from that

The stop condition closes the chain on the first VALID pass that finds zero floor breaches
surviving adjudication.  The diff was delivered in full, the roster is complete with its one miss
named, every seat stated its denominator -- and one in-closure predicate swept the table.  So
pass 9 is a pass that FOUND a breach, the repair below is new floor-bound material, and it owes
pass 10.

**The Opus seat argues AGAINST calling this a floor breach, and its argument is carried here
verbatim so the pass-10 panel adjudicates it rather than inherits my ruling:**

> the (d) rule's own test is "could a PLAUSIBLE future edit produce it"; `&& !(p1 && p2)' is not
> an edit anyone writes.  Every SINGLE-operand form is killed: `== 0' and `!x' by pend*, `< 2' by
> pendn*, `> 0' by `latch all' (pending is 0 there), and the T1/T2 cross forms by the opposite
> label's rows.
>
> admitting arbitrary BOOLEAN COMBINATIONS of the read-set makes the (d) space exponential in the
> number of body-read fields, which is exactly what the DEPENDS-ON bound ("finite, derivable from
> the diff by reading") exists to prevent.  Read as single-operand, the closure is complete; read
> as multi-operand, it is #392.
>
> row demand is PER ENUMERATED MUTANT, never per reachable state, so NO ROW IS OWED.
> => L4: one sentence in the enumeration -- "pending_timer1/2 are held SEPARATELY; no session arms
> both timers, so a predicate over the PAIR is outside the sample" -- and no new row.

**My disposition, provisional on the pass-10 roster: SHIP THE ROW, and put the RULE QUESTION to
the panel by name.**  Four reasons, none of them a vote.  (1) The joint cell is one of FOUR in a
finite two-by-two the class-closure amendment says to close in ONE diff -- "a cell of one state
space left empty ... leaving the symmetric cell open" is the exact shape `#499` paid three passes
for.  (2) It is the guest's ORDINARY state, not an exotic one: OpenBSD/mvme88k runs timer 1 as the
clock and timer 2 as the statclock, so a detector that never holds both pending never holds the
device in its steady state, whatever the mutant's plausibility.  (3) One pend-type session costs
about twenty-five seconds and is VALUE-stable once its callback lands (0x31 is fixed once INT sets),
though starvation-sensitive like every free-running row; the load hazard in the VALUE was the
ovfhi shape, repaired below).  (4) The asymmetry: a surplus row costs four lines; a missing one
makes "shipped a detector with the fix" false about the fix's own repair.  **The bound I propose
for the rule -- PAIRS of body-read lvalues, only where their joint space is finite and a cell is
a reachable guest state; arbitrary boolean combinations beyond that DISCLOSED -- is a question
for the flagship seat at the next boundary, not a ruling.**

# Round pcc2widthkills, pass 8 -- not the closing pass: the pass-7 breakpoint wait was inert, and one non-initial value per lvalue is not a domain

**2026-09-04.  Detector 171 -> 190 rows (this header said 186 until pass 9 caught it); the instrument's free-running wait now works and a
missed breakpoint invalidates its whole session; product code unchanged this pass.**

## What pass 8 found (eight answering seats of nine, agy deliberately not fired)

* **The pass-7 repair to `session()` did not do what its record said** (grok, codex; confirmed
  from the source).  The `(cmd, wait, until)` tuple was unpacked -- `c, w = c[0], c[1]` -- BEFORE
  its third element was read, so `until` became the command's third character, present in the
  buffer at once, and the wait after `continue` returned immediately; the 20 s ceiling was dead
  code.  The pass-7 sentences claiming it were FALSE as implemented (L4).  Parts 7 and 7b passed
  because the queued commands are consumed after the breakpoint anyway -- a no-op wait that
  happened to be long enough on an idle host.  Fixed by reading the tuple before unpacking it.
  And codex measured the companion-row consequence in this round's own artifacts: under the
  bare-swap mutant the arming byte writes were declined, the loop never exited, `pend2 arm` said
  `no-breakpoint` -- and `pend2 decl` stayed GREEN beside it, graded from a phase never reached.
  So a missed token now INVALIDATES the session (no further probe command is sent to the running guest; only the quit) and
  every companion row reports the apparatus reason through `cval()` -- for the missed-token
  half; the DEATH half was labelled only by the rb rows until pass 9 gave `cval()` `alive`
  (Opus, pass 9) -- ; the residual unbounded
  `waitpid` after a failed kill is bounded too.
* **One non-initial value per lvalue is not its domain** (the kimi-k3:cloud substitute, glm,
  codex).  The overflow count was held at 1 (bit 4 only): `&& !(reg & 0xe0)` on the TxCTL guard
  passes every row.  A guest that re-arms the count each loop iteration overflows once per host
  callback and reaches count 8 in ~80 ms (hand-verified: 0x81) -> `ovfhi1 *` / `ovfhi2 *`.  The
  pending counts were held at 1: `&& pending < 2` passes every row; COC with compare 1 makes one
  callback add thousands (`pcc_timer_tick:231-236`; hand-verified) -> `pendn1 *` / `pendn2 *`.
  The value 0 was driven at SCCERR and T1ICR only -> `latch all zero`.
* **TxICR bit 2, an interrupt-level bit, was clear in every preset** (codex): a legal byte
  write 0x14 sets it and `&& !(reg & 0x04)` on the TxICR guard was predicted 171/171 -> `rb
  t2icr il4` / `rb t1icr il4` (preset 0x17).  "Bits 0-4 by presets" was false (kimi: bit 3 is
  never written; the mask is 0x17).
* **Dead bits are dead, not "full bit-domain"** (deepseek, minimax, grok): TxCTL bits 2-3 and
  TxICR bits 3, 6-7 are set by no model writer -- TxCTL 2-3 only through the filed pcc2counter8
  raw copy -- so a guard conditioned on them is E; the listing now names them with the writer
  census, and says why no row is built on a filed defect's path.
* **The GENCTL rows were modified after the fall-through's last measurement** (glm): under
  `M_W4FALL_ALL` the GENCTL rb4/rb8 rows are that mutant's killing rows, so "additions cannot
  un-kill" did not reach them.  Re-measured in part 8, now killing by value (0xd9 / 0x40).
