  `break;' -> `if (len < 4) break;' at all twelve guards announces every wide write and then
  LANDS the 4- and 8-byte ones: **118/118**.  `latch all w' and `latch all d' count the
  announce; every readback row in the detector was `st.h` / `put h`, len 2.  The contract

## The repair -- forty-one rows, three classes closed at every block

The class-closure amendment applied: passes 5 and 6 both found "device state no row held
non-initial at a wide write", so the guard's operand space is ENUMERATED from the twelve bodies
and written into the contract -- `pcctwo_reg[relative_addr]' (`rb *', `rb4 *', `rb8 *'),
`d->warned' (`rb2 *'), `pending_timer1/2' and the TxICR INT bit (`pend1 *', `pend2 *'); out of
closure and disclosed: `reg[IPL]', `cur_int_vec[]'.

* `brd2 *' x9, `brd pscale noig', `brd ipl noro' -- set a byte, read it, read it AGAIN, at
  every storing block (guest path, odd blocks included).
* `rb4 *' x9, `rb8 *' x9 -- byte preset, `put w' / `put d', readback (operator rows: only
  SCCERR is 4-aligned, so a guest word store reaches no other block); `pscale noig4|8',
  `ipl noig4|8' (the print-only bodies at zero); `latch samew', `latch samed' (announce-once
  per width).
* `pend1 arm|decl|rb', `pend2 arm|decl|rb' -- ARM a timer (compare 1, count 0, IEN|IL1, CEN)
  and FREE-RUN to a breakpoint while the guest polls TxICR with `bb0 5, r4, -1' until
  `reassert_interrupts()` sets INT; the 0x31 read after the loop is both the liveness control
  and the device signature (a mis-encoded bb0 reads 0x11); then the wide write with the count
  non-zero (guest `st.h` at T2ICR; `put h` at odd T1ICR).  session() now accepts a
  `(cmd, wait)` tuple so `continue` waits for its breakpoint.  Shape verified once by hand on
  the restored `/tmp/gxopus_p6` fix binary before the rows were written.

## Two instrument defects the table caught, both mine

* **`rb t1ctl' reddened on the fix** (BASE 95/96): the row wanted the input string "0x03"
  and the debugger prints "0x3".  The value was right.  Fixed; part 3b BASE 96/96.
* **`acc all' could not see the arm it was written for.**  Its first form used the debugger's
  `put b'; a guard grown to refuse bytes at PSCALEADJ escaped it TWICE with the mutation
  PROVEN in the source and the binary newer than the source (3b's proof lines).  `put b'
  calls memory_rw with NO_EXCEPTIONS, and memory_rw.c dispatches a device only under
  `!no_exceptions || (flags & DM_READS_HAVE_NO_SIDE_EFFECTS)'; pcc2 registers DM_DEFAULT.
  So twelve byte writes reached no arm and the row was VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION -- the CHANNEL
  rule's failure condition, caught by the table.  `put h/w/d' go through store_Nbit_word and
  do reach the arms, which is why every other cardinality row worked.  The row is now twelve
  GUEST `st.b' stores, legal at every offset, and the contract states the `put b' fact.

## The pre-table block, run this time, and what it yielded

`killtable2_20260903/PRETABLE.out` was written at 13:07 BEFORE table 2 (Section 0 records
honestly that table 1 had none -- the third recorded skip of the mandate).  Its guard-field /
body-field question yielded a row nothing else would have: the guard reads `len`, the body

## The ruling, and its measurement

Section 2 of that block disclosed that PSCALEADJ/SCCICR/SCCRX/SCSIICR had no readback, so a
guard that ANNOUNCES and then lets the halfword land would escape -- and called it "the
sentence owed".  The builder asked whether a disclosure can discharge a floor clause.  **Ruling:
it cannot.**  Clause (d) is a floor ("the guard kept, its effect removed"); clause (e) governs
claims ABOVE it, or every breach becomes dischargeable by a paragraph.  Four rows were added
before any measurement (Section 5), and the builder then measured both halves: the four
fall-throughs are **four total sweeps of the 78-row detector** and **four one-row kills on the
82-row repair** -- `rb sccicr` 0x18 (0xb8 & 0x1f), `rb sccrx` 0x98 (0xb8 & 0xdf), `rb scsiicr`
0x98, and for PSCALEADJ, whose write body stores nothing and only prints, `op pscale noig`
counting the "ignored" line at zero.  The channel is matched to what each arm's body does;
a count-based row cannot see this shape because the announce survives by construction.

## Round pcc2widthkills -- twelve width kills become a direction split, and the tree knew the width was legal all along

`DEVICE_ACCESS(pcc2)` had **twelve** `if (len != 1)` blocks that ended the host on a
guest-chosen access width: ten `fatal(); exit(1);` kills and two `#119` function-static
latches.  An ordinary aligned halfword load of a documented register was enough.  Same class as
`#337` and `#497`, at the largest site count yet.  Only consumer: the MVME187.

### Test-first, and the witness took three runs to be honest

`regress/pcc2_width_witness.py`, rung 3 on the unmodified `-E mvme88k -e mvme187`, real MC88100
instructions through real decode.  Run 1 was **0/10 for the wrong reason** -- `-e 187` is not a
subtype alias and the pure-RAM control said so.  Run 2 had a witness-side defect: the liveness
loads read a scratch word no earlier instruction had stored.  Run 3, preserved: **4/10 on the
committed build, all four controls green**, three aligned accesses each `exit1`.

### The design pass changed the design, on six of nine seats

Two Opus firings died on API 529 and two grok firings on CLI errors, each retried once; agy was
spent on the concurrent `#500` panel as its builder.  The six that answered converged, and the
main loop verified every checkable claim by reading:

* **The tree already knew wide access is LEGAL.**  `mvme_pcctworeg.h` says the registers "can be
  accessed as bytes, two-bytes, or four-bytes."  Neither my brief nor the 2026-09-02 adjudication
  cited it.  That refutes FAULT as a model and reframes DECLINE as refusing a hardware-legal
  access, which the code comment now says plainly.
* **DELETE is measurably wrong for writes.**  `memory_readmax64` composes big-endian, so
  `(uint8_t) idata` is the HIGHEST-address lane: `st.h 0xAABB` to GENCTL would store VECBASE's
  byte.  Mandatory mutant, with a readback row -- and it killed (`M_DELETE`, below).
* **My premise about the write arms was wrong in both clauses** (glm): seven of the ten mask,
  read-modify-write or clear, and SIX call `reassert_interrupts()`, not two.  And from that the
  cleanest justification of the split: *reads copy raw bytes in address order and are
  width-correct by construction; every write arm uses a composed value that is "the addressed
  byte" only at length one.*
* **The seven odd-offset arms are OPERATOR-reachable**, and the split over whether to fix them
  was settled by measurement rather than argument: the debugger's `put h` at an odd address
  warns, stores anyway, and the guard ended the host
  (`artifacts/pcc2widthkills/operator_reach_20260903.out`).  So they have an executable row, the
  precedent objection dissolves, and all twelve are converted.
* IPL sits at 0x3e, EVEN -- its `#119` arm was guest-reachable and printed "ignored" about a
  read the memcpy had already served.  Folded in with MASK: twelve bits, not ten.
* An unnamed option member, per-lane COMPOSE, is filed as `pcc2widecompose` with its hazard
  (it must live inside the arms, or it re-kills a legal counter write).

### The fix

`src/devices/dev_pcc2.c`: a twelve-member auto-incremented latch enum with `PCC2_W_NBITS`
(the fork records the `1 << N` form as collision-prone), a `warned` field on the instance,
one helper, and every block becomes `if (len != 1 && writeflag == MEM_WRITE) { decline;
break; }` -- reads fall through to the copy that already served them.  Live `exit(1)`:
**13 -> 3**, and the three left are cited: `pcc2c040kill` (a LEGAL byte write of 0x04 to
GENCTL still ends the host -- NEWLY FILED, HIGH), `pcc2defaultkill`, the interrupt-common
default.

### The detector and its table

`regress/pcc2_width_probe.py`, 60 rows: 4 controls; 24 survival pairs at the five reachable
blocks, read and write, word at SCCERR; value rows proving a wide read composes lanes in
address order; readback rows proving a declined write left BOTH lanes untouched; latch rows in
both directions; 10 accept rows proving the legal width still lands through each arm's own
mask with no message; 14 operator-path rows for the seven odd arms.  Row trap designed out:
every GENCTL lane value keeps bit 0x04 clear.  Gate 14 ARM: **626 checks, 0 FAIL, pcc2 60/60
on its first post-fix run.**

## Round #500 pass 14 -- the closing pass found a FAMILY, one session closed it, and the contract now says what rows cannot

Pass 13 was the enumeration-verifying pass the class-closure amendment prescribes.  **Nine
of nine seats answered** -- the burned one on a 3 KB re-fire, the fourth measured instance of
the burn being the brief -- and the enumeration did not survive them.

### What the readers found, six of them independently

`|| (op == 0x00000000)`.  The bit-mask family is genuinely closed, and every seat that walked
it confirmed the closure with the full denominator of 2^32-1 masks rather than trusting the
brief.  But the EQUALITY family is open: only nine values ever appear on a second reach of the
decline, so equality on any other value is invisible -- and the one value a guest reaches with
**no register write at all** is POINT, the reset value, this round's own headline case.

Two seats also struck a word from my premise.  "A second announcement of the SAME op literal"
is wrong: `two once` stores two different literals and observes through a prefix.  The correct
criterion, from the measuring seat, is *observable iff some session reaches `default:` at least
twice with the predicate true on a later reach* -- and asking about ALL state at the second
reach is what exposed the next thing.

### What the measuring seat found, and the readers could not

**Four more clean sweeps of the shipped 47-row detector, MEASURED**, two of them a family:

    M_XFER      || (drawmode & DE_DRAWMODE_XFER_EN)   47/47   control measured both ways
    M_SRCMODE   || (src_mode & 0x00001c00)            47/47
    M_OPEQ      || (op == 0x07000000)                 47/47   -> contract
    M_FG        || (fg & 0x80)                        47/47   -> contract

> **`draw_primitive()` reads eleven registers.  Five of them -- `drawmode`, `src_mode`,
> `dst_mode`, `rop`, `stipple_mode` -- were identically ZERO on every path that reached the
> decline**, because the only sessions that wrote any of them used implemented ops.  A bypass
> on any bit of any of the five was invisible to all 47 rows, and the transfer-enable bit is
> one real blit code sets: a guest-reachable flood on an ordinary path.

**The brief's own scoping hid it.**  It asked for predicates on values "the guarded BODY
reads".  `drawmode` is read by the enclosing FUNCTION, above the switch.  Whether that is
inside clause (d)'s DEPENDS-ON bound is filed as a **rule question** rather than decided here:
the bound says "the guarded body", but the carrier's own exemplar of a qualified condition uses
`writeflag`, likewise an enclosing-function value.  The detector is repaired regardless.

### THE REPAIR: one session, three rows, and a contract

`dec regs` sets all five registers to all-ones and draws POINT twice.  Every register bit-test
fires on the second reach, and so does `op == 0x00000000`.  Measured (table 12, with the one
instrument row subtracted -- see below):

| cell | kind | pre-repair | post-repair |
|---|---|---|---|
| `M_XFER` `M_SRCMODE` | CLOSE | 47/47 escape, measured | `dec regs` red |
| `M_DSTMODE` `M_ROP` `M_STIPPLE` | CLOSE | derived open | `dec regs` red |
| `M_OPEQ0` (the reset value) | CLOSE | predicted 47/47 by six seats | `dec regs` red |
| `M_OPEQ07` `M_FG80` | **LIMIT** | 47/47 | **still 50/50 -- as the contract now declares** |
| `M_FLOOD_B25` | CONTROL | 3 rows red | same 3 rows red |

**The two LIMIT cells are the point of the contract.**  Equality on an arbitrary value and a
sub-bit of an operand are infinite or combinatorial families; each new two-draw session pins one
member.  The class-closure amendment's own instruction is to write into the CONTRACT which cells
are deliberately not covered, so a later escape there is *outside the contract, as stated*
rather than a breach.  The probe's contract now lists what is closed (every op bit-mask, op
inequality, the five registers, `op == 0`, latch bits 0-8, operand zero/nonzero) and what is
deliberately not (other equalities, mask conjunctions within no single literal, range
comparisons, operand sub-bits, cross-field compounds).  Both limits are MEASURED, not asserted.

### The instrument caught its own defect, and the driver did not

BASE measured **49/50**: `dec regs set`, the new precondition witness, was red on the fixed
build.  Its want was 1, copied from a one-draw session; the entry announcement prints once per
draw and this session draws twice.  **That is the canary working** -- a precondition row whose
want does not match its session shape reds on BASE before any mutant is scored.  Corrected to
want=2 in the live probe; the table scored its frozen copy, so every cell carries that one row
red and is read with it subtracted; a single BASE re-run against the corrected instrument is
preserved beside the table.

> **And the driver proceeded past a BASE that was not full score.**  Pass 13 found that the
> table-11 driver's control was a comment with no refusal behind it; this is the second
> instance.  Filed as a driver-practice item: a table whose BASE is not full should say so
> loudly, and whether it should abort is a judgement (aborting here would have thrown away

## Round #500 pass 12 -- the panel refuted my pass-11 answer, MEASURED two clean sweeps, and three seats found the red I had left one line below the one I fixed

Pass 11 adjudicated the chain and reported "no floor breach".  **Its own panel measured two.**

### *** THE L2: A LATCH BYPASS ON SIX HIGH BITS SWEPT THE SHIPPED DETECTOR CLEAN ***

The measuring seat built the mutants and scored them against the shipped 47-row detector:

| mutant | score | rows red |
|---|---|---|
| `M_FLOOD_B25` | 44/47 | `two once`, `xlatch all`, `dec flood` |
| `M_FLOOD_B26` | 46/47 | `dec ops` |
| **`M_FLOOD_B27`** | **47/47** | *** TOTAL ESCAPE *** |
| **`M_FLOOD_B31`** | **47/47** | *** TOTAL ESCAPE *** |

**MY CRITERION WAS WRONG, IN THE ANSWER I HAD WRITTEN ONE PASS EARLIER.**  I said no green
control could exist because every bit is carried by some declining op.  The union claim is
true and **it is not the criterion.**  A latch bypass is only observable on a SECOND
announcement of the SAME op literal, so a row can red only if its session draws twice.  Three
sessions did.  The six `dec b*` rows I cited as proof are **single-draw and structurally
cannot red** -- and `dec b26` stores `0x05000000`, which IS bit 26, and stayed green.

> **Carrying a bit is not observing it.  I cited six rows that could not fire as evidence that
> no control was possible.**

And it is not benign: a bypass on bit 27 makes the device re-announce on every access to
`0x09000000`, a guest-writable value -- the exact log flood the `(once)` latch exists to
prevent, and a class this detector's own contract names.

### THE CLASS CLOSURE -- one line, NO new rows, and MEASURED over the whole open set

Third generation of one class (`TB` -> `B26` -> `B27`), so the carrier's amendment governs:
the repair owes the CLASS, not another cell.  Every `dec b*` op is `LINE|bit_N`, so **making
that loop two-draw closes bit 24 and bits 26-31 at once**, and the rows strengthen from "MUST
decline" to "MUST decline EXACTLY ONCE".

**Verified over all six previously-open bits, not the two that were demonstrated** -- the seat
MEASURED 27 and 31 and DERIVED 24, 28, 29, 30, and a closure that verifies two of six is a
cell repair in closure clothing:

## Round #500 pass 10 -- three defects, one shape: the empty cell of a 2x2, on three different axes

Pass 10 produced **three defects**, and the striking thing is that all three are the *same*
missing cell viewed along different axes.  Row count did not change: every fix made an
**existing row cover strictly more**, which is what a class closure looks like when it is got
right the first time.

|  | ONE draw | TWO draws |
|---|---|---|
| **op bits** | `dec low` | `dec flood` |
| **body operands** | `dec ops` *(was)* | **`dec ops` — was EMPTY** |
| **latch field** | `xlatch all` *(was)* | **`xlatch all` — was EMPTY** |

> **Every one was "I built the SILENCE case and not the FLOOD case."**  Three axes, three
> identical omissions, found by three different seats.  The failure is not inattention to a
> detail; it is a systematic blind spot about DIRECTIONALITY -- I build the case where
> something is wrongly suppressed and never the case where it is wrongly emitted.

### deepseek: my DISCLOSURE was false, which is worse than a hole

Pass 9 disclosed that `dec flood` covered a bypass on bit 16 only, and justified it as
**structural**: *"the bypass must be on a bit the REPEATED-DRAW op carries, so covering all 24
would need 24 two-draw sessions."*

**`dec low` already used `0x02ffffff`, which carries all 24 low bits.**  Put that op in the
two-draw session and a bypass on *any* low bit makes it announce twice.  **One session covers
all 24.**  It is the identical trick I had used on the silence side two passes earlier and
then explicitly ruled out here.

> **A disclosure with a false reason is worse than an open hole.**  An open hole invites
> someone to close it; a disclosure tells the next reader it is unclosable and closes the
> question.  Mine was one constant away from closed.

Measured in three directions: `M_FLOOD_TB` and `M_FLOOD_SK` (two *different* low bits) each
red `dec flood`; `M_FLOOD_B26` leaves it green, because bit 26 is clear in `0x02ffffff`.
**The green control had to MOVE** -- it was TB, and the widened op now legitimately reds on
TB, so leaving it there would have quietly made the honest half vacuous.

### kimi, codex and grok, independently: the operand 2x2 had an empty corner

`|| x1` -- FLOOD keyed on a **non-zero** body operand -- swept 47/47.  `dec ops` set the
operands but drew **once**, so a bypass still announced once; `dec flood` drew twice but left
the operands **zero**, so `|| x1` was false and the latch worked.  Neither could see it.

**Three seats stated the same missing corner and prescribed the same fix**: make `dec ops`
draw twice.  Then `&& !x1` gives zero announces and `|| x1` gives two -- **both red the row**,
closing the operand axis in both directions at once.  Controlled: `M_OPS_SILENCE` and
`M_OPS_FLOOD` each red it; `M_OPS_ROP` leaves it green, because `rop` is read by the
*enclosing function* and not by the latch body, so it is outside the row's claim.

*Three-way independent convergence is the only agreement that counts as evidence here, and it
landed on a gap I would have called closed an hour earlier.*

### grok, second axis: the same corner on the LATCH FIELD

No session both **pre-set a foreign `d->warned` bit** and **drew twice**.  `xlatch all`
pre-set bits 0-8 and drew once; `dec flood` drew twice and pre-set nothing.  So
`|| (d->warned & SGIRE_W_DE_LEN)` -- a predicate on the guard's own field, squarely inside
(d) -- bypassed the latch and flooded invisibly.  One extra draw closes it.

Controlled: `M_LF_DELEN` and `M_LF_TLBA` each red `xlatch all`.  **`M_LF_SELF` (the tautology
`!(w & X) || (w & X)`) reds FOUR rows** -- `two once`, `xlatch all`, `dec ops`, `dec flood` --
so the four two-draw sessions now form a mutually-reinforcing set.  Twelve defects ago there
was exactly one two-draw row.

> **This axis has NO green cell and the control says so** rather than inventing one.  Every
> bit in the enum is either pre-set by the session (so a bypass correctly reds) or is
> `SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP` itself (a tautology that floods unconditionally).  A green control I had
> to manufacture would be exactly the reassuring artifact this round has spent twelve defects
> learning to distrust.

### minimax: REFUTED by reading, and its own caveat named the check

It proposed an accept-side operand mirror (`acc tri mod`) while flagging what it could not
verify: *"which op value corresponds to which drawing primitive ... a seat that can grep the
fork should confirm before treating it as a build."*

**There is no TRIANGLE accept arm.**  The switch has three arms -- `DE_PRIM_LINE`,

## Round #500 pass 9 -- I stopped asking for mutants and asked which symmetry was half-closed; two seats found two

Eight passes had asked seats to find a mutant.  **Pass 9 handed them the failure pattern
instead** -- *"I close one side of a symmetry and leave its mirror open; which one is still
half-closed?"* -- and it was the highest-yield pass of the chain: **two seats, two different
half-closed symmetries, on different axes.**

### grok: the guarded body reads EIGHT values, and seven of them were always zero

The latch's body reads `op` **plus the seven the `fatal()` prints** -- `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`,
`fg`, `bg`, `pattern`.  Clause (d) admits an operand swap on any field the guarded body reads,
so `if (!(d->warned & SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP) && !x1)` is inside the enumeration -- and **every
decline session in the file left all seven at zero**, which the probe's own `declined()` helper
records verbatim (`x1=0 y1=0 x2=0 y2=0 fg=0x0 bg=0x0 pattern=0x00000000`).

> **The evidence was written into my own helper and I never read it as a coverage statement.**

*** AND THE SEAT NAMED HOW I WOULD BOTCH THE REPAIR, IN ADVANCE: *** *"do not pin only `x1` --
that would be pass 2-3 / 6-7 again; a row that only sets `x1=1` leaves `&& !fg` as pass 10."*
So `dec ops` sets **all seven**, and the control proves the class rather than the cell:
`M_QUAL_X1` **and** `M_QUAL_FG` each red `dec ops` alone.  Pinning only `x1` would have left
the `fg` form for pass 10 exactly as predicted.

*It also supplied the fact that would have cost a whole pass: `pattern` needs **bit 31
specifically**, because at reset `stipple_mode` is 0 and the strip chain is `>>= 31; <<= 31`,
keeping only that bit.  A naive non-zero stipple pattern still prints `0x00000000`.*

### codex: `dec low` closed conditional SILENCE and left conditional FLOODING open

```c
if (!(d->warned & SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP) || (op & DE_PRIM_RL))   /* the mirror of pass 8 */
```

A low-bit op **bypasses** the latch and announces on every draw.  It swept all 43 rows for a
structural reason: **every low-bit decline session performs exactly one draw**, so one message
is all there is to see either way; the only repeated-draw row, `two once`, uses ops with every
low bit clear.  Pass 8 closed the silence direction on low bits and left the flood direction on
the same bits untested -- **the same habit one level down.**

`dec flood` is `two once` with a low-bit op: two draws, exactly one announcement.

### *** THE FIRST CONTROL IN THIS CHAIN WITH A DELIBERATELY GREEN HALF ***

    M_FLOOD_RL   (op & DE_PRIM_RL)   bit 16 -> 46/47, dec flood RED
    M_FLOOD_TB   (op & DE_PRIM_TB)   bit 17 -> 47/47, dec flood GREEN

**The green is the honest half.**  `dec flood`'s op (`0x02010000`) has bit 17 clear, so a
bypass on TB cannot reach it; a row that reddened under *both* would be responding to
something other than what it claims -- "green for the wrong reason" inverted.

> **Every control before this pass asked only "does the row fire?".  None asked "does it fire
> ONLY when it should?"**  `M_FLOOD_TB` is now a permanent cell whose expected result is green.

**COVERAGE DEBT, DISCLOSED:** `dec flood` catches a bypass on bit 16, not on all 24.  The
asymmetry is structural, not an oversight -- the silence direction takes one op carrying all 24
bits because the qualification only has to *see* a bit, while the flood direction needs the
bypass on a bit the **repeated-draw** op carries.  Covering all 24 would need 24 two-draw
sessions.

> *** MEASURED FALSE BY PASS 10, ANNOTATED HERE IN PASS 11.  The paragraph above is kept as
> the dated record of what pass 9 believed, but it must not be read as standing: the
> repeated-draw op can simply BE the all-bits op, so ONE session covers all 24 and the pin
> moved to `0x02ffffff`.  A `grep` landing on this block found a confident "structural" claim
> with nothing marking it as overturned -- and this project's own finding is that a disclosure
> with a false reason is worse than an open hole, because it tells the next reader the gap is
> unclosable when it is one constant away from closed. ***

### deepseek: refuted by arithmetic, and its own last sentence did it

It proposed qualifying on bit 24, claiming "no row in the 43-row table has bit 24 set" -- then
closed with *"real decline ops like `0x05000000` have bit 24 set."*  Both cannot hold.
**Seven rows carry bit 24**, including all six `dec b*` (each is `LINE | bit_N`, and LINE *is*
bit 24), so the qualification reddens them rather than sweeping clean.

## Round #500 pass 8 -- the accept side carried all 24 low bits since pass 4; the decline side carried none

Pass 8 fired six seats.  **One found the eighth defect of this chain, and it is an asymmetry
I built in pass 4 and then walked past for four consecutive passes.**

### codex: qualify this round's OWN latch predicate with a bit of `op'

```c
if (!(d->warned & SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP) &&
    !(op & DE_PRIM_RL)) {
```

The canonical clause-(d) form -- `if (X)` becomes `if (X && Y)` on the predicate the fix
depends on -- and it **swept the 41-row detector clean**.  Every op this file sent to
`default:` had bit 16 CLEAR, so the guard was unchanged for all of them; the only bit-16-set
ops (`0x01ffffff`, `0x03ffffff`) enter implemented arms and never evaluate it.  Meanwhile a
real `DE_PRIM_TRIANGLE | DE_PRIM_RL` reaches `default:` and is **silently declined** -- the
announcement this round exists to make, gone, for exactly the ops a guest sets modifiers on.

> *** THE FINDING IS THE ASYMMETRY, NOT THE BIT.  `acc rect mod` and `acc line mod` have
> carried `0x??ffffff` since pass 4, specifically so any mask widening reds them.  The
> decline ops were `0x05000000`, `0x09000000` ... `0x81000000` and a bare `0x02000000` --
> **not one low bit set among them.**  I closed that direction on the accept side and left
> its mirror open on the decline side, in a file I have rewritten seven times since. ***

**Repaired with ONE row, not a row per bit:** `dec low` stores `0x02ffffff` -- still
`default:`, still declined, every low bit set -- so a qualification on **any** of them nulls
the announce and the row sees it.

**Negative-controlled in both directions** (`negctl_dec_low.out`): under codex's own mutant
`dec low` reds **and the six pre-existing `dec b*` rows stay GREEN**, which is what makes the
characterisation right rather than merely the row working.

Pass 7 fired six seats on a one-question brief.  **Three said DO NOT CLOSE, and two of them

### grok: `n25 rectset` matched an UNANCHORED SUBSTRING

Its oracle was `drawmode=0x200000` with nothing after it, and the device prints
`drawmode=0x%x` -- so it matches **inside** `drawmode=0x2000000`.  Swapping `XFER_EN` for the
TRIANGLE constant `0x02000000`, a value this probe already stores in its own `pt`/`tri` loop,
leaves the witness **satisfied while XFER is never enabled**.

Verified by computation before touching code:

    drawmode=0x200000   -> witness matches   (correct)
    drawmode=0x2000000  -> witness MATCHES   (the escape)
    drawmode=0x3000000  -> no match

> **It only ever worked because the pass-6 seat's mutant used `0x03000000`, which happens not
> to prefix-match.**  The row was one constant away from being vacuous the day it shipped.

**And this is a RE-RUN of a finding I was given in pass 4** -- decl rows counting a substring
shared with another string -- **which I fixed there and reintroduced here in new code.**
Anchored with a trailing ` src_mode=`, which the format string guarantees cannot extend.

because the guard holds, but because there is no LINE to diagnose.**

Closed by `n25 noxset`, whose oracle was chosen by DUMPING the session rather than reasoning:
it announces `op = 0x01ffffff, drawmode=0x0 src_mode=`, pinning both facts in one anchored
string.  **Negative-controlled against codex's own mutant: 40/41, that row alone, while

## Round #500 pass 6 -- two seats, two floor breaches, and a record that did not match its own artifact

Pass 6 was fired on a deliberately short brief (12 KB, three questions) after pass 5's 36 KB
packet burned a seat.  **It still refused the round**, and the two dissents were both right.

### codex: a one-token operand swap CLEAN-SWEEPS the 38-row detector

In the rectangle session, swap the drawmode store's value for a value already present in the
edited body -- `val=XFER_EN` becomes `val="0x03000000"`.  XFER is then never enabled, so
`n25 rect` counts zero **for the wrong reason** and stays green; and under `M_NARROW_25` the
folded rectangle reaches the LINE arm with XFER disabled, emits nothing, **and the intended
kill is defeated.**  Squarely inside clause (d)'s enumeration -- an operand swap on the edited
body.  L2, repaired in-round.

> **ITS Q3 IS THE PART THAT MATTERS, and it is a criticism of my whole pairing:** *"The panel
> treated a positive control in a DIFFERENT SESSION as proof that the rectangle session did
> something.  It is not."*  `n25 line` proves the LINE setup works in ITS session; `n25
> rectliv` proves only that the trailing load ran.  My comment claiming otherwise was false
> and is corrected.

**This is the `xlatch all` failure for the THIRD time in one round** -- a row green because
its set-up silently did nothing -- and I had built the repair for the second instance INTO A
DIFFERENT SESSION, where it cannot do the job.

**The repair is `n25 rectset`**, an IN-SESSION witness chosen by DUMPING the session's raw
output before picking an oracle: `draw_primitive` announces its entry with both operands the
row needs (`op = 0x03000000, drawmode=0x200000`).  Negative-controlled against the seat's own
mutant -- the three older rows all stay GREEN and only this one reds, 38/39
(`negctl_n25_rectset.out`).  **So the hole was real and the repair closes it, from one run.**

### kimi: a SMALLER escape, an empty corner of the two-by-two, and a false record of mine

Its answer was 221 KB with **no verdict line**, so the extractor filed it as a format miss.
*It contained the sharpest findings of the pass* -- the unread-review class, which this
project's own record calls its most expensive.

**(1) `if (drawmode & XFER_EN)` -> `if (1)`, one token, smaller than the disclosed conjunct.**
Nowhere was **(LINE, no-XFER) -> 0** asserted: the pair covered only two cells of a two-by-two.
**And closing it cost no new session** -- the `acc line mod` session already draws a LINE with
drawmode clear, so `n25 nox` is one count on a transcript this file had been collecting all
along.  CLOSED rather than disclosed, because unlike the conjunct it needs no
which-primitive-ran channel.

## Round #500 pass 5 -- the disposition I had ACCEPTED was wrong, and a seat overturned it by reading

`80cab9e` shipped a 35-row detector and closed with a disclosure: a mask narrowing at bits
24-25 collapses the two IMPLEMENTED primitives onto each other, and I recorded that as
**uncoverable** -- no host kill restored, and no pixel oracle at reset.  `M_NARROW_25` was
built anyway and its escape PREDICTED IN WRITING, three tables running.

**Pass 5 refused the round.  Four of five answering seats said the chain does not close.**

### The finding, and how it was found

`case DE_PRIM_LINE:` opens with a diagnostic present in **that arm and nowhere else**:

```c
	if (drawmode & DE_DRAWMODE_XFER_EN)
		fatal("[ sgi_de: XFER_EN for LINE op? ]\n");
```

So the two primitives ARE distinguishable, with no pixel oracle at all: set `XFER_EN`, draw
a RECTANGLE, and the message must not appear.  Under `& 0xfd000000` the rectangle folds onto
LINE and it does.

> **EVERY FACT IN MY DISCLOSURE WAS TRUE AND THE CONCLUSION DID NOT FOLLOW.**  A collapse
> really does restore no host kill; a pixel oracle really does not exist at reset.  But *"no
> pixel oracle"* is not *"no oracle"* -- and **I had grepped that `XFER_EN` line myself
> earlier in the same round without connecting it.**

*Found by the grok seat, which I had asked to be HARDER on its own earlier "the chain of this
class ends here" call.  It reversed itself and then found the hole in mine:* **"I was wrong
then; I am not going to make the same call on a leftover I have not finished enumerating."**

### The repair: THREE rows, because one would have been vacuous

| row | asserts |
|---|---|
| `n25 rect` | `count("XFER_EN for LINE op?") == 0` -- RECTANGLE must not reach the LINE-only arm |
| `n25 rectliv` | the guest runs on -- so the row above is not satisfied by nothing happening |
| `n25 line` | `count(...) == 1` -- the SAME channel DOES fire for LINE |

**`n25 rect` alone is negative-only**: satisfied if the channel is dead for any unrelated
reason -- a wrong register offset, a guard misread, a drawmode that never lands.  `n25 line`
proves it is live.  *That is this round's own `xlatch all` lesson applied three hours late,
and this time the companion went in BEFORE the table rather than after a nine-mutant sweep
found the hole.*

### What the pair does NOT catch -- named, not left unknown

The glm seat, asked for the smallest edit defeating the pair, found one: **a single added
conjunct**, `(drawmode & XFER_EN) && !(op & 0x02000000)`, silences the diagnostic for a
folded RECTANGLE while keeping it firing for a genuine LINE.  Both rows stay green.  It
reached that by elimination and said why nothing smaller works -- the two rows differ in
exactly ONE input, so any edit leaving both green must consult `op` itself.

**DISCLOSED, not repaired, on a SCOPE rule rather than difficulty:** that guard is product
code this round does not touch, and clause (d)'s enumeration is closed over the diff's own
hunks.  A conjunct on an unrelated guard is coverage debt to state, not a floor breach to
repair.  Also recorded: `n25 line` depends on there being exactly ONE emission site for that
string (`grep -c` = 1 today) -- **a layout fact, not an invariant.**

## Round #500 follow-up -- the CLASS CLOSURE, three tables, and a repair of mine that a table falsified

`#500` shipped a detector with its fix.  That detector then failed **four consecutive
panels**, every time on one class: **a cell of a state space left empty, repaired at
exactly the address the mutant had used, leaving the symmetric cell open for the next
pass.**

| pass | what escaped | what I did |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | mask width unpinned | added rows for bits 16 and 18 -- **cell-shaped** |
| 3 | bit 17 unpinned | enumerated all three modifier bits -- closed |
| 3 | narrowing unpinned | added bit 26 -- **cell-shaped again** |
| 4 | bits 27-31; widening into 0-23; a latch-bit alias | **enumerated the whole space** |

Twice I repaired by patching the cell a mutant had just demonstrated -- the second time
within the hour of writing *"the mask has two failure directions, not one"* into the very
file, closing the widening direction with all three modifier bits and then pinning the
narrowing direction **at a single bit**.

> **This round is the first application of the repair-chain rule's amendment: when two
> consecutive passes find breaches of ONE class, the next repair owes the CLASS CLOSURE**
> -- enumerate the full space from the function's own inputs, close every cell in one
> diff, and write into the contract which cells are covered and which are deliberately
> not.  Pass-per-instance converges linearly in cells; three passes bought one cell each.

### The mask space, enumerated from the function's own inputs

The selector is `op & 0xff000000`.  `op` is a function-**local** `uint32_t` loaded from
`d->de_reg[]` and **passed to no callee** -- `horrible_getputpixel` takes no `op` argument
-- so the enumeration is closed over `draw_primitive`'s body.  *That answers a seat's
pass-4 challenge; the earlier brief asserted a function-scoped grep was sufficient without
saying why.*

| mask bits | direction | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| **0-23** (outside the mask) | WIDENING declines a legal op | both accept ops carry **all 24 bits** -- one row each closes 24 cells |
| **26-31** (must be zero in any implemented value) | NARROWING aliases an unimplemented op onto an implemented case and **silently draws** | six rows, `dec b26`..`dec b31` |
| **24-25** (information-carrying: LINE `0x01`, RECTANGLE `0x03`) | NARROWING collapses the two implemented cases onto each other | **DISCLOSED, NOT COVERED** |

**Why 24-25 is uncoverable rather than uncovered, and why that is a measurement rather
than an excuse.**  Collapsing LINE onto RECTANGLE restores no host kill: both values stay
accepted and the guest stays alive, so every row stays green *correctly*.  Seeing it needs
an oracle for what was DRAWN, and there is none at reset -- `horrible_getputpixel` returns
early at `if (!(tileptr & 0x80000000))`, and for `tlb_mode` 0-2 the pointer is
`d->re_tlb_a[tile_nr] << 16`, zero on a reset machine.  **A successful draw writes
nothing.**  A missing CHANNEL, not a missing row, so adding rows cannot close it.

> The table therefore **builds that mutant and predicts its escape in writing, before each
> run** -- `M_NARROW_25`, a clean sweep on all three tables.  *A predicted escape is a
> measurement; an unpredicted one is a breach.*  Filed as `sgideprimopdraw` with the round
> that would close it: a drawing oracle, which closes two other filed residuals at once.

### *** THEN THE CHECK I HAD SKIPPED FOUND A FIFTH BREACH IN ONE GREP. ***

The ARM gate passed at 543 checks and this was about to be committed.  Then the
**mandatory pre-table block, which this round had skipped**, was run:

    grep -c 'd->warned |=' src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c   ->   10

**Ten writers of the guard field, bits 0..9.  The detector pre-set THREE of them.**
Aliasing this round's own `SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP` onto any of bits 0-5 -- the six `*_LEN`
latches -- escaped every row.  A one-token edit to the constant this round ADDED: floor
clause (d), L2, repaired in-round however late it is found.

*Four panels, sixteen mutants and three repairs did not find this.  One grep did.*

`PRETABLE.out` records it, and its Section 0 states plainly that table 1 had **no** block
and that the file's mtime proves order only for later tables.  **An unrun check and an
on-time one must not render the same**, and backdating it would be laundering.

### *** AND MY REPAIR FOR IT WAS ITSELF WRONG -- THE SWEEP THAT EXISTED TO VERIFY IT FALSIFIED IT. ***

The repair was **one row, not nine**: every `*_LEN` latch fires on a wrong access length
at its own window, so one session raises bits 0-8 and any alias then goes silent.  The
closure is over the FIELD, not the individual bits.

**Table 2 measured `M_ALIAS0`..`M_ALIAS5` at a CLEAN 34/34 apiece.**  The row was green
because **nothing had set those bits** -- vacuous by construction, a row whose channel
cannot vary under its named mutant.

The cause is one line of the device.  `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)` does
`relative_addr += 0x1000` (`dev_sgi_re.c:303`) because the device is registered at
`baseaddr + 0x1000` with length `0x1000`, so `CRIME_RE_TLB_A` sits at device offset
`0x000`.  **The row used the CONSTANTS as offsets, and all six accesses landed past the
end of the device.**  `#499`'s `UNMAP_W`/`UNMAP_R` were right for the same reason these
were wrong: those are already device-relative.

> **THE ROW PASSED ON THE FIXED BUILD, ON EVERY MASK MUTANT, AND ON THE SIX ALIAS MUTANTS
> IT WAS WRITTEN TO KILL.  Only the last of those was a defect -- and a sampling approach
> builds exactly the three cells (`M_ALIAS6/7/8`) that pass.**  The nine-mutant sweep
> existed only because the amendment says a closing pass verifies the enumeration rather
> than hunting cells; it is what turned a confident repair into a measured falsification.

### The durable fix is a precondition row, and it is the cheap half

`xlatch all` asserted "with ALL NINE other latch bits set" and **nothing verified that
precondition**.  It now does: `xlatch pre` counts the six `*_LEN` declines the set-up must
produce and requires exactly six.

> **A ROW THAT DEPENDS ON A SET-UP STEP OWES A ROW THAT THE SET-UP STEP HAPPENED.**

**Negative-controlled in both directions** (`negctl_xlatch_pre.out`): reverting the six
offsets to their broken values leaves `xlatch all` **green** -- exactly as it was -- while
`xlatch pre` reads **0 against 6 and goes RED**.  So the class that cost four panels, three
repairs and a nine-mutant sweep to surface is now caught **on a clean build, in four
minutes, with no mutant at all.**

Predictions were written into the driver before each run, so order is provable by mtime.
**Three tables were run; only this one is cited, because tables 1 and 2 describe detectors

(table 2 is kept beside it as `..._table2_FALSIFIED`, named for what it did).

## Round #500 sgideprimop -- a drawing op a guest never chose, and the reset value was one of them

`draw_primitive()` in `src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c` ended with

```c
default:fatal("[ sgi_de: UNIMPLEMENTED drawing op = 0x%08x, ... ]\n", op, ...);
	exit(1);
```

and `op` comes straight from a guest-written register (`CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE`). The switch
discriminates on the **top byte only**, so the domain is 256 values and two are implemented.
**A guest-written drawing op ended the host process.**

Now a latched decline that falls out of the switch and returns. Live `exit(1)` in that file:
**13 -> 12**. The latch is `SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP = 1 << 9`, **its own bit** -- `#498` measured what a
shared one costs (23/25: the other site's ordinary traffic silences the announce this fix exists
to make). The enum ends there on purpose, so a maintainer scanning to the last enumerator finds
`1 << 10`.

### The severity is not "254 of 256 exotic values"

`crmfbreg.h` names four primitives -- `DE_PRIM_POINT` **0x00000000**, `LINE` **0x01000000**,
`TRIANGLE` **0x02000000**, `RECTANGLE` **0x03000000** -- and the model implements **LINE and
RECTANGLE only**.

> *These are FULL 32-BIT VALUES, and writing them as "0x01" is a trap this round fell into three
> separate times -- in the product-code comment, in the detector's docstring, and then again in
> the first draft of this very paragraph, which is the one recording the correction. The switch
> compares `op & 0xff000000`, so a maintainer trusting "LINE 0x01" and writing `case 0x02:` for
> TRIANGLE gets a label that CAN NEVER MATCH. Found by the opus5 seat.* So POINT and TRIANGLE,
two *documented* primitives, land in the killing `default:`, **interleaved with** the implemented
pair rather than off in exotic territory.

*** AND POINT IS `0x00000000`, WHICH IS ALSO THE RESET VALUE. ***  `dev_sgi_re_init` memsets the
device struct, so `CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE` reads 0 until a guest writes it. **A guest that set the
START bit having never written the primitive register at all died here. It need not choose a bad
value; it need only omit a good one.**

### Witness, both directions

`regress/artifacts/sgideprimop/witness_20260831.sh`, run against the committed build and then the

### The oracle re-pin, and why the obvious one is a trap

The fix makes `tail_acc_x` in `sgi_de_width_probe.py` **certain-red** -- that row pinned a host
DEATH on purpose. `#499` had already predicted this blast radius in three tiers and derived the
design constraint, **KEEP THE MESSAGE TEXT AND ADD `(once)`**, which this fix obeys: `tail_acc`
stays green and `hi_draw`/`hi_rd_draw` are not silently blinded.

**The natural correction, `exit1` -> `exit0`, was NOT taken.** It would read GREEN under a future
`exit(0)` reinstatement, because **exit status cannot vary between "declined and then quit" and
"died with status 0"** -- the `exit0oracle` class, which a sibling round MEASURED the same day as a
48/48 clean sweep. Re-pinned instead onto a **positive post-draw observable**: the guest performs a
further load after the drawing access and the row asserts the value, so it reds on a death however
the death is spelled. The exit check is kept as a labelled second channel (`tail_acc_h`).

**ORDER PROVEN**, one frozen instrument, same script both ways:
`committed build 28/30` (both re-pinned rows RED) -> `working tree 30/30`.

### The L2 breach that arrived after the round had stopped

The opus5 seat returned late, having measured eight mutants in its own clone, and found a
**19/19 TOTAL ESCAPE** of this round's detector from **one hex digit**:
`switch (op & 0xff000000)` -> `& 0xffff0000`.

Both accept rows stored `0x03000000` -- low 16 bits ZERO -- so they pinned the predicate's VALUE
at two points on one axis and said nothing about the mask's **WIDTH**. `crmfbreg.h` puts three
real modifier bits down there, and `dev_sgi_re.c` reads all three:

```
  DE_PRIM_RL             0x00010000   right to left    read at :703
  DE_PRIM_TB             0x00020000   top to bottom    read at :704
  DE_PRIM_LINE_SKIP_END  0x00040000   line bound       read at :735
```

So `RECTANGLE|RL` and `LINE|SKIP_END` are legal, implemented primitives that the widened mask
**silently declines instead of drawing**. That is the de-escalation clause exactly: before this
round the mutant `exit(1)`s on the first right-to-left rectangle, unmissable; after it, the
refusal is silent and the accidental tripwire is gone. It is also clause (f)'s accept-side lesson
wearing a mask -- an accept row at the BASE tests one bound twice and the other never.

**REPAIRED IN-ROUND (L2) AND DISCHARGED BY A MEASURED KILL, NOT BY EXISTING.** Two rows,
`acc rect rl` (0x03010000) and `acc line se` (0x01040000), 19 -> 21. Measured against THIS file
rather than inheriting the seat's numbers from its own clone -- a different claim:

```
  BASE          21/21
  M8_maskwide   19/21   RED = `acc rect rl', `acc line se' -- and nothing else
```

Prediction written into the driver before the run; it matched exactly.
Logs: `killtable_20260831/table3_l2/`, both ending `OPUS500_DONE`.

### Two records corrected, and one script

**`sgi_de_width_probe.py`'s contract was forbidding the row this diff adds.** It said *"Every
access to +0x800..+0xfff already ends the host ... A row that wanted survival up there would be
testing the wrong defect."* This round removes that kill and re-pins `tail_acc_x` into exactly
such a survival row. Corrected in place with the superseded text quoted.

**The primitive constants were wrong in my own comment, in product code and in the detector.**
I wrote *"POINT 0x00, LINE 0x01, TRIANGLE 0x02, RECTANGLE 0x03"*; `crmfbreg.h` defines them as
full 32-bit values. Only POINT coincides. Since the switch compares `op & 0xff000000`, a
maintainer trusting *"LINE 0x01"* and writing `case 0x02:` gets a label that can never match.

**And the propagation script was fixed rather than the tree.** `build-asan` came back

## Round #499 sgireunmapped -- a 2080-byte door, and the obvious oracle escapes

`DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)` in `src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c` ended the host on any unmatched address,
at ANY width, in EITHER direction, with no width predicate at all.  The handler dispatches guest
offsets `0x1000-0x1fff`; the six windows cover `0x1000-0x17ff` with one internal gap, leaving
`0x16e0-0x16ff` (32 bytes) plus `0x1800-0x1fff` (2048) = **2080 bytes** falling through to
`exit(1)`.  A single guest `lb` at `0xb5001800` was enough.  Every other kill in that handler
needs an unusual WIDTH or a DIRECTION; this one needed neither.

Now a per-direction latched decline falling through to the function's common tail.  Live
`exit(1)` in that file: 14 -> 13.  Two bits, `SGIRE_W_UNMAP_WR = 1 << 7` and
`SGIRE_W_UNMAP_RD = 1 << 8`, because a driver probing an unmapped window commonly reads and
writes it in one pass and one bit would announce the first and silence the other -- measured, as
`M3shared`, which escaped.

**The enum placement is load-bearing.**  An earlier draft inserted both after `1 << 5`, leaving
the enum ending at `1 << 6`, so a maintainer scanning to the LAST enumerator for the next free
bit would take `1 << 7` -- already used, legal C, silent, and the four handlers share one
`malloc`'d struct.  That collision is not hypothetical: it happened between `#498` and this
round's own generator and measured a 14/14 total escape.  Both bits now sit after
`SGIRE_W_DE_LEN` in numeric order.

### The obvious oracle escapes, and so did the first replacement

The sibling probe's `other kill` row asserted `how == "exit1"` and would have gone red by
succeeding.  Its own comment had already filed it as `otherkilldeath` and prescribed the fix.
The natural re-pin is `exit0+txt`.  **Measured: it ESCAPES an `exit(0)` mutant** -- the message
prints, the process exits 0, `got == want`, GREEN.  Exit status cannot vary between *declined
and then quit* and *died with status 0*.

The measuring seat's own first-choice replacement -- a `DE_STATUS` device-signature read --
**escaped two further mutants**, because that read goes to a DIFFERENT device registration: it
proves the emulator is alive and proves nothing about the catch-all's return path.  What shipped
is a sentinel-preset read of the unmapped address itself, which fails all three.

*Correcting an overclaim made in this round's own justification: the three failures carry TWO
distinct values, not three -- `mexit0` and `mrdexit0` both give `exit0/txt/died`, `mret0` gives
`exit0/txt/0xdeadbeef`.  The argument that matters survives (the channel varies where the
alternatives do not); the stronger framing does not.  Caught by a packet-fed seat reading the
parenthetical against the claim it was offered to support.*

```
fixed build,     SAME oracle   35/35

```

Re-pin applied BEFORE the code changed; all four runs sentinel-verified and re-run locally

### What this round got wrong

**It shipped without a pass 2 on its own diff.**  The gate refused the NEXT commit with
`NO PASS-2 RECEIPT` and noted it was the third such omission.  The pass was then run late, on
shipped code, and found three defects no green gate can see: this block's absence, the
distinctness overclaim above, and a death oracle that could not fail in a witness artifact
committed alongside (`${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is `printf`, not the emulator -- corrected to index 1,
which now reports the actual kill).

Adjudicated as an undischarged obligation rather than a floor breach or a wrong record: nothing
anywhere CLAIMED a pass 2 had happened, and an absence is not a false assertion.  The honest
assessment of the late pass is that it is worth about half a timely one, and the discount scales
with how much of a round's risk was DESIGN rather than EXECUTION -- so this round is the best
case for lateness, and "it worked out this time" must not become the precedent.

### Pass 3 (`4daa506`): three more breaches, two of them MEASURED clean sweeps

The 36-row detector was reviewed by eight seats.  **agy was DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED** -- it is
reserved for measurement by owner ruling, and that is neither a seat failure nor agreement.

| seat | verdict | what it contributed |
|---|---|---|
| opus5 | DO NOT CLOSE | **MEASURED** `M1` and `M2`, both **36/36 TOTAL ESCAPE** |
| fable5 | DO NOT CLOSE | the gate defect below, + the adjudication of the chain rule |
| kimi | DO NOT CLOSE | found the gate defect INDEPENDENTLY, by a different route |

| minimax | CLEAN | minority |
| grok | CLEAN | **and its own body names `M2`** -- see below |

**THE FRAME WAS FITTED TO THE MUTANTS IT WAS BUILT FROM.**  Pass 2's repair added a
*component x width* two-by-two.  The catch-all's behaviour is a function of FIVE inputs, and the
two-by-two spans `relative_addr` collapsed to two values, times `len` -- dropping `writeflag`
at one of those values and POSITION at both:

* **`M1`, direction.**  `} else if (relative_addr < CRIME_RE_LINEAR_A) { fatal; exit(1); }` on
  the READ arm.  Component 1 was touched by exactly two sessions and **both were stores**, so
  every row stayed green: **36/36**.
* **`M2`, position within a component.**  `>= CRIME_RE_LINEAR_A` to `- 0x10`.  All four
  component-1 rows sat at the component's BASE; component 1 is a 32-byte RANGE, not a point.
  **36/36**, and a write at `0x16f0` was then silently accepted into `re_linear_a[]` with no
  message at all.

**`M2` IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN NEWEST RULE, UN-TRANSFERRED BY ONE HOP.**  The carrier says an
accept row written at a window's BASE tests the near bound twice and the far bound never, so it
must sit at the last legal slot.  That was applied to the six named windows in this very file
and NOT to the catch-all's first component.

### A RED gate on a GREEN detector -- and the harness could not see it

Found by **two seats independently**.  Both new row names -- `clip narrow surv`, `clip narrow
decl` -- are **exactly 16 characters**, and the probe prints names through `%-16s`.  A 16-char
name gets zero padding plus the format's single separator space, while the gate's per-row
pattern needs **two**.  Measured against this round's own preserved 36/36 log, both checks
scored `got=0` against `want=1`.

**The probe was green and the gate was red, on the same build.**  It is the padded-column trap
this project has a standing note about, and the reason it survived is that the gate SCRIPT was
never run after the rows were added -- only the probe.  The kimi seat put the shape best:
*"the layer the diff edited (the gate list) is the layer the harness bypassed."*

Repaired structurally rather than by renaming alone: `row()` now carries
`assert len(name) <= 15`, so the trap cannot be reintroduced silently.  Both names are now 13
characters.

**The assert is negative-controlled in BOTH directions**, because a guard against a
check-that-cannot-fail must not itself be one: re-injecting the exact 16-character name that
shipped fires it (`row name 'clip narrow surv' is 16 chars; the gate pattern needs <= 15`), and
the 13-character replacement is accepted.  The bound is derived, not guessed -- `%-16s` pads a
name of length L to 16, the format contributes one more space, so L <= 15 is exactly the
condition for the gate's two-space pattern to match.

### A verdict line that closed a chain its own body had broken

**The grok seat's verdict reads `CLEAN -- zero floor breaches; the chain closes`.**  Item 3 of
its own body reads: *"CLIP is probed only at `0x16e0`.  `LINEAR_A`'s near bound sliding down by
`0x10` eats `0x16f0-0x16ff` and leaves `clip *` green."*

That is `M2`, described exactly, in the answer that ratified closure -- and the opus seat
measured it as a total escape in the same panel.  The carrier already states the rule this
instance confirms: **a verdict line is a summary written against the brief's own framing, so it
is the LEAST likely part of an answer to carry the correction.  Read the body of any seat whose
verdict merely agrees.**  Recorded because the tally would otherwise have read 6-2 rather than
7-1, and because a seat that finds a breach and then closes is worse for a reader than one that
finds nothing.

### Pass 4: the CLASS closed rather than the cells -- 36 -> 48 rows

Both seats that reached the class level said the same thing, from opposite ends.  The measuring
seat: *"adding two more rows at the corner I just named will produce a fourth."*  The
adjudicator, ruling on the chain rule and asked to be harder on it because it favours finishing:
**when two consecutive passes find breaches of ONE class, the next repair owes the CLASS
CLOSURE -- enumerate the full space, close every cell in one diff, and the closing pass verifies
the enumeration rather than hunting cells.**

So pass 4 does not add two rows at the corner.  It enumerates the catch-all's **five inputs**
-- `relative_addr` (component AND position within it), `writeflag`, `len`, `idata`, `d->warned`
-- closes every cell, and writes into the probe's CONTRACT which cells are covered and which are
**deliberately not**, so a later escape is *"outside the contract, as stated"* rather than a
fourth breach.

**MEASURED, all logs preserved at `regress/artifacts/sgireunmapped/killtable_20260831/pass4/`
and each verified by its `OPUS499T_DONE` sentinel rather than by existing:**

| mutant | what it edits | vs 36 rows | vs 48 rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| base (the fix) | -- | 36/36 | **48/48** (`base.out`) |
| `M1` direction | read arm qualified to component 2 | **36/36 ESCAPE** | **41/48**, 7 red (`M1.out`) |
| `M2` position | `>= CRIME_RE_LINEAR_A` -> `- 0x10` | **36/36 ESCAPE** | **45/48**, 3 red (`M2.out`) |
| `V` value | `writeflag == MEM_WRITE` -> `&& idata` | never built | **47/48**, 1 red (`V.out`) |

The red rows are exactly the cells built for each, which is the enumeration verifying itself:
`M1` reds the five component-1 read rows plus the two `cliphi` reads; `M2` reds only the three
far-slot rows; `V` reds `wr zero decl` alone -- **and NOT `wr zero surv`, correctly**, since
under `&& idata` the host still survives and only the message is wrong.  A survival-only oracle
would have scored `V` a clean sweep, which is the refusal-effect-site lesson recurring.

**`V` is the guard-field/body-field check paying for itself.**  The predicate reads `writeflag`;
the guarded body reads `relative_addr` AND `idata`.  Every write in the detector carried a
nonzero datum, so the two fields could never be seen to disagree.  The measuring seat derived

**FLOOR CLAUSE (a), MEASURED AGAINST THE 48-ROW VERSION** (`PREFIX.out`, `PREFIX48_DONE`):

## Round #498 sgidewidth -- a guest `sb` ended the host, and the OBVIOUS fix scores 24/25

`DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)` in `src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c` insisted on a 4- or 8-byte access and
ended the host process otherwise. One guest `sb` anywhere in a 4 KB window did it. Witnessed
at rung 3 on an unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32`: `sb`, `sh`, `lbu` and `lhu` each gave exactly one
`len = N not implemented` and `exit(1)` -- 4/4, with a liveness control and a device-signature
control that echoes our own value back in the device's diagnostic.

    live exit(1) in dev_sgi_re.c    15 -> 14

### The fix is NOT #497's splice, and the difference is measured rather than stylistic

`#497`'s tail only answered a read. **This function's tail also calls `draw_primitive()`** when
the guest set `CRIME_DE_START`, so falling through runs a rendering primitive for an access the
model just refused. Nine builds, 25 rows:

    mR   latched decline + goto to the common exit    25/25   <- shipped
    mB   latched decline + early return 1             25/25   (not shipped: diverges the day
                                                               the tail grows)
    fix  decline + startFlag = 0, switch still runs   24/25   <- the shape the design implied
    mC   shared latch, reusing #497's bit             23/25
    mE   repair hoisted to every access               22/25
    mF   repair qualified to writes only              21/25
    mA   the naive #497 splice                        19/25
    mD   brace slip into the len == 4 arm             17/25

**`fix` reds `dec_switch`**: a declined 1-byte write still reaches the register switch, which
announces `TODO: non-zero CRIME_DE_SCISSOR` about **a write that never happened**, from an
`idata` the arm discarded. Product code shipping a wrong record inside a diagnostic -- the same
class the ACCEPT member of the option set was discovered through.

`goto <label>` to a common exit is house idiom, derived rather than asserted: **10 device files
use `goto` and 8 use it inside a `DEVICE_ACCESS` body.** (A first grep said 6 because it pinned
three label names; `dev_sgi_mec.c` uses `goto skip`.)

### One latch bit, and it must be its own

Per-message-site gives ONE bit here: one guard, one text. `#497` took six because six windows
with six texts are walked in a single session. **But `mC` measured 23/25** -- the four handlers
share one `malloc`'d struct, so reusing `SGIRE_W_TLBA_LEN` lets any odd-width access to
`sgi_re`'s TLB_A window silence `sgi_de`'s decline entirely. `1<<6` is free.

### Accept rows sit at +0x7fc / +0x7f8, and that is a fact about the device

The nominal last slots `+0xffc`/`+0xff8` have bit 0x800 set, so they reach `draw_primitive` and
die there. **The last legal slots with `startFlag` CLEAR are the real anchors** -- the
last-slot rule from `#497`'s sibling round, constrained by a second defect.

### What this round does NOT fix, stated so no reader concludes the window is safe

*** EVERY access to `+0x800..+0xfff`, AT ANY WIDTH INCLUDING ACCEPTED ONES, STILL ENDS THE HOST
-- inside `draw_primitive()`, whose `default:` arm is fatal on 254 of 256 drawing ops, and whose
reset value is one of them. *** That is `sgideprimop`, filed HIGH, witnessed by a 24/24
attribution probe on offsets differing only in bit 0x800. Half this window is still lethal and
the second kill is not this round's to fix.

### The detector, and two instrument defects caught before it shipped

**29 rows** (22 at first draft, 25 after three measured rows were found missing, 29 after pass 2
found a hole), self-contained (no `gxprobe` dependency -- every committed probe in this tree rolls its
own pty, and that precedent settled the question without asking). **Every row is one the
nine-build table measured killing a specific mutant**, and the contract names what it does not
catch.

**`lw` SIGN-EXTENDS.** `acc4_last` read `0xffffffffcafebabe` against a wanted `0xcafebabe` --
failing on MIPS semantics while the device was entirely correct. The two neighbouring accept
rows passed only because their fixtures happen to have bit 31 clear. Masked rather than given a
friendlier constant, so the row is correct *by construction* for any value.

### Pass 2 found a hole two seats reached independently, and a process breach

**`len == 2` was not pinned as a live decline anywhere.** The witness killed on `sb`, `sh`, `lbu`
and `lhu`; the detector's survival and answer rows used `sb` and `lbu` only. `sh` appeared solely
as the SECOND access in `two_widths_*`, whose oracle is *"len=2 is never announced"* -- and that
row stays green whether `len==2` is **accepted**, **still killed**, or **correctly declined**.
Three machines behind one green row, and the single latch bit is why: after `sb`, a later `sh` is
*supposed* to be silent, so silence proves nothing.

fable5 predicted the escaping edit as `else if (len == 4 || len == 2)` at a full 25/25, walked it
row by row rather than building it during a live panel; grok reached the same hole from the
witness side. Four rows added, each in its own session so the fresh latch makes the len=2
announcement observable. **25 -> 29, all green.**

**And `#498` is the FIRST post-mandate kill-table round with no `PRETABLE.out`** -- five sibling
rounds carry one, including this round's own parent. Both of its costs showed up here: the
CLAIM->ROW check is exactly what polices *a contract naming a row that is not in the file*, and
the de-escalation enumeration is where the `len==2` hole would have surfaced at writing time.
Back-writing the block now would violate its own mtime-order rule, so the record is *skipped,
costs enumerated*.

**One disposition was wrong: deleting the 22-row artifact.** The house remedy for a misleading
record is freeze-with-banner, not destruction. The deletion was pre-commit and is unrecoverable,
and it strips evidence from prose that cites it -- including a "sweeps clean" claim which the
surviving neighbour log shows is itself imprecise: without the tail rows the draft scores that
mutant 21/22, caught rather than clean.

**And the first attempt to fix that silently did nothing.** The anchor carried regex backslashes
through a heredoc, matched ZERO, and the re-run scored the unchanged file at the same 21/22 --
indistinguishable from a real result. Only the `AssertionError: 0` gave it away.

### A pre-specified trigger fired and was honoured

`#497` filed `gatedevicesplit` with a criterion in the gate's own words: *"the NEXT device probe
wired into this gate converts it from filed to OWED."* This is that probe. The row moved
**filed -> OWED, low -> med**, in this commit. The detector is still wired into `gate_arm.sh`,
deliberately -- the split is a harness round owing its own controls, and holding a HIGH device
fix hostage to a gate refactor would be the tail wagging the dog. **A trigger that fires and is
ignored is worse than one never written, because the next reader trusts it.**
