## Round #497 widthkillclass -- six guest-reachable host kills, and a detector that escaped
## its own mutant until the round measured it

A guest choosing an unusual ACCESS WIDTH ended the host process at six address windows of
the SGI CRIME rendering engine (`src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c`). One `sb`, `sh` or `lw` to
`CRIME_RE_TLB_A/B/C`, `_TEX`, `_LINEAR_A` or `_LINEAR_B` and the emulator died. `#337` fixed
this class in `dev_wdc.c`; these six are the same shape, witnessed at rung 3 on unmodified
`-E sgi -e ip32` -- **26/26 across all six sites and both directions.**

    live exit(1) in dev_sgi_re.c        21 -> 15
    DEVICE_ACCESS bucket, whole tree    83 -> 77

Both by `exit_census.py`, not by grep -- which counts commented-out code as live and
mis-attributes plain functions to the preceding handler. That tool was corrected the same day
for exactly those two defects.

### The bytes shipped are the bytes measured

The artifact's md5 is `5821e801...`, and `table2_master.log:17` records that md5 for the
source under test. Verified at every hop before the copy -- artifact = measured, SEC = base,
est = base -- and re-verified across all five trees afterwards. Two of those five were missed
on the first pass and caught by the gate, which is the no-VPATH propagation rule doing its job.

### The fix is an `else if` splice, and both alternatives were refuted before it was written

**`break` is not legal C at these sites** -- they are `if`/`else if` arms, not `switch` cases.
Eight of eight answering seats said so on pass 1, which is unanimity against the brief's own
sketch and the premise-audit instruction working as designed.

**`return 0` is not a decline either**: `memory_rw` coerces it to -1 and raises
`EXCEPTION_DBE` on MIPS. So control must reach the common tail, which ends `return 1`. A
declined read now runs that tail for the **first time in the fork's history**, handing the
guest a defined zero -- `odata` is explicitly initialised, read rather than assumed.

Six per-site latch bits in one new `uint32_t` with the `(once)` marker. Per-site rather than
shared because `dev_wdc.c`'s own comment adjudicates the discriminator -- *SIX FLAGS, NOT
FOUR* -- sharing being licensed only across sites mutually exclusive at runtime, and these six
windows are walked in one session by any driver bringing up the RE.

### The LINEAR sites carry a different comment, and the wording is what `offsetof` measured

For `TLB_A/B/C` and `TEX` the width guard protects correctness only. For `LINEAR_A/B` it is
additionally the only thing preventing an out-of-bounds array write. **The brief called that
"load-bearing HOST memory safety" and the measuring seat refused to ship it**, compiling
`offsetof` instead: the over-run lands INSIDE the struct, so it is UB plus silent cross-array
corruption, **invisible to plain ASAN**. Not a wild write, not a host crash.

> **And the fix nearly re-introduced that defect.** Placing the new latch between
> `re_linear_b` and `de_reg` made `re_linear_b[32]` alias the latch itself -- falsifying the
> comment above it and creating a worse mode where an over-run **silences the device's own
> diagnostics**. The field sits last, and `ADJACENCY_AS_DOCUMENTED=YES` is a hard gate in
> table 2.

### The escape, and why there are two tables

`d_returnzero` -- the declined path returning 0 instead of falling to the tail -- **escaped
all 35 v1 rows.** The evidence is one line:

    tlb_a lw surv    got exit0/0xdeadbeef    want exit0/0x0

**The exit status is identical on both sides.** Only the untouched sentinel shows the guest
load never completed. The v1 rows were **survival-only oracles at a refusal-effect site** --
vacuous by construction, because a guest bus error leaves the *host* alive. That is a
clause-(d) null-repair, so **L2, repaired in-round**: the v2 rows read a *value* and kill it
at 29/35.

It was disclosed as an explicit no-row in `PRETABLE.out` **before table 1 ran**, and predicted
in advance. That is the CHANNEL line's claim -- that a row's channel-under-its-mutant is
knowable at writing time -- holding on its first mandated application. Its one measured limit
is worth more than the ratification: **it validates the channel a row NAMES, not whether that
observable matches the CLAIM the row carries.**

`d_lessthan` scored 35/35 and is a **result, not an escape** -- measured equivalent by
construction over the reachable domain `len in {1,2,4,8}`.

Floor (a)-(f) all discharged by measurement. Clause (c) got *stronger* as a side effect: the
null medium fell **12/35 to 6/35**, because the v2 rows demand a value and no longer pass
trivially against a binary that merely exits 0.

### The residual is pinned by rows, not claimed by a sentence

The width guard is evaluated FIRST, so an ordinary 8-byte `ld` **still ends the host** at all
six windows. That is `sgirekills`, filed separately -- and the round ships **six measured `ld
kill` rows** pinning it. Consequence, recorded now rather than rediscovered: **fixing
`sgirekills` will turn a green gate RED by succeeding**, six rows' worth, so it inherits the
oracle-correction ordering -- re-pin first, measure the committed build red, then edit.

`sgidewidth` (a seventh width kill in the same file, different handler) and `sgireunmapped`
(the unmatched-address arm, no width predicate at all, 2080 bytes) are filed and named, so
nobody reads this round as "the file is safe".

### What pass 2 found, which was mostly about the record

Both Anthropic seats ratified the code and tables. The packet-fed seats found **three defects
in the brief** -- a pre-fix census presented as current state inside a SETTLED PREMISES block,
a section claiming the round had not shipped while the header called it shipped, and a **null
pattern** (`grep -i 'sgi|width'` without `-E` is a literal). The measuring seat found a
**measured escape**: `other kill` is a death-only oracle and a text change scores 35/35.
Filed as coverage debt with its reasoning, not claimed as a floor breach.

It also discharged an obligation the two tables never did: **seven rows were red under no
mutant in either table**, so for those the CHANNEL line was satisfied on paper. Six of the
seven are now measured failable; one remains blind and is filed.

*The honest summary, in the measuring seat's own framing: the diff is right, the tables are
real, the bytes shipped are the bytes measured -- and the round's own record was the weakest
part of it.*

## Round panelargvcap -- `panel.sh` warned about the argv cap and then launched anyway

A 38 KB brief killed **both** argv-fed seats with `Argument list too long`. Codex and Kimi
had to be recovered by hand -- while this block printed advice sixty lines above the launch
that ignored it:

```
WARNING: brief is ${BSZ} bytes (>30KB). Codex/Kimi take it on argv and
         may fail with 'Argument list too long'. Trim, or point those
         seats at the file path instead of piping its contents.
```

> *** IT IS THE CHECK-THAT-CANNOT-FAIL FAMILY'S SIBLING: **a message reporting an ACTION the
> code does not take.** ***

The `re-firing once (a wall can be minutes long) ...` message -- followed by a `return 2`
every caller discards -- is the same defect, and its recorded lesson applies here unchanged:
**telling the operator it was handled is WORSE than silence**, because the one person who
could fix it by hand is told not to.

### The fix is that both seats already read files

So the remedy the message *recommended* is one the script can simply **take**. Grok has been
immune all along (`--prompt-file`) and agy too (`--add-dir` plus a pointer prompt); Codex and
Kimi were the only two still fed the brief on argv. Above `ARGV_CAP` they now get a POINTER
-- read `$BRIEF_ABS` and review it as its own Questions section directs -- and below it the
inline form is **byte-unchanged**.

### Controlled in both directions, and the control reads the REAL file

`sed` extracts the decision block and the prompt-build out of `panel.sh` and `eval`s them,
rather than re-typing them into the test. That is deliberate: **a verification that shares
the defect of the thing it verifies always passes**, which this project has measured -- a
cross-check once reported `VERDICT: MATCH` because it used the same first-match regex as the
edit it was checking.

```
POST-FIX   6/6 rc=0     incl. BOTH boundary rows (exactly 30000 -> inline,
                        30001 -> pointer) and a both-seats-agree column
PRE-FIX    EXTRACT FAILED rc=9    "this form has no cap branch at all"
```

**The pre-fix run is the load-bearing half.** Without it this is a green test nobody has
shown can fail. Artifacts: `regress/artifacts/panelargvcap/controls_20260830/`, including
the control script itself so the measurement can be re-run rather than trusted.

`PANEL_ARGV_CAP` overrides the cap **only** so the branch is testable without keeping a 38 KB
fixture, and the comment says so. It is not a tuning knob and no caller should set it.

### The carrier's Codex row is corrected in the same commit, and it gained the BOUND

It still told a human to hand-trim briefs. It now also carries the limit, which matters more
than the fix: **the pointer form only helps seats that can open the file.** This is not
licence to grow briefs without limit -- the packet-fed Ollama seats still get the whole thing
POSTed, and brief complexity is the measured driver of thinking-burn, where a seat spends its
entire output budget on hidden reasoning and emits nothing.

*Filed as a known defect and left unapplied for a day before this round, because a change to
the script every panel runs owes two negative controls. That was the right call and the delay
cost nothing -- but note the failure it was waiting on had already happened once.*

## Round #496 gdromcondlies -- two guest-reachable host kills, and the store that made
## the obvious fix worse than the defect

Two sites in `src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` ended the host process on **one guest
store each**, witnessed at rung 3 on an unmodified `-E dreamcast`:

    GDROM_UNKNOWN_0x88   a write of any value but 0x0b
    GDROM_COND           a write of anything outside {0xa0, 0xef}

Both are the `#443` BADVAL class -- a KNOWN register rejecting a VALUE by ending the host.
The witness reads **15/15 pre-fix**; re-run against the fixed build with the same
instrument, unedited, it reads **11/15**, and the four rows that flip are exactly the kill
rows (`witness_20260830/`, `postfix_20260830/`).  That inversion is why the witness is
`CLASS_WITNESS` and correctly ungated: gating it would manufacture a regression.

### The half of this fix that is not about `exit()`

`d->cond = idata;` ran **unconditionally, above the dispatch**.  `COND_DATA_AVAIL` (`0x08`)
is a bit of that byte and it **gates the whole `GDROM_DATA` read path**, so deleting the
`exit(1)` and nothing else would have handed every unmodelled value a direct write to the
readiness flag the guest polls -- forging data-available where no command produced any, or
revoking a genuine one.  Silent, and worse than the kill it replaced.

The store now lives inside the two accepted arms, byte-identically ordered.  **Both Agent
seats named that relocation independently on pass 1** as the round's clause-(d) mutant, and
`agy` later MEASURED it: with the store restored above the dispatch the detector's keystone
row stays green, and the three-pre-state repair reds it (`agy_r5escape_measurement.out`).

### The scope cost, recorded here because a record is what discharges it

*** THIS ROUND SHIPS A `case` WHOSE WRITE ARM ANNOUNCES ONCE AND WHOSE READ ARM, SEVEN
LINES ABOVE IT, FLOODS WITHOUT BOUND. ***  The `GDROM_UNKNOWN_0x88` READ arm and the
`GDROM_STAT` write arm are both already-de-fatalised, unlatched `fatal()` sites, measured
at **3 accesses / 3 diagnostics each** (`witness_20260830/extras_run1.out`).

**They are FILED under `floodclass`, not taken**, and the two Agent seats disagreed about
that: `opus5` argued TAKE (same `case`, already being edited, and shipping it half-
disciplined is a wrong record); `fable5` argued FILE (a flood is not the BADVAL class, so
the round-scope rule's same-semantic-class arm fails, and taking one site alone splits the
flood FAMILY).  **Ruled FILE, against the rule's own text rather than by vote.**

The adjudication pass upheld it, and `fable5` -- whose position won -- scrutinised it
harder rather than accepting it, sharpening the reason: `#460`'s joined-on-the-merits
precedent in this same file is the strongest case for `opus5`, but there both sites were
one predicate family with the same lethality, whereas here the classes differ in kind (kill
vs hygiene).  **Three seats then noted that the ruling's discharge was still OWED**, since
no round block existed and `PRETABLE.out` said *"the cost is recorded"* in the present
tense.  This block is that discharge, and it names BOTH sites rather than only the read arm.

### The detector, and what pass 2 cost it

`regress/gdrom_cond_probe.py`, **21 rows**, gated in `gate_sh_rounding.sh`.  It began at 16
and grew under measurement.  Two of the repairs are general and neither is about this
device:

* *** A CLAUSE-(b) FLOOR BREACH CREATED BY STATING A RULE TOO BROADLY. ***  The probe
  header banned the SURVIVAL channel outright, on the true observation that post-fix every
  one of these accesses exits 0.  But reinstating `exit(1)` **prints the diagnostic and
  then dies** -- count 1, byte correct, row green, defect back.  **Survival is dead on the
  ACCEPT side and is the ONLY channel that sees clause (b) on the DECLINE side.**  The
  round's own witness had measured that shape pre-fix (`a88 says` = 1 AND `a88 kill` =
  exit1 in one session) and nobody read the two rows together.  Found by a PACKET-FED seat
  from the diff alone.
* *** ONE ANCHOR PROVES A VALUE, NOT AN IDENTITY. ***  The keystone drove one pre-state, so
  `d->cond = 0xef;` in the decline arm passed it while forging `COND_DATA_AVAIL` out of a
  fresh decline.  *"Unchanged" is a claim about a FUNCTION of the prior value, and one
  sample cannot distinguish a function from a constant.*  Three pre-states now, one of them
  declining `0x08` itself so the forge subspace is MEASURED rather than inferred.

Also repaired: `R7` FAILED OPEN -- an absent read folded to `"clear"`, which was its want,
so **the one row whose oracle is an absence was the one an apparatus failure scored green**;
`R10` was HOLLOW (it read STAT, which `update_stat` recomputes on every read, so it could
not see site A growing an effect); `R11` was weaker than the `#490` precedent it cited and
now stages an old bit with a benign DATA read; site A's byte fidelity was untested; and
**`R12` was named in the adjudication pass as the thing all nine seats had missed** -- no
row exercised the DATA read path the whole fix exists to protect.  It keys on the
diagnostic and not on the returned value, because this file's own comment records that the
no-data path returns `0xffff` and *"this device's TOC is memset(0xff), so 0xffff is
LEGITIMATE PAYLOAD here and no returned value is self-identifying."*

### Counts, with their deriver, because every carried one in this round was wrong

    grep -c 'd->warned |=' src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c   ->  12 RAW
    ... minus ONE inside a comment block                       ->  11 LIVE writers
    of which, inside a DEVICE_ACCESS                           ->   8

(Pre-round: 10 raw, 9 live, 6 inside.)  `PRETABLE.out` said *"8 before, 10 after"* -- `#490`'s
numbers with its own two additions never folded in -- and the probe header said *"ten sites,
six inside"*.  Three seats reached 9 -> 11 independently.  **The raw grep of 12 is the same
comment contamination `tools/pipeline/exit_census.py` exists to defeat, and it caught me one
command after I cited that tool.**  Two L4s in product code were corrected with it: *"Nine
bits today"* above the disjointness assert (`#496` made it eleven) and a decline comment
saying *"the guest has sent no packet"*, which is too broad -- nothing stops a bad COND write
arriving after a `0xa0` or midway through a packet.  The warrant is that THIS write began
nothing, not that nothing is in flight.

### An apparatus defect, and the sentinel that refuted my own diagnosis of it

The probe seeded its destination register to **0** before each load, so a `step` that did
not complete left the register at its initialiser -- and *"RAM would read 0"* is exactly what
every device-signature control here tests for.  `devsig sh4` reported `got=0x0`, which reads
as *the SH4 register window is dead*.  **I diagnosed host contention and wrote that reason
into the file.**

It was not contention.  The row was simply WRONG -- I had written it from memory as a 16-bit
load of `0xa4000150`, where the sibling probes read **32 bits from `0xffd00010` masked to
16** -- and it had been failing correctly the whole time.  **The seed change settled it on
the very next run: a step that never executed would have left `0xdead`, and it left `0x0`.**

> *A sentinel earns its keep by making you wrong faster.*  Kept, with its warrant now the
> measured one rather than the guessed one.  And it reproduced the fail-open defect one
> level down -- `0xdead` has bit 3 set, so an unexecuted load would have scored `"set"` on
> the two rows whose want IS `"set"` -- which is why `bit()` returns `SEED-NEVER-RAN`.

### NOT DONE, said plainly rather than implied

**The first CLEAN run came only after the control itself was repaired**, and the earlier
`GDROMCOND_CONTROL=DEAD` had TWO causes that were conflated -- one real and one imagined.
The real one was the wrong `devsig sh4` row above.  The imagined one was host contention,
which I wrote into the previous commit message as the cause and which the seed change then
refuted: the failure was DETERMINISTIC across four runs, and a contention artifact is
intermittent.  *Determinism is the discriminator, and stating the wrong cause in a durable
record is the defect this round corrected twice elsewhere.*  Contention was real and did
cost measurements -- three probes ran on one machine -- but it was not what killed that
control.  The 21-row table has **not** run
clean, and the kill table has not run at all (`kill496_mut.py` does not exist).  **The
vacuity floor is therefore NOT yet discharged for this detector**, and this round is not
closable until it is.

*The lesson is one the carrier already states about gates and had not extended to probes:
a rung-3 probe needs the machine to itself just as much.  Farming a seat wide requires
isolating its WORKSPACE, not merely giving it a distinct brief -- three `agy` jobs on three
different briefs all built in one scratch tree before diverging.*

### The panel

**Nine seats on pass 1, nine on pass 2, nine on the adjudication pass.  Nothing down.**
This is the first round to run the ADJUDICATION PASS (owner directive, 2026-08-30): every
seat's findings consolidated into one numbered packet with the author's disposition on each,
disagreements listed with both sides in their own words, and all nine re-fired on it.
**Eleven findings upheld, none overturned, three refined, and one row nobody had thought of.**

### *** THE ADDENDUM: A PASS-2 SEAT MEASURED ONE OF THIS ROUND'S OWN ROWS TO BE VACUOUS,
### AND THE ROUND HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN THE RULE IT BROKE. ***

`R5d` was **STORE-DEATH VACUOUS** in the 24-row detector this round shipped.  Cut the one
store the row exists to test and the detector still reports **24/24** -- byte-comparable to
the round's own preserved `baseline_24of24.out`.  Its want (`printed(t,"r2") == "0xef"`)
was placed entirely by the ANCHOR store; the `0x09` decline it names contributed no channel
at all.

> **The part that outlives the row: this same commit STATES the governing rule, in `R12`'s
> own comment -- *"wants an observable ONLY THE STORE CAN PRODUCE"* -- and violates it 130
> lines earlier, in a row added by the same diff.  R12's repair and R5d's introduction
> shipped together.**

That is the pre-table block's CHANNEL check failing at row-writing time **with its own
sentence already in the file** -- this project's trigger-versus-memory finding arriving
inside the artifact built to fix it.  Knowing a rule and having it fire on the right object
are different problems, and only the second is solved by writing more.

The repair is measured in BOTH directions: the same cut against the repaired row gives
`0xef|absent` against `0xef|09`, **the only FAIL in 28 rows**.  The detector is now 31 rows.

**THE CITABLE BASELINE**, which the shipped oracles owed and did not have:

    regress/artifacts/gdromcondlies/baseline31_20260830/run31_full.out
    31/31, 0 FAIL, GDROMCOND_CONTROL=OK *and* GDROMCOND_CONTROL_END=OK

The trailing control pair is not decoration.  A contended run once scored **18/25 with
`CONTROL=OK`** -- seven phantom failures -- because the controls all run in the first third
of the log, so a run that degrades afterwards reports healthy apparatus beside a wall of
product FAILs.  The pass-2 seat reached that same hazard independently, from the other side,
after its own three-store cut cascaded and it **retracted its first result rather than
filing it**: the unmodified probe scores 25/25 on an idle machine, so the cascade was the
seat's, not the probe's.  *A structural observation with no measured instance, recorded as
exactly that.*

The run's log also carries the **two-part clearance in its own header** --
`PART1_cmp_vs_SEC=CLEAN`, `PART2_binary_newer=YES` -- rather than asserting it beside the
record.  That is deliberate: this round's `build/` tree was found with the binary **fifteen
minutes OLDER than the source it was built from**, `cmp` clean, no `.MUTANT` sentinel, and
`CHECKPOINT.md` asserting the clearance held.  Third recorded instance of
propagate-and-forget-to-rebuild.  Severity was NIL here and the seat said so rather than
inflating it -- the delta was comment-only, verified as zero non-comment diff lines -- so a
wrong RECORD, not a wrong measurement.  **Run it; do not assert it.**

One honest narrowing, because the seat bounded its own finding: `R12b` **subsumes R5d's
stated mutant** (`0xff` carries bits 0 and 3 both).  R5d still earns its place -- a
conjunction ANDed with `idata < 0x80` escapes R12b -- but *"R5d is needed for the conjunction
family"* is a stronger claim than the evidence supports, and the row comment should say the
narrower thing.


## Round wdcatapistswap -- the accept side of #495's guard, and a floor breach found
## while pinning it

**A HARNESS round: no product code changed.**  It adds two accept arms to the rung-3
detector `#495` shipped, closing a measured hole in its accept side.  What arrived as
*"one accept row"* left as **two vehicles, three access widths and a repaired floor**,
every step of that growth forced by a seat.

### The hole

Swap the guard's flag operand for `d->atapi_st != NULL` and it escapes every row.  It is
not a contrived edit: `dev_wdc.c`'s own comment records that `atapi_cmd_in_progress`
*conflates two roles* and files exactly this refactor.  `atapi_st` has ONE write site and
**no clear site anywhere**, so after a single packet command the swapped guard refuses
every ordinary data-port write for the life of the device.

### *** THE BRIEF'S OWN MECHANISM WAS WRONG, AND A PACKET-FED SEAT REFUTED IT FROM THE
### INLINED FACTS ALONE ***

The brief said the differential runs *post-packet, with no command in between*.  The glm
seat objected that this needs some completion path to clear `atapi_cmd_in_progress`, and
named the absence of one as a hole in the narrative.  Checked: the flag has exactly two
write sites, and **no completion path clears it**.

> So the naive form of this row -- push and pop straight after the transfer -- is
> **VACUOUS**: the flag is still 1, the SHIPPED guard refuses too, both legs read `ff`.
> It would have shipped green on both legs, looking like coverage.
>
> **The clearing command is load-bearing, not scene-setting.**  The states where the two
> builds differ are exactly `flag == 0 && atapi_st != NULL`, and only a command produces
> them.  A correction that strengthened the design rather than weakening it.

A second seat then argued the row is too weak, because RECAL leaves `phase == 0` where
*the real hole* leaves `PHASE_COMPLETED`.  **That state does not exist**: the reset zeroes
flag and phase in the same three lines, and all SEVEN nonzero-phase writes lie on paths
where the flag is 1 -- so `flag == 0` implies `phase == 0`.  Refuted twice over, because
the mutant it proposed is #495's own M2, already measured KILLED at 18/22.

### Two vehicles, because one conjunct exempts one opcode

With only a RECAL arm, the grok seat found `&& d->cur_command != WDCC_RECAL` re-opens the
hole and sweeps every row: after RECAL `cur_command` is 0x10, during DATA-IN it is still
`ATAPI_PKT_CMD`, so the defect rows match the fix and the accept row stays green -- while
every OTHER no-fill command refuses again.

**A detector built from one scenario is blind along the axis that scenario holds fixed.**
#495 learned this twice in one round -- M5 on the PHASE axis, M6 on the WIDTH axis -- and
the axis here is *which no-fill opcode cleared the flag*.  Closed by a second arm through
`ATAPI_SOFT_RESET`: one conjunct cannot exempt two opcodes.  **Measured: E3 reds the N
rows and leaves the M rows green**, which is the design working rather than an argument
that it should.

## Round 495 (#495) -- a host store during an ATAPI DATA-IN transfer was pushed into the ring, and the guest read its own bytes back as disk data

Real ATAPI hardware never accepts host data-register stores while the direction is
device-to-host.  This model accepted them.  The injected bytes grew `inbuf_head`
**without growing `atapi_len`** -- which counts only what the DATA-IN arms pushed -- so
they sat ahead of the next chunk, the re-arm refilled on top of them, and the guest's
whole next chunk arrived shifted.

**AND IT WAS SILENT.**  The one diagnostic that could have announced a stray write
requires `!atapi_cmd_in_progress`, and that flag is 1 for the whole of DATA-IN.  The
single guard that might have caught this was disabled exactly when it was needed.

### The witness -- rung 3, and it had to be asked for

Unmodified `evbmips -e malta`, wdc via the machine's own committed `bus_pci`/`piix4_ide`
path with no `device_add`, free-running, 1.52 s.  **20 of 20 predictions across both
legs** (`wdcaddtoinbufbound/killtable_20260830/RESULTS_shipped.txt`, sentinel `ADDTOINBUF_RUNG3_DONE`):

    G  *** DEFECT ***  1st byte after the re-arm   base a5  fix c2
    H  *** DEFECT ***  2nd byte after the re-arm   base 5a  fix c3
    I  *** DEFECT ***  3rd byte after the re-arm   base c2  fix c4

`a5`/`5a` are **the guest's own injected bytes handed back as disk data**.  `c2`/`c3`/
`c4` are the poisoned image's content at the chunk-2 boundary -- an ABSOLUTE oracle,
tied to disk content through a channel outside the ring.

Controls green on both legs: RAM liveness; a DEVICE SIGNATURE (two reads of the same
address returning `5a` then `a5`, which a memory cell cannot do); encodings 46/46 words
AND mnemonics against the emulator's own disassembler; and row D returning the image
byte at offset 0, so the ring demonstrably holds real disk data rather than scratch.

*** THE SKETCH THIS ROUND BRIEFED COULD NOT HAVE EXHIBITED THE DEFECT AT ALL. ***  It
asked for 32 blocks on a CD-ROM, assuming 2048-byte blocks.  In this tree a CD-ROM's
`logical_block_size` is **512** -- the 2048 branch sits inside `#if 0` -- so 32 blocks
is 16384 bytes, under the 32768 chunk clamp: no second chunk, no re-arm, nothing to
measure.  It needs 128.  **A seat that had merely followed the brief would have produced
a clean run and reported the defect absent.**

### The floor determined the deliverable's shape, rather than auditing it

    base (defect LIVE)   128 rows,  0 failures
    fixA (shipped)       128 rows,  0 failures
    fixB (re-arm)        128 rows,  1 failure

**The shipped 128-row offline detector scores ZERO failures with this defect live.  It
cannot see the defect at all**, so vacuity-floor clause (a) -- fails on the pre-fix
build -- was **unsatisfiable from any existing row**.  That is why the rung-3 witness
ships AS a detector (`regress/wdc_addtoinbuf_probe.py`) rather than as evidence: not a
preference, the only way clause (a) could be met.  Its ROWS block is byte-identical to
the instrument that produced the 20/20.

The two are COMPLEMENTARY and neither subsumes the other, which was measured rather than
assumed: a guard-dropping mutant moves 14 rows in the offline detector and 2 in the
witness; the two clause-(d) mutants move 0 offline and 3 in the witness.

### The test is the PHASE, not the flag, and that is not cosmetic

`#477` measured that guarding these pushes could CREATE a use-after-free: a suppressed
push leaves occupancy at 12 and the CDB dispatch fires anyway.  **That hazard lives at
occupancy 12, which is CMDOUT** -- so a guard keyed on the PHASE never suppresses there
and cannot reach it.  A guard keyed on the FLAG ALONE matches CDB collection too and
re-arms the objection in full.  Derived by a packet-fed seat from the packet's own
internal consistency, and it is the difference between this fix and a wrong one.

**THE GUARD IS NOT SELF-CONTAINED, and the diff says so rather than leaving it to be
rediscovered:** it is safe only because `#477`'s READ-arm phase test stops a stray read
moving `atapi_phase` off CMDOUT mid-CDB.  Remove that and this starts refusing
legitimate CDB bytes.

### What this round does NOT do

* **`len` is not consulted** and the write arm still reads `data[0]` only.  Unchanged by
  this fix and not claimed.
* **The silence is not fixed.**  A pass-1 seat argued it is a separate defect from the
  push -- a guest can inject into a live transfer and nothing anywhere says so -- and
  proposed decline plus a latched `(once)` announce, the house idiom of which this very
  file is the reference implementation.  **The owner chose the guard without an
  announce.**  Recorded so a future reader sees a decision rather than an oversight.
* **The root cause is untouched.**  `#477`'s own comment names it: `atapi_cmd_in_progress`
  conflates *a packet command is active* with *I am collecting a CDB*.  A separate flag
  would make this guard trivially correct and remove the dependency above.  Bigger round.
* **The re-arm option was not taken.**  It is the only one that reds the shipped
  dirty-ring row, so it alone triggers the oracle-correction protocol -- and it is a
  PARTIAL fix by construction: an injection during the last chunk has no following
  re-arm and it never sees those bytes.

**M5 was predicted by a packet-fed seat that said plainly it could not check its own
claim from the packet.**  It was checkable here, and it was right: every row injected
during DATA-IN, where the narrowed guard still refuses, so a phase-narrowing edit swept
clean.  **A detector built entirely from one scenario is blind along the axis that
scenario holds fixed.**  Repaired by draining the whole transfer, injecting again in
PHASE_COMPLETED, and reading the status byte -- and a control a pass-1 seat had
correctly called WEAK becomes SHARP because the phase changed under it: `status_byte()`
ORs DRQ from three conditions during DATA-IN, but `PHASE_COMPLETED` is
`(WDCI_IN | WDCI_CMD)` and carries no `WDCS_DRQ`, so there DRQ reflects ring occupancy
alone.

**M6 is the mirror of M3, and M3 was the round's own mutant.**  Both injections were
2-byte stores, so `&& len == 2` refused both and passed everything -- *the table had
measured the inert member of the family and concluded the family was covered.*  Closed
by ONE INSTRUCTION: the second injection is now a single-byte store, so `len == 1` lets
the 2-byte one through and `len == 2` lets the 1-byte one through.  No single width
qualifier can refuse both.

### *** AND THE DEEPEST FINDING WAS ABOUT THE INSTRUMENTS, NOT THE FIX ***

**Four committed detectors reported `parked: yes` for a guest that never parked.**  Each
tested `if "BREAKPOINT" in <tail>.upper():` -- and the transcript contains the probe's
OWN echoed setup command, `breakpoint add 0x...`.  **The check matched its own input and
could never return False.**  It was right by accident in every run where the guest
parked, and silently wrong in the first run where it did not.  The emulator prints
`BREAKPOINT: pc = 0x...` on a real hit; that is now the pattern.  Controlled both ways:
the old check says parked on an echo-only transcript AND on a real hit; the new one
separates them.

**And the kill scorer would have scored such a run as a kill.**  A measuring seat
triggered exactly that three times in one table -- runs with `words 0 of 46`, pc already
at HALT and elapsed 0.00 s, on BOTH legs including the unmutated base, scored
`KILLED (20 red)`.  Re-run quietly, two ESCAPED.

*** EVERY ONE OF THOSE RUNS CARRIED THE COMPLETION SENTINEL.  The sentinel proves the
probe finished WRITING; it says nothing about whether it MEASURED.  Those are different
questions and only the first was being asked. ***  A false kill is worse than a false
escape: it certifies coverage that was never taken, and nothing downstream can tell.

`kill495.sh` now refuses to score a run whose BASE leg's controls failed.  **The
discriminator is the base leg, not a threshold** -- the base binary is known-good and
runs in the same invocation, so a control failure there is environmental while one
confined to the mutant leg is a result.  A threshold would have rejected M7, whose
mutant leg legitimately kills the guest.

The cause was this round's own concurrency: a second table ran during the first.  The
`#489` precedent licenses concurrent tables in scratch clones -- **but that precedent is
about TREE SAFETY, not MEASUREMENT VALIDITY**, and a pty-driven wall-clock instrument
corrupts silently under load.

### Two escapes FILED rather than fixed, and the distinction is the DEPENDS-ON bound

* **`wdcatapistswap`** -- swap the guard's flag operand for `atapi_st != NULL` and it
  escapes all 22 rows.  The seat measured the damage rather than reasoning it: after ONE
  packet command the swapped guard refuses every ordinary data-port write for the life
  of the device, because `atapi_st` is allocated at first dispatch and never set back to
  NULL.  **Not a clause-(d) breach by the letter** -- `atapi_st` is not read by the
  guarded body, so the operand-swap enumeration does not reach it -- but it shows the
  detector's accept side is unpinned for ordinary writes.  Owes one accept row.
* **`wdcprobeendian`** -- the write arm branches on `cpu->byte_order` and every rung-3
  probe here runs little-endian only, so a guard applied on one path and omitted on the
  other escapes by construction.  Structural, and it applies to every guard in that
  switch, not just this round's.

### Records repairs this round owes

**`shipped.diff` was rewritten IN PLACE after the table consumed it** -- the
immutable-artifact rule's exact shape, committed by this round.  The as-run bytes
survived only as a staged git blob and were recovered from it; both versions now sit in
`wdcaddtoinbufbound/killtable_20260830/` with `wdcaddtoinbufbound/killtable_20260830/PROVENANCE.txt` naming
which run consumed which, and the
comment-only claim was CHECKED rather than asserted (three code lines each, identical).

**Two files in that directory were written by a SEAT, not by this loop** -- an
independent replication of the M5 kill with clean apparatus, kept for that reason.  The
seat's report states it wrote nothing to the repo; the timestamps are consistent with a
cleanup pass after the report, so it is recorded as a timing gap rather than a false
statement.  **The general point is that an agent's account of what it touched is a
CLAIM, and `git status` is the check.**
### A live hazard on the machine, found by a seat rather than by a check

`/tmp/gxsec-build` -- the WSL arc tree -- held a **pre-`#494`** `dev_wdc.c` while
`build/`, `build-asan/` and `est/` all carried the fix.  A scratch clone taken from it
would have measured `#494`-less code in the very file under review **and `cmp`-ed clean
against its own donor**, so the two-part clearance would have passed on it.

Filed as `novpadfourth`: the no-VPATH rule names FOUR trees and precommit section B

## Round 494 (#494) -- the alt-ctrl handler never decoded its own offset, so a store to a read-only register aborted a live transfer

`DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus)` read `relative_addr` **zero times** across its 91 lines while
`dev_wdc_init` registered the region **two bytes wide**.  Offset 0 is Device Control (`0x3f6`);
offset 1 is the Drive Address register (`0x3f7`).  The handler could not tell them apart.

`#481` corrected the reset bit from `WDCTL_4BIT` to `WDCTL_RST` -- right for offset 0 -- and
wired in `wdc_new_command_reset()`.  From then on a guest store to a register it may not write
**aborted a live ATA write and purged the queued ring**.

Measured at rung 3 on unmodified `evbmips -e malta`, reached through the machine's own
committed `piix4_ide` path with no `device_add`, free-running.  Both legs from
`git archive HEAD` (the fix leg patched with the round's own working diff), built in `/tmp`;
**no project build tree was touched and no `.MUTANT` sentinel is owed.**  The two-part
clearance was RUN per leg rather than asserted.

    P1  accept    0x3f6 SRST aborts the write        50 on both legs   unchanged
    P2  DEFECT    0x3f7 store aborts the live write  base 50   fix 58
    P2  DEFECT    0x3f7 store purged staged bytes    base ff   fix 71
    P4  DEFECT    0x3f7 bare RST 0x04, same two      base 50/ff   fix 58/71
    P3  control   0x3f7 without WDCTL_RST: DRQ set   58 on both legs   unchanged

`0x58 -> 0x50` is DRQ clearing (the write aborted); `0xff -> 0x71` is `wdc_get_inbuf`
returning `-1` on a purged ring.  **On the committed build the two adjacent addresses are
byte-identical.**  Eighteen rows, both legs, **36 of 36 row predictions**
(`wdcaltoffset/killtable_20260830/RESULTS_detector18.txt`, sentinel `ALTOFF_DET_DONE`).

### The fix declines the WHOLE action, and that is the round's main finding

The reset has **two effects with two owners**: `d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET;` is assigned
by the caller, and the ring and DRQ are cleared inside `wdc_new_command_reset()`.  A fix that
guards only the helper call leaves the ATAPI signature latched.

That is not hypothetical.  The measuring seat built it (`m3`) and it **passed all 18 rows, 36
of 36 predictions**, because every defect row observes DRQ or the input ring -- both cleared by
the helper -- and nothing observed `cur_command`.  It proved non-equivalence rather than
asserting it: the signature is keyed on `cur_command == COMMAND_RESET` AND a CD-ROM image, so
the channel is **dead on the `iR:` rig the witness uses**.  Re-run with `ciR:`:

    L1  cyl_lo/cyl_hi round-trip BEFORE any poke   55/66 on every leg
    D   cyl_lo/cyl_hi after the 0x3f7 poke         base 14/eb   fix 55/66   m3 14/eb
    L2  cyl_lo/cyl_hi after the LEGAL 0x3f6 poke   14/eb on every leg

Both control pairs green on all three legs, so the fix leg's quiet D row is a **refusal and not
a dead path** (`RESULTS_signature.txt`, sentinel `ALTOFF_SIG_DONE`).

### The decline is silent, and the census that was owed changed the reason

The de-fatalisation option set carries an obligation to grep the fork for the existing idiom
before choosing.  The pass-1 brief invoked the rule and reported no census; the glm seat caught
that, and the census was run (`readonly_write_census_20260830.txt`, with its deriver recorded).

It answers a different question than it was run for.  **All three announcing sites in the tree
report a guest ANOMALY** -- nothing legitimately writes `CHIPID`, `IPL` or `MBC`, and PCTL warns
only `if (idata & 0x78)`, the anomalous subset.  A store to `0x3f7` is **correct guest
behaviour on a PC**: the tree says so twice, in `wdcreg.h` (`#if 0` -- NOT MAPPED, fd uses this
register on PCs) and in `dev_fdc.c` (`DEV_FDC_LENGTH 6`, TODO 8 but collision with wdc).

So the decline stays at `debug()` level with no latch, and returns through the common tail with
**`return 1` (handled), never 0** -- a `0` routes the access to unassigned-address handling,
measured this round as one unbounded `non-existant paddr` warning per access, a read returning
`0x00`, and `running = 0` on every CPU under `-T`.

### The kill table, with its counts corrected

    m1  over-reach     `!= 0` -> `!= 2`      2 red, 34/36   killed by the ACCEPT rows
    m2  nulled decode  `!= 0` -> `>  1`      4 red, 32/36   killed by the defect rows + sig
    m3  partial guard  helper-only           0 red, 36/36   KILLED ONLY BY THE SIGNATURE
    m4  value guard    `&& idata == 0x06`    2 red, 34/36   killed by the PHASE 4 rows

**Two of the four are killed only by a row `wdcaltoffset/killtable_20260830/PRETABLE.out` prescribed before the product edit**,
and both survived the row-list rewrite -- no `#490` recurrence.  `m4` is the shape a well-meaning
hand makes: `0x06` is both the witness's value and the one `#481`'s comment documents as real
OpenBSD traffic, so *tighten the decline to known traffic* re-opens the defect for `0x04`,
`0x0c` and `0x0e` while every earlier row stays green.

*** THE COUNTS ABOVE ARE CORRECTED.  `wdcaltoffset/killtable_20260830/TABLE.txt` AS RUN REPORTS EACH NONZERO FIGURE ONE
TOO HIGH. ***  `grep -c ' FAIL '` also matched the probe's own verdict line -- *SOMETHING DID
NOT HOLD -- read the FAIL line*.  Found by the fable5 seat and cross-checked against the
probe's independent `N of 36` figure.  **The only count that was right was the zero**: with
nothing failing there is no verdict line to miscount, so the anomalous-looking row was the
correct one.  Every KILLED verdict is unchanged -- the counter was wrong about magnitude, never
about sign.  `wdcaltoffset/killtable_20260830/TABLE.txt` is corrected IN PLACE rather than re-run, because silently restating
history is indistinguishable from fitting the record to the answer.

### What this round does NOT do -- and the width qualifier is load-bearing

It **decodes the offset of a byte store and declines stores addressed at offset 1.  A `len == 2`
store at offset 0 still passes the decode with its `0x3f7` byte silently consumed** -- the
handler reads `data[0]` only and never examines `len`.  Width is `wdcaltwidth`, open, and must
not be read as closed by this.  *(This round already paid for the dropped-qualifier class once:
see the L4 below.)*

* **The read side is unfixed and deliberately unshipped.**  Offset 1 reads still return
  alt-status on all four platform layouts, which matches no hardware anywhere.  Filed as
  `wdcaltdigin`.  A seat refuted the earlier ruling that it has no oracle: the test is an
  INVARIANCE, not a value -- `status_byte()` never reads `d->head`, so `0x3f7` reads `51` at
  head 0 and `51` at head 15 while the SDH readback of `0xaf` proves the head write landed.  A
  second, independent refutation: the read returns `58` with DRQ raised, and a real Drive
  Address register never carries DRQ.  That says today's value is wrong without saying what is
  right, which is why it files rather than ships.
* **The region was NOT narrowed.**  The fdc TODO of 8 ports is `0x3f0..0x3f7` and the alt region
  is `0x3f6..0x3f7`, so the overlap is two bytes: freeing `0x3f7` still blocks fdc at `0x3f6`.
  Filed as `wdcaltownership`.  *The glm seat noted that this warrant assumes contiguous
  registration, which the packet never stated; the conclusion survives on the measured return-0
  cost instead, and the stated warrant is not what carries it.*
* **Two mutants pass BOTH detectors** and are recorded as coverage debt, not a floor breach:
  guarding the inner `if` with `relative_addr == 0`, and conditioning the decline on the reset
  bit.  Both still refuse the destructive action; what they revert is the corrected diagnostic
  text.  Named by the minimax seat, which drew the distinction itself.

### Disclosure: the battery defends none of this today

Both detectors are `CLASS_DETECTOR` and **dated-exempt from gate wiring until 2026-09-20**.
They are two-leg differentials -- they take a pre-fix binary and a post-fix one -- and no gate
builds a second leg; the signature probe additionally needs a `ciR:` CD-ROM rig the battery does
not build.  Wiring them needs a single-leg mode, which is a change to the instrument and owes
its own red-on-pre-fix order proof.  **Until then the kill table is the evidence, not the gate.**

Both probes now carry a clause-(e) CONTRACT naming what they catch and what they are blind to
by construction.  A label collision to note: `killtable_20260830/PRETABLE.out`'s C5 uses `m4` for the width-1
registration experiment while `killtable_20260830/TABLE.txt`'s `m4` is the value guard -- same label, two mutants,
one round.  `killtable_20260830/PRETABLE.out` is left unedited because it is an order-proof artifact.

### Pass 2 refused to ratify, and it was right: one L2 floor breach, repaired in-round

The measuring seat built six mutants and found **a one-conjunct edit that escapes BOTH
shipped detectors**:

```c
else if (relative_addr != 0 && !(idata & WDCTL_4BIT)) {
```

36 of 36 on the main detector, declined on the signature.  **The reason is structural, not
bad luck.**  The detectors' only three offset-1 values were `0x06`, `0x02` and `0x04` --
**all three with bit 3 clear** -- so every offset-1 row sat in one `WDCTL_4BIT` equivalence
class.  The round defended the value axis against EQUALITY guards (that is what `m4` and the
PHASE 4 rows are) and never against MASK guards.

And it is not an exotic bit.  `dev_wdc.c`'s own `#481` comment records that `WDCTL_4BIT` is
what libata holds as its **steady-state `ap->ctl`**, and that comment's own level-vs-edge
measurement asserts SRST with `0x0e`.  **A mask guard re-opens the defect at exactly the
values the commonest driver actually writes.**  Measured at `0x0e` on offset 1: base `50/ff`
(reset), fix `58/71` (declined), mutant `50/ff` -- the defect fully restored.

**Repaired in-round** (clause (d) is a floor clause, so L2 however late it is found) by a
third detector, `regress/wdc_altoffset_4bit_probe.py`: a P5/P6 phase pair at `0x0e`, 47 of 49
predicted cells, **and the two so-called misses ARE the predicted P6 red under an
over-reaching decline** -- so the accept row is discharged by a measured kill rather than by
existing.  It ships as a separate probe rather than as extra phases on the main one, because
adding rows perturbs every mutant's score and forces a full re-table; that is the cost `#462`
paid and there was no reason to pay it twice.

The seat shipped a **positive control** with the finding -- a nulled decode reds at 32/36 --
which is what makes three escapes evidence rather than proof that the harness is inert.

### And it refuted this round's own reason for `return 1`

The shipped comment said a `0` would fall through to unassigned-address handling and warn per
access.  **False on the path and false on the symptom.**  This device is REGISTERED, so a `0`
never reaches that path: `memory_rw` sets `res = -1`, raises `EXCEPTION_DBE` and returns
MEMORY_ACCESS_FAILED, and `memory_warn_about_unimplemented_addr` has exactly one caller,
*after* the device loop.  Measured under `-v`: the return-0 mutant produced **19,793**
`device 'wdc_altstatus' ... failed` lines and **zero** `non-existant` ones.

At default verbosity it is **silent**, while the guest loops forever re-executing the faulting
store.  That is worse than a warning flood, not better -- which is precisely why the wrong
reason had to be corrected rather than quietly dropped: *a maintainer who reads "only noisy
warnings" may well decide a 0 is acceptable.*  The decision is unchanged; its warrant is now
the true mechanism, which is the stronger one.

Two lesser warrants in the same comment were also weak and are gone: `#95` already zeroes the
caller's buffer, so the untouched-buffer hazard cannot arise, and this arm is write-side, so
the common tail is a no-op for it either way.

### Three things the pass found that this round does NOT fix

* **`killtable_20260830/PRETABLE.out`'s GUARD-FIELD `N/A` is refuted.**  It recorded that the predicate reads no
  device field the body writes.  One escaping mutant is precisely a predicate reading
  `d->atapi_cmd_in_progress` -- a field the block's own body list names.  Two of the six
  mutants live in the space that `N/A` declared empty.  The block is left unedited (it is an
  order-proof artifact) and the refutation is recorded here and on the row.
* **No probe in this family READS the alt region.**  Every access in all three is a store, so
  the handler's read path -- the register's primary function -- is pinned by zero rows.  That
  is `wdcaltdigin`'s territory and is now stated in all three contracts.
* **One flat claim of mine was wrong about three platforms.**  Offset 1 is the Drive Address
  register at `addr_mult == 1`; on landisk (2) and macppc (0x10) it is a byte lane, because
  the alt region is hardcoded two bytes wide and never divides by `addr_mult` the way the main
  handler does.  The behaviour is still correct there; the claim was not.

The pass-1 adjudication rejected narrowing on the warrant that *the tree's own bundled header
defines TWO registers in the aux region*, citing `wd_digin`.  **That define sits inside**

register and disables the other with an annotation saying the opposite of the reading taken.
The grok and codex seats found it independently.  **I had already reported that warrant

### The row-3 result is the one worth copying

It went green with **no pin raised, no allowlist widened, no exemption, and the

### *** THE DETECTOR THIS ROUND SHIPPED WAS AN L2 FLOOR BREACH, AND ITS KILL TABLE WAS CLEAN. ***

The row-5 replacement counted per-latch PRESENCE.  Every mutant in its table happened
to target a SINGLE-SITE latch, so **the table ran on a population that structurally
could not exhibit the defect**.  `warned_inbuf_overrun` has two sites:

```
if (!d->warned_inbuf_overrun) {   ->   if (1) {      at ONE of its TWO sites
=> set=2 read=1, census says SET=6 READ=6, gate GREEN
=> the producer flood is unbounded again -- #464's exact defect
```

Floor clause (b) demands failure on reinstatement at EVERY fixed site, so that is L2,
fixed in-round.  **Note the inversion, which is the lesson:** the old pin counted
OCCURRENCES, so a second site moved it -- loud, wrong, but alive.  Presence-only made
losing one of two INVISIBLE -- quiet, wrong, and silent.

Replaced by per-latch `set_count == read_count` (RELATIONAL, so growth increments both
sides and it is growth-invariant by construction) plus a latch-population count, which
restores a tripwire this round would otherwise have DELETED -- the de-escalation clause
one level up.  Eleven mutants, all killed, base clean, artifact `killtable3.out`.

### The same defect, four generations, the last two mine in the repair

1. the original pin counted **lines** where it meant occurrences -- read 15 against 12;
2. my replacement counted **presence** -- the L2 above;
3. my kill table's M1/M2 **never applied** (the guards are multi-line) and my vacuity
   guard caught only TOTAL no-ops, so a partially-applied mutant scored as something
   it was not.  *fable5 found this from the published numbers alone: 'a true pair
   deletion reads 5/5, and the table shows 5/6.'*  It now reads exactly 5/5/5/11;
4. my replacement pattern-check used `grep -c`, which **counts lines**, so it demanded
   two lines when the mutant put both mentions on one.

The promptless census was wrong three times on its own account -- a false universal, an
impossible partition (3+8+1=12 over a nine-member set), and then a claim that
`drive_guest.py` is neither, when it budget-drains under a different SPELLING.  **I had
grepped for `time.time() < end` and measured the spelling instead of the mechanism**,

## Round 491 (#491) -- two compiler warnings were costing an entire GATE, and the battery that would have said so had been red and unread for five days

`#472` replaced `len > OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE? OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE : len` with
`len > remain? remain : len`.  `len` is a `size_t` parameter; `remain` is `off_t`.
gcc warns twice at `diskimage.c:1382` under the tree's own `CWARNINGS`.

### *** IT IS NOT A LIVE BUG, AND THIS ROUND WILL NOT IMPLY OTHERWISE. ***

`inblock = curofs & (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE - 1)` gives `[0, 511]`, so `remain` is in
`[1, 512]` and is positive by construction.  The implicit conversion is
value-preserving at every reachable value.  **Both casts are provable rather than
plausible**, and the comment says which fact makes each safe:

```c
lentoread = len > (size_t) remain? remain : (off_t) len;
```

`(size_t) remain` -- remain is never negative.  `(off_t) len` -- that arm is reached
only when `len <= remain <= 512`.

### THE REASON IT IS A ROUND AND NOT A TIDY-UP: IT WAS COSTING A GATE

`gate_build` wants ZERO warnings, so it FAILED.  It withdraws
`$RIG/gxsec-gxemul` at start and republishes **only on success**.  `gate_mips`
then `need_exec`s that binary and reported:

    mips-rigs: SKIP -- missing or non-executable binary: .../gxsec-gxemul

**A whole gate's coverage lost, and scored as SKIP rather than FAIL.**  That is
byte-identical in shape to what ONE stale allowlist line cost on 2026-08-23 --
the defect `gatebuildallow` records, whose own summary reads *"one line of text
cost two gates."*  It has now happened twice, by two different routes, through
the same withdraw-and-republish mechanism.

### MEASURED -- control first, and the FIRST attempt was vacuous

| | rc | object | sign-compare |
|---|---|---|---|
| reconstructed pre-fix line | 0 | 44072 b | **2** |
| shipped `#491` | 0 | 44112 b | **0** |

Then the cascade itself, which is the claim that actually matters:

    BEFORE       arc rig binary ABSENT -- withdrawn by the failed battery run
    gate_build   ok pmax: warnings 0 / ok arc: warnings 0 / PASS (18 checks)
    republished  gxsec-gxemul  6155864 b
    gate_mips    mips-rigs: PASS (6 checks)        <- was SKIP

*The ABSENT row is the control: it shows the binary really had been withdrawn, so
the republication is attributable to this fix rather than assumed.*

> *** MY FIRST VERIFICATION WAS VACUOUS AND ITS OWN NEGATIVE CONTROL CAUGHT IT.
> ***  It reported **0** warnings for the PRE-FIX form, which must be 2.  The

### HOW IT SURVIVED TWO DAYS, stated as exposure rather than blame

Warnings need a BUILD; builds are too slow for `precommit_check.sh`; so warnings
are checked **only by the weekly battery**.  A warning-introducing commit is
therefore invisible for up to seven days -- and only surfaces then if someone
READS the result.  The battery had been RED since 2026-08-23 on an unrelated
stale allowlist entry, and `nightly_check.sh` cannot distinguish *fixed* from
*never looked at*.  **So this sat behind a red everyone already had an
explanation for.**

*#472's own round is not at fault: the per-commit targeted gate is narrow by
design, and that is the documented two-tier structure working as written.*

### FILED, not fixed here

The same battery run surfaced five more reds, all harness bookkeeping and none
product defects.  They go to their own round because two are NOT simple re-pins:
`readiness: whole-buffer full-prompt` is a **fail-closed allowlist over a pattern
#392 measured at 0/80** and must not be raised, and `wdcflood: six warned_ guards`
needs an equality->floor change plus an L4 correction to its own comment, which
claims immunity to the growth that just broke it.

## Round 490 (#490) -- two guest-reachable host kills in the GD-ROM command handler, and a detector that a capped ask-again then escaped three times

`handle_command()` ended the host process on two ordinary guest writes.  `case 0x30` killed on any data format outside {0x20, 0x24}; the `default:` arm killed on any unimplemented command byte.  Both are reached by a guest assembling a 12-byte packet through the data port -- no harness, no direct call.

Both are now DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE, the house idiom (`N = 1` per device instance, `(once)` in the message text), then `break` to the function's common tail.

### The two things that were NOT obvious, and both are measured

**TWO latch bits, not one.**  A one-bit form was built (`M3shared`) and it ESCAPED: a session declining at BOTH sites sees the second fall silent, because the first already latched.

**`break`, not `return`, and the tail is why.**  The common tail zeroes `d->cnt`, clears `COND_DATA_AVAIL` and fires the completion event.  `M_retA`/`M_retB` measure a `return` leaving `cnt` at 0x98 with no event -- **two channels, both sites** -- so an early return leaves a guest waiting for a completion that never comes.  *That was a claim in a comment until the table made it two rows at two sites.*

### THREE MEASURED ESCAPES IN THE ASSERT, and the form already landed closes all three

The supplementary panel's ninth seat attacked the compile-time assert from
the side no control had varied.  The shipped controls changed only the
`#define` block, which pins `GDROM_W_NBITS` at 9 in every state and makes the
equality a genuine pigeonhole.  **Vary the ENUM instead and it collapses**:
an explicit enumerator initialiser renumbers every later enumerator, so
`NBITS` falls in lockstep with the lost bit and the equality RE-BALANCES.

Eight states x both operator forms, generated from the real file with md5s
per source state (`supp_p2_20260829/bothstates_20260829.out`):

| state | `|` (as first written) | `+` (shipped) |
|---|---|---|
| `enum CMD_B = FMT_B`, one token | **COMPILES -- ESCAPE** | REFUSED |
| `enum FMT_B = OVERREAD_B`, relocated | **COMPILES -- ESCAPE** | REFUSED |
| `FMT` redefined as a 2-bit superset | **COMPILES -- ESCAPE** | REFUSED |
| `#define` aliases; completeness at front and back | correct | correct |

The seat's own diagnosis is the sentence worth keeping: an OR test *"proves
coverage relative to a count derived from the possibly aliased last enum
value; it does not independently count masks."*  **That is vacuity-floor
clause (f) -- the ANCHOR RULE -- one level down, inside a constant
expression: a RELATIVE check where an ANCHORED one was needed.**  A sum
cannot absorb a duplicate, so `+` is the anchored form.

`+` had already landed from fable5's multi-bit finding, before this seat
answered.  It is **strictly better than the seat's own proposal** -- its
`SUM == OR` candidate would have lost the two completeness cases -- and the
seat recorded its superseded suggestion rather than dropping it.

**Note the in-place / relocated pair.**  The same alias is REFUSED in place
and ESCAPES when moved, because an alias left where it was keeps `NBITS`
unchanged.  A control that varies one and not the other reports a clean
sweep.

## Round 489 (#489) -- a guest-supplied length ended the host, and deleting the guard would have been worse than the kill

`handle_command()`'s `case 0x14` (Read Table-Of-Contents) read:

```c
	if (d->cnt != 408) {
		fatal("GDROM Read TOC not 408 bytes?\n");
		exit(1);
	}
	alloc_data(d);
```

`d->cnt` is **GUEST-SUPPLIED** -- two 16-bit stores to `GDROM_CNTLO`/`GDROM_CNTHI` -- so an
ordinary guest register access ended the host process.

*** AND THE GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A DECLINE AND NOT A DELETION. ***
`alloc_data()` mallocs `d->cnt` bytes, but the TOC writer below uses HARDCODED indices --
`grep -oE 'd->data\[[0-9]+\*4(\+[0-9])?\]'` gives a highest byte index of **407** -- so it
needs 408 bytes regardless of `cnt`. Deleting the `exit(1)` would have converted a host kill
into a **GUEST-CONTROLLED HEAP OVERFLOW of up to 408 bytes**, with `malloc(0)` at `cnt == 0`.
So the decline lands BEFORE the guarded statement, not after it.

`break` and not `return`: `free_data()` at the top of the function left `d->data == NULL`, so
the common tail takes its else branch -- `cnt = 0`, `COND_DATA_AVAIL` cleared -- and **still
fires `SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT`**. An early return would skip that event and hang the guest.
`case 0x30` already ships that idiom twice in this same function -- its `sector_count` clamp
and its `sector_count * 2048 != d->cnt` mismatch both `break`.

> *** THAT SENTENCE CITED THE ANCHOR `OB-20: was exit(1)` AND THE CITATION WAS WRONG TWICE.
> Corrected 2026-08-28; the measuring seat found both halves. ***
>
> **It is not unique** -- the anchor has ONE product hit, and the second "hit" is the
> instruction TELLING you to grep, quoting itself.  A self-referential anchor counts itself,
> which is the same shape as a `ps | grep` that matches its own command line.
>
> **And it misdescribes one of the two sites.**  The `sector_count <= 0` clamp **does not
> exist in pristine 2021 upstream at all** (`grep -c 'rejecting sector_count'`: 0 upstream, 1
> here), so it was never an `exit(1)` -- it is a guard this fork ADDED.  "Ships this idiom
> twice" is true of the *break* idiom and false of the *"was exit(1)"* framing the anchor
> spells.  Cited by CONSTRUCT now, per the citation-form rule, which is what that rule is for.

Latched per the house idiom, N=1 per device instance with an explicit `(once)` marker, because
`fatal()` cannot be silenced by `-q`. This is the SEVENTH warn bit -- the condition
`gdromwarnbits`' pre-set trigger was written for, discharged one commit earlier.

*** THE ROUND SHIPPED A DETECTOR WITH A MEASURED ESCAPE AND A REVIEW SEAT FOUND IT. ***  The
FIRST version had 13 rows and scored **13/13 against `break;` -> `return;`** -- a total escape.

*** THAT SCORE HAS NO DIRECT ARTIFACT, AND THE RECORD SAYS SO RATHER THAN IMPLYING ONE. ***
Table 1 contains no M7 run -- M7 did not exist when it was built, which is the whole point.
The proof is INDIRECT but complete: `killtable2_20260828/M7_return.raw` shows all THIRTEEN

so a 13/13 sweep is entailed.  **Cite that artifact for the claim** -- a score whose log does
not exist is the frozen-number class, and the honest form is to name the log that ENTAILS it.

**`bad cond`, the clause-(d) carrier, is STRUCTURALLY BLIND to it**, and the reason is worth
recording because it looks like the row that should catch it: the guest writes `0xa0` to start
the command, and **bit 3 is already clear in `0xa0`**, so the tail's
`d->cond &= ~COND_DATA_AVAIL` is a NO-OP on this path. `break` (tail runs, clears an
already-clear bit) and `return` (tail never runs) both leave `0xa0`. A row can only separate
them by observing something the TAIL WRITES.

**And this round's own product comment CLAIMED that property** -- *"an early return would skip
that event and leave the guest waiting forever"* -- **while shipping no row for it.** That is
the CLAIM -> ROW pre-table check, unrun, on the round's own diff.

On the decline path the tail writes exactly two things, so there is one row each, and both
expectations were DERIVED FROM SOURCE AND THEN CONFIRMED -- not read off the binary:

| row | derivation | correct | mutant |
|---|---|---|---|

## Round 488 (#488) -- a short read in a NON-FINAL iteration corrupted twice, and the round that touched these exact lines was asking a different question

`fread_helper()` splits an overlayed read into 512-byte pieces, and three accounting
lines disagreed about which length they use:

```c
	len          -= lentoread;      /*  REQUESTED  */
	totallenread += lenread;        /*  ACTUAL     */
	buf          += lentoread;      /*  REQUESTED  */
```

So a short read in a **non-final** iteration left a stale HOLE at its own position while
every later iteration still landed correctly, and the caller's tail
`memset(buf + lendone, 0, len - lendone)` -- correct only if the shortfall was at the END
-- then destroyed an equal number of **valid** bytes at the far end. The access returned 1.

**MEASURED on the committed build before any edit**, 1536 bytes at offset 0 over a
200-byte overlay claiming block 0: **312 stale caller bytes in the middle, 712 of 1024
base bytes surviving**
(`regress/artifacts/shortread/repro_20260827/PREFIX_committed_6faba0f.out`).

### The fix is two lines

```c
	if (lenread != lentoread) {
		fatal(...);
		memset(buf + lenread, 0, lentoread - lenread);   /*  ADDED  */
	}
	len -= lentoread;
	totallenread += lentoread;                              /*  was += lenread  */
	buf += lentoread;
```

### *** THE ALTERNATIVE WAS BUILT AND IT REPRODUCES THE DEFECT. ***

The obvious alternative -- stop the loop, report the contiguous prefix, and let the
caller's tail memset become correct by construction -- was built and measured. A **rung-3
witness on unmodified `landisk`**, a guest `READ SECTORS` reading the data port:

| build | halfword at byte 1534 |
|---|---|
| committed | `0x0000` -- FAIL (the disk holds `'B','B'`) |
| the alternative | `0x0000` -- **FAIL, byte-identical to the defect** |
| this fix | **`0x4242` -- ok** |

The adjudicating seat had already reached it by argument -- *"A is not fail-stop, it is
fail-more"*: the caller fixes the postcondition either way, so the only freedom is WHICH
bytes are fabricated zeros, and the alternative fabricates the lost bytes plus every
healthy byte after them, up to 63.5 sectors of a 64-sector `wdc__read`. **The measurement
agreed and went further than the argument had.**

### The severity is higher than "stale caller bytes", and it was verified before being written down

In `wdc__read` the hole is not abstract memory. The common arm reads straight into the
**persistent ring**, so the hole retains **previous ring contents** -- prior-sector data
replayed to the guest. The wrap arm reads into `unsigned char buf[512 * MAX_SECTORS_PER_CHUNK]`,
an **uninitialised automatic array**, and then copies *every* byte into that ring
regardless of what the read filled -- so the hole is **uninitialised host stack memory
handed to the guest**. SCSI holes read as zeros (its transfer buffer is allocated zeroed),
so this is wdc-specific.

**The precondition is host-side and the trigger is ordinary guest I/O.** A guest cannot
truncate a host file; what produces the state is a hand-made `.map`, a user `V:` overlay,
truncation of an already-claimed overlay, or a genuine read-side I/O error.
**`R:` cannot CONSTRUCT it** -- it starts empty+empty and unlinks both files, so no
persistent bitmap/data-length mismatch can accumulate there.  *An earlier draft said flatly
"`R:` cannot", and a review seat called that too absolute: a genuine read-side I/O error
can short-read an `R:` overlay like any other.  What `R:` rules out is the CONSTRUCTION
route, not the defect.* But once the state exists, `wdc__read`
issues up to 64 sectors in one `diskimage_access()` and the corrupt buffer reaches the
guest -- and wdc **discards the boolean return entirely** (`/* TODO: result code from the
read? */`), so nothing anywhere objects.

### An L4 in shipped code, found by a seat that could not open the file

`#472`'s comment sat directly above the defective line and read *"advance by what was
CONSUMED"*. **`lentoread` is what was REQUESTED.** The two are equal on a full read and
differ on exactly the short read this round is about -- so the comment was true in the
common case and false in the only case it was written for. `#472` named the hazard class
correctly (*"leaves HOLES"*, *"a row counting bytes the read never wrote"*), shipped a
detector row for it, named the fix, and then advanced by the requested length anyway.

*That is why this survived: the round that edited these exact lines was asking a different
question.* Found by **minimax**, a packet-fed seat, from inlined text alone, while four
file-reading seats had the whole tree. Corrected in place.

### The detector: 98 rows

```
PRE-FIX   98 rows, 18 failures, 0 faults   DISKIMAGE_IO_FAIL
POST-FIX  98 rows,  0 failures, 0 faults   DISKIMAGE_IO_PASS
```
`regress/artifacts/shortread/round_20260827/{PREFIX,POSTFIX}_98rows.out`

> ### *** AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS BLOCK SAID 'every new row fires on the REAL defect'.
> ### THAT IS FALSE, and the round's own pre-fix log refutes it. ***
>
> **ROW L, ROW I, ROW W and ROW T fire on the real defect.**  ROW P, ROW U, ROW Z and
> ROW S are **green pre-fix by design** -- they probe positions where the caller's tail
> memset already handled the shortfall correctly -- and are discharged by their own
> mutants instead.  Deriver: `PREFIX_98rows.out`, 18 failures, none of them P/U/Z/S.
>
> *Found by three seats independently.  The sentence was written from the intent of the
> rows rather than from the log they produce, which is the same failure the NUL-count row
> demonstrates one paragraph down: `NUL fill covers exactly the unbacked hole = 312` is
> **ok on the broken build**.  The anchors are what make position absolute.*

**Pass 1 found SIX escapes against a detector that had just reproduced the defect
cleanly, and every one was the same shape: the fixture varied one dimension and the mutant
lived in another.**

| escape | why the rows were blind | closed by |
|---|---|---|
| `remain - lenread` | every probed iteration had `inblock == 0`, so `remain == lentoread` -- **equivalent over the probed set** | ROW P, ROW U |
| `if (lenread > 0)` | no row probed an **empty** overlay | ROW Z |
| `&& overlay_nr >= 0` | every row shorted on the **overlay** layer | ROW L |
| `&& totallenread == 0` | every row shorted in **iteration 1** | ROW I |

### The vacuity floor, clause by clause

(a) 13 rows red pre-fix. (b) `M1_revert` killed. (c) `[IDENTITY]` pinned at 90.
(d) `M3_countonly` -- guard kept, count reverted -- killed, as `glm`, `minimax`, `grok` and
`codex` all independently predicted. (e) contract in the section header. (f) **ten** `[ANCHOR]` rows --
deriver `grep -c 'check("\[ANCHOR\]' regress/diff_diskimage_io.c`, because an earlier
draft said six and a seat counted.

**Mutant denominators, named because two of them are different artifacts:** the
measuring seat's 17-mutant table was run at **86 rows** and is preserved verbatim at
`round_20260827/seat_table_86rows/` (20 logs).  The four escape mutants were re-run
against the **shipped 98-row** set and are `mutant_E{1,2,3,4}_*_98rows.out`.  *Adding
rows cannot resurrect a mutant that already failed, so the 86-row kills stand -- but a
score claim names the artifact that produced it, and these are two artifacts.*

### Two mutants measured EQUIVALENT, recorded as results rather than gaps

A 149,072-case sweep over base size x overlay size x bitmap x offset x length, hashing the
whole buffer, with **two controls that DO fail** (69,880 and 9,686 differing cases):

* `len - lenread` as the fill length -- **0 differing.** And provable rather than merely
  measured: `buf` rises by `lentoread` exactly as `len` falls by it, so **`buf + len` is
  invariant at the original request's end** and the fill can never write past it.
* `lenread < lentoread` for `!=` -- **0 differing** (`fread` cannot return more than
  requested).

### The ask-again found three escapes; ONE row taken, TWO filed

* **TAKEN -- `&& d->writable` (ROW W).** It passed all 86 rows **and all 149,072 sweep
  cases**, because neither ever opened a read-only disk. Writability is not a length, an
  offset or a layer, so no amount of sweeping those could reach it. *This round's own
  finding, turned on the instrument built to enforce it.*
  **Discharged by a MEASURED KILL, not by existing**: the mutant was built against the
  **90**-row set (the seat had only measured it against 86) and ROW W reddens --
  `mutant_E1_writable_98rows.out`, 2 failures, both ROW W's. Honestly: **2 of ROW W's 4
  rows discriminate**; the base-byte count is unchanged under the mutant because only the
  fill is skipped.
* **THEN PASS 2 CLOSED BOTH OF THEM, AND ADDED A THIRD ESCAPE AND ITS ROW.**

  **ROW T** -- `&& d->type == DISKIMAGE_SCSI`, found by `grok`.  `mkdisk()` hardcodes
  `DISKIMAGE_SCSI` and neither the rows nor the sweep ever varied it.  **It is sharper
  than the other two because of where it fires**: `wdc__read()` looks up `DISKIMAGE_IDE`
  and landisk's default type is IDE, so this conjunct **re-opens the defect on the only
  guest path the round actually drove** -- the rung-3 witness would go red while the
  detector stayed green.  Killed by ROW T: `mutant_E4_scsitype_98rows.out`, 2 failures.

  **ROW S** -- two shorts in ONE call (overlay 200 bytes, bitmap `0x05`, read 1536), and
  it kills **both** previously-filed escapes: `mutant_E2_threshold_98rows.out` and
  `mutant_E3_firstshort_98rows.out`, 3 failures each.  The adjudicating seat argued for
  taking rather than filing it, and its reason is the one that convinced me: this
  `fatal()` is unlatched and guest-floodable, the house idiom for such a site is
  latch-plus-fatal, and **the natural bad latch edit braces this memset in with the
  fatal** -- which is exactly the first-short-only shape.  Not a hypothetical future edit;
  the most plausible one in the round.

  **So no escape from either pass remains open.**  What stays filed is a CLASS rather than
  an escape: **fitted-threshold conjuncts**.  ROW S kills `< 1024`'s instance, but
  `< 2048` escapes, and so on -- the ladder's limit is the fix itself, so no finite row set
  closes it and chasing it is the unbounded fix-of-fix shape.

  *** AND MY WARRANT FOR TAKING ONE AND FILING TWO WAS WRONG EVEN WHERE THE ACTIONS WERE
  RIGHT, which the adjudicator corrected: the ask-again's cap limits ASK-AGAINS, not
  FINDINGS *** -- `#452` added six rows from a single ask.  And `E1` was never
  discretionary: `if (X)` -> `if (X && Y)` aimed at the predicate dominating the memset is
  the canonical clause-(d) qualification form, and it swept the detector clean, so under
  DEPENDS-ON it is a **floor breach repaired in-round**, not a row I chose to take.

### What pass 2 caught in the BRIEF rather than the code

Two packet-fed seats refused to ratify, both naming the same missing fact: the brief
inlined a four-line window and **not the function's `return`**, so "the only consumer of
`totallenread` is the tail memset" and "the overlaid path returns `len` or 0" were **not
checkable from the packet**. Both are true -- `return totallenread;`, one call site,
consumed only by the tail memset and a write-only check -- and both were settled by
reading. **The seats were right and the defect was mine**, and it is the "inline every fact
a cloud seat needs" rule broken by the person who keeps citing it.

`deepseek` additionally caught a real writing defect: §2 said the alternative "makes the
tail memset correct by construction" *and* "fabricates every healthy byte after them".
Both true -- the memset becomes correct *relative to what was read*, and less was read --
but "correct" was doing double duty and it reads as a contradiction.

### The rung-3 witness, cited -- and its scope limit stated

Driver and all three transcripts are preserved beside the row logs:
`round_20260827/shortread_witness.py`, `witness_{committed,fixA,fixB}.txt`. It carries
`live`, `devsig`, `ovl` and `accept` controls; `ovl` proves the truncated overlay really is
serving block 0, and `accept` (a 3-sector read crossing no overlay block) is green on all
builds, so the failing row is a statement about the short read and not about reads in
general.

**SCOPE LIMIT, stated because the witness itself states it and the round block did not:**
it measures the **tail-destruction half only**. The caller buffer there is the device's own
`d->inbuf`, which is zeroed at devinit, so the stale hole at `[200,512)` is invisible from
the guest on a *fresh* device. **That is a property of the fresh-device configuration, not
of the defect** -- a ring with history replays prior data on the same arm, and the wrap
arm's uninitialised stack buffer is a different path the witness never drove. The offline
differential keeps that half because it owns the buffer.

The `kimi-k3:cloud` substitute returned the best packet-fed answer of the pass and found

*Three packet-fed seats declined to ratify and named the same missing facts rather than
agreeing.  That is the honest form, and it is the reason their agreement elsewhere in this

Under this fix `fread_helper` returns **`len` or 0** on the overlaid path, so the caller's
