## Round 485 (#485) -- 242 of 256 opcodes ended a command and never raised its interrupt

> ### *** THIS ROUND SHIPPED WITHOUT A PASS 2, AND A GATE CAUGHT IT RATHER THAN I DID. ***
>
> It went from pass-1 design straight to implementation and commit. `precommit_check.sh`
> refused the **next** commit until a pass-2 receipt for `d819188` existed.
>
> **The pass then paid for the rule in one use.** It found three things, from three different
> seats, one of them a substitute transport that cannot read a file:
>
> * **`M10_seclock`** -- the SEC arm's assert behind a latch of its own -- **escaped all four
>   legs**, 128 rows, 0 failures. Fixed in-round with a fifth leg.
> * an **L4 in the shipped comment**: a boot census resting on an artifact that was not
>   preserved.
> * a **second L4 in that same sentence**, which my correction quoted verbatim and so carried
>   forward: **`0xE0` is `WDCC_STANDBY_IMMED` and has no case**, so it lands in `default:`,
>   not in the SEC arm where the comment said *here*. One arm's comment claimed the other
>   arm's traffic.
>
> *Recorded here and not only in the round's table, because the CHANGELOG is what a reader
> consults, and without this the block reads as a normal lifecycle.*

`wdc_command()` has five arms that terminate a command with `WDCE_ABRT`. Two never raised the
completion interrupt: the six `WDCC_SEC_*` opcodes and `default:`. Two statements, two arms.
Detector **128 rows**, gate **PASS (334 checks)**, kill table **7 of 7**.

### The warrant is an invariant, not an analogy

Derived over all 256 opcodes rather than from a few neighbours:

> **Every command `wdc_command()` finishes raises the completion interrupt.** The only opcodes
> that stay silent are the three that hand control back for a data phase — `WDCC_WRITE`,
> `WDCC_WRITEMULTI`, `ATAPI_PKT_CMD` — and each asserts when its data phase drains.

The 242 were the only violations. And the two defect arms were **the only terminal arms in the
function with no interrupt decision recorded at all** — no assert, no comment. Six arms carry a
`TODO … interrupt` hedge; in five the author asserted, and in the sixth he left the assert
*commented out*, so that decision is visible in the source. A question never reached, not a
decision to stay silent.

No specification is cited and none is available. A sibling model settles the direction:
`dev_mb89352.c` asserts on any non-zero interrupt status regardless of success.

### My first detector was below the floor, and it took a seat to measure it

I shipped a two-observable sweep — ABRT and assert-count, 256 opcodes. **Four of seven mutants
read `ABRT+NO-irq = 0` and pass it entirely:**

| mutant | killed by |
|---|---|
| `M5_inlatch` — assert moved inside the unimplemented-command latch | leg 2, a **second command on one device** |
| `M4_hoist` — one assert after the switch | the **identity pin** on the silent set |
| `M7_noclear` — STATUS read stops clearing the request | leg 3, **retraction** |
| `M8_sfabortonly` — SET_FEATURES asserts only on abort | leg 4, **`precomp = WDSF_SET_MODE`** |

`M4_hoist` is the sharp one: it "fixes" all 242 and starts asserting **at dispatch** for the
three deferred opcodes — a spurious completion interrupt on every disk write a real guest
issues. A count-only oracle passes it, so the silent set is pinned as an **identity**
`{0x30, 0xa0, 0xc5}`, not a count.

`M5` cannot be seen by a sweep at *any* oracle width: one fresh device per opcode means the
latch is 0 on every leg. `M8` is the input-coverage lesson — the sweep varies the command byte
and never `precomp`, so SET_FEATURES' success path never ran. **Input coverage in one dimension
is not input coverage.**

And `M9_notailtick` is the one my *reproduction* could not see: it called `wdc_command()` and
ran the tick by hand, so a fix whose repair depends on `dev_wdc_access()`'s tail tick was
invisible. Leg 1 now drives the real register path — a command store.

### Severity, corrected downward against my own earlier record

`WDCS_BSY` is **never set anywhere in `dev_wdc.c`**, so a polling driver's wait returns at once
with `DRDY|DSC|ERR`. OpenBSD 7.6 reaches both arms routinely — `0xF5` on every attach, `0xE0` on
every halt — and completes boot and shutdown against the old behaviour. **There is no measured
hang.** Nine ledger entries carrying "waits forever" were corrected in place. The licence is
protocol correctness at trivial cost.

### Witness

A seat built and measured a **rung-3** witness on unmodified `-E landisk`: 2/5 pre-fix, 5/5
post-fix, with liveness, attribution and device-signature controls. **Its script was not
preserved** — the seat's scratch directory did not survive — so the artifact this project's own
rule requires does not exist. The round ships `detector:`, the term adopted the same day for
exactly this case, and records that the rung-3 attempt was made and succeeded. `none` would be
false; claiming `probe:` without the script would be laundering.


## Round 486 (#486) -- a scored gate row that was not merely red, but NON-DISCRIMINATING

`regress/wdc_flood_probe.py`'s `overrun x2` drove 1026 undrained IDENTIFY commands and wanted
the latched ring-overrun message once. **`#479` made every command reset the ring**, capping
per-command occupancy at 512, so 1026 commands cannot lap a 262,656-byte ring.

A harness round: no product code. Probe **26/26** (was 25/26), gate `gate_sh_rounding` row list
unchanged at 26, and the clause-(b) mutant dies **145 to 1**.

### It was worse than a red row

Measured on the committed binary: the old stimulus reads `OVERRUN = 0` on the shipped latch
**and 0 on a build with the latch deleted.**

> **Clause (b) was OPEN at the ring producer, with nothing anywhere saying so.** A row that
> reads the same on the fix and on its absence is not a failing detector; it is no detector.

The re-aimed row reads **1 against 145** — it discriminates by a factor of 145.

### 145 was predicted before it was measured, three times independently

My brief derived it, the timing seat measured it, and I measured it again on my own mutant.
`WDC_INBUF_SIZE = 512*513 = 262,656`; nothing drains so `tail` stays 0; the producer refuses at
`head == 262,655`, so push 262,656 is the first refusal — the **second push of store 131,328**.
At two pushes per `mov.w`: `1 + 2*(131,400 - 131,328) = 145`.

### The count is 131,400 and it sits 72 stores above a cliff

| n | 131,328 | 131,329 | 131,400 |
|---|---|---|---|
| shipped | 1 ok | 1 ok | 1 ok |
| latch DELETED | **1 — VACUOUS** | 3 red | 145 red |

**At the exact fill point the unlatched mutant is green.** Shrinking 131,400 to the
arithmetically exact 131,328 reads like tightening a hand-waved number, makes the comment *more*
precise, and silently re-opens the breach. The margin is a load-bearing product of the row and
the comment says so.

### Why free-running, and the obvious reason is the wrong one

Not "394,200 single-steps are too slow". `dev_wdc.c` sets `d->data_debug = 1` at attach, so
every data-port write calls `debug()` — which **prints** under stepping and is silent
free-running at verbose 0. Measured at full size:

```
  step  mov.w x131400   30.684 s   131,400 debug lines   20,369,040 bytes of pty
  fast  mov.w x131400    0.005 s         0 debug lines
```

The stepped form *works*, at 30 s and 20 MB per row. And free-running is a **capability gain**: a
`fatal(` → `debug(` downgrade at this site now reds, which a stepped row could not see — so the
probe's own contract sentence about channel downgrades is narrowed rather than left overclaiming.

### The anti-fake control is the third oracle value

The smallest way to fake this row is to re-anchor `P_OVERRUN` onto the `:704` DATA text: every
build then reads 1, and **`disjoint` cannot catch it**, because its own stimulus fires neither
pattern. So the row counts both sites and asserts that **no single line is matched by both**.
Asserting `1,1` alone does not close it — a `P_OVERRUN` aimed at the DATA line still gives `1,1`.

### The option set I posed was incomplete by three members

The adjudicating seat named them, and one is aimed squarely at this round's own deadline
pressure:

* **re-pin the want to `0` and keep the dead stimulus** — one character, gate goes green.
  Rejected as laundering *and* as a check that cannot fail: with a dead stimulus the shipped
  bytes, the unlatched mutant and the silenced mutant all read 0. *"Named because it is the
  cheapest path to a green battery and someone under Sunday pressure will think of it."*
* **revive the stimulus by product edit** — rejected; a harness round does not edit product code
  to keep a test alive.
* **re-aim AND add a redundant carrier in the offline differential** — filed as its own item; it
  is a second detector with its own oracle.

### Cause of death, by single-variable control

Reverting **only** `#479`'s unconditional `wdc_new_command_reset()`, keeping `#484`'s ring:

`wdc_addtoinbuf()` advanced `head` unconditionally and checked `head == tail` **afterwards**.
That predicate means BOTH empty and full, so a wrapped ring reported occupancy **0** while
holding 262656 staged bytes, and the next push silently overwrote an unread one. The bulk

### The invariant is OCCUPANCY IS SOUND, deliberately not "full is distinguishable from empty"

**Six** sites read the emptiness predicate; only the producer implements it. Naming the weak
property invites a later edit to trade the strong one away, so the fix comment names the one
the other five depend on. (The adjudicating seat's point, adopted.)

### Written as A3, and the difference is a memory-safety class

My own brief proposed `int next = (head + 1) % SIZE; ... head = next;`. That **deletes the
masked advance** and makes the mask inside `next` safety-critical -- and dropping a mask is a
one-token simplification. Built as a mutant it aborts with `free(): invalid next size`: **a
real heap overflow past the allocation.**

> **A brief proposing a fix SHAPE can introduce a memory-safety class the defect never had.**

The shipped form leaves both original statements byte-for-byte untouched and adds only the
guard, which makes that edit inexpressible as a single change.

### The measuring seat overturned three reading seats -- and pass 2 overturned it back, halfway

On pass 1, codex, grok and the adjudicator all read the bulk arm as unreachable, and a
measuring seat **measured** it stepping `head` past `tail`: occupancy `262156 -> 1548`, a
plausible-looking number, with 1548 bytes of unread guest data replaced by disk contents.

> *** ON PASS 2, CODEX REFUTED THE WORD *REACHABLE*, AND IT WAS RIGHT. ***  `wdc__read()` has
> exactly ONE caller and it sits AFTER the unconditional ring reset, so the ring is EMPTY on
> every real invocation. **The fixture built a function state, not a product route.**

So the arm is occupancy-blind *as code* and the state that exposes it is not guest-reachable
today. The hunk ships as **defensive**, licensed by the caller invariant being written down
nowhere else -- not by a live defect. The code comment is corrected in place. *The reading
seats were right about the product and the measuring seat was right about the function; the
round's error was calling the second one the first.*

The disk-image sink, by contrast, was
measured reachable via **width-mixing**: mixed 2- and 4-byte stores hold occupancy at
`2 (mod 4)`, which can never be `0 (mod 512)`, so the drain never fires and the ring wraps
*with the writer armed*; two more stores steer occupancy onto 2048 and the drain commits 512
bytes at the guest's LBA with `first=0x55` where the guest staged `0xA5`.

Disagreements here are settled empirically, never by vote.

### The anchored rows are not interchangeable with the rest

Two mutants that keep occupancy **sound** while destroying **data** -- the `return` moved
inside the warning latch, and drop-oldest -- are green under *every* occupancy-shaped and
DRQ-shaped row. Only the marker byte at the tail cell and the real consumer's FIFO order kill
them. That is clause (f) one level down: **an oracle computed the same way as the code under
test cannot see an edit that preserves the computation.**

The `return`-inside-the-latch mutant deserves its own line: it is exactly the structure
`wdc_get_inbuf()` already forbids in the **consumer** (*"the `return` MUST STAY OUTSIDE it"*),
so a maintainer copying that function's shape into the producer writes it by accident.

### Witness

**Rung 3**, on one ask -- second instance of the standing ruling that a round must *ask* for a
rung-3 probe before recording itself rung-1. A guest program on **unmodified `evbmips -e
malta`**, reached through the machine's own committed `piix4_ide` path with no `device_add` of
ours, free-running, 34 hand-encoded MIPS instructions, shipped-vs-fixed 20/20, 1.53 s. Both
controls: RAM liveness, **and** a device signature -- two reads of the *same address* return
`0x5a` then `0xa5`, which a memory cell cannot do and only a FIFO can.

Honest limit, kept: the route is the orphan ring. The witness proves the ambiguity is
guest-**reachable**; it does not prove any real OS driver travels it.

### Measured cost, named rather than discovered later

`WDC_INBUF_SIZE` is `512*513`, so the saturated occupancy 262655 is never `0 (mod 512)` while
the old 262656 always was. A saturated ring's pending sector write therefore **stalls** instead
of committing its oldest sector. Reachable only through the width-mixing pathology that fills
the ring in the first place, and a stalled write is strictly better than a write of bytes the
guest did not supply.

### Two defects of my own, both caught by the gate rather than by me

* `grep -c 'R2 anchor: inbuf[tail] survives'` -- **`[tail]` is a character class**, so it
  matched `inbuft`/`inbufa`/`inbufi`/`inbufl` and never the literal label. It returned 0 and
  the gate went red, which is the loud direction; had the class matched anything, the row
  would have read as pinned while pinning nothing. All eight labels now use `grep -cF`.
* The blind fix was worse than the bug: replacing `grep -c 'R` across the file matched
  **fourteen** sites, six of them pre-existing checks unrelated to this round. The anchor
  assertion caught it.

### Pass 2 found a one-character escape that all 119 rows missed

**Three seats named the same mutant independently** -- codex, glm and deepseek, none able to
see the others: tightening the bulk bound `>` to `>=`. It refuses a refill that *exactly*
fits, silently shortening the transfer, and it **escaped every one of the 119 rows**, because
R8 pins only the REFUSAL side. deepseek named the settling fact precisely -- *"whether the
119-row battery includes a case with `free == 512*to_read`"*. It did not.

> **A guard is half-tested by showing it refuses what it should. The other half is showing it
> ACCEPTS WHAT IT MUST -- and that is the half a bound-tightening edit escapes.**

That is the de-escalation clause's accept-row reasoning reached from the opposite direction:
there the lost tripwire is a crash, here a refusal. Row `R9` was built from deepseek's
sentence and codex's arithmetic, and it is the **sole carrier**: 122 rows, exactly 1 failure.

### And pass 2 then found an L2 floor breach -- three escapes with ONE cause

The measuring seat built three edits that scored **zero reds across all 122 rows**:

| mutant | edit | measured harm |
|---|---|---|
| `M3_onesector` | `512 * to_read >` -> `512 >` (two tokens) | **275 integrity violations in 960 trials** -- at `head=0, tail=513, free=512, to_read=2` it admits 1024 bytes and destroys 511 unread ones |
| `M2_breakinside` | move the bulk `break` inside the latch | the **second** `wdc__read()` falls through and head lands **on** tail -- the ambiguity this round removed, restored |
| `M1_return` | `break` -> `return` | the completion interrupt is dropped |

> **All three escape for one reason, and the seat said it in a sentence: no row had
> `free >= 512` with `to_read >= 2`, so the multiplier `* to_read` was entirely unpinned;
> and no row called `wdc__read()` twice, so the bulk arm's latch interaction and its common
> tail were unpinned.**

`M3` is clause (d) by the book -- a bound **relaxed** on the predicate this diff added -- so
it was fixed in-round, not filed. Rows **R10** (the multiplier) and **R11** (the second call)
close all three, each dying to exactly one row and to a *different* one.

**R11's first cut did not work, and that is a result rather than an embarrassment.** It filled
the ring to `free == 0`, where `head + 512*to_read` exceeds the buffer, so the fall-through
takes the **byte-wise** arm whose per-byte producer guard saves the mutant -- which survived at
126/126. The row was re-cut onto the memcpy arm (`head = 0, tail = 512, free = 511`) and the
mutant died. *A mutant that will not die is a result: here the row was mis-cut, not the target
dead.*

### The dead check is now deleted, and the warrant is a measurement

The old post-hoc `head == tail` test was kept at first on the warrant that dead code with a

## Round 483 (#483) -- the sweep pinned the decode across 256 values and the purge at none

A **harness round**: zero product code changed.

`#482`'s panel ratified its rows and then both flagship seats built the same escape
independently. `#483` adds three rows for it — an **orphan ring** (bytes staged with neither
tenant armed), a **packet/empty-ring parity** row, and a **bit-2 sweep** over all 256 control
values. Kill table **11 of 11, five sole carriers**, baseline 103 rows / 0 failures, gate
**PASS (321 checks)**.

### And the panel found the same shape one observable over

The sweep varied the *input* across 256 values and read only `cur_command`. So a guard
qualifying the **abort** alone escaped all 103 rows — and both flagship seats built it
independently:

```c
if (idata & WDCTL_RST) {
        d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET;
        if (idata & WDCTL_4BIT)          /* the whole mutant */
                wdc_new_command_reset(d);
}
```

**Root cause: all six purge rows used the reset value `0x0c`**, so any guard keyed on a bit
`0x0c` carries escaped every one of them. **And it is reachable by real driver behaviour** —
`0x04` is the canonical soft-reset bit and `0x06` is what this tree's own row documents as
OpenBSD's; neither carries bit 3. Under the mutant, `0x06` latches the signature and leaves a
stale writer and a stale ring, which is `#479`'s corruption defect returning.

The remedy is the opus seat's, measured before it was proposed: stage state before each of the
256 writes and assert **both** effects IFF bit 2. A *half reset* is wrong whichever way bit 2
went. Pristine stays 103/0, the whole abort-nulling family dies, and **every existing kill is
preserved at its exact count.**

### L4 — and the fix made the claim true rather than softening the prose

The record said the sweep **subsumes** the `0x88` point pin. Measured false: a mutant aborting
on a high bit *without* latching died to the point pin and **escaped the sweep**, so the pin
was a sole carrier for something the sweep could not see.

> **The claim conflated INPUT COVERAGE (the sweep wins, 256 values against 1) with ORACLE
> BREADTH (the point pin won, three observables against one).**

That is the round's most transferable finding: *a sweep is not automatically stronger than a
pin — it is stronger along one axis and can be strictly weaker along the other.* After the
strengthening that mutant dies to seven rows including the sweep, whose diagnostic names the
exact failure (`h 4`: at `0x04` it latches without purging).

### Three more L1s in this round's own rows

* **The sweep printed a literal `"256 of 256"`** after an unconditional `rows++`, with the
  NULL path doing `continue` rather than `return` — a sweep that tested nothing would have
  reported a full pass, and the row-count tripwire could not have caught it. **The row's own
  comment warns about that shape and the row reproduced it.** Now counted and asserted.
* **The orphan row's liveness control guarded the wrong threat** — it excluded "never staged"
  but not "purges on *any* control write", since the live leg performs no altstatus access.
* **It pinned one occupancy value**, so `occ > 8` passed it while leaving smaller orphan rings
  stale. The row now reports `16/0/16/2/0` — five failable observations.

### Filed

`wdcaltfixture` — **eleven** single-field qualifications escape every row, because
`altctl_fresh()` memsets the struct and any predicate true at zero escapes the file. Filed as
**one** item with a measured one-row remedy, not eleven; `&& !d->lba` is its exemplar, not a
row. With an honest bound: a guard can be added on any of ~40 fields, so the principled scope
is *the fields a real driver sets in ordinary operation* — **today every altctl row runs in a
state no real driver is ever in.**

`wdcaltwidth` — the control register's access width is unpinned; every row uses `len == 1`
while the region is registered two bytes wide.

`#481`'s sole-carrier abort row armed `write_in_progress`, `atapi_cmd_in_progress`, the phase

independently measured the consequence: **any single-conjunct qualification of the helper
call still passed it.** The worst leaves SRST no longer aborting a plain ATA write -- the

The repair is not a better assertion. It is **four rows that arm one tenant each.**

| mutant | reds | carried by |
|---|---|---|
| `Mo_abt_atapi` | 2 | ATA-write-alone; empty-ring |
| `Mo_abt_wip` | 1 | packet-alone — **SOLE** |
| `Mo_abt_ring` | 1 | empty-ring — **SOLE** |
| `Mo_hob` | 1 | `0x88` control write — **SOLE** |

### The reason `#481`'s row was weak is the opposite of the intuition

> **A row that arms more state is WEAKER against guard over-restriction, not stronger.**
> More state satisfies more guards, so a composite row is maximally satisfying and minimally
> discriminating.

Measured twice, and **both went against my own reasoning**: `Md_nohelper` now reds four rows,
so the composite row is no longer sole; and `Mo_conj` (abort only when both tenants are live)
reds the three isolated rows and **not** the composite one -- because it arms both, satisfies
the conjunction, and the abort runs.

The row is **kept**: two shapes is not proof of general redundancy, the addition licence has
a mirror, and it remains the only row asserting all four clears happen together. Both
measurements are preserved so a future round starts from evidence.

A sibling audit found this class has **exactly one member** in the file, and it is the one
repaired here. The discriminator, cheap enough to apply at construction: *does this row
assert something HAPPENED, and did I arm more than the minimum needed to make it happen?*

### The panel ratified, then built the same escape twice

Opus's `M1_disj` and Fable's `disj2` are the same edit, reached independently:
`if (d->write_in_progress || d->atapi_cmd_in_progress)`.

**It is precisely the repair a maintainer writes after reading these four rows**, and it

> **A row set can be individually correct and collectively misleading.** Each of the four is
> right; together they teach the wrong property. Nothing in the vacuity floor catches that,

Filed as `wdcaltctrlcov` with the escape list. **The two seats rank the remainder

## Round 481 (#481) -- the reset bit was the head-count bit

`dev_wdc.c`'s Device Control write arm was four lines:

```c
if (idata & WDCTL_4BIT)
        d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET;
```

`WDCTL_4BIT` is `0x08` -- *"use four head bits (wd1003)"*, a head-addressing mode selector
that Linux libata holds as its **steady-state `ap->ctl`**. The reset bit is `WDCTL_RST`,
`0x04`. Three measured defects fell out of that one constant, and a fourth thing turned out
not to be a defect at all.

**And that latch value is not a reset action.** Its only readers are the two
cylinder-register read arms, and both make them return the ATAPI signature `0xEB14` for a
CD-ROM. **It is the signature latch** -- which is why the wrong bit survived: triggering on
libata's steady state kept the signature on almost always.

*(Stated structurally rather than as a count: a line that spells the identifier while
counting it invalidates its own number, which is what section D refuses.)*

### Test-first, with an oracle correction inside it

`artifacts/wdcaltctrl/killtable_20260827/PREFIX_committed_device.out`, the committed device
against this detector:

```
FAIL a real SRST (0x06) is a reset          cur_command 0x0
FAIL a routine 0x08 preserves the command   0xec -> 0x100
FAIL an nIEN write is not a reset           0x0a->0x100 0x02->0xec
FAIL an SRST aborts what was in flight      wip 0x30 flag 1 occ 40
FAIL a real SRST still signs the CD-ROM     0x0000 want 0xeb14
94 rows, 5 failures
```

Post-fix: **94 rows, 0 failures**. Same scripts, opposite colour.

**One row was re-pinned before any code changed.** It read `cur_command != COMMAND_RESET`,
which conflates *"this write did not latch"* with *"the device is not latched"* -- and a
seat **measured the old form going red on correct code** once a power-on signature is
modelled. The delta form asks whether the write *changed* `cur_command`.

> **The harm is sharper than this round's own brief claimed.** The brief called the wrong
> bit *"a wrongly-timed signature rather than a wrongly-performed reset"*. Measured
> `0xec -> 0x100`: **a routine Device Control write destroys the record of which command is
> executing.** `cur_command` is also the value assigned into `write_in_progress`, harmless
> today *only* because `wdc__write()` has exactly one caller immediately after the
> assignment. An accident, not an invariant.

### The one contested decision, settled against a flagship seat by measurement

The two flagship seats split on the edge. One argued **B1** -- add `prev_ctl`, act on the
0→1 assertion, borrowing `dev_sgi_mec.c`'s `prev_asserted` idiom. The other **built the
edge-dropped mutant** and measured it escaping every row with a **byte-identical scenario
differential**.

A measured delta of zero is not a licence to add state, and the borrowed warrant does not
transfer on inspection: `mec`'s `prev_asserted` suppresses spurious *interrupt*
re-assertion, which has no analogue here.

> **B4 removes a failure mode rather than adding one.** The same seat built `m7` -- a
> `prev_ctl` update mis-scoped inside the `if` -- which escapes every row and makes **every
> subsequent SRST be ignored**. Under B4 that mutant cannot be written.

### The blind spot was in how the rows were CUT, not in what they asserted

Every `#479` reproduction row called `wdc_command()` **directly**, with
`stub_disk_exists = 1`, using two **different** opcodes. Thirteen mutants of the body all
die; the call itself was watched only by `Mb_revert`, which deletes it outright.

The generalisation went through **three forms**, and the first two excluded this round's
own headline mutant:

* **v1** *"...reds if that call becomes conditional."* `M4` is a **relocation**, not a
  condition -- so the headline mutant was not an instance of the rule. Named by the
  kimi-k3:cloud seat.
* **v2** *"...conditioned, or moved below a decision point."* Covers `M4`. Still
  existential: *"at least one row"* is discharged by **any** single condition, and the
  shipped detector satisfied it while fourteen other conditionalisations escaped.
* **v3, the opus seat's, and the one to carry forward** -- a detector for a fix that adds
  an unconditional call owes a row for each way the call can **stop running on a path the
  fix claims**: *(i)* a condition in front of it, enumerated over **the classes the
  enclosing function dispatches on** -- for a command dispatcher that is the switch's
  arms, not the opcodes some row happens to use; and *(ii)* a **move below any early
  return** in the same function, one row per return.

For `wdc_command()` that enumerates 20 case labels plus default and 2 early returns, both
readable straight off the source -- closed over the diff's own hunks, so it cannot become
`#392`. **It is discharged by two rows.**

### Why each of the two rows was necessary rather than tidy

**`row_absent_drive_resets` -- the early return nobody covered.** Measured cause: all
seventeen `wdc_command()` calls across all rows ran with `stub_disk_exists = 1`, so **the
no-disk guard fired in no row anywhere**. Moving the call below that guard *only* --
strictly smaller than `M4` -- escaped everything:

```
HEAD   ok    absent-drive command resets   0 cmd(s) flag 0 abrt 1
PRE    ok    absent-drive command resets   0 cmd(s) flag 0 abrt 1
p1     FAIL  absent-drive command resets   1 cmd(s) flag 1 abrt 1
```

Note the PRE column: a **would-be regression past the pre-`#479` baseline**, on the most
common path there is -- every ATA bus scan probes absent drives.

**`row_every_opcode_resets` -- because a killed mutant's family is not killed.**
`M23_exemptfill` is scored KILLED and **three of its four conjuncts escaped alone**. Two
seats reached this independently and named different smallest members (fable
`!= WDCC_READ`, opus `!= ATAPI_IDENTIFY_DEVICE`). The structural reason, by reading:
across all rows the only opcodes ever issued through `wdc_command()` over a *dirty* device
were WRITE, IDENTIFY, ATAPI_PKT_CMD and ATAPI_SOFT_RESET -- READMULTI and
ATAPI_IDENTIFY_DEVICE never passed through it at all.

> **The table killed the measured mutants and not their families.**

The oracle that collapses twenty rows into one is `occ % 512 == 0`: a command that
legitimately fills the ring leaves exactly 512, one that does not leaves 0, and an
unflushed 100-byte residue makes both impossible whatever the opcode does afterwards.

| `wdcringnoflush` | the input ring | residue from an under-drained transfer was never cleared; the drain then fires early and the guest's sector arrives with the previous transfer's bytes at its head |

### *** THE DETECTOR HAD ONLY EVER TESTED ONE ENDIANNESS ARM ***

Found on `#478`'s pass 2 by the Fable seat, and it is the largest coverage finding of the
session. Deleting `badlen_this = 1;` from the **little-endian** default alone produced a
detector run **byte-identical to the unmutated one -- same md5**. Not one row could tell
them apart.

`fake_cpu()` memsets `stub_cpu` and nothing ever set `byte_order`, while the device
branches on `cpu->byte_order == EMUL_LITTLE_ENDIAN`. **Every row in the file, and every
kill table measured against them this session, exercised only the big-endian switch.**

And the rung-3 witness machine for this defect family, `evbmips -e malta`, is
**little-endian**. The detector was testing the opposite arm from the machine the defect
was witnessed on.

**Both arms of the rejected-width setter** are now covered, with a `stub_byte_order`
control, an LE decline row, and a liveness control that proves the LE arm actually ran (the
two arms push a 16-bit store in opposite byte order). The default is unchanged.

> #### *** TWO L4 CORRECTIONS TO THIS PARAGRAPH, FROM TWO SEATS ON THIS ROUND'S OWN PASS 2.
> #### The second is a MEASUREMENT against a reason I asserted without measuring. ***
>
> **(1) SCOPE, named by codex.** An earlier draft said **"Closed"**, which reads as the
> endianness gap being shut. It is not. The LE opt-in proves the rejected-width setter ran and
> checks **the first byte of one legal two-byte store**. End-to-end CDB dispatch, a complete
> sector write, and second-byte behaviour remain **BE-only**.
>
> **(2) THE STATED REASON WAS FALSE, and opus measured it.** This paragraph justified keeping
> the default by claiming a flip *"would silently re-point 80 rows at the other arm, and any row
> that then failed would be indistinguishable from a real defect."*  **Flipped: 0 failures, 0 of
> 80 result lines changed, output byte-identical.** No row fails, so the precaution guards a
> hazard that does not exist.
>
> And the flip is REAL -- negative-controlled both ways (`Mbe_nobad` 2 red -> **0 red** against
> the flipped detector; `Mle_nobad` 1 red -> 3 red). So both hold at once: **the code path
> genuinely swaps, and no row's output can tell.** *"78 of 80 rows run one arm" understates it --
> those 78 do not DISTINGUISH the arms at all.*
>
> **THE MECHANISM IS A PALINDROME CENSUS, and it is this file's own word-47 lesson recurring at
> the data port.** Nearly every 2-byte payload in the suite is a byte-palindrome -- `0x7c7c`,
> `0x6d6d`, `0x3333`, `0x7777`, `0x6b6b`, `0x5555` -- so a swap is invisible by construction. Two
> further mutants escaped byte-identically on BOTH arms: `Mbe_swap` (swap the BE push order, the
> arm 78 rows run) and `Mle_rdswap`/`Mbe_rdswap` (**the entire READ-side endianness branch, which
> is pinned by nothing at all**). No oracle anywhere inspects the CDB bytes the dispatch
> assembles, because `diskimage_scsicommand` ignores `xferp->cmd`.
>
> **Disposition:** the control and the LE row stay -- they are right. The prose is corrected here
> rather than superseded. The coverage residue is filed as `wdcletwins`, carrying opus's own
> measurement that **looping the suite over both arms costs nothing**, which is a cheaper and
> stronger answer than adding LE twins row by row.
>
> *A precaution and a coverage claim are both claims about things that did NOT happen, which is
> exactly the kind this project keeps asserting and not measuring. One flipped run settled both.*

Verified against the mutant that was invisible: `base` md5 `83322ca4`, `le_nobad` md5
`ce9e0551`, one row red, `first=0xbe` -- 512 bytes of unread payload reaching the guest's
LBA through the arm nothing was watching.

### A live defect `#478` left, found by two seats independently

`#478` guarded the sector drain with `badlen_this` and **not** `#477`'s CDB dispatch, which
runs on every data-port write regardless of what the write did. So a store of an
unimplemented width -- announced as `(ignored)` -- still **issued a SCSI command** whenever
occupancy already stood at 12. codex found it by reading; opus by measuring a 3-byte store
allocate an `atapi_st`.

**A rejected access with a side effect is worse than cleanly accepting or refusing it**,
because the diagnostic then states the opposite of what happened. Closed here by giving the
dispatch the same conjunct; `a rejected width issues no command` is its row.

### And `#478`'s announce could silence itself

Measured end-to-end through registers: a **legal, successful** packet command made the
device print *"no sector buffered; write dropped"*. Nothing was dropped -- and the spurious
emission **burns the N=1 latch**, so a later genuine drop is announced to nobody. `#478`'s
announce could defeat `#478`'s announce, which is the state the decline-and-announce ruling
exists to prevent.

The CONDITION is kept -- it fires where the unfixed code put a spurious sector on the image
-- and the TEXT now says what happened rather than asserting a buffer state it never
checked. `inbuf_len == 0` is reached by two routes and only one is a dropped write.

### `WRITEMULTI` had zero rows

Every drain row used `WDCC_WRITE` with `write_count = 1`, so the multi-sector half of both
the guard and the announce arm had no coverage. That single gap was the root cause of four
sweeping mutants, one of which **reads as pure de-duplication** and writes 131,072 bytes.

*And a shape-only accept row does not close it: a seat's first attempt asserted "one write,
1024 bytes" and a mutant passed by draining at the wrong MOMENT with the right total. The
row pins 511 stores producing zero writes.*

### The kill table caught a gap in the round itself

`regress/artifacts/wdccmdreset/killtable_20260827/`, baseline 73 rows 0 failures. **8 of 8,
three SOLE CARRIERS -- one per site**, so dropping any single clear from the helper is
caught by exactly one row.

*** On the first run `MdNoRing` -- simply DELETING the ring flush -- swept a clean 66
rows. *** The cause was not a subtle mutant: **the rows reproducing the three defects this
round fixes were still in the scratchpad tree and had never been ported.** The round was
about to ship a fix that tested its CONSEQUENCES and not its SUBJECT.

*A detector assembled from consequence rows can be entirely green while the defect it
exists for is untested. No gate could have said so; only a mutant aimed at the fix's own
clause did.*

**`MdLatchReset` is the mutant to keep.** It adds `warned_* = 0` to the helper, which reads
as COMPLETING it -- and undoes `#337`/`#464`. It is strictly worse here than the same
mistake would be in `dev_asc.c`, which states the rule at its own latch declarations:
*"Deliberately NOT cleared by `dev_asc_reset()` or `dev_asc_fifo_flush()`: a guest could
otherwise re-arm the flood."* `wdc_command()` runs far more often than a chip reset. Found
by a seat obeying the brief's instruction to GREP THE FORK -- the constraint was already
written down in the sibling device, by the round that learned it.

### Two oracle situations, both identified before any product code changed

* **`row_stale_phase_write` pinned the DEFECT.** Its liveness control asserted that the
  phase is still `CMDOUT` after a WRITE -- correct when it shipped, since a phase-only
  guard must be shown a stale phase or it proves nothing. This round inverts it. Handled
  under the ORACLE-CORRECTION RULE in the prescribed order: **re-pinned first, the
  committed build MEASURED RED (`phase 9 flag 0 wip 48`, exactly one row), then the code
  changed.** Provenance quoted verbatim rather than summarised.
* **`row_residue_recovery` was NOT an oracle correction**, and I called it one before
  checking. It had never shipped -- scratchpad only -- so it is **L1 pre-ship
  construction**, a lighter rule. Claiming the heavier one would have been a false record
  in the safer-sounding direction.

### Premise 5 was refuted twice, and the second refutation came from a blind seat

The brief asserted the ring residue is **unrecoverable**. A PACKET-FED seat -- which cannot
read the tree at all -- replied that the brief's own inlined facts admit a drain path
nobody had examined. Measured: a guest that arms a WRITE and streams 492 bytes clears the
ring **and the recovery hands the disk `0xaa` where the guest wrote `0x55`**.

Then the sharper replacement -- *"no clean exit at all"* -- was measured false too, before
it shipped: `wdc_get_inbuf()` pops unconditionally at the top of the read arm, so **a guest
that reads the data port drains the residue** and receives 20 bytes of the previous
transfer.

> The defensible form: **`wdcringnoflush` is a DATA-INTEGRITY defect, not a denial of
> service.** No sequence the ATAPI protocol prescribes recovers the ring; a guest that
> drains the data port does. What is unrecoverable is the DRIVER'S situation, because
> nothing reports occupancy.

*Their blindness is a feature, and this is the clearest instance on record: two file-reading
flagship seats had the tree and did not produce it.*

### An L4 in code shipped an hour earlier, and a live operational hazard

* **`row_devctl_preserves_write`'s warrant was wrong in the reassuring direction.** It said

* **`build/gxemul` was a STALE BINARY** -- binary `05:52`, source `10:43`, predating `#477`
  and `#478`. It carried no sentinel and `cmp`'d clean against SEC, so the ONE-part

### Filed, not fixed

`wdcaltctrlbit` is re-scoped: **low as a standalone defect, LOAD-BEARING as a precondition**
for F-wide. Those are different numbers for different questions and the row now carries

## Round 477 pass 2 (post-commit) -- a seat REASONED a sweep it could not build, and the build confirmed it

`0922465` shipped, then its own pass-2 panel took it apart. Nine seats answered (the kimi
CLI is 403-walled and its `kimi-k3:cloud` substitute carried the seat -- **its first panel
since the `PACKET_PREAMBLE` fix, answering 6.3 KB where it had stalled at 127 bytes one
panel earlier**). Verdicts were GO / REASONED / sound-on-the-packet, with **codex
dissenting DO NOT CLOSE**. The dissent was right.

### *** THE FLAG CONJUNCT IS LOAD-BEARING, AND `#477`'s COMMENT SAID IT WAS NOT ***

codex reasoned that deleting `atapi_cmd_in_progress` from the dispatch guard -- leaving
the phase test alone -- would sweep the detector while reopening spurious CDB dispatch.
**It could not build the mutant**, saying so plainly: read-only workspace. Built here:

```
M_phaseonly against the shipped detector:   52 rows, 0 failures   CLEAN SWEEP
```

**The mechanism is a STALE PHASE, and it is a defect in its own right.**
`wdc_command(ATAPI_PKT_CMD)` sets `PHASE_CMDOUT`. A following `wdc_command(WDCC_WRITE)`
clears the flag at the top of that function and arms the write -- and **nothing resets the
phase**. The device then sits with `phase == PHASE_CMDOUT`, `atapi_cmd_in_progress == 0`
and a disk write armed: exactly the state a phase-only guard cannot tell from a real CDB
collection. Six 16-bit payload stores reach occupancy 12, and the guest's own sector data
is issued as a SCSI command.

**`row_stale_phase_write` pins it, and the measurement is WORSE than the seat predicted:**

```
FAIL disk payload is not issued as a CDB    1 SCSI dispatch(es)
FAIL the sector survives a stale phase      0 w, 0 b
```

The sector does not merely lose twelve bytes. **It never reaches the disk at all.** The
row carries both halves deliberately -- a dispatch count alone would miss a mutant that
eats the bytes without issuing them.

**L4, corrected in place:** `#477`'s comment headline read *"THE DISPATCH MUST KEY ON THE
PHASE, NOT ON THE FLAG"*. That is unsafe wording in product code. It now reads *"keys on
the phase IN ADDITION TO the flag"*, with the measurement and the stale-phase mechanism
recorded beside it.

*Per the late-dissent rule: closure changes the licence, never the truth-value. A wrong
record is corrected in place; the detector row is a follow-up commit, which this is. The
shipped code is unchanged -- both conjuncts were already there and both were always
correct. What was wrong was the file's explanation of why.*

### What the panel confirmed rather than overturned

* **The `atapi_st` NULL class IS closed.** codex went looking for a seventh dereference and
  found none -- nine total, three dominated by the NULL-checking chain and six after an
  allocation that cannot return NULL. That is now two seats reaching the same enumeration
  independently.
* **No legal sequence is rejected.** The dispatch difference concerns writes outside
  `CMDOUT`; the read-arm difference concerns a DATA read while an outbound CDB is being
  collected. Neither is part of the normal packet sequence.*** THE ROUND CLAIMED THIS PREDICTION WAS INVERTED IN THE DRIVER BEFORE THE RUN.  IT WAS
NOT, AND A SEAT CAUGHT IT BY READING THE COMMITTED ARTIFACT AGAINST THIS PROSE. ***  The
patch script meant to write the inversion PRINTED SUCCESS AND SILENTLY FAILED on a
whitespace mismatch, so the committed driver still carries table 3's block with /35
denominators and the pre-refutation wording.  The inversion existed only in the round's
narration, never in an artifact.  The RESULT is unaffected and reproducible from the
preserved logs -- M_NARROW_25 reds on `n25 rect' alone -- but **the order proof is not
there**, and the artifact has been ANNOTATED rather than backdated, because a file edited
after its run cannot prove the order it is cited for. Measured on pass 2, through real register accesses, adding the conjunct is a
**LIVE REGRESSION**:

```
L3   PKT + ALTCTL + CDB   shipped: dispatches=1   M2: dispatches=0, occ=12
L3b  a second CDB         shipped: dispatches=2   M2: dispatches=0, occ=24
L3c  a third CDB          shipped: dispatches=3   M2: dispatches=0, occ=36
```

**Zero of three LEGAL packet commands dispatch, and the wedge is permanent** -- the 12-byte
residue blocks dispatch even after `cur_command` returns to `0xA0`. So the reachability of
that state is what makes the conjunct **dangerous**, not what makes it valuable.

**A "coverage debt" filing invites a future round to discharge the debt by ADDING the
conjunct** -- shipping the exact wedge this device's rounds exist to prevent. That is why
this is an L4 and not a wording preference: *the measurement was right both times, and the
sentence drawn from it pointed the next round at a regression.*

The two seats differed on the label -- one held the debt filing correct and sharpened it to
*reset-oracle* debt, the other called for an ACCEPT ROW -- and **agreed on the
measurement**. They are the same row. `row_altctl_cdb_accept` kills `M2_curcmd` BECAUSE it
asserts that a legal CDB still dispatches; baseline 57 rows 0 failures, and M2 reds that
row alone.

One seat added what stops this being an artifact of another filed bug: **the divergence
survives fixing `wdcaltctrlbit`**, because a real `WDCTL_RST` reaches the same state and
`wdcsrstnoabort` shows the flag survives it.

### And the dissent fed the next round

The stale phase is the same sentence as two already-filed defects -- **a new command does
not reset what the old one left** -- in the same function, under one fix design. That makes
three sites for `#479`, and this is the most severe of them, because it silently destroys a
legitimate sector write rather than merely corrupting or wedging.

## Round 478 (#478) -- an empty ring was read as a full sector, and 512 stale bytes went to the disk image

`inbuf_len == 0` satisfies `0 % 512 == 0`. So with a WRITE command live and NOTHING
queued, the write-back block fired and handed `diskimage_access` 512 bytes of whatever
the ring happened to hold, at the guest's own chosen LBA.

The entrance is `#337`'s own de-fatalised arm. A 3- or 8-byte data-port store pushes
nothing -- and **`break` leaves the WIDTH SWITCH, not the handler**, so execution falls
straight through into occupancy-driven logic with an empty ring. **This is the
de-escalation clause's predicted hazard exactly:** `#337` correctly converted a host kill
into a survivable decline, and nothing examined what lay past the `break`.

### A RUNG-3 WITNESS, and the brief said none existed

The Opus seat built one on **unmodified `evbmips -e malta`** (5Kc, wdc via
`bus_pci`/`piix4_ide`). The guest arms WRITE SECTORS through the ordinary registers and
issues **one** `sd`:

```
shipped 0922465   target sector: 0x5a x0   clobbered 512   SPURIOUS DISK WRITE
fixed             target sector: 0x5a x512 clobbered 0     CLEAN
ACCEPT (256 halfword writes)   shipped True / fixed True -- guest bytes land byte-for-byte
```

Machine description and dispatch unmodified, symptom on pre-fix HEAD going green post-fix
with the same script, liveness and device-signature controls present. **So this round is
not rung-1 evidence**, and the brief's "honest scope" paragraph was out of date by the time
the panel answered it.

*And the product-code diagnostic is a WRONG RECORD: it says `unimplemented write len 8
(ignored)` while the access destroyed a sector. `#478` makes it true ON THE DRAIN PATH ONLY.*

> *** THAT SENTENCE ORIGINALLY READ "`#478` is what finally makes 'ignored' true", AND IT
> WAS FALSE WHEN WRITTEN. Measured independently by two seats on `#478`'s pass 2 -- codex
> by reading, opus by watching a 3-byte store allocate an `atapi_st`. ***

`#478` guarded the sector DRAIN with `badlen_this`. It did not guard `#477`'s CDB
dispatch, which by design runs on **every** data-port write regardless of what the write
did. So a store of an unimplemented width -- announced as `(ignored)` -- still **issued a
SCSI command** whenever occupancy already stood at 12, and still asserted the interrupt.

**A rejected access with a side effect is worse than cleanly accepting or refusing it**,
because the diagnostic then states the opposite of what happened. Closed in `#479` by
giving the dispatch the same `!badlen_this` conjunct, with `a rejected width issues no
command` as its row -- which reds without the fix.

*Closure changes the licence, not the truth-value: the claim is corrected in place and
re-scoped to the round that actually earns it.*

### *** THE FIX NEEDED TWO CONDITIONS, AND A THIRD FORM WAS WORSE THAN THE DEFECT ***

Every cell below is measured, not argued:

| variant | empty | leftover | wr+pkt | **ACCEPT** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inbuf_len > 0` only | CLOSED | **OPEN** | CLOSED | CLOSED |
| bad-len decline only | CLOSED | CLOSED | **OPEN** | **OPEN** |
| both, flag a **struct field** | CLOSED | CLOSED | CLOSED | **OPEN** |
| both, flag a **per-access local** | CLOSED | CLOSED | CLOSED | CLOSED |

Each half closes a door the other leaves open, for a structural reason:

* **`inbuf_len > 0` misses the LEFTOVER door.** An unread payload leaves occupancy at a
  genuine 512, so `512 > 0` passes and the guest's own returned data goes to the image.
  MEASURED `first=0xbe`. Named by the **grok** seat.
* **The bad-len decline misses the WRITE+PKT door**, because no bad-len access occurs
  there: a CDB dispatch consumes the LOCAL `inbuf_len` to a **stale zero** while pushing
  fresh DATA-IN into the ring. MEASURED `first=0x5a`. Named by **fable**, independently by
  **opus**.

**The panel converged on the one-line guard, and the one-line guard was not enough.** Had I
shipped what four seats agreed on, a live disk-corruption door would have stayed open under
a round recorded as complete.

### The accept row caught a regression I was one edit from shipping

My first two-condition build used a **struct field** for the bad-len flag. It latches for
the life of the device: after one 8-byte store, **every later legal write is silently
dropped** -- corruption traded for silent data loss, which is worse.

**The 45-row baseline scored it "all green"**, because no pre-existing row performs a legal
write AFTER a bad-len one. `row_badlen_then_legal` was written for exactly that, and
`M9_persist` dies on it ALONE. *That is the de-escalation clause's accept side: a fix that
removes a write owes a row proving the LEGAL write still lands.*

### Kill table: 8 of 8, four sole carriers

`regress/artifacts/wdcdataoutdrain/killtable_20260827/`, baseline 50 rows 0 failures.

**Two mutants read as IMPROVEMENTS**, which is what made them dangerous, and both are
invisible to every empty-ring row:

* **`M3_ptr`** -- `inbuf_len > 0` becomes `d->inbuf_head != d->inbuf_tail`. Live pointers
  instead of a stale local: it reads as *more* correct. The seat that named it warned it
  would otherwise "ship green while writing the CD's payload to the IDE image".
* **`M6_recompute`** -- recompute occupancy from the live pointers before the guard. The
  intuitively correct fix, and measurably worse: it fires on a 2048-byte DATA-IN because
  `2048 % 512 == 0`.

Both die on `a CDB dispatch does not drain to disk` ALONE -- the row that exists only
because two seats independently said it had to.

### *** PREMISE 4 WAS MEASURED BACKWARDS, by two seats independently ***

The brief argued the `else` (wrap) branch was the worse one -- advancing `inbuf_tail` past
`inbuf_head` and latching DRQ. **It is the safe branch.** `wdc_get_inbuf` returns `-1`
*without advancing the tail* when `head == tail` (`#464` deliberately put that `return`
outside the latch), so the wrap arm writes 512 sentinel bytes and desyncs nothing.

**The `if` branch is the harmful one**: it advances `inbuf_tail` by 512 unconditionally, so
an empty ring makes the tail overtake the head, occupancy reads 262144, and `status_byte`
asserts **DRQ permanently**. The predicted figure was right and belonged to the other arm.

*Both seats called it the same thing: correct symptom, wrong arm -- **the same read-only
arm-picking error as the previous round**, which is now a pattern rather than an incident.*

### What this round does NOT close, stated because it was measured

* **The ring alias survives.** With `#478` applied, a guest that issues WRITE SECTORS, then
  a packet command returning 2048 bytes, then 256 ordinary 16-bit words of its own, still
  has the image receive **512 CD-ROM payload bytes and ZERO of its own**. `wdccdbaccum`
  stays open with that measurement attached.
* **The alias root is identified and not fixed here:** `wdc_command()` clears
  `atapi_cmd_in_progress` and does **not** clear `write_in_progress`. A one-line symmetric
  fix closes that door; different site, different class, so it is FILED.
* **The `write_count == 0` division is still a host SIGFPE** if it were reachable. It is
  not, and `inbuf_len > 0` does not remove it. A `write_count > 0` co-guard would close it
  for free -- which under the ADDITION LICENCE is exactly "it cannot hurt", so FILED.
* **The decline is SILENT.** `#264` set an in-tree precedent for *decline **and announce***
  on the identical question (`dev_asc.c`: a zero-length DATA_OUT must not kill the host --
  `if (len == 0) { fatal(...); return 0; }`). Raised as an open question rather than added,
  because it is product code and the licence wants a warrant.

### DECLINE AND ANNOUNCE -- by owner ruling, and the rows are the interesting part

`#478` first declined the spurious drain SILENTLY. The guest got **zero notice** that its
write had vanished: no error bit, the handler returns 1, and the interrupt is still
asserted. A seat found this fork had already set the opposite precedent in **`#264`** --
`dev_asc.c` refuses a zero-length DATA_OUT and SAYS SO. Put to the owner, who ruled for
the announce; `#264` is the transferred warrant the ADDITION LICENCE asks for.

**The condition is the DIFFERENCE between this fix and the code it replaces, not the
negation of the guard.** The old code drained on the modulus alone, so the announce fires
exactly where a spurious sector used to reach the disk image. Negating the guard instead
would fire on all 255 partial stores of an ordinary sector.

`fatal()` and not `debugmsg()`, per `#245`/`#269`: under `-q` the verbosity settles at
`VERBOSITY_ERROR`, so a WARNING would be invisible to the boot-log hygiene grep and an
ERROR would trip `#261`'s break-on-ERROR. `(once)` per instance -- the plurality marker in
the 2026-08-26 census.

#### *** TWO FAULTS OF MINE, BOTH FOUND BECAUSE A ROW FAILED TO KILL SOMETHING ***

**(a) The shared-latch mutant was mis-built.** It set the per-device field FROM a static,
so the guard still read per-device state -- equivalent to the original, proving nothing. It
applied cleanly and scored a clean escape.

**(b) Then the correctly-built mutant ALSO escaped, and the fault was the ORACLE.**
`stub_fatals` counted any `fatal()`, and the per-device bad-len notice fires for the second
device too -- masking the missing announce. A shared latch showed a non-zero count and
passed.

> **The fix is the witness ladder's DEVICE-SIGNATURE control applied to a log line:** count
> only messages the event under test could have produced. `stub_drain_msgs` matches the
> announce specifically, and that alone turned `Mstatic` from a clean escape into two red
> rows.

*An emission count is also the right oracle rather than the latch field, which is a proxy: a
fix that sets the flag without printing, or prints without setting it, satisfies a latch
check and fails the property. Three rows -- it fires, it does not fire twice on the same
device, and it DOES fire on a second device, which is what `per instance` means and what a
`static` latch gets wrong.*

### Two owner rulings landed with this round

* **`build-asan/` joins the twin-tree propagation set.** It was measured four rounds stale
  on 2 of 4 sampled files, and it is the tree that catches heap overflows -- this session
  had two findings where an ASAN build was the discriminator, including one the ordinary
  detector scored 52/52 GREEN. A stale sanitiser tree is a detector that has silently
  stopped detecting. Now a `precommit_check.sh` section-B row, negative-controlled in both
  directions; absence is SKIPPED, not failed, so nobody switches it off.
* **A rung-3 probe must be ASKED FOR before a round is recorded as rung-1.** Three rounds
  blamed the ladder for having no term that fits; then a seat was asked once and built a
  rung-3 witness in a single invocation. **The gap was habit, not a hole**, so this is a
  lifecycle step and deliberately NOT a new ladder term -- admitting differentials as their
  own rung would legitimise the shortcut the ladder exists to discourage. The ATTEMPT is
  recorded, so `none` means "tried and could not" rather than "did not think to".

### The harness: a seat was lost to a wrapper that never existed

`panel_ollama.py` was 24 lines and **POSTed the brief verbatim**. This carrier has asserted
for weeks that it wraps briefs in a `PACKET_BRIEF` -- **there was no such thing.** So every
cloud seat received instructions written for the file-reading seats (*"check the premises
against the source"*, *"grep the fork"*), and a seat that tried to comply stalled.

MEASURED: `kimi-k3:cloud` returned **127 bytes** -- *"I'll check the premises against the
actual tree ... Starting by locating"* -- and stopped. With the CLI 403-walled, that lost
the kimi seat entirely, and `seat_verdicts.py` filed it as *"answered, NO VERDICT LINE
(format miss)"* rather than as the stall it was.

**This is the carrier's own "it was never the seat, it was the BRIEF" recurring, for the
documented reason: the remedy lived in PROSE instead of in the tool that fires every time.**
A `PACKET_PREAMBLE` is now prepended to every cloud seat, telling it plainly that it cannot
read files and asking it to NAME any premise it cannot settle from the packet -- so an
uncheckable premise returns as an honest "not checkable" rather than as silence.

Controlled in four states including the negative one (the pre-fix source must NOT carry the
preamble -- without that control the other three measure nothing). **Then verified live: the
same seat, same brief, same transport went 127 bytes -> 10,620 with a real verdict line.**

## Round 477 (#477) -- a guest data-port WRITE could free the ATAPI transfer the device was still delivering

`atapi_cmd_in_progress` is set when a packet command arrives and cleared only when the NEXT
command does, so it stays 1 through the whole of DATAIN and past `PHASE_COMPLETED`. The CDB
dispatch keyed on that flag plus ring occupancy alone. A guest write during DATAIN that
brought occupancy to exactly 12 therefore re-entered the dispatch, **freed the live
transfer**, and issued a SCSI command assembled from the guest's own returned DATA-IN
payload. MEASURED on the committed build: `freed 1 live transfer(s)`.

THE FIX is option B, a phase guard: the dispatch additionally requires
`atapi_phase == PHASE_CMDOUT`. The flag conflates two roles -- *a packet command is active*
(read at four register sites through completion, so it must stay set) and *I am collecting a
CDB* (what the test actually wants). The phase distinguishes them; clearing the flag would
have broken the completion handshake.

Option A -- guarding the data-port pushes -- was **MEASURED WORSE THAN NO FIX**: with
occupancy already 12 a suppressed push leaves it at 12, so the guard CREATES a free on an
input the unfixed code survives.

### *** THE PHASE GUARD ALONE WAS A REGRESSION, AND A SEAT MEASURED IT ***

I answered the brief's own question 5 -- *does this make anything worse?* -- by reading the
WRITE path, confirming nothing there moves `atapi_phase` between the packet command and the
twelfth byte, and concluding #477 could not block a legal CDB. **That was wrong, and the
Fable seat measured it wrong.** A data-port READ moves the phase:

| sequence | HEAD | phase guard alone |
|---|---|---|
| completed, PKT, CDB | DISPATCHED | DISPATCHED |
| completed, PKT, **stray read**, CDB | DISPATCHED | **NO DISPATCH**, permanently |

`ATAPI_PKT_CMD` assigns only the flag and the phase, so after a prior completed command a new
packet starts with `atapi_len == 0`, `atapi_received == data_in_len`, and `atapi_st` **stale
non-NULL** -- it is freed at the next dispatch and never NULLed. A read then falls into the
`atapi_len == 0` arm, finds `received < data_in_len` false, and sets `PHASE_COMPLETED`.
Recovery is unavailable: the twelve-byte residue means occupancy can never EQUAL 12 again.

**That is worse than the unfixed code on an input the unfixed code survives -- the exact
standard that rejected option A.** L1 (pre-ship), so it was repaired in-round rather than
filed: the read arm now declines to derive completion state while a CDB is being collected
(`atapi_len == 0 && atapi_phase != PHASE_CMDOUT`). In CMDOUT that pair describes the
PREVIOUS transfer -- the same statement #477's own comment makes about the flag, applied one
arm over.

### The detector: 44 rows, and the accept side did not exist

Two seats found independently that **no row proved a legal CDB actually dispatches.**
`row_cdb_already12` asserts nothing is FREED -- a reject assertion -- so a fix that
suppressed every dispatch would have passed the entire table. Added `pkt_cdb_case` with a
control (no stray read, must dispatch) and the regression row, so a red is attributable to
the read rather than to the fixture.

Kill table `regress/artifacts/wdccdbmidxfer/killtable2_20260827/`, baseline **45 rows**
0 failures (`killtable2_20260827/base.out`): **six killed, one escape.**

*This sentence read "baseline 44 rows ... five killed, two escapes" until the same day.
Both numbers were the state BEFORE the `occupancy above 12` row landed and killed
`M7_ge12`; the verdict table and `killtable2_20260827/TABLE.txt` were corrected and this
line was not.
**The grep-for-siblings rule failing inside the session that applies it** -- and the
bare filename-only citation went ambiguous the moment a second kill-table directory
existed, which is the names-its-log rule needing a PATH and not just a filename.*

`Mr_readarm` (revert only the read-arm repair) is killed by the new row ALONE -- the (a)
clause for it. `M7_zerolen`, the seventh mutant **four seats proposed independently**
(`|| atapi_len == 0`), is killed by the COMPLETED row alone.

### *** TWO FIXTURE DEFECTS OF MINE, AND FIXING THE SECOND TURNED A KILL INTO A FINDING ***

**(a) The COMPLETED fixture set `atapi_len = 10`, which the device cannot produce.** Every
real transition to `PHASE_COMPLETED` leaves the count at zero. So `M7_zerolen` passed that
row for the FIXTURE's reason and swept the table, while a real completed command plus twelve
guest writes still re-entered dispatch. `alen` is now decoupled from the ring prefill: ten
bytes still sit in the ring so the dispatch is genuinely attempted; only the COUNT is zero.
Found by the codex seat.

**(b) No fixture set `cur_command`,** though the device assigns it with the flag and the
phase in one arm. `M2_curcmd` was therefore scored KILLED **by `row_arm_overrun`, because
legal dispatch vanished in an unreachable `cur_command == 0` state** -- a false-path kill. A
table entry that proves nothing while reading as coverage.

With the fixtures corrected it ESCAPES -- and the comfortable reading, *redundant conjunct,
provably equivalent*, is **wrong**. The discriminating state is reachable, and chasing it
produced two live defects, both FILED (neither is a measured false pass nor a wrong record,
so the stopping rule keeps them out of this round):

* **`wdcaltctrlbit`** -- the ALT-CTRL arm tests `WDCTL_4BIT` (`0x08`, *use four head bits
  (wd1003)*) where the reset bit is `WDCTL_RST` (`0x04`). Selecting 4-bit head mode is
  treated as a controller reset; a real soft reset is ignored.
* **`wdcsrstnoabort`** -- the same arm leaves `atapi_cmd_in_progress` set, so an in-flight
  packet command survives what the device itself calls a reset.

**An escape chased is worth more than an escape classified.** Filing this one as an
equivalence would have buried both.

### OVERFLOW, NOT AN IMPROVEMENT. ***

This round closed its research stage at **eight of nine** and recorded the ruling as

An earlier draft of this block, and of the kill table, classified `M7_ge12`

that under the phase guard it differs only in CMDOUT, where dispatching on an overshoot

```c

while (inbuf_len > 0) { scsi_cmd[x++] = wdc_get_inbuf(d); inbuf_len--; }
```

`x` is unbounded. **`inbuf_len == 12` is not only selecting the dispatch -- it is the ONLY
thing bounding that copy into a 12-byte allocation.** MEASURED under ASAN: `>= 12` gives a
`heap-buffer-overflow` WRITE at `dev_wdc.c:1048`, **while the detector stays 44 rows
0 failures on both sides.** The rows could not see it at all.

**This is the carrier's SKETCH RULE recurring verbatim** -- *four readers, nine lines,
nobody looked*. agy, kimi, Fable and I all reasoned about `>= 12` as a dispatch-selection
predicate; a grep for `malloc(12)` and `scsi_cmd[x` across the whole artifact directory and
the detector returns **zero hits**, so the bound was never in anyone's field of view. The
brief showed the guard and never the tail it protects, and *when every reader makes the same
mistake, suspect the brief.*

L4, corrected in place in both records. The row **`occupancy above 12 does not dispatch`**
now kills it ALONE. It reaches occupancy 14 by preloading thirteen bytes and writing one --
a fixture writing two at a time would dispatch at 12 and never reach the overshoot -- and
its oracle is the dispatch count, so it reds on an ordinary build with no sanitiser.

The overshoot objection that motivated the wrong classification is real, and it is answered
at the right layer: **flush the ring**, never widen a bound that guards a `malloc(12)`.

*`inbuf_len == 12` sits on the diff's own edited line, so clause (d)'s "predicates
dominating the edited lines" enumeration had already caught it. The enumeration was run;
the consequence of weakening it was assessed BY READING and got the wrong answer. **A
predicate can be correctly enumerated and still misjudged, and only a measurement separates
the two.***

## Round 476 (#476) -- #475's clamp WOKE a NULL dereference, and two guest accesses killed the host

**A regression I shipped one round earlier.** `#475` clamped `consumed` so the ATAPI byte
counter could no longer step past zero. That was right -- and it made `atapi_len` STAY at 0
where it had previously gone negative, so `if (d->atapi_len == 0)` began firing on a path the
negative counter had kept dead. That path dereferences `atapi_st` without checking it.

MEASURED: SIGSEGV at `0x48`, which is `offsetof(struct scsi_transfer, data_in_len)`. Two
guest data-port accesses with no ATAPI transfer armed. The bisect is symmetric -- the kill
appears exactly at `#475` and is absent before it.

THE FIX: decline and latch, per this tree's own idiom -- a device that cannot service an
access must not take the emulator with it (`#337`, `#184`, `#186`, `#315`, `#316`, `#326`).
The guard reads `atapi_len == 0 && atapi_st == NULL`, and the message carries `(once)`, which
the 2026-08-26 census established as the tree's plurality suppression marker.

**DID IT CLOSE THE CLASS OR ONE INSTANCE?** `#475` taught that repairing a counter can wake
dead code, so fixing one dereference proves nothing about the others. All nine `atapi_st`
dereferences were enumerated: three (`:812`, `:877`, `:884`) are the reachable family and all
three sit inside the arm this guard protects; the remaining six follow `scsi_transfer_alloc()`,
which cannot return NULL -- it `exit(1)`s on OOM. **The class is closed**, verified
independently by the codex seat, which reached the same enumeration.

*What was NOT closed is the STALE-`atapi_st` class, and `#477` above is its measured
consequence: the pointer is freed at the next dispatch and never NULLed, so a completed
command leaves it non-NULL carrying the counts of a transfer that is over.*

A note on the guard's shape, since the brief sold it short: the do-nothing disposition is
load-bearing. At the latch there is no ATAPI command in flight -- the device sits between A0h
and the CDB -- so completing-with-error would fabricate a completion for a command never
issued, and under `#477` would wedge a still-deliverable CDB. The Fable seat measured that the
brief's own "the command simply stalls" framing is false.

## Round 475 (#475) -- the ATAPI byte counter stepped past zero, and the transfer length is a guest-chosen byte

`atapi_len -= consumed` had no bound against what REMAINS. With an odd remainder a four-byte
data-port read drives the counter negative, so `if (atapi_len == 0)` never fires again and the
command never completes -- while `atapi_received` ends up larger than `data_in_len`, so the
device claims it delivered more bytes than the transfer holds.

**MEASURED on the committed tree, before any edit:**

    FAIL odd chunk: the count stops at zero      atapi_len = -1, want 0
    FAIL odd chunk: received never exceeds len   received = 4, want 3

### This is `#341`'s class surviving at `#341`'s own site

`#341` fixed `consumed` to count what the reads actually POP (`len == 4 ? 4 : (len >= 2 ? 2 : 1)`)
rather than what the guest asked for -- and **its own comment describes exactly this symptom** as
the thing being fixed: *"let atapi_len step PAST zero, which its `== 0` test then never catches."*
The mismatch it removed was len-vs-consumed. The mismatch that remained is consumed-vs-REMAINING.

### *** THE LENGTH IS A SINGLE GUEST-CHOSEN BYTE. This is not an edge case. ***

`diskimage_scsicmd.c` takes the transfer length straight from the command block -- INQUIRY's
allocation length is `retlen = xferp->cmd[4]`, clamped to a MINIMUM of 36 and never to an even
value -- and `scsi_transfer_allocbuf()` does `(*lenp) = want_len` with no rounding.

**Worked path, no re-arm and no oversized transfer:** INQUIRY with allocation length 37. Nine
four-byte reads consume 36 and leave 1; the tenth drives `atapi_len` to **-3**.

*Two different numbers live in this round and conflating them is easy: the 3-byte fixture lands
on -1, the worked 37-byte path on -3. A panel seat caught that conflation in the fix comment
before it shipped.*

**PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by `#473`.** A small odd transfer reaches it with no re-arm at
all. `#473` added a SECOND road -- an odd FINAL chunk of a multi-chunk transfer, which before
that round could never be walked to. Strictly fewer transfers break than before.

### The fix, and it is the tree's own idiom rather than an invention

```c
        if (consumed > d->atapi_len)
                consumed = d->atapi_len;
```

*** THE WARRANT I FIRST WROTE FOR THIS WAS WRONG TWICE, and a measuring seat refuted both.
Corrected before commit. ***  I cited `dev_asc.c:610-614` as "`#283`'s clamp half ... exactly
this shape".  **`#283` tags the RESIDUAL REPORTING there** (`programmed`/`moved`), and its own
comment says it snapshots the count *"before the clamps below rewrite len2"* -- so the clamp is
untagged upstream code with a bare `TODO` above it.  **And the shapes are not the same:**
`dev_asc` clamps the TRANSFER before the move; this clamps the ACCOUNTING and lets the pop
happen at full width.  *The in-tree precedent for clamping the transfer is option D* -- the one
this round did not take.

The precedent is now cited narrowly (a nearby clamp of a step to a remainder) and the warrant
that carries the decision is the cursor argument below, which is measured.

**WHY CLAMPING `consumed` AND NOT SATURATING `atapi_len`:** `atapi_received` has two live
MID-TRANSFER consumers -- the re-arm's length and the refill's source offset
`data_in[atapi_received + j]`. A guest can make the remainder odd mid-chunk with a single 1-byte
read, then overshoot while `received < data_in_len` is still true. Saturating repairs completion
and leaves those two reading a skewed offset, **permanently skipping up to 3 real transfer bytes
that the guest was served as ring-empty 0xff**. That is `#283`'s defect shape re-created.

### *** MY OWN STRONGEST ARGUMENT WAS FALSE, AND TWO OF FOUR CLOUD SEATS RATIFIED IT ***

The pass-1 brief argued that options B and C would OPEN the re-arm's unsigned-underflow path
(`int = size_t - size_t`). **It is false.** The subtraction sits INSIDE `if (received <
data_in_len)`, and an over-count is exactly the condition that makes that test false:

```c
    if (d->atapi_len == 0) {                        /* B/C make THIS fire  */
            if (d->atapi_received < data_in_len) {  /* ...but THIS still guards */
                    atapi_len = data_in_len - atapi_received;   /* never reached */
```

| seat | on the claim |
|---|---|
| glm, kimi, grok, Fable | **REFUTED it**, each from the branch structure |
| deepseek, minimax | ratified it |

**Settled by reading, not by tally** -- and the brief carried the anti-ratification instruction
and still drew two ratifications. Both ratifying seats verified the ARITHMETIC (the sign-and-width
walk to `0xFFFFFFFF` is genuinely correct) and neither checked the CONTROL FLOW that makes it
unreachable.

> **A hazard found in TYPES is a hypothesis about control flow, and the control flow has to be
> checked separately.** The guard that makes it unreachable was the line immediately above it,
> and I had read that line -- for a different question.

*The carrier already records that a brief presenting a DERIVATION directs seats to check the
arithmetic instead of the premise. This is that, with the instruction present and losing 2-2 on
raw count.*

> Clamping to the transfer remainder is what a helpful future reviewer writes.

**MEASURING BEAT ASSUMING, and it is worth recording which way.**  The seat measured its three

Only `Md5_xferbound` was a live breach.  *Trusting the reported numbers would have added two

**Two further rows came from the same seat and close things no mutant in the table reaches:**

### A fifth option existed, and the reason for rejecting it was itself corrected

**E: count successful pops**, transplanting `#338`'s `transfer_bufpos` idiom. The adjudicator
rejected it partly because `wdc_get_inbuf`'s failure signal is in-band and "indistinguishable".
**A later seat corrected that:** the `(uint64_t)-1` IS distinguishable inside the handler, where
data bytes are 0..255 -- the masking objection applies to the guest-visible byte, not to a pop
counter. **E is implementable.**

Still rejected, on the warrants that survive: byte-identical to A on a clean ring, and on a dirty
ring it advances a TRANSFER cursor over FOREIGN bytes -- corrupting the same two consumers that
make B wrong -- at a cost of four pop sites across two endian branches against one line for A.

*Same disposition, one of three warrants withdrawn. Recorded because a wrong reason gets reused,
and this one was inside an adjudication.*

### Honest scope

Rung-1 offline differential = DETECTOR, never a reproduction; the row is `held`, not closed, and
its witness field carries the reason rather than the bare word `none`. **A seat argues a rung-3
cold-debugger probe is BUILDABLE for this defect** -- real guest stores of a CDB, then real
four-byte data-port loads through decode on an in-tree wdc machine. That is filed against
`rung1exempt`, and it sharpens the owner question: is the ladder gap real, or is it a habit of
reaching for the one-second differential instead of the one-boot probe?

Three constraints adopted from the panel and deliberately NOT implemented: no floor for an
already-negative `atapi_len` (A maintains `>= 0` from a clean command, so extra saturates are
unlicensed); no clamping of `received` to `data_in_len` as a companion to B (mid-chunk that
completes EARLY and drops the rest); no even-padding at the SCSI layer.

`est/`, `build/` and `build-asan/` carry `dev_wdc.c` byte-identically with GXEMUL-SEC.
## Round 473 pass 2 (post-commit) -- the panel broke the fix's load-bearing premise, and one mutant swept the detector clean

`1f1a02b` shipped, then its own pass-2 panel found four things wrong with it. None of them
un-ships the fix; two of them are corrections to what the round CLAIMED, one is a floor breach,
and one is an archive that contradicted itself.

Eight of nine seats answered. **The kimi seat was LOST on both transports** -- CLI 403 on its
weekly limit, and `kimi-k3:cloud` returning HTTP 503 -- while glm, deepseek and minimax all
answered in the same minute, so it was that model's outage and not a shared-transport failure.

### *** L4: "the ring is empty at the re-arm" IS AN OVERCLAIM. Two seats broke it independently. ***

The shipped comment justified the refill by asserting the ring is empty when `atapi_len` reaches
zero. **It is not an invariant.** Verified by reading before acting:

* the unexpected-write latch is **suppressed** while `atapi_cmd_in_progress` is set;
* the data-port WRITE arm then pushes guest bytes with **no phase guard and no capacity check**.

So a guest that WRITES to the data port mid-DATAIN grows `head` without touching `atapi_len`,
and those bytes are still queued when the refill runs.

**My own trace missed it, and the reason is the useful part.** I proved the INITIAL arm is
reachable only from an empty ring -- the packet path needs `inbuf_len == 12` EXACTLY, so a dirty
ring cannot issue a packet command. That is true, and **it does not transfer**: the re-arm is not
reached through the packet path at all. *A guard proved for one entry point was carried to a site
that entry point does not dominate.*

adversarial interleaved write DESYNCHRONISES that guest's own transfer.  **The arithmetic
here was stated BACKWARDS in the device comment and the correction did not reach this block --
a panel seat caught the survivor.**  The refill route needs **229889** injected bytes and the
direct write route **262657**: the refill route is cheaper by 32768, FEWER not more.

*Two further qualifications from the same seat, both adopted.*  "Route needs" is too absolute:
262657 is the EMPTY-RING direct threshold, and with 32768 DATAIN bytes already queued the direct
route also overwrites after 229889.  And "corrupts only that guest's transfer" is too
categorical -- the same shared ring feeds the CDB-dispatch and disk-image-drain paths filed as
`wdccdbmidxfer` and `wdcdataoutdrain`.  The defensible claim is narrower: **this adds no
demonstrated host-memory-safety primitive, and the measured case corrupts returned transfer
data.**
was false**, and closure is no shield for false prose.

### *** A FIFTH CLAUSE-(d) MUTANT SWEPT THE DETECTOR CLEAN -- floor breach, closed here ***

The capped ask-again asked for one more null-repair mutant. A grok seat supplied it, and it is

```c
    if (d->inbuf_head == d->inbuf_tail)      /* <-- the mutant */
            for (int j=0; j<d->atapi_len; j++)
                    wdc_addtoinbuf(d, d->atapi_st->data_in[d->atapi_received + j]);
```

**MEASURED: 23 rows, 0 failures. A clean sweep**, because every other row leaves the ring empty
at that point. On a dirty ring it skips the refill while the guest is still told 32768 bytes are
ready.

> **A guard built from a round's own argument is invisible to rows written under that same
> argument.** The rows were not weak; they were all derived from one premise, and the mutant
> attacks the premise rather than the arithmetic.

Closed by one row that establishes a NON-EMPTY ring at the re-arm -- five bytes queued behind the

### The archive contradicted itself, and a seat caught it

codex checked the cited artifact against the shipped detector: every archived run said **22 rows**
while the committed source had 23. The kill table was real, but it **was not produced from the

Worse than reported, on inspection: the per-mutant logs HAD been refreshed and only

CALL SITE while everything else was
written by the script. **An artifact assembled by its caller is an artifact that can be

Also codex: `wdcaddtoinbufbound` and `wdcrearmwalk` were named in `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` and were

*The same seat noted that `witness: none` and `state: open` were wrong as committed. Both were

The round said the two defects were **inseparable**. codex showed a two-stage ordering does exist:
