## Round 474 (#474) -- a guest READ of the footbridge timer-clear register performed the clear

`case TIMER_1_CLEAR:` in `dev_footbridge.c` carried **no `writeflag` test at all**, while
`case TIMER_1_CONTROL:` immediately above it does. So a guest READ ran the whole body: it
reloaded the counter when periodic, decremented the pending-interrupt count, and DEASSERTED the
interrupt. A guest that merely READ the register silently acknowledged a pending timer interrupt.

**The guest-visible consequence is a LOST interrupt, not a bad value** -- which is why it survived:
nothing returns wrong data, a timer just stops firing.

FOUR addresses, not one: the timer fold normalises 0x30C / 0x32C / 0x34C / 0x36C onto this case.

### Confirmed against the datasheet, not inferred from the code

DC21285 section 7.3.42, verbatim:

    Any write to the TimerNClear register (any data) clears the associated interrupt.
    The write has no effect if the associated interrupt was already clear.
    TimerNClear is a write-only register.

    Dword Bit  Name    R/W  Description
    31:0       Clear   W    Clears interrupt. Data is ignored.

*The brief cited Table 7-10. That is the interrupt-controller table; a panel seat corrected it to
the timer section / Table 7-12 and was right.* A read therefore has **no architecturally specified
value**, so the rows pin DETERMINISM (a stable zero), not architecture.

### The fix -- guard the body, keep the `break`

The enclosing function ends with `if (writeflag == MEM_READ) memory_writemax64(...); return 1;`.
An early `return` inside the case would skip that and hand a guest read an **untouched buffer** --
a defect the current code does not have. That is the sketch-rule trap four readers walked into on
an earlier round, so the fix was shaped to avoid it from the start.

### *** THE ROUND SHIPPED NO PASS 1, AND THE PASS-2 PANEL RETURNED DO NOT SHIP ***

The brief disclosed the skipped pass 1 and asked the panel to say if it mattered. It did. The
codex seat returned **DO NOT SHIP** on a detector that was already green, with two live gaps.
Every claim was verified before acting, and both gaps are now closed:

| the seat's finding | verified how | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| the rows never examine `buf`, so `break` -> `return 1` passes both | read the rows: `memset(buf, 0xff, ...)` and no read-back | **CLOSED** -- common-tail row added |
| the rows use `control = 0` only, so a guard widened to admit a PERIODIC read still passes | read the rows; built the mutant | **CLOSED** -- two periodic rows added |
| four new trailing-whitespace lines | `git diff --check` names exactly 434/437 and 688/691 | **FIXED** |
| the brief's datasheet table number is wrong | opened the datasheet | brief defect, corrected above |

**The first is the sharpest, because the fix's own comment argues for the `break` and nothing
tested it.** A stated rationale with no row behind it is a claim, not a property -- and the
mutant that exercises it is exactly the edit the comment warns against.

### The kill table -- 5 of 5

    M_bare        KILLED  3/5   (b) drop the guard entirely -- the pre-fix code
    M_earlyret    KILLED  1/5   (d) `return 1` instead of `break`
    M_periodicor  KILLED  2/5   (d) guard widened to admit a PERIODIC read
    M_null        KILLED        (c) null medium, caught at compile
    M_notread    *ESCAPED 0/5   (d) `writeflag != MEM_READ` -- EQUIVALENT, see below

`regress/artifacts/fbclearread/killtable_20260827/`. Baseline 24 rows, 0 failures,
`DIFF_FOOTBRIDGE_PASS`.

**`M_notread` is an EQUIVALENCE, not coverage debt -- but the seat's REASON for it was
incomplete, and the reason is the part that gets reused.** It said the domain is
`{MEM_READ, MEM_WRITE}`. `memory.h`'s own block headed *"Writeflag:"* documents a THIRD value,
`MEM_DOWNGRADE 128`. What actually makes the mutant equivalent is narrower and checkable:
**`MEM_DOWNGRADE` appears only in `cpu_dyntrans.c`'s TLB-invalidation path and never reaches a
device handler.** Right conclusion, wrong warrant.

### Scorer defects found while measuring, both self-announcing

The first table read `M_bare KILLED (compile failed)` and two `*ESCAPED 0/0 red`. Neither was a
result:

* `M_bare` replaced the body but left `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE) {` **with no closing brace**,
  so the file failed to compile for a reason unrelated to the mutant -- and a build fault scored
  as a detection is the exact confusion the mutant rules warn about.
* the row regex was anchored at the start of the label, but every token appears MID-label, so it
  selected **nothing**. `0/0` is not a measurement, and printing the denominator is the only
  reason that was visible rather than convincing.

*Both were caught by the apparatus-check discipline rather than by reading the numbers.*

### Honest scope

Rung-1 direct-call harness = DETECTOR, never a witness.  The ledger row is `held`, not closed,
and its witness field carries the reason -- `none` alone would assert DOCUMENTED-ONLY, which is
false of a round that shipped a fix. The rows exercise timer 1 only -- the four-address fold is read from the code and
is **not** detector-backed, which is stated rather than implied.

The datasheet also says clearing *"has no effect if the associated interrupt was already clear"*,
while the write arm reloads a periodic timer unconditionally. **That is a separate, pre-existing
question and is filed, not folded into this round.**

`est/`, `build/` and `build-asan/` carry `dev_footbridge.c` byte-identically with GXEMUL-SEC.
## Round 473 (#473) -- the ATAPI DATAIN chunking pushed a whole transfer into a ring that cannot hold it, and then reported zero bytes left

Two defects in one piece of machinery, closed by one diff.  The adjudication took them as ONE
round with TWO row ids: the arm and the re-arm are the two halves of a single chunking protocol,
and bounding the push WITHOUT repairing the re-arm would have injected new corruption into the
(32K, 64K] band that works today.

  `wdcringambig`  the initial arm pushed every byte of the transfer into a 513-block ring
  `wdcrearmzero`  the re-arm reported ZERO bytes remaining and the command never completed

### What was wrong

`WDC_INBUF_SIZE` is `512 * (WDC_MAX_SECTORS + 1)` -- exactly 513 blocks, 262656 bytes.  The
initial arm did `atapi_len = data_in_len`, pushed every byte, and clamped to 32768 **afterwards**.
The clamp was not missing; it was on the wrong side of the loop.

At the re-arm, `if (atapi_len > 32768) atapi_len = 0;` -- where the initial arm clamps to 32768
under the identical condition.  With more than 32768 bytes left the guest is told zero remain
while `received < data_in_len`, and there is no recovery: the next read decrements from 0, steps
PAST zero, and `== 0` never fires again.  That is the `#341` class, reintroduced by the re-arm.

**MEASURED on the committed build, before any edit**, by the same script that later ran green:

    FAIL arm: pushes one chunk, not the whole   occupancy = 512, want 32768
    FAIL arm: block 0 survives the push         first byte = 0xc3, want 0x5a
    FAIL re-arm: >32768 left is not zeroed      atapi_len = 0, want 32768
    ok   re-arm: the branch was actually taken  1
    FAIL re-arm: the chunk is REFILLED          occupancy = 0, want 32768
    FAIL re-arm: refill starts at received      first byte = 0x00, want 0x3c
    22 rows, 5 failures  WDC_IDENTIFY_FAIL

263168 bytes pushed into a 262656-byte ring reports **512** -- the ring cannot even say how much
it lost -- and block 0's marker byte is gone, overwritten by block 514.  That second row is the
corruption oracle: it shows data destroyed, not merely miscounted.

### The fix -- three edits, all in the DATAIN chunking

1. **initial arm:** move the existing 32768 clamp BEFORE the push loop, so one DRQ chunk is
   pushed, which is what the re-arm already assumed.
2. **re-arm:** clamp to 32768 instead of assigning 0.
3. **re-arm:** refill the next chunk from `data_in[atapi_received + j]`.

The refill is what makes the bounded push correct.  It is safe at that point because `atapi_len`
is 0 -- the guest has drained the previous chunk and the ring is empty -- and `data_in` is still
live, the transfer struct being freed only when the next command arrives.

### The reproduction took three attempts, and the first two were red for the WRONG REASON

Attempts 1 and 2 reddened on `atapi_len = 2`, the value the fixture itself had set, and both were
REMOVED rather than shipped.  The cause was found with gdb: a NULL function pointer, because
`dev_wdc_tick()` runs unconditionally after every access and calls `INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->irq)`.
DEVINIT wires that with `INTERRUPT_CONNECT` -- a **macro**, invisible to a scan for field
assignments, which is why reading DEVINIT for field sets missed it twice.

### *** A DETECTOR AIMED ONE LEVEL BELOW THE FIX, and it went red for a reason the fix does not address ***

The first ring row called `wdc_addtoinbuf()` DIRECTLY, 514 blocks' worth.  It was red on the
committed build, which made it look like a reproduction.  It is not: that primitive is unbounded
and **the fix did not bound it** -- the repair is in the CALLER.  So the row pinned a property
still true afterwards and could never go green.

> **A detector aimed at a primitive cannot verify a fix made in its caller.**  Right defect,
> wrong instrument -- the red-for-the-wrong-reason failure moved one level up, where it is harder
> to see because the row is red on the correct build for a real reason.

Replaced by a row that drives the ARM: `atapi_cmd_in_progress` plus ten queued bytes, then a
2-byte `wd_data` write completes the 12-byte packet and calls `diskimage_scsicommand()`.  The
SCSI stub was made **controllable rather than productive** -- a file-static byte count, zero by
default -- because that file's own header correctly warns that a stub returning a fabricated
transfer would overwrite the re-arm row's placed state.

*The packet fires on `inbuf_len == 12` AFTER the access pushes its own bytes.  Queueing twelve
gives 14 and the command silently never fires; the first version of the row measured exactly
that, reporting occupancy 14.*

### The kill table -- 8 of 8, and TWO clause-(d) escapes closed in-round

    Mb_arm       KILLED  2/6   (b) clamp back after the push loop
    Mb_rearm     KILLED  3/6   (b) = 0, no refill
    Mb_both      KILLED  5/6   (b) both sites -- the full pre-fix code
    Mc_null      KILLED        (c) null medium: comment-only source, caught at compile
    Md_widenarm  KILLED  1/6   (d) arm clamp widened to the ring size
    Md_armzero   KILLED  2/6   (d) arm clamp inverted to 0
    Md_norefill  KILLED  2/6   (d) clamp kept, REFILL LOOP DELETED
    Md_wrongoff  KILLED  1/6   (d) refill re-based to data_in[j]

`regress/artifacts/wdcchunking/killtable_20260827/TABLE.txt`, one file per mutant run, the
pre-fix source, and `regress/artifacts/wdcchunking/killtable_20260827/PREFIX_RUN.txt`.  Baseline 22 rows, 0 failures, `WDC_IDENTIFY_PASS`.

*Five of the six rows red pre-fix; the sixth is the liveness control, which is green in BOTH
builds by design -- it proves the fixture reached the re-arm branch rather than that the branch
computed the right value.  The logs live at a durable path because a citation into a reused
scratch buffer becomes CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN EVIDENCE on the next run.*

**The last two ESCAPED the first table**, and they are the dangerous pair: `Md_norefill` tells the
guest 32768 bytes are ready while the ring is EMPTY, and `Md_wrongoff` returns chunk 0's bytes for
every chunk -- silent data corruption.  Both kept the guard and nulled its repair, and the length
check alone passes both.

The arm row already carried a corruption oracle; the re-arm row carried only a length check.
**The sibling-parity check exists precisely to catch that asymmetry and would have found it before
the table ran.**  Closed under L1 -- pre-ship construction, the rows being part of a deliverable
still being built -- though the same finding against shipped material would have been an L2 floor
breach.

### A padded-column near-miss

FOUR of the six new labels were AT or OVER the `%-38s` column width (39, 38, 38, 39), which is
the trap that has previously made a gate check unsatisfiable so a row silently stops being
tested.  All four shortened below the boundary and re-measured.

### Honest scope

`wdc_addtoinbuf()` **remains unbounded** -- the fix bounds its caller, and no row here constrains
the primitive.  Only the FIRST re-arm is pinned; a transfer crossing several re-arms is not walked
end to end.  The fixture drives one packet command; interleaved commands, aborts and resets are
outside the contract.  All three are written into the differential's clause-(e) contract block
rather than left to be discovered.

Rung-1 direct-call harness = DETECTOR, never a witness.  **`wdcrearmzero` still owes a rung-3/4
witness**; that obligation is unchanged by this round and is recorded, not discharged.

*Both ledger rows are `held`, NOT closed, and their witness field carries the reason rather than
the bare word `none`.  A draft of this block said `none` was the honest value; it is not.
`state_semantics` defines `none` as DOCUMENTED-ONLY, and this round shipped a fix -- so the bare
value asserts that no code changed.  `b115` (#472) set the precedent deliberately: no ladder term
fits "fix shipped on rung-1 evidence", and that absence is the signal a round needs an owner
exemption or a rung-3 probe.  THREE rounds now sit here, so it is filed as a standing question.*

`est/`, `build/` and `build-asan/` carry `dev_wdc.c` byte-identically with GXEMUL-SEC.
## Round 472 (#472) -- an unaligned overlay read took its bytes from the wrong layer

`fread_helper()` picks an overlay layer for the block containing `curofs`, then reads up to a
whole block from that layer **without clamping to what remains in the block**.  With an
unaligned offset the read runs past that block's end into blocks that may belong to a different
layer, while `buf` advances on a fixed `OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` stride.

**MEASURED, on the committed build, before any edit:** a 1024-byte read at offset 511 of a disk
whose overlay holds only block 0 returned **512 overlay bytes where exactly one was correct**,
and returned **1 = success**, so nothing surfaced to the caller.  Silent wrong data.

### The asymmetry is what makes it unambiguous

`fwrite_helper()` explicitly REFUSES a non-multiple length and an unaligned offset, both under
`#164`.  `fread_helper()` has no such guard anywhere.  The read path was never given the check
the write path has -- and the loop's own advance expression proves unaligned starts were
anticipated: `curofs = (curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1` rounds UP to the next boundary,
which would simply be `curofs + OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` if offsets were always aligned.

A panel seat supplied the algebra that makes the clamp provably consistent with that advance:
`curofs + remain` **is** `(curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1`, identically.

### The fix

Clamp `lentoread` to the current block's remainder, and advance `buf` by what was consumed.

> *** 'WHAT WAS CONSUMED' IS CORRECTED BY `#488`, WHICH FOUND THE SAME WORDING IN THE
> PRODUCT COMMENT THIS ROUND SHIPPED. ***  `buf` advances by `lentoread`, which is what was
> REQUESTED.  The two are equal on a full read and differ on a SHORT one -- and the short
> case is the defect `#488` fixed.  What tips this from ambiguity to a wrong record is the
> sentence below pairing it with *"indexes the buffer by bytes actually delivered"*, which
> is the file-side reading; the two halves of this block cannot both be right.  Corrected
> here rather than only at the code, because `#488` corrected the code and left these
> siblings standing for several hours -- the grep-for-siblings rule, broken by the round
> that was applying it.
Same shape as `diskimage_access__cue()` in the same file, which already clamps to the remainder
of the current sector and indexes the buffer by bytes actually delivered.

**`buf += OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` appears TWICE.** `fwrite_helper()` has it too, and there the
fixed stride is CORRECT because that path refuses unaligned access outright.  Patching the
first occurrence would have broken the write path; an anchor-count guard caught it.

### The detector, and the mutant that pass 1 found

Six rows in `regress/diff_diskimage_io.c`, which `#include`s the real `diskimage.c` and builds
with one compiler invocation in under a second.  The oracle is a COUNT, not a value: a
value-only oracle can be satisfied by reading the same byte twice.

**Two seats independently named a mutant that ESCAPED the first draft** -- apply the length
clamp and keep the fixed stride.  Under it the wrong-layer row reads 1, which is the CORRECT
answer, because iteration 1 writes one byte and the stride then skips 511 positions.  The
buffer does not receive wrong bytes; it receives HOLES.  So a second row counts bytes the read
never wrote.

**The kill table, measured in a copied tree so no repo file was mutated:**

```
  arm                        wrong-layer row      never-wrote row
  PRISTINE (committed)       FAIL 512, want 1     ok 0
  MUTANT   (clamp only)      ok 1  <- ESCAPES     FAIL 511, want 0
  FIXED    (clamp + stride)  ok 1                 ok 0
```

The two rows are measurably non-redundant: each catches what the other misses.

### The floor breach pass 2 found, and the panel I misread

*** THE FIRST DETECTOR BREACHED VACUITY FLOOR CLAUSE (d), AND I ARGUED THE WRONG CLAUSE WHEN
DECLINING TO FIX IT. ***

The fix INTRODUCES the predicate `len > remain`.  Clause (d) says weaken an introduced
predicate to the least-restrictive form that still READS like the same check.  Two such
mutants passed all six rows:

```
  len > OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE ? remain : len     the bound relaxed
  remain = inblock ? 1 : OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE   the remainder faked
```

Both survived because the section produced only `inblock` in {0,511} and `len > 512`.  **The
uncovered caller is real, and this round's own census had named it**: `bootblock_iso9660.c`
reads 256 bytes at an offset snapped only to 2048 -- arbitrary mod 512.

I declined a fixture change on an L1 argument (*these rows are not vacuous*).  True, and the
WRONG CLAUSE: this is (d)/L2, replaced in-round however late.  ONE row closes both, MEASURED:

```
  arm        short-unaligned row (510+3, want 2)   total
  fixed      ok                                    53 rows, 0 failures
  pristine   FAIL                                  2 failures
  relaxed    FAIL  <- GREEN before this row        1 failure
  faked      FAIL  <- GREEN before this row        1 failure
```

*** AND I REPORTED THE PANEL AS THREE RATIFICATIONS WHEN IT WAS NOT UNANIMOUS. ***  grok said
**DETECTOR IS NOT DONE**; minimax said **NO RATIFICATION**, twice; codex said GO WITH CHANGES.
I carried that misreading INTO A BRIEF, so a later seat was told the panel agreed.

**The dissenting seats were right, and their objection IS the clause-(d) breach above.**  Not
merely failing to read a dissent, but propagating the misreading forward.

### Assessed, not changed

* **The short-read path is UNCHANGED and still has a pre-existing concern**: on a short read in
  a non-final iteration, `len` decrements by the requested amount while `totallenread` grows by
  the actual, so the caller's zero-fill can cover the wrong region.  **The patch WEAKLY HELPS**
  -- the hole shrinks from `BS - lenread` to `lentoread - lenread`.  An earlier draft said it
  "neither helps nor worsens", which is wrong in the safe direction.  Filed as `shortread`.
* **The aligned path is byte-for-byte unchanged**, proven rather than asserted: when `curofs` is
  aligned, `remain` is the block size and both expressions reduce to the originals.
* **RUNG 1 IS A DETECTOR, NEVER A WITNESS.**  This harness calls the function directly, so it
  is graded by the vacuity taxonomy, not the witness clauses.  A rung-3 witness still needs a
  real emulator run, which the machine embargo forbids.

### Collateral, and a build tree I missed

*** THE WSL ARC TREE WAS NEVER PROPAGATED TO, AND I REPORTED THE OPPOSITE. *** I said
"both build trees byte-identical", counting `build/` and `build-asan/` and **forgetting
the WSL arc tree at `/tmp/gxsec-build` entirely**.  It was still at 2386 lines with ZERO
`#472` markers against SEC's 2400 and two.  Found by the adjudicating seat, verified, then
propagated and confirmed by `cmp` against SEC -- never against a backup -- with the stale
`.o` removed.

**This is the no-VPATH rule's exact hazard**: any arc measurement taken meanwhile would
have measured unfixed code and looked clean.  The correct statement is now FOUR trees --
`est/`, `build/`, `build-asan/` and the WSL arc tree -- all byte-identical to SEC.

Eleven offline differentials run in ten seconds total; all green afterwards.  One of them
needs `-Wl,--wrap=fsync -Wl,--wrap=fflush` and reads as failing without them -- it passes
clean with the fix and the right flags.


## Round 467 (#467) -- the pty deadline now means SILENCE, not elapsed time

The owner asked whether Windows could ever be idle enough to trust the battery. The honest
answer was **no** -- and that reframes the problem. Do not chase idleness; remove the
load-sensitivity.

### *** THE FIRST FRAMING WAS WRONG AND WAS CORRECTED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS TOUCHED ***

The proposal was to convert the worst offenders to **work-accounting**, on `#419`'s precedent:
`LUNA_BUDGET` counts guest instructions, so a loaded host executes the same work and the oracle
holds. Classifying all 249 wall-clock references showed that is not the defect here:

| kind | count |
|---|---|
| guest-side budgets, already work-accounted | 3 |
| **pty TRANSPORT timeouts** | **245** |
| true measurement oracles (the `#419` case) | 1 |

**Work-accounting cannot fix a transport timeout.** While you wait for bytes there are no guest
instructions to count -- the whole point is that you do not know whether the guest is running.
Converting literally as proposed would have changed ONE thing.

### The real defect is bigger: ZERO files used an inactivity deadline

Every pty probe read `t = time.time()` once and looped `while time.time() - t < timeout` -- a
**total-time** budget, spent by the clock rather than by the guest. A boot that normally takes
40 s and takes 90 s on a loaded host FAILS, while bytes arrive steadily throughout. **Slow was
indistinguishable from stuck**, which is precisely why the battery needed a quiet machine.

The fix resets the clock whenever the buffer grows, so `timeout` means SILENCE. `rd()` cannot
report progress -- it returns `True` both when data arrives and when its `select()` times out
quietly -- so progress is `len(self.buf)` changing.

**SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION FOR SUCCESSFUL RUNS, and the qualifier is load-bearing:** the new
deadline is strictly more permissive for any run that produces output, and identical for one
that produces none. *It cannot turn a passing run into a failing one.*

*** BUT IT IS NOT FAILURE-SAFE, AND TWO PASS-2 SEATS REFUTED THE LEMMA AS FIRST WRITTEN. ***
A run that FAILS WHILE PRODUCING OUTPUT never trips the deadline at all -- noisy failure
defeats the bound. The original claim was correct and INCOMPLETE, which is worse than wrong
because it reads as a proof. The property is: **monotonic for successful runs, unbounded for
noisy failures.** A run that hangs SILENTLY is still caught, which is the case the deadline
was written for. What it can do is let a genuinely hung
run sit longer -- bounded, because silence still trips the same `timeout`.

### *** `free_run(seconds)` IS DELIBERATELY NOT CONVERTED ***

It is not a timeout at all. It is an **exposure window**: it runs the guest for a set wall-clock
period and then SIGINTs. Converting it would change the experiment rather than protect it --
**and a naive sweep over `time.time()` sites would have eaten it.** That is why this round
converts one NAMED METHOD rather than a pattern.

### The detector, and why one leg is not enough

`selftest_inactivity.py` ships with the fix, wired into gate 2 beside `selftest_budget`. Two
legs, **opposite in sign**:

| leg | old shape | new shape |
|---|---|---|
| slow-but-progressing (60 ticks, short deadline) | **FAILS** -- that IS the defect | PASSES |
| genuinely stuck (no output at all) | fails | **must STILL fail** |

**The second leg is the one that matters.** A conversion that made the timeout UNREACHABLE
would sail through the first and defend nothing -- the check-that-cannot-fail shape this tree
keeps finding in its own work. Both legs are separate gate rows, not just the verdict line, for
the same reason. A third leg pins the reset's presence in each converted probe, catching a
silent revert.

Negative-controlled in both directions before landing: removing the reset from one probe turns
the selftest RED and names the file; restoring it goes GREEN. No rig, no build, no wall-clock
oracle of its own -- **as load-insensitive as the property it defends.**

### Assessed, not changed

* **Scope is two probes** -- the measured worst offenders, 7 tight budgets each. The remaining
  ~245 sites are the same class and are FILED as `loadfragile` rather than swept, because each
  needs the `free_run` distinction checked by hand. A sweep is exactly what would have broken
  the exposure window.
* **`fbpending_drain_probe.py` is one of only two CRLF files in the tree** and was converted
  PRESERVING its line endings (+16/-0). Normalising would have produced the ~500-line churn diff
  this session already had to justify once.
* `check_probe_wiring.py` caught the new detector as unwired and refused the commit until a gate
  ran it. That is the checker whose blind spot was filed the same day as `probewiringscope` --
  it cannot see below `regress/`'s top level, and this detector sits at top level, so it saw it.
  **The check working exactly where it can see, one round after `#465` shipped a detector
  nothing ran.**

## Round 465 (#465) -- dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c: `data` and `data_len` were released apart

`alloc_data()` sets the two together -- `d->data_len = d->cnt;` then the allocation. **Both
release sites cleared only the POINTER**, leaving `data_len` describing a buffer that no longer
exists. Every later reader tests one field and indexes with the other, so a stale length is a
read of freed or absent memory, and a guest PIO sequence reached it: nine accesses on the cheap
route, eighteen on the staged route, both ending in SIGSEGV of the host process.

**THE FIX IS OPTION B, THE `free_data()` HELPER -- and the ADDITION LICENCE governs it, not
minimal-surgical.** A helper is an addition to product code, so it needs a measured delta or a
transferred warrant. It has both. *** THE LICENCE'S MEASURED DELTA IS STRONGER THAN THIS BLOCK FIRST CITED, and the
evidence was already committed. *** The delta is not a 16/16 sweep -- the sibling
mutant reproduces that identically, so it measures nothing about A-vs-B. It is
`E:mism how` in `killtable_20260826/`: the SAME one-word edit gives **sig11 on
`m_ret415`** (the defect measurably returns under the rejected tail form) and **exit0
on `m_helper_ret`** (it does not under the shipped helper). Same edit, both candidate
fixes, opposite outcomes. Found by the pass-2 Fable seat in this round's own logs.

The measured delta: Option A cleared `data_len` at the
function tail, and a mid-switch `return` bypasses that tail -- the opus5 seat built exactly
that mutant (`m_ret415`, one word, `break;` -> `return;`) and it scored **16/16 on the
INTENT-ONLY 16-row table** (`killtable_20260826/gxo465_det_m_ret415.txt`). *This block
first said "swept a clean detector 16/16", naming no table -- see the pass-2 correction
below, which is why a count now names its deriver.* The transferred warrant: `#182`'s rule that a pointer and its length must be updated
together, which is the same defect class one device over.

Releasing both fields in one place makes the disagreeing state **unrepresentable** rather than
merely unreached. That is the whole argument for the helper over a second assignment.

### The oracle correction, in the mandated order -- and it is why this round took four runs

`staged quiet` pinned **`0 of 8`** -- *"NO diagnostic on the silent route"* -- and the round's
own draft prose said the fix *"invents no new behaviour"*. **Both were false.** The repaired
state routes into `#460`'s once-latched `GDROM_W_OVERREAD` decline, so the silent route emits
exactly one line. The fix is louder, by design, and the detector had to say so.

Re-pinning an oracle is observationally identical to fitting the test to the binary. The rule
says the discriminator is ORDER, and this round has the four logs to prove it followed:

| log | build | pin | score | what it establishes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prefix_HEAD_13of13.raw` | committed | old | **13/13** | the defect reproduces, controls live |
| `repin_HEAD_RED.raw` | committed | **new** | **12/13** | the re-pin measured RED *before* any edit |
| `postfix_465.raw` | fixed | new | 11/13 | crash gone; witness rows still pin the defect |
| `postfix_465_final.raw` | fixed | final | **13/13** | detector complete |

Same scripts, opposite colour, and the RED came first. The two trigger rows were **witness**
rows pinned to `sig11`; they are now **detector** rows pinned to `exit0`, and that inversion is
licensed by the preserved pre-fix logs -- same script, same row names -- not by the new binary.

### *** THE DETECTOR WAS WIRED INTO NO GATE, AND THE ROUND WOULD HAVE CLAIMED OTHERWISE ***

Grepping the battery for the probe's own name returned **nothing**. The probe had been
committed under `regress/artifacts/gdrompionull/` and **no gate executed it** -- so "shipped a
detector with the fix" would have been a false record, an L3 undischarged obligation, in a
round whose entire subject is fields that disagree.

Now a section of `gate_sh_rounding.sh`, modelled on `wdc_flood` so the two read alike: PARSE
BEFORE SCORE, the denominator pinned against a literal, per-row presence checks, and -- new
here -- **CONTROLS ASSERTED SEPARATELY**. That last one is from a failure of mine this round: a
run scored **1/13 with all five controls dead** and read as a catastrophic regression, when the
real cause was a nonexistent image path I had invented. A dead-control run must announce itself
as an APPARATUS failure, not as twelve product failures.

*Wiring it also surfaced a collision: `GDLOG` was already taken by the `gate_gdrom_data`
section, and reusing it would have silently overwritten that section's log. Caught by reading
the variable definitions before writing, rather than by a confusing gate run afterwards.*

### Assessed, not changed

* *** THE `m_ret415` FRAMING IN THIS BLOCK WAS WRONG, AND PASS 2 REFUTED IT TWICE,
  INDEPENDENTLY, FROM THIS ROUND'S OWN LOGS. *** The claim that it "sweeps the detector
  clean" is true only of the INTENT-ONLY subset. On the full table it is **23/26 -- three
  rows kill it** -- and, decisively, **it attacks the REJECTED tail-assignment design, not
  the shipped helper.**

      m_ret415      INTENTONLY 16/16   FULL 23/26   the REJECTED tail form
      m_helper_ret  INTENTONLY 16/16   FULL 25/26   the SHIPPED design: KILLED
      m_swapcnt     INTENTONLY 10/16   FULL 14/26   the real clause-(d): STRONGLY KILLED

  **So the shipped fix's own repair IS defended and there is no floor breach.** Filing the
  missing tail rows was the right disposition; calling them **L1** was not, and the two
  together were internally inconsistent -- **L1 means finish in-round.** They are
  ABOVE-FLOOR COVERAGE DEBT, which is what they always were.

  *Both refutations came from seats that re-derived the scores from the committed logs
  rather than from the brief -- the distinction this project draws between a reading and a

### Pass-2 residuals

* **`alloc_data()` does not release before it allocates, and nothing enforces the pairing.**
  Found by the grok seat, verified here: `free_data(d)` runs once at the function entry
  (`:343`) and both `alloc_data(d)` sites (`:359`, `:435`) are downstream, so the buffer is
  always released before replacement *today*. But `alloc_data()` overwrites `d->data`
  unconditionally — **a future third call site not preceded by that entry release leaks the
  previous buffer silently.** #465 added `free_data()` as `alloc_data()`'s counterpart
  without making the pairing structural. Filed as `gdromallocpair`, deliberately not fixed:
  a release inside `alloc_data()` is an ADDITION, and with no third caller there is no
  mutant that can measure the delta the licence requires.
* **`d->cnt` is guest-writable** at `GDROM_CNTLO`/`CNTHI` and reaches `data_len` only via
  `alloc_data()`. Assessed by the grok seat as a related pair, not this defect.
* **Device construction zeroes the whole struct** — a writer the round's "only two writers"
  premise omitted, supplied by the codex seat. Safe, because it sets both fields; but the
  premise as stated was incomplete, and a grep is not a proof.
* **`m_free` and `m_top` escape COMPLEMENTARY halves** -- 13/16 each, and not the same 13. Each
  witnessed route is the sole killer of one relocation mutant, so the two are **not redundant**,
  and a future round tempted to drop one as duplicative is measured wrong.
* The eight mutant binaries are not preserved (6.1 MB each, rebuildable from the recorded
  edits); the 22 logs that are evidence are, under `killtable_20260826/`.

## Round 464 (#464) -- dev_wdc.c: six unlatched `fatal()`, each guest-drivable without bound

`dev_wdc.c` held ten `fatal()` calls. Four were latched by `#337`; **six were not**, and
`fatal()` cannot be silenced -- `core/debugmsg.c:384-390` has no early-out, unlike `debug()`'s
at `:375`. Measured pre-fix: **20 stores produced 20 host lines, with AND without `-q`**
(`regress/artifacts/wdcflood/witness_20260825/fr_no__q.out`, `fr_with__q.out`), and the
**over-read site** at 500 iterations produced **2000 lines / 158,449 bytes** (`n3.out`, same
directory).

*An earlier wording called that second figure "the read path", which points a reader at the
non-8-bit READ guard. It is the ring over-read: `n3.out` is 2000x "reading too much". Same
numbers, wrong site named -- and the wrong name had reached the source comment and the gate
comment before it was caught.*

The fix is six per-instance latch flags wrapping **only** the `fatal()`. Every guest-visible
side effect stays outside the guard: `d->error |= WDCE_ABRT`, `return (uint64_t) -1`,
`idata = data[0]`, and `data[0] = odata` -- the last inside the function's common `ret:` tail.

**`fatal()` is kept rather than downgraded**, on this fork's own recorded warrant at
`dev_asc.c:248-257`: under `-q` verbosity settles at `VERBOSITY_ERROR`, so a WARNING-level
`debugmsg` would be invisible to the boot-log hygiene grep and an ERROR-level one would trip
`#261`'s break-on-ERROR.

### Test-first, and the denominators differ because the detector grew

    pre-fix   8/14    committed HEAD, 14-row script  (table1_14rows/prefix_HEAD.raw)
    post-fix  26/26   26-row script                  (table5_indep/probe_base26.raw)

**Never write "8/26".** The two runs used different scripts. **Twelve** rows were added after
the pre-fix run and have never measured against the unlatched build; five of the six sites take
their clause-(b) evidence from the pre-fix run itself rather than from a mutant.

### SIX flags, not four -- and the argument that settled it dissolved the conflict

The panel split on pairing. Both sides cited precedent: `#337` shares one flag across two sites;
`#460` records a measured warrant for per-site bits. **Neither is wrong** -- `#337`'s two sites
are the two arms of ONE ENDIANNESS BRANCH, mutually exclusive at runtime, so sharing there loses
nothing. These six can all fire in one session.

### What the round had to correct about itself

Nothing here was found by a gate. All of it was found by reading, and most of it by a seat
rather than by me.

* **Two detector rows were measured VACUOUS.** `r16 value`'s oracle passed on any echoed hex
  value -- structurally incapable of failing while the emulator lived, and green under every one
  of table 2's ten mutants. *(It did not exist for table 1, which measured a 14-row detector; an
  earlier draft said "the first two tables", which is false.)* Both width value rows also checked
  the **wrong fire**: the escape they cite corrupts the FIRST access, and they read once, after
  both.
* **An L2 FLOOR BREACH.** `:145` had no row, so the fix had six fixed sites and the detector saw
  five. Until `overrun x2` existed, deleting that guard scored a clean sweep.
* **Three shipped comment warrants were non-sequiturs**, and two more citations were simply
  wrong. The no-disk warrant (`wdc_addtoinbuf` IS reachable from the DATA-write path); the
  accept-section comment invoking the de-escalation clause, which this fix does not trigger; a
  citation to `:709` landing on an `inbuf` line that **reads like a confirmation**;
  `dev_wdc.c:597` for the `addr_mult` division, which was the PRE-FIX line; and an `i:R:`
  warrant citing `diskimage.c:1700-1755`. That last one is instructive: the conclusion is right
  and the mechanism is not. `strchr(fname, ':')` at `:1652` takes the FIRST colon and
  `while (fname <= cp)` consumes only up to it, so `i:R:path` reads `i` as the sole prefix and
  `R:path` becomes the FILENAME. It never reaches the invalid-prefix arm at `:1752` that the
  comment blamed. **A wrong reason gets reused.**
* **A contract bullet warranted a MEASURABLE claim on an UNMEASURABLE one.** Flag pairing was
  disclosed as unmeasurable "because the rig has one controller". That explains the
  process-global case only -- pairing survived because **no row fired two sites in one session**,
  a property of the row set. Now `wr indep`, measured.
* **The ask-again found a real escape against a clean 24-row table.** Keying the `:607` latch on
  the access WIDTH sweeps clean while a guest alternating `mov.w`/`mov.l` floods at one line per
  store. Invisible because 2 and 4 never co-occur in a session. Closed by `w mixed` / `r mixed`,
  both measured killed (`Mwid`, `Mwidr`).

The fix adds ~97 lines, so `:145`, `:160`, `:583`, `:607`, `:704` and `:1025` all resolve to the

### The sibling this round does NOT fix, named because its own filing named it

`wdc_command()`'s no-disk early return emits `[ wdc: command 0x%02x drive %i, but no disk
image ]` through **`debug()`**, once per failed command. It is **outside this round's scope
rather than a missed site**, and the reason is stronger than `-q`: `debug()` computes
`v = verbose - (emul_executing ? 1 : 0) + (stepping ? 1 : 0)` and returns at
`core/debugmsg.c:375` when `v < 0`. **Free-running at the default verbosity that is
`v == -1`, so the arm emits NOTHING AT ALL** -- it becomes one line per command only under
`-v` or under stepping. `fatal()` has no such early-out, which is what made the six sites
this round latched unavoidable. Different channel, different remedy; it rides with
`floodclass`.

*An earlier wording here said the sibling "floods identically", full stop. That is an
OVERSTATEMENT and the qualifier was not missing from the evidence -- it was missing from my
summary. The original filing in `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` already reads "floods identically
(100 lines) through `debug()` -- **invisible free-running at verbosity 0**, visible in every
cold-debugger probe." I kept the headline and dropped the scope. Caught by the pass-2 codex
seat, which re-derived from `debugmsg.c` what this project's own record already said.*

*This is the MIRROR of the dropped-qualifier failure the carrier records: there a seat
silently NARROWED a brief's claim so a defect hid behind a locally-true sentence; here I
silently WIDENED a filing's claim by deleting its scope. Both survive every check except
comparing the summary against its source.*

`wdcringambig`, `wdcperopcode`, `wdcexpecteddata`, `wdcflagindep`, `wdchpcmipsaddr` -- all five
in the ledger AND in OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md. The four new ones were absent from the bug file until

It was in none -- `grep wdc_flood regress/*.sh` was empty, so the battery never ran it. Now in
`gate_sh_rounding.sh`, with a **source-grep** guard: `fatal(` -> `debug(` scores a clean sweep
against every row, because they all single-step and `debug()` always prints under stepping. A

## Round 463 (#463) -- dev_dreamcast_asic.c: one guest load ended the host process

`DEVICE_ACCESS(dreamcast_asic)` computed `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` and then ran
`exit(1)` when `r == 3`, **above the switch and above the writeflag test**. So the kill
needed no store, no staging and no command sequence: a single guest load did it.

### The census in the pass-1 brief was wrong by 4x, and six of nine seats ratified it

The brief said **sixteen** offsets reach the kill. The true number is **sixty-four**.
`relative_addr` need not be word-aligned -- `memory_rw.c` computes
`paddr -= mem->devices[i].baseaddr` with no sub-word mask -- so a BYTE access at `+0x0d`
gives `0x0d / 4 == 3` and dies exactly like `+0x0c`. The sixteen cited were the
word-aligned quarter.

Four seats derived the correction independently. One **silently narrowed** the claim to
"exactly 16 *word-aligned* offsets", inserting a qualifier the brief did not have -- a
locally-true restatement that repairs the sentence and hides the defect, which is harder
to catch than a plain wrong answer because it survives every check except asking what the
qualifier was doing there. Four seats did not engage with alignment at all.

And one of the four correctors put **the wrong number in its verdict line**, ratifying
"the sixteen word-aligned killing offsets" while deriving 64 eight paragraphs down. The
policy here is verdict-line-first so an answer survives truncation; here the surviving
half would have been the wrong half.

*Consequence, and it is why this is recorded rather than tidied away: a detector built
from the wrong census walks sixteen addresses, covers a QUARTER of the defect, and reports
full coverage.* `kill byte` (+0x0d) is the row that pins the correction.

### And SIXTY-FOUR is itself a FLOOR, which the assess stage found LAST

The round stated `fmov.d` at +0x18 as a vivid example of why this was not merely reserved
space. **It is a CLASS and was never counted as one.** A base OUTSIDE the 64 dies when any
LANE of its transaction lands inside: **16 eight-byte bases** (0x08, 0x18, 0x28 ...) whose own
offset is perfectly safe die on their high word, and **all 8 aligned 32-byte store-queue
bases** span exactly two killing words -- base 0 hits 0x0c and 0x1c -- **dying MID-BURST, with
earlier words already committed.** Verified independently before crediting.

*Found by the seat filling the assess stage at 8/9 -- the stage this round nearly closed by
exemption. The reachability was UNDERSTATED, which is the safe direction for a shipped fix, but
the round's own "sixty-four" was a floor rather than a total and a future reader deserves the
distinction.*

### The structural form, which is what a future edit actually needs

`r == 3` is exactly `(relative_addr & 0x0c) == 0x0c` -- **the fourth word of every 16-byte
group** -- while all twelve implemented cases are three CONSECUTIVE words at group bases
`0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30`. An enumeration tells a future edit today's answer; the invariant
tells it what it must not do.

It is also not merely reserved space. An SZ=1 `fmov.d` at `+0x08` is 8-byte aligned and
issues `addr+4` first, so it reached `0x0c` and died **before ever touching the implemented
register it names** -- and likewise at `+0x18`, `+0x28`, `+0x38`, the third register of
every implemented group.

### All three parts of the block were removed, not just the `exit(1)`

* Keeping `fatal()` converts a host kill into a **guest-drivable flood**. `fatal()` has no
  early-out -- unlike `debug()`, which returns when `(quiet_mode && !ss) || v < 0` -- so
  `-q` cannot silence it.
* Keeping `r = 0` leaves a **latent aliasing hazard**: dead today, but a later widening
  would send `0x08/0x18/0x28/0x38` here, clamp them to index 0 and alias them silently.
* Deleting the block costs little diagnostically. `0x0c` is not a case label, so it falls
  to `default:`, which prints the ADDRESS that "Bad address" never did. **This is a trade,
  not parity** -- see the overclaim corrected below.

The invariant is recorded as a **comment, deliberately not a runtime guard** -- a guard
that cannot fire is not insurance. It is scoped to this file only: `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR()`
reaches a fourth word whenever `(e>>5) & 3 == 3`, and that edit adds a `#define` to a header, so no
comment here can govern it. Filed as `asiceventaddr`.

**The event ceiling is what makes that filing LATENT rather than live, so it gets a citation
like every other number here** -- a consistency audit caught it as the one bare figure in the
block. `dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:74` defines
`SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e) = SYSASIC_BASE + 4*((e)>>5)`. **An audit seat refuted the form this
round first wrote** -- "reaches 0x0c for any event >= 96" is FALSE, because `e` in `[128,159]`
gives `+0x10`, which is r = 0. The true predicate is `(e>>5) & 3 == 3`: `[96,127]` -> `+0x0c`,
`[224,255]` -> `+0x1c`, `[352,383]` -> `+0x2c`. **That makes the filing STRONGER, not weaker** --
it is not one range but the SAME fourth-word-of-every-group pattern as the defect itself, one
level up. Over all **21** `SYSASIC_EVENT_*` defines the maximum is **67**
(`SYSASIC_EVENT_MATOUTOFMEM`, `:72`) -- computed over the set, not eyeballed -- and
`67 >> 5 == 2` lands at `+0x08`. Two whole registers of headroom, and no defined event can
reach the fourth word today.

### Measured in both directions, same script, opposite colour

| | |
|---|---|
| committed HEAD `6cae5e4`, pre-fix | **scored 5 of 9 -- FOUR rows red** (`regress/artifacts/asic463/witness_prefix_HEAD.raw`) |
| with this diff | **scored 9 of 9 -- none red** (`regress/artifacts/asic463/witness_postfix.raw`) |

The witness is rung 3: real guest instructions through real address decode and real
`memory_rw`, on an unmodified in-tree machine description. It carries a liveness control
(`live`, a known value through the same decode), a device-signature control (`devsig`) and
an `asic ok` readback that RAM cannot fake.

**The two accept rows were green BEFORE and AFTER.** `safe 8` (+0x08) and `safe 4` (+0x04)
show the deletion removed the kill **without widening anything** -- a fix that had broken
the accept side would show there, and does not.

### The witness's first draft committed the sin its own header names

Its three killing rows were `+0x0c`, `+0x0d` and `+0x0c` -- **all inside the single 16-byte
group [0x0c,0x0f]**, group 0 of 16 -- while the header asserted the fourth word of EVERY
group. A group-narrowing mutant (`if (r == 3 && relative_addr < 0x10)`) re-introduces the
kill for 15 of the 16 groups and every row would have stayed green. `kill far` at `+0xfc`
(group 15, the maximally distant one, and in the `default:` region so no case interaction
can confound it) is the row that closes it. Caught in design review before the first run,
which is the only reason it cost nothing.

### The de-escalation obligation this fix incurred

Removing a host-fatal guard **deletes the accidental tripwire** that made guard growth
self-announcing: before, adding a selector to that guard meant `exit(1)` on the first legal
access, unmissable. After, the same edit is silent. So `safe 8` and `safe 4` are ACCEPT
rows, and an accept row is discharged by a **measured kill**, never by existing.

### A seat read "5/9 RED" as *five rows red*, and it was right to

The prose named FOUR reddening rows beside a headline of `5/9`. The measurement is
sound -- the vector is `1,1,1,1,0,0,0,1,0`, five passed and four red -- but the
notation is ambiguous, and a seat spent part of its answer asking which row was
missing. **A round that criticised its predecessor for a wrong census cannot ship an
ambiguous count.** Both directions are now written as "scored N of M -- K rows red".

### The kill table: floor clauses (a), (b), (c) and (d), all measured

Artifacts: `regress/artifacts/asic463/table1_9rows/`.

| mutant | score | rows reddened | what it discharges |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 9/9 | -- | baseline |
| verbatim reinstatement of the whole block | 5/9 | kill word, kill byte, kill store, kill far | floor **(b)** |
| kill rerouted to `r == 2` | 8/9 | **`safe 8` ALONE** | floor **(d)** + accept failability |
| kill rerouted to `r == 1` | 8/9 | **`safe 4` ALONE** | accept failability |
| device stubbed to answer 0 | 8/9 | **`asic ok` ALONE** | floor **(c)**, null medium |

Clause (a) is the pre-fix run itself. Each accept row reddens **alone**, which is what
makes the de-escalation obligation discharged rather than merely asserted: `r >= 2`
would have reddened the kill rows too and attributed nothing to `safe 8`.

The restore was verified by `cmp` against the repo source -- never against the
script's own backup, because a crashed run once captured a mutant as its "original".

### The pass-2 panel found four things the table could not

Four packet-fed seats answered; none walled. Two named `& 3` -> `& 2` **independently**:
it restricts `r` to {0,2}, so `+0x14` aliases onto `+0x10`, every row still reads
"survived", and the round-trip agrees -- a clean escape. A third named `& 3` -> `& 7`:
`r` reaches 4, and because `:54-57` declares `pending_irq[3]`, `mask_13[3]`,
`mask_11[3]`, `mask_9[3]` **consecutively**, `mask_13[4]` LANDS ON `mask_11[1]` under this
toolchain (the subscript is UB regardless of adjacency -- see the close-out) -- a mask_13
write lands in mask_11 and still reads back.

**And the same seat found the comment was only half a rule.** The invariant as first
written constrained the `case` labels and said nothing about the `& 3` mask. Both
escapes leave every label compliant, so *the comment would not even have been
violated*. It now states both halves, and the two new rows `alias` and `crossarr` pin
the second. They are deliberately complementary: under `& 7` the three mask_13 words
map to three distinct cells that round-trip, so a same-array distinctness row cannot
see it; only a cross-ARRAY read can.

### Two premises were challenged and HELD, and one claim was overclaimed

Seats challenged three of the brief's premises. Opening the files settled all three:

* **`fatal()` does not exit** and has no early-out (`core/debugmsg.c:384-390`, against
  `debug()`'s `if ((quiet_mode && !ss) || v < 0) return;` at `:375`). The
  guest-drivable flood warrant HOLDS.
* **`fmov.d` issues `addr + 4` first** -- the decoder says so in its own comment
  (`cpu_sh_instr.c:790-791`, the read at `:798`, the first word only at `:811`). One
  seat expected low-address-first from the architecture and was wrong for this tree.
* **But "deleting the block removes no diagnostic" was OVERCLAIMED.** `default:` prints
  via `debug()` (`:228`, `:231`), which the early-out silences under `-q` and when
  free-running at verbose 0 -- where the deleted `fatal()` printed unconditionally.
  The comment now states the TRADE rather than claiming parity.

*The two premises that held cost one grep each. The one that did not was the one no
seat could check and I had not either.*

### A file-reading seat noticed the brief had gone stale under it

The pass-2 brief inlined the diff; the two comment corrections above were then made
**while the panel was still running**, so seats that read the tree saw a newer file than
the packet described. One said so plainly -- *"the on-disk file already diverges from the
brief's comment"* -- which is the seat doing its job.

Comments only, so nothing measured changes. But it is worth recording as a process fact
rather than leaving it to look like a discrepancy: **a brief is a snapshot, and correcting
the tree mid-panel silently invalidates the packet for exactly the seats that can check
it.** The cheap fix next time is to freeze the source during a pass, or to re-issue the
hunk when it changes.

### The adjudication re-labelled the work, and THAT is what bounded it

I justified the three new mutants as **L1, pre-ship construction** -- the detector has not
shipped, so improving it is not a reopening. The adjudicating seat rejected the LABEL while
approving the work, and its reason is the useful part:

> **"L1 -- still being built" has NO TERMINUS.** *"The detector hasn't shipped, so I can keep
> improving it"* is exactly the sentence the six-pass runaway round told itself.

The correct labels are **L2 (floor clause (d)) and L3 (undischarged obligation)**, and those
are *bounded and enumerable from the diff today*: `& 2` and `& 7` both weaken
`r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3`, a predicate the fix DEPENDS ON -- it dominates the deleted
lines inside the enclosing function -- and the carrier's own canonical clause-(d) example is
a narrowed mask. `asic ok` is the sole carrier of the r=0 accept side the de-escalation
clause forces, so a vacuous sole carrier is L3.

**The stopping point is therefore a finite list, not a judgement:** (a) pre-fix fail, (b)
verbatim reinstatement, (c) null medium, (d) repair-null on the depended-on mask in its two
distinct failure modes, (e) a contract header, plus the accept side r in {0,1,2} each
discharged by a measured kill. *The line would be crossed the moment a mutant OUTSIDE that
enumeration -- `/4` -> `/2`, `& 6`, `>>1`, a case-label relocation -- got fixed in-round
instead of filed.*

**Pre-committed here, in writing, so the cap is not a judgement call later: pass 2 was HUNT
ONE. The ask-again is HUNT TWO. There is no hunt three.** A floor gap found by hunt two may
be fixed and re-verified, because the floor is always fixable; anything above the floor from
hunt two is FILED. Counting hunts rather than labels is what stops *"that was not really the
ask-again either"* from becoming the door back in.

### The deleted guard was ALSO a bounds check, and that is the thing this round nearly missed

`r == 3` is out of range for `uint32_t[3]`. So the block did two jobs, and the round had
only reasoned about one: **before this commit the switch had never once executed with
r == 3**, because the `exit(1)` fired above it.

*** CORRECTED: THE ROUND CALLED THAT CODE PATH "BRAND NEW" AND IT IS NOT. *** A research seat
measured that `default:` was ALREADY reachable for **180 of the 256 offsets** pre-fix (256 minus
12 case labels minus the 64 killing ones) -- confirmed here independently. What is new is not the
PATH but the `(r, path)` PAIRING, and `default:` ignores `r` entirely. **So the shipped fix is
SAFER than this round's own caution claimed**, and the correction cuts against the dissent the
round had been crediting. The adjudicator applied the same correction to its own framing.

The comment asserted the invariant; it had not shown it was CHECKED. It has been now, by
enumeration rather than by argument:

| all 12 case labels | 0, 4, 8, 0x10, 0x14, 0x18, 0x20, 0x24, 0x28, 0x30, 0x34, 0x38 |
|---|---|
| **max r** | **2** |
| `default:` (`:227`), where r == 3 lands | indexes **nothing** -- two `debug()` calls, no `[r]` |

So deleting the whole block is safe, and the recorded reason is now the right one. It is
**not** "`r = 0` was dead code" -- it is *"the invariant is verified, so r == 3 addresses are
genuine non-registers and the `default:` decline is the single correct handling."* Had the
enumeration found an indexing case at an r == 3 offset, the correct ship would have been
`if (r == 3) return;` instead -- bounds-safe regardless of the invariant.

**And a clamp would have been actively harmful.** `if (r >= 3) r = 0;` neutralises the r == 4
escape in product code and would have DEFEATED the `crossarr` row -- the detector would have
gone green on a build that had silently absorbed the defect it was written to catch.

### The detector went 9 -> 11 -> 12 rows, and every addition came from a seat, not from me

Four escapes were named against a table that was already clean, by four different seats,
and they are not variations on one idea -- they are four distinct ways to break the index:

| escape | what it does | named by | caught by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `& 3` -> `& 2` | aliases +0x14 onto +0x10 | glm, deepseek, agy -- **independently** | `alias` |
| `& 3` -> `& 7` | r reaches 4; `mask_13[4]` LANDS ON `mask_11[1]` (UB, not defined C) | kimi, agy | `crossarr` |
| `& 3` -> `& 1` | aliases **+0x18** onto +0x10 | grok | `alias2` |
| `/ 4` -> `/ 2` | also aliases **+0x18** onto +0x10 | codex | `alias2` |

**All four are MEASURED, not predicted.** The adjudication caught `/ 2` being carried as *"caught
incidentally by `alias2`"* with **no artifact** -- a catch claimed without a log, which the
score-claims rule does not allow. It was built and run: `Mdiv2` scores **11/12, reddening

the mechanism rather than just the colour -- the row read `0xb2` where `0xa1` was written, which
is the +0x18 store landing on `mask_13[0]`. Measuring a named prediction is not a new hunt.

**The unit of coverage is the COLLISION PAIR, not "aliasing" in the abstract.** Three
register words admit distinct pairs, and one distinctness row pins exactly one pair. My
first aliasing row pinned words 0 and 1; `& 1` and `/ 2` both collide words 0 and **2**,
so it was blind to both. `alias2` was added for grok's mutant and closed codex's for free
-- and codex, arriving at it from the opposite direction, prescribed precisely that row:
*"add a distinctness row for +0x10 versus +0x18."*

**Said precisely, because the difference matters for the stopping rule: `alias2` was added
for grok's `& 1`, which weakens the index expression and is INSIDE the depended-on
enumeration. It catches codex's `/ 2` INCIDENTALLY.** No work was undertaken in-round for
`/ 2`, and the round claims no credit for closing it -- a filed mutant that a row happens to
kill is a bonus, not a fix.

*** AND THAT EXPOSES AN INCONSISTENCY IN THE ADJUDICATION ITSELF, surfaced by a packet-fed
seat with no file access. *** The adjudication classified `& 2` and `& 7` as INSIDE the
enumeration because they "weaken `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3`, a predicate the fix DEPENDS
ON" -- and in the same answer listed `/4 -> /2` as an example of OUTSIDE it. **Both edits
weaken the same expression.** Either both are inside or both are outside; the boundary
cannot run between the mask and the divisor of one assignment. Referred back for

its own enumeration.

### codex refuted the round's own framing twice, on precision

**"`r == 3` is itself out of bounds" was wrong as written**, and both the round and the
adjudicating seat had said it. Computing 3 is not an out-of-bounds access; only `array[r]`
would be, and nothing on the r == 3 path indexes -- `default:` is two `debug()` calls. The
substance survives (the deleted block *was* doing bounds duty, and that path is new), but
the sentence overstated it and is now precise.

**And the "two halves" invariant was itself incomplete.** `/ 2` keeps `& 3` *and* keeps
every case label compliant -- it satisfies both stated halves textually while breaking the
mapping. Half (ii) now pins the WHOLE index expression, divisor and mask together, because
that is what the escapes actually attack.

### The assert question was settled by source, not by aphorism

The round argued "a guard that cannot fire is not insurance." A seat called that too broad
-- correctly -- and supplied the real reason: `configure:312-314` adds `-DNDEBUG` unless
`DEBUG=YES`, so **an `assert(r < 3)` compiles out of every default build and protects
nothing shipped**. In a debug build it would abort the host on guest input, which is the
defect being removed. Comment plus rows is the right form, for a checkable reason rather
than a slogan.

### "Reddens ALONE" is a property of the ROW SET, and carrying it forward would be a false record

Table 1's headline result was that each accept mutant reddened exactly one row: `r == 2` hit
`safe 8` alone, `r == 1` hit `safe 4` alone, the null medium hit `asic ok` alone. That
isolation is what proves a row carries something *by itself* -- it is the whole reason
`r == 2` was chosen over `r >= 2`.

**At twelve rows those same mutants no longer isolate**, and nothing went wrong: `alias2`
writes +0x18 (r = 2), so `r == 2` legitimately kills it too; `alias` and `crossarr` write
+0x14 and +0x24 (r = 1), so `r == 1` kills them as well. The new rows exercise the same
selectors on purpose.

So the two claims have to be kept apart, because only one of them survives the row set
growing:

* **DISCHARGE** -- "this accept row dies under a guard-growth mutant" -- holds at 9 rows and
  at 12. That is what the de-escalation clause actually requires.
* **ISOLATION** -- "it dies ALONE" -- is a NINE-ROW result and is cited as such.

*This is the same shape as the frozen-number defect: a number, or a qualifier, that was true
of the artifact that produced it and is quietly restated about a different one.*

### *** THE ADJUDICATION CORRECTED ITSELF, IN THE STRICTER DIRECTION, AND A PACKET-FED SEAT IS WHY ***

The section above records the re-label of the three new mutants from **L1** to **L2/L3**. That
re-label was **partly wrong, and the adjudicator withdrew it** after a seat with no file access
found the inconsistency in it.

**The inconsistency.** The adjudication called `& 2` and `& 7` INSIDE the depends-on
enumeration because they "weaken `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3`, a predicate the fix DEPENDS
ON" -- and in the same answer listed `/4 -> /2` as an example of OUTSIDE it. Both edit the
same assignment. **No principled line runs through the middle of one expression.**

**The ruling, and the reason it is credible: it is STRICTER than what it replaces.** All four
mask/divisor mutants are OUTSIDE the floor. The adjudicator's own diagnosis of its error is
worth keeping: it had imported an earlier round's `& 3 -> & 1` example *without its licensing
condition* -- there the mask was **ADDED by the fix**, so weakening it nulled a shipped repair;
here `& 3` predates the fix, and this diff adds no predicate and keeps no guard, so that branch
never applies. And the strictness point lands on cleaner ground than dominance: the assignment
*is* a CFG predecessor of the deleted lines, but the bound clause enumerates **predicates**,
and a definition is not one.

> **THE RULE, FINAL FORM.** A mutant is INSIDE the depends-on enumeration iff it (1) weakens a
> predicate the DIFF ADDED; (2) for a de-fatalisation, swaps the KEPT guard's operand to a
> field the guarded body reads; or (3) for a pure deletion, re-introduces the REMOVED behaviour
> under a different predicate over the same operands the deleted predicate read.
> **Definitions feeding those predicates are NEVER inside -- even in the same statement.**
> One-question test: *does this mutant restore the removed behaviour, or null a repair the diff
> shipped?* If it instead changes address decode, value semantics or struct layout, it is
> COVERAGE.

**Applied to this round:** `Mb` is floor (b). `Md1`/`Md2`/`Mr0` are shape 3 -- floor-(d)
reroutes doubling as the de-escalation accept kills. **`M2`/`M1`/`M7` and `/ 2` are COVERAGE**,
added under L1 from the pass-2 harvest while the detector was unshipped. They carry no clause
letter.

*** AND THE SENTENCE THAT HAD TO BE RETRACTED IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. *** The earlier
adjudication said a post-ship `M2`/`M7` escape would be an **"L2 floor breach"**. It would
not -- it is **coverage debt, and it gets FILED**. A mislabelled floor is a standing licence to
fix in-round, pre-authorised by the adjudicator, which is the worst possible place for a
widened enumeration to live.

**Credit, distributed accurately rather than flatteringly:** the round's ORIGINAL `L1` label
for the three decode rows was **right**. The re-label was right only for `Mr0`/`asic ok` (L3,
de-escalation) and for the reroutes' floor status.

*And one observation that falls out of the corrected structure:* under `& 7` the **original
guard would not have announced the out-of-bounds either** -- +0x10 gives r = 4, and `r == 3`
never tested that. So the mask family is not even in the de-escalation clause's "edits the old
`exit(1)` would have announced" class. **It is protection the pre-fix code also lacked**, which
is the honest way to describe what `crossarr` adds.

### The N/M convention, stated once, because a seat spent 59 KB deciding which number was which

**`N/M` throughout this record means N rows PASSED of M run.** The reddened count is `M - N`.

That is not pedantry. An audit seat produced 59 KB of visible reasoning cycling between "N is
the reddened count" and "N is the passing count", resolving it only by back-inference from a
prose sentence. A second seat read a table row as an ENUMERATION of every reddened row when it
named only the obligation-relevant one, and correctly reported the arithmetic as impossible.

**Both are the same defect: a number whose meaning is inferable rather than stated.** This round
already fixed one instance -- "5/9 RED" read by a seat as *five rows red* -- and did not
generalise it. The obligation table above now names rows without a score beside them, so a row
list is never read as a complete census; the full per-mutant scores live in the kill table, where
the vectors make the count unambiguous.

### *** THE CAPPED ASK-AGAIN BROKE THE CLEAN TABLE, AND THE REASON IS THE FINDING ***

The detector was green: twelve rows, ten mutants, every prediction matched name-for-name. The one
permitted ask-again then produced a **measured 12/12 escape** — and a second one alongside it.

```diff
-	r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3;
+	r = ((relative_addr / 4) + 1) & 3;
```

**Why all three purpose-built rows miss it, and this is worth more than the mutant:**

> `alias`, `alias2` and `crossarr` are **distinctness** tests, and all three read back `+0x10`.
> Together they assert only `cell(+0x10) != cell(+0x14), cell(+0x18), cell(+0x24)`. **They never
> assert WHICH cell any offset names. Distinctness is invariant under any injective re-map, and a
> translation is injective** — slide every address one word and all three pairs stay distinct.

They were blind **by construction, not by omission** — which is precisely what a clean table
cannot reveal and what the ask-again exists to find.

**And it is a real defect, verified by compiling the declaration rather than reasoning about it.**
`offsetof`: `pending_irq 0, mask_13 12, mask_11 24, mask_9 36, asserted_13 48`. Under `+1` every
`+0x?8` register moves from r = 2 to r = **3** — one past a `[3]` array — and `mask_9[3]` **IS**
`asserted_13`. So one aligned 32-bit guest store to `+0x38`, a documented register, writes the
interrupt-assertion latch; the write arm's own `dev_dreamcast_asic_tick()` then recomputes and
issues a spurious `INTERRUPT_DEASSERT`, dropping a legitimately pending IRQ13. ASan cannot see it
— member-to-member inside one allocation.

### The disposition turned on a membership test, not on how clean the sweep was

A 12/12 escape outside every obligation is FILED however clean. The de-escalation clause carries
its own membership test, and it is mechanical:

> **Apply the candidate edit to the PRE-FIX code. Does the old `exit(1)` fire on legitimate
> traffic?**

| edit | pre-fix `exit(1)` fires on legal registers | in class? |
|---|---|---|
| `+1` | `+0x08`, `+0x18`, `+0x28`, `+0x38` | **YES** |
| `-1` | `+0x00`, `+0x10`, `+0x20`, `+0x30` | **YES** — already killed by `crossarr` |
| `& 2`, `& 1`, `& 7`, `/ 2`, array shrink | none | no |

So `+1` is an edit the defect **used to announce** and this fix de-announced — the accidental
tripwire, in the clause's own words. An accept obligation is discharged by a **measured kill,
never by existing**, and *a fortiori* never by prose. **Words could not pay this debt.**

`mask9 rt` ships as **L3**, and its oracle is ANCHORED rather than relative: it is tied to a
specific cell by a channel outside the decode under test — the tick zeroes `asserted_13`, so the
readback is `0x0` rather than merely different. **Measured: `Mplus1` scores 12/13, reddening
`mask9 rt` ALONE** (`table5_13rows/probe_Mplus1.raw`); base is 13/13.

*The adjudication's own membership table omitted `-1`, having used it only as an asymmetry
control. Running the test exhaustively put it in the class too — already discharged, but it is
why the contract now claims **±1 measured** rather than "translations".*

### What was NOT taken, and why that matters more than what was

The second escape — `uint32_t mask_13[3]` → `[2]`, also a clean 12/12 — is **FILED**. It fails
the membership test (pre-fix, r = 2 passes the old guard and the out-of-bounds access is silent
under the original code too), it edits the ARRAY BOUND rather than the bound on `r`, and the
detector has shipped so L1 is unavailable. Its closing row was **already built and measured** —
which is exactly why filing it took discipline. *"Built and works" was never a license*, and each
shipped row enlarges the re-measure surface of every future table.

### The gate wiring was reviewed before installation, and the review found a false green

Three seats read the 51-line block before it went in. All three independently found the same
defect:

```sh
check "asic_badaddr rows correct" "${asres%/*}" "${asres#*/}"
```

If the result line is present but MALFORMED, the outer `grep -q` still succeeds, `asres` is
empty, and **both sides expand to the empty string — so the check PASSES while nothing was
measured.** The sibling `rows run` check would still redden the gate, so it was never a silent
green overall; it was a false green ROW, which is worse than useless because a reader scanning
check output is misled about which part failed. It is the project's own *"a pattern that matched
nothing reports zero for everything"* class wearing shell-expansion clothes.

Fixed with a parse guard and **negative-controlled in five directions**, run rather than reasoned:

| result line | outcome |
|---|---|
| `13/13` | 0 FAIL, all thirteen per-row checks pass |
| `13` (no slash) | `result parses` FAILS — was a vacuous PASS |
| `=` (empty) | `result parses` FAILS |
| absent | `probe completed` FAILS |
| **a row silently dropped** | **TWO FAILs — the denominator pin AND the per-row presence check** |

One seat also computed a hard bound the block now documents: **row names must be <= 13 characters.**
The probe's `%-14s ` leaves `15 - L` spaces after a name of length L, so at 14 the two-space grep
anchor becomes unsatisfiable and **the row silently stops being tested while the gate stays
green.** Longest name here is `kill store` at 10, so there are three characters of headroom.

*A gate that reddens correctly on four kinds of broken input and on a missing row is worth the
one invocation it cost to review.*
